title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I needed a new phone because I was fed up with my 15 that I'd gone el cheapo on. It was too small compared to the android I had switched from, and it didn't have enough storage space so it was to the point that I didn't even have space to install updates and that caused some weird things like my calendar events just disappearing.

I'm not great at texting with my thumbs. My vision isn't what it used to be, I guess the pads of my thumbs aren't as full either. I struggled with texting so I tended to use the voice-to-text feature mostly. And even though they've been doing dictation software since the 90s, it's still pretty terrible. Don't get me started on the camera either. My android's camera blew the iPhone's out of the water and it was at least 3 years older.

So, this 16 Pro Max phone hits on a few areas that I was looking to improve and it does it well. It's the largest screen they offer and comes with twice the storage. The voice-to-text seems to be somewhat better but still causes some frustration at times. The camera is much better but I'm still not sure if it's better than the old android.

But now I have to talk about the fact that this is a "renewed" phone to begin with. I went with the "Renewed Premium" because I wanted as close to a new phone as possible but without spending all that money. I considered this the last chance I would give to Apple before I switched back to Android - I didn't want to pay a fortune to find out that I was still unsatisfied - and this seemed the best route to take.

I was not disappointed. Other than not coming in an iPhone box, there wasn't the slightest clue that it was not a new phone, cosmetically. I had no issues getting it set up - I mean it was crazy easy using the tools / instructions that you can find just by going into AI mode on a Google search. I love my phone now. My old mantra was "I hate this phone" or "This phone is a piece of ..." . I had dreams of running it over with my car.

I haven't had any issue with the functionality of this renewed phone either. I'm finding a lot of features that are endearing me to the brand too. I don't have to worry about storage, I have a larger screen (but I'm still not that much better at texting), and I'm dealing with the voice to text still. But as far as the product I received, I'm soooo very happy I went this route.

Now for the thing that I really was disappointed about. The trade-in value of my old phone (which was in excellent condition) is about $35 less than I would have gotten through Apple - but they only sell the most current version of a Pro Max phone, so I couldn't have gotten the 16 Pro Max through them anyway as the 17 model was already out in stores.

When I was working with my budget I thought that the $275 would be taken off the price of the phone but I can see now how naive it was to think that. They're not going to give you money for a phone upfront, sight unseen. So I just figured that it would work out since they would apply the credit back to the card once they'd received and checked out my trade-in.

Ooooh was I mistaken! First of all, they do not treat it like a refund where they add the funds to your original method of payment. Instead, you get Amazon credit. And by credit, I mean that you can ONLY spend that money on Amazon.

You cannot buy a gift card offered on Amazon for another store (for example, Best Buy), you cannot even get an Amazon gift card with it. I needed the funds to go towards my car stereo that I was planning to buy at a different store (because they install it for free as long as I purchase it from them) but I wasn't permitted to use the credit on that. I thought that maybe I could get it in a Amazon gift card, and then get my friend to buy that from me. Nope.

If it weren't for the trade in process I would have been 100% happy with my purchase.

It's only because this phone was exactly as described and pictured that I am happy. And ultimately, things worked out for me with the trade-in credit situation when my son was buying an eScooter and agreed to send me the money so I could purchase it from my account and apply that credit towards the purchase.

So the moral of the story is that this renewed phone was a great route to go (I'm speaking to the Renewed Premium offerings), and I was very happy with the phone, both cosmetically and functionally. You just need to be fully aware of how the trade-in works (and its limitations) so you don't get frustrated in the end.

The voice-to-text seems to be somewhat better but still causes some frustration at times. The camera is much better but I'm still not sure if it's better than the old android.

But now I have to talk about the fact that this is a "renewed" phone to begin with. I went with the "Renewed Premium" because I wanted as close to a new phone as possible but without spending all that money. I considered this the last chance I would give to Apple before I switched back to Android - I didn't want to pay a fortune to find out that I was still unsatisfied - and this seemed the best route to take.

You just need to be fully aware of how the trade-in works (and its limitations) so you don't get frustrated in the end.

Video recording is equally strong, giving vibrant colors and smooth stabilization across formats I’ve tested. For both casual snaps and more ambitious content, the iPhone 16 Pro delivers.

What’s particularly impressive about this renewed model is how new it feels in everyday use. Battery life remains strong throughout a full day of regular use. I can comfortably go from morning to night without needing a top-up. When I do need to charger, fast charging gets me going quickly, and wireless (MagSafe or Qi) charging is smooth and reliable.

Compared to buying new, getting this unlocked 256 GB version saved a significant amount of money, making it excellent value for what is still a top-tier device.

If you’re after a powerful, premium smartphone that performs just like new but without the full retail cost, the Apple iPhone 16 Pro (256 GB, Black Titanium, Unlocked and Renewed) is an excellent choice. title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I bought this phone to replace my very beloved yellow iPhone 11. Its battery desperately needed replaced, I had long outgrown the 128gb internal storage, and it recently developed a few dead pixels that turned into... many... that spread across the top of my screen. Nail in the coffin. I was quoted about $400 to repair it at the authorized shop Apple directed me to, so I decided it was just time to upgrade altogether. I LOVE my stupid little banana yellow phone and I don't care too much about new gen features, the only notable exception being the new camera specs, so I almost got a 15 instead. I don't think there's enough of a difference between 15 and 16 overall, but I obviously like my phones to last a long time, so I opted for the latest model purely for longevity's sake. The 16 Pro is also basically the same dimensions as the 11, so it doesn't feel any different in my hand than what I've been used to for the past 6 years.

I use Mint Mobile, so I needed an unlocked phone, hence why I purchased here. I bought a listing being sold and shipped directly by amazon.com instead of a third party seller. I had originally bought a listing from the seller "Wcell" but they never shipped it, then gave me a new shipping estimate of another month... So I canceled and reordered directly from amazon. I figured it would be less hassle to skip a third party seller if I needed to return the phone, anyway.

I paid for shipping so I would get it sooner. I did NOT get it sooner (or even soon in general) and it was shipped via USPS instead of UPS or Fedex, which shocked me. I've never had something so expensive shipped parcel select before. Why did I even pay shipping? Phone arrived in an unassuming box aside from the giant lithium battery warning sticker, which gives away that it's an electronic no matter how discreet they try to be. Inside package was another plain box with a serial number sticker on it, containing the phone and an unbranded double USB C charging cable. Nothing else. No paper, no invoice, not even an Amazon Renewed flyer I've seen in other reviews. It sat in my mailbox under the hot sun for a few hours before I could get to it, which is Not Great for the battery, and when I opened it the phone was hot to the touch. So keep this in mind when ordering.

The phone's outer condition is okay, but not quite up to the standard promised. This phone was listed as REFURBISHED - EXCELLENT, which states it should have "no visible cosmetic imperfections when held at an arm's length". However there are multiple scrapes on the titanium trim around the screen, leaving highly visible shiny silver specks against the black titanium, and a large scratch in the screen itself (pictured) The placement of the scratches lead me to believe the screen has been removed and the metal was scraped by a jimmy tool while prying it open. Maybe the screen was replaced? Maybe the screen had to be removed for another repair? Who knows. I would be surprised if it was a replacement unless they managed to scratch the new screen immediately after.

The battery is GREAT. It arrived to me at 1%, but that's the mail's fault. Phone has been anctive since December 2024 but battery only has TWO (2) cycles on it and 100% capacity. The battery was definitely freshly replaced.

I personally don't mind the cosmetic damage enough to worry about trying to get a replacement, it took long enough to get it as is and the phone itself works just fine. If anything now I won't feel bad if I add a flaw in the future, but I know a lot of people won't feel the same way I do so I wanted to put my experience out there.

So to recap, phone is what I would call Repaired. Brand new battery replacement, suspected screen replacement, with some cosmetic damage. Otherwise perfectly fine phone. I'll update if anything changes with normal use.

RIP in peace banana phone. You served me well 🍌 🫡

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I bought this phone to replace my very beloved yellow iPhone 11. Its battery desperately needed replaced, I had long outgrown the 128gb internal storage, and it recently developed a few dead pixels that turned into... many... that spread across the top of my screen. Nail in the coffin. I was quoted about $400 to repair it at the authorized shop Apple directed me to, so I decided it was just time to upgrade altogether. I LOVE my stupid little banana yellow phone and I don't care too much about new gen features, the only notable exception being the new camera specs, so I almost got a 15 instead. I don't think there's enough of a difference between 15 and 16 overall, but I obviously like my phones to last a long time, so I opted for the latest model purely for longevity's sake. The 16 Pro is also basically the same dimensions as the 11, so it doesn't feel any different in my hand than what I've been used to for the past 6 years.

I use Mint Mobile, so I needed an unlocked phone, hence why I purchased here. I bought a listing being sold and shipped directly by amazon.com instead of a third party seller. I had originally bought a listing from the seller "Wcell" but they never shipped it, then gave me a new shipping estimate of another month... So I canceled and reordered directly from amazon. I figured it would be less hassle to skip a third party seller if I needed to return the phone, anyway.

I paid for shipping so I would get it sooner. I did NOT get it sooner (or even soon in general) and it was shipped via USPS instead of UPS or Fedex, which shocked me. I've never had something so expensive shipped parcel select before. Why did I even pay shipping? Phone arrived in an unassuming box aside from the giant lithium battery warning sticker, which gives away that it's an electronic no matter how discreet they try to be. Inside package was another plain box with a serial number sticker on it, containing the phone and an unbranded double USB C charging cable. Nothing else. No paper, no invoice, not even an Amazon Renewed flyer I've seen in other reviews. It sat in my mailbox under the hot sun for a few hours before I could get to it, which is Not Great for the battery, and when I opened it the phone was hot to the touch. So keep this in mind when ordering.

The phone's outer condition is okay, but not quite up to the standard promised. This phone was listed as REFURBISHED - EXCELLENT, which states it should have "no visible cosmetic imperfections when held at an arm's length". However there are multiple scrapes on the titanium trim around the screen, leaving highly visible shiny silver specks against the black titanium, and a large scratch in the screen itself (pictured) The placement of the scratches lead me to believe the screen has been removed and the metal was scraped by a jimmy tool while prying it open. Maybe the screen was replaced? Maybe the screen had to be removed for another repair? Who knows. I would be surprised if it was a replacement unless they managed to scratch the new screen immediately after.

The battery is GREAT. It arrived to me at 1%, but that's the mail's fault. Phone has been anctive since December 2024 but battery only has TWO (2) cycles on it and 100% capacity. The battery was definitely freshly replaced.

I personally don't mind the cosmetic damage enough to worry about trying to get a replacement, it took long enough to get it as is and the phone itself works just fine. If anything now I won't feel bad if I add a flaw in the future, but I know a lot of people won't feel the same way I do so I wanted to put my experience out there.

So to recap, phone is what I would call Repaired. Brand new battery replacement, suspected screen replacement, with some cosmetic damage. Otherwise perfectly fine phone. I'll update if anything changes with normal use.

RIP in peace banana phone. You served me well 🍌 🫡

text:
I bought this phone to replace my very beloved yellow iPhone 11. Its battery desperately needed replaced, I had long outgrown the 128gb internal storage, and it recently developed a few dead pixels that turned into... many... that spread across the top of my screen. Nail in the coffin. I was quoted about $400 to repair it at the authorized shop Apple directed me to, so I decided it was just time to upgrade altogether. I LOVE my stupid little banana yellow phone and I don't care too much about new gen features, the only notable exception being the new camera specs, so I almost got a 15 instead. I don't think there's enough of a difference between 15 and 16 overall, but I obviously like my phones to last a long time, so I opted for the latest model purely for longevity's sake. The 16 Pro is also basically the same dimensions as the 11, so it doesn't feel any different in my hand than what I've been used to for the past 6 years.

I use Mint Mobile, so I needed an unlocked phone, hence why I purchased here. I bought a listing being sold and shipped directly by amazon.com instead of a third party seller. I had originally bought a listing from the seller "Wcell" but they never shipped it, then gave me a new shipping estimate of another month... So I canceled and reordered directly from amazon. I figured it would be less hassle to skip a third party seller if I needed to return the phone, anyway.

I paid for shipping so I would get it sooner. I did NOT get it sooner (or even soon in general) and it was shipped via USPS instead of UPS or Fedex, which shocked me. I've never had something so expensive shipped parcel select before. Why did I even pay shipping? Phone arrived in an unassuming box aside from the giant lithium battery warning sticker, which gives away that it's an electronic no matter how discreet they try to be. Inside package was another plain box with a serial number sticker on it, containing the phone and an unbranded double USB C charging cable. Nothing else. No paper, no invoice, not even an Amazon Renewed flyer I've seen in other reviews. It sat in my mailbox under the hot sun for a few hours before I could get to it, which is Not Great for the battery, and when I opened it the phone was hot to the touch. So keep this in mind when ordering.

The phone's outer condition is okay, but not quite up to the standard promised. This phone was listed as REFURBISHED - EXCELLENT, which states it should have "no visible cosmetic imperfections when held at an arm's length". However there are multiple scrapes on the titanium trim around the screen, leaving highly visible shiny silver specks against the black titanium, and a large scratch in the screen itself (pictured) The placement of the scratches lead me to believe the screen has been removed and the metal was scraped by a jimmy tool while prying it open. Maybe the screen was replaced? Maybe the screen had to be removed for another repair? Who knows. I would be surprised if it was a replacement unless they managed to scratch the new screen immediately after.

The battery is GREAT. It arrived to me at 1%, but that's the mail's fault. Phone has been anctive since December 2024 but battery only has TWO (2) cycles on it and 100% capacity. The battery was definitely freshly replaced.

I personally don't mind the cosmetic damage enough to worry about trying to get a replacement, it took long enough to get it as is and the phone itself works just fine. If anything now I won't feel bad if I add a flaw in the future, but I know a lot of people won't feel the same way I do so I wanted to put my experience out there.

So to recap, phone is what I would call Repaired. Brand new battery replacement, suspected screen replacement, with some cosmetic damage. Otherwise perfectly fine phone. I'll update if anything changes with normal use.

RIP in peace banana phone. You served me well 🍌 🫡

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I bought this phone to replace my very beloved yellow iPhone 11. Its battery desperately needed replaced, I had long outgrown the 128gb internal storage, and it recently developed a few dead pixels that turned into... many... that spread across the top of my screen. Nail in the coffin. I was quoted about $400 to repair it at the authorized shop Apple directed me to, so I decided it was just time to upgrade altogether. I LOVE my stupid little banana yellow phone and I don't care too much about new gen features, the only notable exception being the new camera specs, so I almost got a 15 instead. I don't think there's enough of a difference between 15 and 16 overall, but I obviously like my phones to last a long time, so I opted for the latest model purely for longevity's sake. The 16 Pro is also basically the same dimensions as the 11, so it doesn't feel any different in my hand than what I've been used to for the past 6 years.

I use Mint Mobile, so I needed an unlocked phone, hence why I purchased here. I bought a listing being sold and shipped directly by amazon.com instead of a third party seller. I had originally bought a listing from the seller "Wcell" but they never shipped it, then gave me a new shipping estimate of another month... So I canceled and reordered directly from amazon. I figured it would be less hassle to skip a third party seller if I needed to return the phone, anyway.

I paid for shipping so I would get it sooner. I did NOT get it sooner (or even soon in general) and it was shipped via USPS instead of UPS or Fedex, which shocked me. I've never had something so expensive shipped parcel select before. Why did I even pay shipping? Phone arrived in an unassuming box aside from the giant lithium battery warning sticker, which gives away that it's an electronic no matter how discreet they try to be. Inside package was another plain box with a serial number sticker on it, containing the phone and an unbranded double USB C charging cable. Nothing else. No paper, no invoice, not even an Amazon Renewed flyer I've seen in other reviews. It sat in my mailbox under the hot sun for a few hours before I could get to it, which is Not Great for the battery, and when I opened it the phone was hot to the touch. So keep this in mind when ordering.

The phone's outer condition is okay, but not quite up to the standard promised. This phone was listed as REFURBISHED - EXCELLENT, which states it should have "no visible cosmetic imperfections when held at an arm's length". However there are multiple scrapes on the titanium trim around the screen, leaving highly visible shiny silver specks against the black titanium, and a large scratch in the screen itself (pictured) The placement of the scratches lead me to believe the screen has been removed and the metal was scraped by a jimmy tool while prying it open. Maybe the screen was replaced? Maybe the screen had to be removed for another repair? Who knows. I would be surprised if it was a replacement unless they managed to scratch the new screen immediately after.

The battery is GREAT. It arrived to me at 1%, but that's the mail's fault. Phone has been anctive since December 2024 but battery only has TWO (2) cycles on it and 100% capacity. The battery was definitely freshly replaced.

I personally don't mind the cosmetic damage enough to worry about trying to get a replacement, it took long enough to get it as is and the phone itself works just fine. If anything now I won't feel bad if I add a flaw in the future, but I know a lot of people won't feel the same way I do so I wanted to put my experience out there.

So to recap, phone is what I would call Repaired. Brand new battery replacement, suspected screen replacement, with some cosmetic damage. Otherwise perfectly fine phone. I'll update if anything changes with normal use.

RIP in peace banana phone. You served me well 🍌 🫡

text:
I bought this phone to replace my very beloved yellow iPhone 11. Its battery desperately needed replaced, I had long outgrown the 128gb internal storage, and it recently developed a few dead pixels that turned into... many... that spread across the top of my screen. Nail in the coffin. I was quoted about $400 to repair it at the authorized shop Apple directed me to, so I decided it was just time to upgrade altogether. I LOVE my stupid little banana yellow phone and I don't care too much about new gen features, the only notable exception being the new camera specs, so I almost got a 15 instead. I don't think there's enough of a difference between 15 and 16 overall, but I obviously like my phones to last a long time, so I opted for the latest model purely for longevity's sake. The 16 Pro is also basically the same dimensions as the 11, so it doesn't feel any different in my hand than what I've been used to for the past 6 years.

I use Mint Mobile, so I needed an unlocked phone, hence why I purchased here. I bought a listing being sold and shipped directly by amazon.com instead of a third party seller. I had originally bought a listing from the seller "Wcell" but they never shipped it, then gave me a new shipping estimate of another month... So I canceled and reordered directly from amazon. I figured it would be less hassle to skip a third party seller if I needed to return the phone, anyway.

I paid for shipping so I would get it sooner. I did NOT get it sooner (or even soon in general) and it was shipped via USPS instead of UPS or Fedex, which shocked me. I've never had something so expensive shipped parcel select before. Why did I even pay shipping? Phone arrived in an unassuming box aside from the giant lithium battery warning sticker, which gives away that it's an electronic no matter how discreet they try to be. Inside package was another plain box with a serial number sticker on it, containing the phone and an unbranded double USB C charging cable. Nothing else. No paper, no invoice, not even an Amazon Renewed flyer I've seen in other reviews. It sat in my mailbox under the hot sun for a few hours before I could get to it, which is Not Great for the battery, and when I opened it the phone was hot to the touch. So keep this in mind when ordering.

The phone's outer condition is okay, but not quite up to the standard promised. This phone was listed as REFURBISHED - EXCELLENT, which states it should have "no visible cosmetic imperfections when held at an arm's length". However there are multiple scrapes on the titanium trim around the screen, leaving highly visible shiny silver specks against the black titanium, and a large scratch in the screen itself (pictured) The placement of the scratches lead me to believe the screen has been removed and the metal was scraped by a jimmy tool while prying it open. Maybe the screen was replaced? Maybe the screen had to be removed for another repair? Who knows. I would be surprised if it was a replacement unless they managed to scratch the new screen immediately after.

The battery is GREAT. It arrived to me at 1%, but that's the mail's fault. Phone has been anctive since December 2024 but battery only has TWO (2) cycles on it and 100% capacity. The battery was definitely freshly replaced.

I personally don't mind the cosmetic damage enough to worry about trying to get a replacement, it took long enough to get it as is and the phone itself works just fine. If anything now I won't feel bad if I add a flaw in the future, but I know a lot of people won't feel the same way I do so I wanted to put my experience out there.

So to recap, phone is what I would call Repaired. Brand new battery replacement, suspected screen replacement, with some cosmetic damage. Otherwise perfectly fine phone. I'll update if anything changes with normal use.

RIP in peace banana phone. You served me well 🍌 🫡

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I bought this phone to replace my very beloved yellow iPhone 11. Its battery desperately needed replaced, I had long outgrown the 128gb internal storage, and it recently developed a few dead pixels that turned into... many... that spread across the top of my screen. Nail in the coffin. I was quoted about $400 to repair it at the authorized shop Apple directed me to, so I decided it was just time to upgrade altogether. I LOVE my stupid little banana yellow phone and I don't care too much about new gen features, the only notable exception being the new camera specs, so I almost got a 15 instead. I don't think there's enough of a difference between 15 and 16 overall, but I obviously like my phones to last a long time, so I opted for the latest model purely for longevity's sake. The 16 Pro is also basically the same dimensions as the 11, so it doesn't feel any different in my hand than what I've been used to for the past 6 years.

I use Mint Mobile, so I needed an unlocked phone, hence why I purchased here. I bought a listing being sold and shipped directly by amazon.com instead of a third party seller. I had originally bought a listing from the seller "Wcell" but they never shipped it, then gave me a new shipping estimate of another month... So I canceled and reordered directly from amazon. I figured it would be less hassle to skip a third party seller if I needed to return the phone, anyway.

I paid for shipping so I would get it sooner. I did NOT get it sooner (or even soon in general) and it was shipped via USPS instead of UPS or Fedex, which shocked me. I've never had something so expensive shipped parcel select before. Why did I even pay shipping? Phone arrived in an unassuming box aside from the giant lithium battery warning sticker, which gives away that it's an electronic no matter how discreet they try to be. Inside package was another plain box with a serial number sticker on it, containing the phone and an unbranded double USB C charging cable. Nothing else. No paper, no invoice, not even an Amazon Renewed flyer I've seen in other reviews. It sat in my mailbox under the hot sun for a few hours before I could get to it, which is Not Great for the battery, and when I opened it the phone was hot to the touch. So keep this in mind when ordering.

The phone's outer condition is okay, but not quite up to the standard promised. This phone was listed as REFURBISHED - EXCELLENT, which states it should have "no visible cosmetic imperfections when held at an arm's length". However there are multiple scrapes on the titanium trim around the screen, leaving highly visible shiny silver specks against the black titanium, and a large scratch in the screen itself (pictured) The placement of the scratches lead me to believe the screen has been removed and the metal was scraped by a jimmy tool while prying it open. Maybe the screen was replaced? Maybe the screen had to be removed for another repair? Who knows. I would be surprised if it was a replacement unless they managed to scratch the new screen immediately after.

The battery is GREAT. It arrived to me at 1%, but that's the mail's fault. Phone has been anctive since December 2024 but battery only has TWO (2) cycles on it and 100% capacity. The battery was definitely freshly replaced.

I personally don't mind the cosmetic damage enough to worry about trying to get a replacement, it took long enough to get it as is and the phone itself works just fine. If anything now I won't feel bad if I add a flaw in the future, but I know a lot of people won't feel the same way I do so I wanted to put my experience out there.

So to recap, phone is what I would call Repaired. Brand new battery replacement, suspected screen replacement, with some cosmetic damage. Otherwise perfectly fine phone. I'll update if anything changes with normal use.

RIP in peace banana phone. You served me well 🍌 🫡

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I needed a new phone because I was fed up with my 15 that I'd gone el cheapo on. It was too small compared to the android I had switched from, and it didn't have enough storage space so it was to the point that I didn't even have space to install updates and that caused some weird things like my calendar events just disappearing.

I'm not great at texting with my thumbs. My vision isn't what it used to be, I guess the pads of my thumbs aren't as full either. I struggled with texting so I tended to use the voice-to-text feature mostly. And even though they've been doing dictation software since the 90s, it's still pretty terrible. Don't get me started on the camera either. My android's camera blew the iPhone's out of the water and it was at least 3 years older.

So, this 16 Pro Max phone hits on a few areas that I was looking to improve and it does it well. It's the largest screen they offer and comes with twice the storage. The voice-to-text seems to be somewhat better but still causes some frustration at times. The camera is much better but I'm still not sure if it's better than the old android.

But now I have to talk about the fact that this is a "renewed" phone to begin with. I went with the "Renewed Premium" because I wanted as close to a new phone as possible but without spending all that money. I considered this the last chance I would give to Apple before I switched back to Android - I didn't want to pay a fortune to find out that I was still unsatisfied - and this seemed the best route to take.

I was not disappointed. Other than not coming in an iPhone box, there wasn't the slightest clue that it was not a new phone, cosmetically. I had no issues getting it set up - I mean it was crazy easy using the tools / instructions that you can find just by going into AI mode on a Google search. I love my phone now. My old mantra was "I hate this phone" or "This phone is a piece of ..." . I had dreams of running it over with my car.

I haven't had any issue with the functionality of this renewed phone either. I'm finding a lot of features that are endearing me to the brand too. I don't have to worry about storage, I have a larger screen (but I'm still not that much better at texting), and I'm dealing with the voice to text still. But as far as the product I received, I'm soooo very happy I went this route.

Now for the thing that I really was disappointed about. The trade-in value of my old phone (which was in excellent condition) is about $35 less than I would have gotten through Apple - but they only sell the most current version of a Pro Max phone, so I couldn't have gotten the 16 Pro Max through them anyway as the 17 model was already out in stores.

When I was working with my budget I thought that the $275 would be taken off the price of the phone but I can see now how naive it was to think that. They're not going to give you money for a phone upfront, sight unseen. So I just figured that it would work out since they would apply the credit back to the card once they'd received and checked out my trade-in.

Ooooh was I mistaken! First of all, they do not treat it like a refund where they add the funds to your original method of payment. Instead, you get Amazon credit. And by credit, I mean that you can ONLY spend that money on Amazon.

You cannot buy a gift card offered on Amazon for another store (for example, Best Buy), you cannot even get an Amazon gift card with it. I needed the funds to go towards my car stereo that I was planning to buy at a different store (because they install it for free as long as I purchase it from them) but I wasn't permitted to use the credit on that. I thought that maybe I could get it in a Amazon gift card, and then get my friend to buy that from me. Nope.

If it weren't for the trade in process I would have been 100% happy with my purchase.

It's only because this phone was exactly as described and pictured that I am happy. And ultimately, things worked out for me with the trade-in credit situation when my son was buying an eScooter and agreed to send me the money so I could purchase it from my account and apply that credit towards the purchase.

So the moral of the story is that this renewed phone was a great route to go (I'm speaking to the Renewed Premium offerings), and I was very happy with the phone, both cosmetically and functionally. You just need to be fully aware of how the trade-in works (and its limitations) so you don't get frustrated in the end.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Ok, I’m a galaxy gal with a S25 Ultra phone. People tell me try Apple’s iPhone, and I put it off for more than 12 years. However, I do own 2 Apple Mac Minis, and I like the computers. Well, I looked up iPhones on Amazon and other sites and came across this iPhone 16 Max Pro with 8 gig ram and 1 terabyte storage for just a little over 900 dollars. A lot of money for an iPhone that’s a year old I thought.

So I took the risk and made the purchase.

When I got the package in the mail I hesitated even opening the box and contemplated just returning it back without giving it a chance. Well, after opening the box and charging it up, I transferred my data over to the iPhone 16 Pro Max and it worked well and fairly easy too.

I still wasn’t too impressed with the iPhone just yet, but I gave it a chance.

As I began using it and saw the battery life was at 98 % I thought, WOW, nice iPhone with a pretty decent battery too. I also noticed it still has an Apple warranty until March of 2026.

The phone is beautiful and works great thus far, but my niece said I should get the iPhone 17 Pro Max. So I looked it up and didn’t see why I should go into a 2k debt for an iPhone 17 pro max with a 1 terabyte storage drive. After all, my iPhone 16 Pro Max still gets another 6 years of updates on the iOS software.

I have to say I still have time to return this iPhone, but, right now, this is a well made and solid purchase and I feel very comfortable with it after 2 weeks of use. I still have my android Galaxy S25 Ultra, and I’m gonna keep it too, but the seller of this iPhone certainly does ship out beautiful and quality iPhones to the buyers. No scratches or dings and a great battery life too. The item arrived with great packaging and I am impressed with this seller.

Now my niece with the iPhone 17 pro max with 256 gig of storage loves her phone, she’s had it for about a month now, and yes,she paid more than me and I have a 1 terabyte storage drive on mine, and her first complaint about the iPhone 17 is, the aluminum casing gets scratched up easily forcing her to get a cover so she doesn’t have to look at the scratched up case on her new iPhone.

The IPhone 16 Pro Max has a titanium frame that is solid, and I do have a case over it to protect it from drops or falls.

Would I recommend this iPhone and seller on Amazon. ABSOLUTELY YES!

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I needed a new phone because I was fed up with my 15 that I'd gone el cheapo on. It was too small compared to the android I had switched from, and it didn't have enough storage space so it was to the point that I didn't even have space to install updates and that caused some weird things like my calendar events just disappearing.

I'm not great at texting with my thumbs. My vision isn't what it used to be, I guess the pads of my thumbs aren't as full either. I struggled with texting so I tended to use the voice-to-text feature mostly. And even though they've been doing dictation software since the 90s, it's still pretty terrible. Don't get me started on the camera either. My android's camera blew the iPhone's out of the water and it was at least 3 years older.

So, this 16 Pro Max phone hits on a few areas that I was looking to improve and it does it well. It's the largest screen they offer and comes with twice the storage. The voice-to-text seems to be somewhat better but still causes some frustration at times. The camera is much better but I'm still not sure if it's better than the old android.

But now I have to talk about the fact that this is a "renewed" phone to begin with. I went with the "Renewed Premium" because I wanted as close to a new phone as possible but without spending all that money. I considered this the last chance I would give to Apple before I switched back to Android - I didn't want to pay a fortune to find out that I was still unsatisfied - and this seemed the best route to take.

I was not disappointed. Other than not coming in an iPhone box, there wasn't the slightest clue that it was not a new phone, cosmetically. I had no issues getting it set up - I mean it was crazy easy using the tools / instructions that you can find just by going into AI mode on a Google search. I love my phone now. My old mantra was "I hate this phone" or "This phone is a piece of ..." . I had dreams of running it over with my car.

I haven't had any issue with the functionality of this renewed phone either. I'm finding a lot of features that are endearing me to the brand too. I don't have to worry about storage, I have a larger screen (but I'm still not that much better at texting), and I'm dealing with the voice to text still. But as far as the product I received, I'm soooo very happy I went this route.

Now for the thing that I really was disappointed about. The trade-in value of my old phone (which was in excellent condition) is about $35 less than I would have gotten through Apple - but they only sell the most current version of a Pro Max phone, so I couldn't have gotten the 16 Pro Max through them anyway as the 17 model was already out in stores.

When I was working with my budget I thought that the $275 would be taken off the price of the phone but I can see now how naive it was to think that. They're not going to give you money for a phone upfront, sight unseen. So I just figured that it would work out since they would apply the credit back to the card once they'd received and checked out my trade-in.

Ooooh was I mistaken! First of all, they do not treat it like a refund where they add the funds to your original method of payment. Instead, you get Amazon credit. And by credit, I mean that you can ONLY spend that money on Amazon.

You cannot buy a gift card offered on Amazon for another store (for example, Best Buy), you cannot even get an Amazon gift card with it. I needed the funds to go towards my car stereo that I was planning to buy at a different store (because they install it for free as long as I purchase it from them) but I wasn't permitted to use the credit on that. I thought that maybe I could get it in a Amazon gift card, and then get my friend to buy that from me. Nope.

If it weren't for the trade in process I would have been 100% happy with my purchase.

It's only because this phone was exactly as described and pictured that I am happy. And ultimately, things worked out for me with the trade-in credit situation when my son was buying an eScooter and agreed to send me the money so I could purchase it from my account and apply that credit towards the purchase.

So the moral of the story is that this renewed phone was a great route to go (I'm speaking to the Renewed Premium offerings), and I was very happy with the phone, both cosmetically and functionally. You just need to be fully aware of how the trade-in works (and its limitations) so you don't get frustrated in the end.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I needed a new phone because I was fed up with my 15 that I'd gone el cheapo on. It was too small compared to the android I had switched from, and it didn't have enough storage space so it was to the point that I didn't even have space to install updates and that caused some weird things like my calendar events just disappearing.

I'm not great at texting with my thumbs. My vision isn't what it used to be, I guess the pads of my thumbs aren't as full either. I struggled with texting so I tended to use the voice-to-text feature mostly. And even though they've been doing dictation software since the 90s, it's still pretty terrible. Don't get me started on the camera either. My android's camera blew the iPhone's out of the water and it was at least 3 years older.

So, this 16 Pro Max phone hits on a few areas that I was looking to improve and it does it well. It's the largest screen they offer and comes with twice the storage. The voice-to-text seems to be somewhat better but still causes some frustration at times. The camera is much better but I'm still not sure if it's better than the old android.

But now I have to talk about the fact that this is a "renewed" phone to begin with. I went with the "Renewed Premium" because I wanted as close to a new phone as possible but without spending all that money. I considered this the last chance I would give to Apple before I switched back to Android - I didn't want to pay a fortune to find out that I was still unsatisfied - and this seemed the best route to take.

I was not disappointed. Other than not coming in an iPhone box, there wasn't the slightest clue that it was not a new phone, cosmetically. I had no issues getting it set up - I mean it was crazy easy using the tools / instructions that you can find just by going into AI mode on a Google search. I love my phone now. My old mantra was "I hate this phone" or "This phone is a piece of ..." . I had dreams of running it over with my car.

I haven't had any issue with the functionality of this renewed phone either. I'm finding a lot of features that are endearing me to the brand too. I don't have to worry about storage, I have a larger screen (but I'm still not that much better at texting), and I'm dealing with the voice to text still. But as far as the product I received, I'm soooo very happy I went this route.

Now for the thing that I really was disappointed about. The trade-in value of my old phone (which was in excellent condition) is about $35 less than I would have gotten through Apple - but they only sell the most current version of a Pro Max phone, so I couldn't have gotten the 16 Pro Max through them anyway as the 17 model was already out in stores.

When I was working with my budget I thought that the $275 would be taken off the price of the phone but I can see now how naive it was to think that. They're not going to give you money for a phone upfront, sight unseen. So I just figured that it would work out since they would apply the credit back to the card once they'd received and checked out my trade-in.

Ooooh was I mistaken! First of all, they do not treat it like a refund where they add the funds to your original method of payment. Instead, you get Amazon credit. And by credit, I mean that you can ONLY spend that money on Amazon.

You cannot buy a gift card offered on Amazon for another store (for example, Best Buy), you cannot even get an Amazon gift card with it. I needed the funds to go towards my car stereo that I was planning to buy at a different store (because they install it for free as long as I purchase it from them) but I wasn't permitted to use the credit on that. I thought that maybe I could get it in a Amazon gift card, and then get my friend to buy that from me. Nope.

If it weren't for the trade in process I would have been 100% happy with my purchase.

It's only because this phone was exactly as described and pictured that I am happy. And ultimately, things worked out for me with the trade-in credit situation when my son was buying an eScooter and agreed to send me the money so I could purchase it from my account and apply that credit towards the purchase.

So the moral of the story is that this renewed phone was a great route to go (I'm speaking to the Renewed Premium offerings), and I was very happy with the phone, both cosmetically and functionally. You just need to be fully aware of how the trade-in works (and its limitations) so you don't get frustrated in the end.

title: 1.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Update (12/17/23): Additional observations: 1) the Amazon Renewed certification card is marked 10/27/23, and when I received it 12/2/23 (about 5 weeks), the battery was completely dead; 2) after charging back to 100%, I put it in airplane mode (to turn off both WiFi and bluetooth), and also put it in battery saver mode; I checked the battery percentages once a day, and it was losing 10-15% per day, so this battery is very weak. I did a parallel test with another iPhone (11 pro max), and that one only lost 10% (100% > 90%) over a week. This is an excellent test to check the true condition of the battery.

Update (12/15/23): Ordered a 5th Amazon Premium Renewed phone (iPhone 12 Pro Max), and the battery life, which should be above 90%, is actually 88%.

Update (3/28/23): After lengthy discussions with Amazon, they will not honor the 90% battery guarantee stated on the Amazon Premium Renewed page, because it is "not stated on the Amazon invoice". 1-star, no longer recommended.

Update (2/1/23): Ran into some issues, probably things that should be checked upon receipt of a renewed or premium renewed product: 1) battery life [below advertised 80 or 90%], 2) parts replaced, either with genuine or non-genuine Apple parts, 3) overall functionality [defective charging port]. Reducing overall rating to 4-stars.

Summary: Upgrading from an iPhone 7 plus, and decided I would go with the 11 Pro Max version. I was on the fence whether the extra money for the premium renewed is worth it, so will be discussing what I considered.

Observations: The high level basic differences are: 1) about a $100 difference; 2) three vs. 12 months return period: 3) battery level of 80% vs. 90%.

Recommendation: After considering the factors, I decided to look into how much a replacement battery would cost, which is $40 right now. However, starting with the iPhone 8 (i think), Apple started sealing the cases, which requires a heat gun to separate the case because of the extra waterproofing adhesive. To breakdown the addition $100 cost, subtract the $40 battery from that, leaving $60 for an additional 9-months (or $6.67/month) to "insurance" to return the phone if issues come up.

Carrier Lock: I decided I wanted an unlocked version, and that appears to be another feature that is included with Premium Renewed, with the majority of carrier locked versions being offered as renewed only.

Conclusion: For the additional $100, I elected to go with the Renewed Premium. I rate both the Renewed and the Premium Renewed as 5-stars. Which you chose would depend on individual financial and personal factors.

title: 1.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Update (12/17/23): Additional observations: 1) the Amazon Renewed certification card is marked 10/27/23, and when I received it 12/2/23 (about 5 weeks), the battery was completely dead; 2) after charging back to 100%, I put it in airplane mode (to turn off both WiFi and bluetooth), and also put it in battery saver mode; I checked the battery percentages once a day, and it was losing 10-15% per day, so this battery is very weak. I did a parallel test with another iPhone (11 pro max), and that one only lost 10% (100% > 90%) over a week. This is an excellent test to check the true condition of the battery.

Update (12/15/23): Ordered a 5th Amazon Premium Renewed phone (iPhone 12 Pro Max), and the battery life, which should be above 90%, is actually 88%.

Update (3/28/23): After lengthy discussions with Amazon, they will not honor the 90% battery guarantee stated on the Amazon Premium Renewed page, because it is "not stated on the Amazon invoice". 1-star, no longer recommended.

Update (2/1/23): Ran into some issues, probably things that should be checked upon receipt of a renewed or premium renewed product: 1) battery life [below advertised 80 or 90%], 2) parts replaced, either with genuine or non-genuine Apple parts, 3) overall functionality [defective charging port]. Reducing overall rating to 4-stars.

Summary: Upgrading from an iPhone 7 plus, and decided I would go with the 11 Pro Max version. I was on the fence whether the extra money for the premium renewed is worth it, so will be discussing what I considered.

Observations: The high level basic differences are: 1) about a $100 difference; 2) three vs. 12 months return period: 3) battery level of 80% vs. 90%.

Recommendation: After considering the factors, I decided to look into how much a replacement battery would cost, which is $40 right now. However, starting with the iPhone 8 (i think), Apple started sealing the cases, which requires a heat gun to separate the case because of the extra waterproofing adhesive. To breakdown the addition $100 cost, subtract the $40 battery from that, leaving $60 for an additional 9-months (or $6.67/month) to "insurance" to return the phone if issues come up.

Carrier Lock: I decided I wanted an unlocked version, and that appears to be another feature that is included with Premium Renewed, with the majority of carrier locked versions being offered as renewed only.

Conclusion: For the additional $100, I elected to go with the Renewed Premium. I rate both the Renewed and the Premium Renewed as 5-stars. Which you chose would depend on individual financial and personal factors.

title: 1.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Update (12/17/23): Additional observations: 1) the Amazon Renewed certification card is marked 10/27/23, and when I received it 12/2/23 (about 5 weeks), the battery was completely dead; 2) after charging back to 100%, I put it in airplane mode (to turn off both WiFi and bluetooth), and also put it in battery saver mode; I checked the battery percentages once a day, and it was losing 10-15% per day, so this battery is very weak. I did a parallel test with another iPhone (11 pro max), and that one only lost 10% (100% > 90%) over a week. This is an excellent test to check the true condition of the battery.

Update (12/15/23): Ordered a 5th Amazon Premium Renewed phone (iPhone 12 Pro Max), and the battery life, which should be above 90%, is actually 88%.

Update (3/28/23): After lengthy discussions with Amazon, they will not honor the 90% battery guarantee stated on the Amazon Premium Renewed page, because it is "not stated on the Amazon invoice". 1-star, no longer recommended.

Update (2/1/23): Ran into some issues, probably things that should be checked upon receipt of a renewed or premium renewed product: 1) battery life [below advertised 80 or 90%], 2) parts replaced, either with genuine or non-genuine Apple parts, 3) overall functionality [defective charging port]. Reducing overall rating to 4-stars.

Summary: Upgrading from an iPhone 7 plus, and decided I would go with the 11 Pro Max version. I was on the fence whether the extra money for the premium renewed is worth it, so will be discussing what I considered.

Observations: The high level basic differences are: 1) about a $100 difference; 2) three vs. 12 months return period: 3) battery level of 80% vs. 90%.

Recommendation: After considering the factors, I decided to look into how much a replacement battery would cost, which is $40 right now. However, starting with the iPhone 8 (i think), Apple started sealing the cases, which requires a heat gun to separate the case because of the extra waterproofing adhesive. To breakdown the addition $100 cost, subtract the $40 battery from that, leaving $60 for an additional 9-months (or $6.67/month) to "insurance" to return the phone if issues come up.

Carrier Lock: I decided I wanted an unlocked version, and that appears to be another feature that is included with Premium Renewed, with the majority of carrier locked versions being offered as renewed only.

Conclusion: For the additional $100, I elected to go with the Renewed Premium. I rate both the Renewed and the Premium Renewed as 5-stars. Which you chose would depend on individual financial and personal factors.

title: 1.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Update (12/17/23): Additional observations: 1) the Amazon Renewed certification card is marked 10/27/23, and when I received it 12/2/23 (about 5 weeks), the battery was completely dead; 2) after charging back to 100%, I put it in airplane mode (to turn off both WiFi and bluetooth), and also put it in battery saver mode; I checked the battery percentages once a day, and it was losing 10-15% per day, so this battery is very weak. I did a parallel test with another iPhone (11 pro max), and that one only lost 10% (100% > 90%) over a week. This is an excellent test to check the true condition of the battery.

Update (12/15/23): Ordered a 5th Amazon Premium Renewed phone (iPhone 12 Pro Max), and the battery life, which should be above 90%, is actually 88%.

Update (3/28/23): After lengthy discussions with Amazon, they will not honor the 90% battery guarantee stated on the Amazon Premium Renewed page, because it is "not stated on the Amazon invoice". 1-star, no longer recommended.

Update (2/1/23): Ran into some issues, probably things that should be checked upon receipt of a renewed or premium renewed product: 1) battery life [below advertised 80 or 90%], 2) parts replaced, either with genuine or non-genuine Apple parts, 3) overall functionality [defective charging port]. Reducing overall rating to 4-stars.

Summary: Upgrading from an iPhone 7 plus, and decided I would go with the 11 Pro Max version. I was on the fence whether the extra money for the premium renewed is worth it, so will be discussing what I considered.

Observations: The high level basic differences are: 1) about a $100 difference; 2) three vs. 12 months return period: 3) battery level of 80% vs. 90%.

Recommendation: After considering the factors, I decided to look into how much a replacement battery would cost, which is $40 right now. However, starting with the iPhone 8 (i think), Apple started sealing the cases, which requires a heat gun to separate the case because of the extra waterproofing adhesive. To breakdown the addition $100 cost, subtract the $40 battery from that, leaving $60 for an additional 9-months (or $6.67/month) to "insurance" to return the phone if issues come up.

Carrier Lock: I decided I wanted an unlocked version, and that appears to be another feature that is included with Premium Renewed, with the majority of carrier locked versions being offered as renewed only.

Conclusion: For the additional $100, I elected to go with the Renewed Premium. I rate both the Renewed and the Premium Renewed as 5-stars. Which you chose would depend on individual financial and personal factors.

text:
I bought the iPhone 14Pro. It is beautiful and didn’t have a scratch on it. It looked brand new. The packaging was very nice and the charging cable and adapter was included. I was very happy with it. However, immediately after turning on the phone, the screen went black and would not come back on, so I had to return it.
Amazon said they offered free returns. What they didn’t tell me was that in order for me to return it and get my $835.42 back I’d have to either stay home from work or have someone come to my house because I wasn’t permitted to take and drop the phone off at a UPS location. They had to send someone to pick it up from my house. So, I missed an entire day of work which cost me almost $400.00 and the UPS driver never showed up. I called UPD only to find out 1, that Amazon hadn’t notified them of the pickup and 2, the Return Authorization Slip that Amazon emailed me that was supposed to ensure the returned product was credited back to my credit card in case the mailing label had gotten damaged was invalid. So, apparently, if someone would have picked up the phone and damaged the mailing label I would not have had my money refunded.

I called Amazon back to tell them what UPS told me. Amazon’s solution was to start the return process all over again. Meaning that I would have to miss another day of work in order to wait for UPS to pick up the phone. I told them that was absolutely unacceptable. The customer service rep was adamant that that was my only option and it wasn’t until I got angry and insisted they email me a return label, so I could drop it off at a UPS store that they finally agreed to do so.
I printed off the label and repackaged the box with the new Return Authorization Slip (I hope it’s valid this time) and dropped it off at UPS.
I HOPE my money is refunded without issue even though they told me it could take up to 40 DAYS to do so.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I wanted a second phone as a backup. Something I could take with me sometimes while I am fishing, or traveling. A phone I don't really care about if I lost it / broke it / it got stolen; but, can come in handy in certain situations. My main phone is a Galaxy S9 on a major network. I was thinking of getting a standard sized pay as you go phone; however, I saw this and had to try it.

I don't plan to use much data, just emergency phone calls / texts, and, looking up stuff like, "where is the nearest gas station", etc.. This phone does most of these things great! Typing is not easy! I am an adult, but, I don't have all that huge of hands. I thought it would be ok. It really is a bit hard to type though. I am going to look for a keyboard update / app. One that allows for the swiping typing style. For now, I carry a tiny pointed stylus which works great. Not as fast as typing on my S9, but, doable for the purposes I need. I got a low cost ($5 a month) plan from SpeedTalk (I heard from other reviews this was a company that worked well with this phone). I get just 100 mins + 100 text + 100mb data for a month. The phone works great. Clear sound on my end, and others can hear me clearly too. Internet is fine for my needs while away from home. I can also connect to Xfinity hotspots as well while out, or my own wifi at home.

The phone came with a clear plastic / rubber case that is alright. Nothing special, kind of looks like a toy case. But hey, the phone looks like a toy phone anyways. It also came with a screen protector and power cord (no power adapter). I almost got their 7S+, which is even more limited (look it up, it costs more like $25 and is more of a standard old type phone). Honestly, that probably would have suited my needs, but, I wanted the cool factor of a tiny fully functional Andriod phone.

Overall, as long as it lasts for at least a year, I'd say it is worth it if you know what you are getting. Having this small, easy to carry phone, with just a $5 a month service plan, means I have a very inexpensive little gadget I can take anywhere to stay connected. I'm sure I will find some more cool uses for it. Because I have so little data, I can't really use it as a music player while out of the house (unless Xfinity hotspots are available). But, maybe I can find some way to get some music on this. I do sometimes like to play some music while fishing. Google play store does work, so, I'll be sure to keep messing with the phone. I'll update if anything major (good or bad) comes to my attention.

Anyways, hope this helps anyone wondering about getting this phone.

Last tip. SpeedTalk requires you to enter a credit card number when activating your sim (most prepaid companies do this). Upon purchasing this phone, I also purchased a $50 Visa gift card. It worked just fine during activation. I've heard some stories that they like to charge you monthly even if you uncheck the box to auto refill; and, that it can be a bit of a pain to fully cancel. So, I figured having this sim on a prepaid card was best. If I ever want to change providers or cancel services, I can empty my prepaid card at a local store, and, toss the sim. Simple and done.

title: 1.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I received the phone within 2 days of ordering. The packaging was fine and initially it appeared to be in great condition. However, I checked the battery health on the first day which stated “Important Battery Message: Your battery’s health is significantly degraded.” The Maximum Capacity for the battery was 78%. No problem, I thought, because one of the reason’s I bought from Amazon is that the phone was advertised “to have a battery which exceeds 80% capacity relative to new” and was “Guaranteed by Amazon” to be “eligible for replacement or refund within 90 days of receipt if you are not satisfied. “

Well clearly, I was not satisfied to receive a phone with a significantly degraded battery. So, I called Amazon Customer service to explain the problem and request a replacement. I did this on the same day I received the phone. The representative was helpful and told me he would send out a replacement immediately, and even upgrade the shipment method for no extra charge. He also told me, both in conversation and in writing to “use the box the replacement comes in to return the original.” That way, I would not be without a phone while waiting for the replacement to arrive.

The day the replacement was scheduled to arrive and but had not, I called Amazon customer service back to inquire about the status. Much to my surprise, I was told the replacement phone order had been cancelled by the third-party seller because the original had not been returned. This irritated me for two reasons: (1) I had never been notified the replacement order had been cancelled—apparently, had I not called Amazon was simply going to drop the issue, and (2) I was specifically told by Amazon Customer Service that I did not need to return the original until the replacement was received.

I told the agent this was unacceptable and wanted the replacement sent to me, as had been previously arranged. When it became clear that she would not be able to help me, I asked to speak with her manager. After providing her with my phone number, she said her manager would call me back. That phone call never happened.

The following day I called Amazon customer service again, now the third time trying to get this issue resolved. I explained the steps I had taken thus far and was put on hold so the representative could verify if my replacement order “was legit.” When I asked what “legit” meant, she said she needed to verify if this was unusual activity on the account because it was a phone purchase. I told her that of course it was legit, as I had email documentation regarding the entire process!

After being on hold, she came back and told me the replacement phone would be delivered within 5 days. She also said she would personally call me on that day to verify that it was received. I asked her to clarify that I would receive the replacement first, prior to sending the original back, according to the instructions I had previously received via email. She looked up that email and saw it said: “Please feel free to use the box the replacement comes in to return the original…” After reading that she placed me on hold again.

After a minute or so, she came back on the line and asked if she could place me on hold for an additional few minutes. I asked why. She said she was trying to find out what went wrong with the first replacement order. When she came back on the line, she told me “to be on the safe side” I should return the original defective phone first to receive a replacement. I reiterated that this was unacceptable and that I had held up my end of the bargain and done exactly as Amazon had told me to do. I wanted the replacement sent first before I returned the defective phone. She said the email I received was in error and the person who sent it made a mistake—the defective phone would need to be returned before the replacement is shipped out. I told her that while I understand that people make mistakes, I did not think I should be penalized (i.e., be without a phone for at least 5 days) for a mistake that Amazon made. She apologized for the mistake but made it clear that I would not receive a replacement until the original was returned. I informed her I would be writing a negative review.

To summarize: I was sent a defective phone, was given incorrect information about how to replace it, had the replacement order silently cancelled without being notified, and Amazon refused to follow through on the terms of their agreement. One star.

text:
I received the phone within 2 days of ordering. The packaging was fine and initially it appeared to be in great condition. However, I checked the battery health on the first day which stated “Important Battery Message: Your battery’s health is significantly degraded.” The Maximum Capacity for the battery was 78%. No problem, I thought, because one of the reason’s I bought from Amazon is that the phone was advertised “to have a battery which exceeds 80% capacity relative to new” and was “Guaranteed by Amazon” to be “eligible for replacement or refund within 90 days of receipt if you are not satisfied. “

Well clearly, I was not satisfied to receive a phone with a significantly degraded battery. So, I called Amazon Customer service to explain the problem and request a replacement. I did this on the same day I received the phone. The representative was helpful and told me he would send out a replacement immediately, and even upgrade the shipment method for no extra charge. He also told me, both in conversation and in writing to “use the box the replacement comes in to return the original.” That way, I would not be without a phone while waiting for the replacement to arrive.

The day the replacement was scheduled to arrive and but had not, I called Amazon customer service back to inquire about the status. Much to my surprise, I was told the replacement phone order had been cancelled by the third-party seller because the original had not been returned. This irritated me for two reasons: (1) I had never been notified the replacement order had been cancelled—apparently, had I not called Amazon was simply going to drop the issue, and (2) I was specifically told by Amazon Customer Service that I did not need to return the original until the replacement was received.

I told the agent this was unacceptable and wanted the replacement sent to me, as had been previously arranged. When it became clear that she would not be able to help me, I asked to speak with her manager. After providing her with my phone number, she said her manager would call me back. That phone call never happened.

The following day I called Amazon customer service again, now the third time trying to get this issue resolved. I explained the steps I had taken thus far and was put on hold so the representative could verify if my replacement order “was legit.” When I asked what “legit” meant, she said she needed to verify if this was unusual activity on the account because it was a phone purchase. I told her that of course it was legit, as I had email documentation regarding the entire process!

After being on hold, she came back and told me the replacement phone would be delivered within 5 days. She also said she would personally call me on that day to verify that it was received. I asked her to clarify that I would receive the replacement first, prior to sending the original back, according to the instructions I had previously received via email. She looked up that email and saw it said: “Please feel free to use the box the replacement comes in to return the original…” After reading that she placed me on hold again.

After a minute or so, she came back on the line and asked if she could place me on hold for an additional few minutes. I asked why. She said she was trying to find out what went wrong with the first replacement order. When she came back on the line, she told me “to be on the safe side” I should return the original defective phone first to receive a replacement. I reiterated that this was unacceptable and that I had held up my end of the bargain and done exactly as Amazon had told me to do. I wanted the replacement sent first before I returned the defective phone. She said the email I received was in error and the person who sent it made a mistake—the defective phone would need to be returned before the replacement is shipped out. I told her that while I understand that people make mistakes, I did not think I should be penalized (i.e., be without a phone for at least 5 days) for a mistake that Amazon made. She apologized for the mistake but made it clear that I would not receive a replacement until the original was returned. I informed her I would be writing a negative review.

To summarize: I was sent a defective phone, was given incorrect information about how to replace it, had the replacement order silently cancelled without being notified, and Amazon refused to follow through on the terms of their agreement. One star.

title: 1.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I received the phone within 2 days of ordering. The packaging was fine and initially it appeared to be in great condition. However, I checked the battery health on the first day which stated “Important Battery Message: Your battery’s health is significantly degraded.” The Maximum Capacity for the battery was 78%. No problem, I thought, because one of the reason’s I bought from Amazon is that the phone was advertised “to have a battery which exceeds 80% capacity relative to new” and was “Guaranteed by Amazon” to be “eligible for replacement or refund within 90 days of receipt if you are not satisfied. “

Well clearly, I was not satisfied to receive a phone with a significantly degraded battery. So, I called Amazon Customer service to explain the problem and request a replacement. I did this on the same day I received the phone. The representative was helpful and told me he would send out a replacement immediately, and even upgrade the shipment method for no extra charge. He also told me, both in conversation and in writing to “use the box the replacement comes in to return the original.” That way, I would not be without a phone while waiting for the replacement to arrive.

The day the replacement was scheduled to arrive and but had not, I called Amazon customer service back to inquire about the status. Much to my surprise, I was told the replacement phone order had been cancelled by the third-party seller because the original had not been returned. This irritated me for two reasons: (1) I had never been notified the replacement order had been cancelled—apparently, had I not called Amazon was simply going to drop the issue, and (2) I was specifically told by Amazon Customer Service that I did not need to return the original until the replacement was received.

I told the agent this was unacceptable and wanted the replacement sent to me, as had been previously arranged. When it became clear that she would not be able to help me, I asked to speak with her manager. After providing her with my phone number, she said her manager would call me back. That phone call never happened.

The following day I called Amazon customer service again, now the third time trying to get this issue resolved. I explained the steps I had taken thus far and was put on hold so the representative could verify if my replacement order “was legit.” When I asked what “legit” meant, she said she needed to verify if this was unusual activity on the account because it was a phone purchase. I told her that of course it was legit, as I had email documentation regarding the entire process!

After being on hold, she came back and told me the replacement phone would be delivered within 5 days. She also said she would personally call me on that day to verify that it was received. I asked her to clarify that I would receive the replacement first, prior to sending the original back, according to the instructions I had previously received via email. She looked up that email and saw it said: “Please feel free to use the box the replacement comes in to return the original…” After reading that she placed me on hold again.

After a minute or so, she came back on the line and asked if she could place me on hold for an additional few minutes. I asked why. She said she was trying to find out what went wrong with the first replacement order. When she came back on the line, she told me “to be on the safe side” I should return the original defective phone first to receive a replacement. I reiterated that this was unacceptable and that I had held up my end of the bargain and done exactly as Amazon had told me to do. I wanted the replacement sent first before I returned the defective phone. She said the email I received was in error and the person who sent it made a mistake—the defective phone would need to be returned before the replacement is shipped out. I told her that while I understand that people make mistakes, I did not think I should be penalized (i.e., be without a phone for at least 5 days) for a mistake that Amazon made. She apologized for the mistake but made it clear that I would not receive a replacement until the original was returned. I informed her I would be writing a negative review.

To summarize: I was sent a defective phone, was given incorrect information about how to replace it, had the replacement order silently cancelled without being notified, and Amazon refused to follow through on the terms of their agreement. One star.

I honestly would have kept my old iPhone 8 Plus if not for the fact that I couldn't get iOS 17 on it and I loved the new features of the operating system upgrade. I also wanted a better camera.
