title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Outside my house I can just about always make a call. It may drop if it lasts long, but I can call. Data is sometimes slow like less than 2mbps. Mostly it is either too slow to use or nonexistent. Indoors I might be able to make a call sometimes near the larger windows. Indoors otherwise is a no call zone or one that won't hold up for more than 3 minutes. No data is possible.

With the booster over a 700 square foot area I can make calls just fine and drops are not a problem. Data runs from slow, but usable 3 mbps around the edges of my indoor coverage to 20-25 mbps near the indoor antenna. I can hotspot with my phone right next to the antenna and get 30-35 mbps reliably.

With friends over for a ball game using 5 phones on 4 different provider systems everyone reported good connections and decent data speeds all using the booster concurrently. Everyone was much happier than when they have trouble unless they go outdoors.

Fine details now. Readings from Network Cell Info lite app on Android from Wilysis. Outdoors on LTE coverage I have a weak fluctuating signal around -115 db. No booster: Indoors near nothing LTE, some 3G sometimes. With Booster Indoors near the limit of the indoor booster antenna I get a solid -110 db LTE, in the middle around -100 db LTE and near the antenna -90 db. Right next to the antenna gets me 80-85 db which is plenty good.

You do need to heed the instructions on setting this up. It can be tricky, but just stick with it. They suggest 50 ft horizontal distance or 20 feet vertical distance between outdoor booster antenna and indoor antenna. They also should not point at each other. With two interior walls and a brick wall between the two I could only get all lights green at 47 feet direct distance. This worked well enough to make the device worth the cost and useful. Moving further than the minimum to get green lights helps a large amount. I eventually mounted the two antennas 65 feet apart to get the results I did. So go further if you can. The device sets gain if you unplug and then replug it. So with antennas further apart it will turn up the gain closer to max. Also I tried measuring signal on a tall ladder outdoors, and to my surprise, it made no difference I could tell. I expect higher usually helps, but not in my case.

The unit comes with two 30 ft pieces of coax. I wish it came with one 30 ft and 50 ft coax since you likely will need at least 50 ft. I actually used one 30 ft piece and the supplied coax joiner to connect a 50 ft piece of RG6 I already had for 80 ft total. That let me run it into the basement, outside underneath a porch and up a pole to where I placed the outdoor antenna without the coax being visible.

I also wish the connection to the indoor antenna was about twice as long. Plus the power cord to the indoor booster unit is too short and needs to be at least twice as long. The indoor booster unit also runs very hot. Not quite enough to burn you, but hot even with excellent ventilation and nothing in the way. Makes me wonder if this will shorten life. If you don't provide ventilation I think it would surely shorten the life of the unit. Those short cords on the indoor antenna and booster unit hamper placing the unit in a place with good ventilation and so it won't be an ugly spider's nest of wiring.

The instructions could be better. Read several reviews and you will run across enough info to answer any questions. Plus think about where you can put it, how you can run the coax ahead of time and it should work out for you. I think you would only get coverage of 1500 sq. ft if you had it in a completely open unobstructed space, and have a fair bit of signal outdoors already.

So deducting a star for the short antenna, short power cord, no 50 ft coax included, and the unit running so hot.

text:
There are good and bad points with this purchase. First, I was pleasantly surprised to see that a head band was included with Bluetooth headset even though it was not advertised. That is so much nicer than just hanging the headset on the ear.

I also liked that the headset works on its own, so that the two handset phone system actually has the ability for three users to use it at the same time. Very cool.

It was also nice that there were extra parts for the headset ear piece, including a padded sleeve for the ear loop. The headset allows the mic to be pushed away from the cheek, as well. Once one gets familiar with the somewhat tiny and hard-to-feel button, it does pickup and hangup the phone call easily.

There is nothing special about the handsets. They have very common controls with decent backlighting on both the display and the buttons. I will mention that the displays are a little on small side.

As most of these types of boom mics go, this one was short and would not extend. I can only assume it picks up a whisper properly.

The Amazon pricing was good for this unit, and for other systems of this type.

When I had spoken to the tech support person about this unit before buying, I was told that the range could reach as much as 50 meters indoors and 300 meters outdoors in best conditions, which I considered very good. I think I would be happy with half that. If the base unit is near the window, I should be able to wander all around my yard and use the phone without a problem. YMMV.

There was a legal issue that popped up. When the package was opened, the flap states that there is a bonus and an extended warranty of 3 months if registering on their web site or using the QR code. But the listed page does not exist, and when I called in I was told that the warranty is no longer offered. I had to explain to a supervisor that such a position was illegal in my country since they were clearly advertising it. They tried to get out of it because of policy change, but then I asked if they had taken all the old packaging off the shelves when they changed the policy.

I was required to take a picture of the serial number on the bottom of the base (even though I had already been asked to read it off to the supervisor; which seems odd since I am not the one who had the problem of sticking to their word), a picture of the box flap and a copy of the invoice, and send them all to the provided email address. I can only assume that they will honor the one year plus three months warranty after all that.

Update:
It turns out that this phone, and indeed all phones from Vtech, cannot keep their time correctly once the user sets it. There is an override "feature" entitled Caller ID Time Sync. This causes the phone to change time whenever a call comes in if you have Caller ID (and who wouldn't want caller ID). Talk about a thoughtless and boneheaded idea! What was wrong with a simple setting of time as has been done in all devices for literally decades? All one needs is a phone that knows the DST option table and the ability to turn that one if applicable. This is something we have had for almost as long as there has been digital devices.

One now wonders what else is going on in the background on these digital devices from foreign countries.

If you are in the middle of searching for a contact, and you start dialing a number, Teams knows what you're doing. There are small nuances of issues that I'm sure will change weekly or monthly as the Teams software changes (nothing really to do with this phone model). For example, Teams on my cell phone shows me the time & duration on the call history list. But on this phone, only the number (or contact or callerid) is shown. You have to touch the screen in order to reveal the call time. So if you walk into your office after lunch and wish to quickly glance at your call history and you see 10 missed calls, you have no idea how often and the time frame of what's going on. title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
My employer runs on Zoom Workplace, and I work from home. AFAIK, you can use all of the features of Zoom Workplace from the Zoom desktop app or from a standard web browser, and you can also operate some aspects of Zoom Workplace via a smartphone app -- but I decided to purchase this device after missing an important Zoom voice call.

Ease of Use - It is much easier to respond to an inbound call by picking up physical handset than it is to: unlock my computer screen, put-on headphones, and surface the Zoom app. This is the primary reason I purchased the phone, and it has solved that problem completely.

While I only expected to use this device for Zoom Phone service, it also does a fine job of accepting Zoom video calls or joining Zoom meetings in a voice-only capacity. It connects to your (Zoom) company contact list and Zoom calendar, making it easy to call colleagues. It provides a second screen which wakes itself up and reminds you of upcoming Zoom meetings, which is also helpful.

Admin / Maintenance - If you've used Yealink VOIP devices before, this one is exactly the same -- until you log-in to Zoom, at which point Yealink delegates some control to your company Zoom administrator and locks-out the ability to configure your own phone via a local web browser. The device is maintained by updating the Zoom app (which you can do from the touchscreen while logged-on and registered w/Zoom as a normal user) and by updating the Yealink firmware (I haven't done that but expect it would be the same as flashing any other Yealink phone).

Teams vs Zoom - I purchased the Microsoft Teams version of this phone, and followed instructions from Yealink to flash it over to the Zoom firmware. AFAIK the only physical difference between the Teams version and the Zoom version is a branded button on the phone keypad, so my Zoom phone has a Microsoft Teams button on it.

Zoom-Only - the phone is 100% dedicated to Zoom workplace (or Microsoft Teams). You can't provision additional lines to connect with other VOIP providers.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Highly recommended if you're looking for a low-cost landline replacement with advanced calling features. I've been using a wired Ooma at my house since 2016 and just purchased this wireless one for my Mom. We're using cordless Panasonic DECT phones with the Ooma at both locations ... the setup works great.

Service cost is ~$5/month without Ooma Premier service and ~$15/month with Premier. Get the Premier, which gives you a second line, caller ID, spam blocking, call forwarding, conference calling, free calling to Canada and Mexico, etc., etc. Previously, I was paying ATT ~$35/mo for basic local service and another $10/month to a budget long-distance service. With Ooma, I'm paying about 1/3 of that for a service with many more features.

Pros:
- Simple installation
- With Ooma Premier, all the features mentioned above and more. Spam blocking is particularly great and almost completely eliminates nuisance calls
- Fax compatible, prepend *99 to outgoing fax numbers
- You can keep your existing landline number. Ooma will "port" it for you and give you a temporary number in the meantime. Porting takes 1-4 weeks. I've done trouble-free ports of Pacific Bell (CA) and CenturyLink (CO) numbers
- Sends standard voicemail waiting signals to connected phones -- just like phone company voicemail -- so that you can be notified of, and pick up, Ooma voicemails on connected phones that support this signaling
- Reverse powers wired jacks in your house if you want multiple phones or fax machines connected (disconnect your house from the phone company's lines to do this safely and *don't* try this if you have DSL Internet ... it'll likely disable your Internet connection)
- Smartphone app allows you to send/receive calls from your Ooma number, pick up Ooma voicemail and monitor incoming/outgoing calls from anywhere; the app isn't amazing, but it works.
- Informative browser/web interface for monitoring and configuration of the service.
- Sends address information to public safety when calling 911. Be sure to configure your address correctly during setup

Cons and things to be aware of:
- Requires a reliable Internet connection with a few 100 kbps of bandwidth for the Ooma. You can set up Ooma to automatically forward calls to another number if your home Internet goes out. Otherwise, your Ooma voicemail will record incoming calls, which can be retrieved after your Internet comes back (or from the app or the browser interface).
- Sound quality of voicemails recorded by the Ooma is muddy. If your home phone has a built-in answering machine, try using that instead (just set the phone answering machine to pick up after a smaller number of rings than the Ooma).
- If you wire the Telo in your house, rather than connecting via WiFi, note that you have the options of (a) installing it between your Internet modem and router or (b) behind your router on your home network. While Ooma recommends (a) for wired Telos, note that the Telo will limit throughput to your home network to 100 Mbps in this configuration, slower than many of today's Internet plans. My $0.02: connect a wired Telo behind your home router.
- The "flower" light on top of the Telo is very bright by default. It's brightness can be adjusted by logging in to the Telo (not your Ooma dashboard) or with the Telo rewind button (see https://support.ooma.com/home/ooma-telo-basic-functions-and-faq/)

What Makes It Stand Out
Crystal-Clear 4K Input: The SeeMo supports up to 4K30fps HDMI input, and the output on my iPhone is sharp and vibrant. It’s a huge step up from relying on my camera’s small LCD, especially for critical focus and framing.
Lightning Fast Setup: It’s truly plug-and-play. Connect your camera to the SeeMo via HDMI, plug it into your iPhone or The Accsoon app is intuitive and offers tools like focus peaking, false color, and LUT previews, making it feel like a pro-grade setup.
MFi Certified Reliability: The fact that it’s MFi (Made for iPhone) certified gives me peace of mind about compatibility and performance. It just works, every time.
Compact and Practical

Power Options That Work

Who’s It For?

Final Thoughts
The Accsoon SeeMo is a simple yet powerful tool for anyone looking to step up their monitoring game. It’s affordable, reliable, and makes great use of devices you probably already own. For wired HDMI monitoring, it’s hard to beat.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Every once in a while, a product comes along that's a total game changer in its field. In the world of camera rigs gear that can kill multiple birds with one stone are the most appreciated because space is a premium and weight has to be considered with everything. The SeeMo 4K by Accsoon is a revolutionary piece of gear that kills multiple birds with one beautifully designed stone.

When setting up a camera rig one of the main things you have to consider is how are you going to monitor? How are you gonna see your signal since the viewfinder and the LCD screen are gonna be covered up with your battery, your cage, all that stuff. They make proprietary monitors, they make field recorders that have monitors, those are all fine and dandy, but what if you didn't have to buy an extra display?

What if you could have a super bright display that looked great in direct sunlight and had wonderful colors and resolution, you know like an iPhone. I never go anywhere without my iPhone, so be able to use it as a monitor would be a big score. It's brighter than most monitors. The resolution is higher than most monitors and major bonus, it's an always connected Internet device. Wouldn't it be great if you could use your iPhone as a monitor, use it to record whatever your camera sees, and allow you to share clips as soon as you take them to any streaming service or messages or email or anything you could think of? Thats what SeeMo 4K does! On top of all that it has other great features like the ability to see LUTs over your log footage as you shoot. How about false color, focus peaking, zebras, scopes, and histograms? It has all that. In addition, hardware wise it has a SD card slot so you can offload footage from your camera and your iPhone to the SD card slot, which also allows you to load your own LUTS. So many features in one little device!

Now, having these features is great, but no big deal if they don't work that well. On the SeeMo 4K everything is implemented in a thoughtful, well designed manner. You could have the layout of your monitor screen be as full featured or as minimalist as you want, it's completely customizable. Every single monitoring feature that it has can either be added to or taken away from the main screen with a simple tap. It has the killer feature of being able to apply your lots to the footage your recording to the iPhone so you can have stuff where you go for socials or to share, already graded. You don't have to worry about compressing footage or switching stuff up to share file format, and codec wise. The SeeMo 4K takes your 4K footage and transcodes it into 1080P 60 FPS on the fly, so it's ready for streaming, sharing, whatever you wanna do with it. Such a time saver!

The hardware is really well built. It's super lightweight too, but seems like it could take the kind of drops or bumps that happen on set. Wanna know another major bonus? It charges your device well it's monitoring so you never have to worry about your phone running dead while you shoot it does this by having an attachment for a Sony battery, or in my case, a dummy battery attached to a V-mount big battery. I also bought the Accsoon Power Cage so I can use the SeeMo 4K with my 11 inch iPad Pro and have all the same features only on a bigger screen. It also charges my iPad Pro and if I wanted to, it could take another Sony battery on the cage and use its USB out to power other devices.

Another thing I love is that it's very versatile as far as ways you can mount it. I go back-and-forth from having it on my rigs top handle with a monitor mount for my phone or mounting it to the back of my rig on the battery with some Velcro while running the iPad off of a magic arm. The combination of the power cage, and the SeeMo 4K is awesome if you need lots of screen real estate.

All this functionality and problem-solving for under 150 bucks is insane. I can also say that it's the most important thing on my rig right now with the amount of things that it takes care of the workflow time reduction is incredible. I can shoot now in 4K and at the same time have it go to my phone in 1080P and immediately after shooting, have it uploaded to my editors or while I'm shooting I can stream LIVE to YouTube and Facebook! When I'm done sharing the clips or streaming them, I can offload them from my phone onto an SD card or AirDrop them off so I don't use up a bunch of my phone space.

I looked all over for something like this and it usually involved having to use two or three products. This one nails it all in one easy to use, handy, elegant device that I couldn't imagine living without. Total home-tun by Accsoon!

text:
Este accesorio permite convertir tu iPhone en un monitor de campo para tu cámara digital y realizar streaming utilizando tu cámara Mirrorless. No voy a hacer una revisión exhaustiva ya que hay muchas disponibles en internet, pero hablaré de sus ventajas, inconvenientes y mis impresiones personales.

PROS:
✅ Muy compacto: No necesitas llevar un monitor de campo adicional, ya que tu iPhone puede cumplir esa función. Si tienes un iPhone 15 Pro, la calidad de la pantalla es sobresaliente comparada con otros monitores no profesionales.
✅ Permite hacer streaming directamente usando tu cámara.
✅ Grabación directa en el iPhone: Puedes grabar directamente en el iPhone lo que está enfocando la cámara y editarlo al instante.
✅ Ranura SD: Tiene una ranura para tarjeta SD, permitiendo almacenar los videos capturados.
✅ Soporte inclinable: El soporte para acoplar el conjunto a la zapata es inclinable y ofrece una fricción adecuada para evitar movimientos indeseados.
✅ Salida USB-C adicional: Cuenta con una salida USB-C adicional para alimentar accesorios externos como luces.
✅ Resolución 4K: Permite capturar videos en 4K, garantizando la máxima calidad.

CONTRAS:
❌ Requiere una batería adicional: La batería no está incluida.
❌ Necesita cable HDMI: Es necesario un cable HDMI para conectar tu cámara al adaptador.
❌ Incompatible con Android: Solo funciona con iOS.
❌ Pequeño retraso: Hay un ligero retraso entre la escena en vivo y lo que se muestra en el iPhone.
❌ Control limitado: No permite controlar la cámara desde la pantalla del iPhone. Las funciones de la app están limitadas a su propio funcionamiento (no se pueden ajustar apertura del diafragma, tiempo de exposición, etc.).

CONCLUSIÓN:
Este accesorio está dirigido a un público muy específico y requiere conocimientos avanzados de video para aprovechar al máximo la app. Considero que el precio debería incluir una batería y un cable HDMI corto para comenzar a usarlo con tu cámara de inmediato. En resumen, este accesorio potencia las capacidades del iPhone, permitiéndole utilizar objetivos de mayor calidad de una cámara, en lugar de sus propias cámaras integradas. Si solo necesitas grabar videos rápidos para redes sociales, el iPhone es suficiente. Sin embargo, si necesitas una óptica superior a la del iPhone, este accesorio es esencial.

text:
There are not many SSD ** external drives that are 8 TeraBytes in size so there are not a lot to choose from. SanDisk has a good reputation. I would have prefered black but only this powder-blue was in stock and desparate times call for desperate color choices. :-)

Drive has worked well for a number of months under heavy use. It does get very "warm" bordering on "hot".
It needs the external power supply as I assume the USB-C port does not supply enough power for this case and it is about 4"x4"x1" so it is smallish but not pocket size.

Since it is called a DESK drive, they are not trying to hide any of these facts. Unfortunately, IMO, 8TB SSD drives are still expensive but as one expects, it is a bit cheaper than are two 4 TB Sandisk SSD drives.
Those do not need the AC adapter and do fit in your pocket (I have a few) and that is an attraction of a smaller drive.

It is also safer to have two independent 4TB drives than one 8TB unless you need to have the full larger size drive space for projects like film, animation or even a data backup.

Bottom line = If you need 5 to 8 TB of continuous SSD drive space this is a good choice. If not, I personally would buy two 4 TB SSD drives I needed the larger space so bought it for that reason alone.

*SSD = Solid State Drive. It is NOT a mechanical hard drive so it is much more costly per TB and much faster. You should know which to choose based on the purpose but let me assure you that both mechanical drives and SSD drives do not last forever and both can fail. Never fill up a SSD completely or that can accelerate the failure.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
The NETGEAR CM1000 is a modem that targets users who primarily are interested in gaming, or streaming HD video on multiple devices. This modem definitely delivers that type of performance. The design is very much in this vein, it looks vaguely futuristic, perhaps alien in its elongated hexagonal case. The two-tone dark charcoal unit affixed to a gray stand also seems a bit off, why two colors? Anyways, the stand is connected by a single screw, but it seems to also be attached using plastic rails, and it seems sturdy enough. It is very obviously meant to only be used in this upright orientation the reasoning for which brings me to my next point...

The triangular venting mixes form and function but is heavy on the form, as this modem does throw off some heat! It will warm your hands in the winter no problem. Might even save you on heating bills. It is almost concerning how warm it runs. I often think to power it down overnight or if I leave the house for an extended period.

The modem is DOCSIS 3.1, which is a international standard that allows for higher bandwidth over existing Cable TV service. The next generation of internet speed offerings from ISPs will be in the multiples of Gbps, and to take advantage, you will need a modem that is DOCSIS 3.1. Thankfully, this modem is backwards compatible with the older standard DOCSIS 3.0.

The modem came assembled on the stand out of the box, along with the customary canary category 5 cable, and power adapter. I didn't use the cat 5, I opted for the Vandesail CAT7 Cable because, well, why not? The category 7 cable has a much higher bandwidth, and will be used in future equipment, so best to be prepared! I also upgraded the coaxial cable in my house to Quad Shield RG-6 Coax 75 Ohm 3Ghz Cable as you see in the included picture.

I have the CM1000 connected to a NETGEAR AC1600 which I had from using with DSL internet service. The pair is working seamlessly together, and I am regularly seeing download speeds at the maximum of my service rating of 200Mbps, using Comcast as an ISP. See the included screencap of the speed test.

During install, the modem powered up, and went through a few reboots, and after about 10 to 15 minutes, the connection was made. It initially didn't want to to play with the NETGEAR AC1600 router, but after a few power cycles, everything resolved itself, and the two now peacefully coincide.

The status indicators are only on the left side of the front, which itself is angled at about 30 degrees away from you if you are looking straight on. A strange design decision, it limits one's vision of them, especially if you must place it on your left. Not a huge deal, but it seems so easy to design a better solution. Fortunately, I haven't had a need to check the indicator LEDs.

Conclusion: BUY. An A+ modem, fit for heavy gaming or streaming HD video.

PROS:
+ Easy setup
+ DOCSIS 3.1 and 3.0 compatible
+ FAST
+ Will work with the next generation of speed tiers
+ Don't have to rent from ISP

CONS:
- Expensive
- LEDs are difficult to view
- Runs really warm!

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text: Review of Netgear CM1000v2. I got a notice from my internet company, xFinity, that I should upgrade my old DOCSIS 3.0 modem to a newer 3.1 version. Even though my internet package only gets me up to 59Mbps, nowhere near the gigabyte speed offered by the new modems, I decided to replace my old modem anyway, since I was starting to get more internet outages over the past few weeks. I figured the older technology maybe wasn't being supported as well on the network, and I had to keep resetting my modem and waiting for connectivity to come back again. Installation was pretty easy. 1. First, unplug old modem from power, cable and ethernet. 2. Plug all of those into the new modem and wait for all the lights to stay on, which can take up to 10 full minutes. 3. Go into the xFinity app on your phone, log into your account, then tap Account, Activate xFi Gateway or Modem, Your Own Modem, Start Activation, then follow prompts from there. You will need to enter the MAC address, which is printed on the bottom of the modem. It may take another 10 minutes after activation for you to have internet access. All worked well for me and there were no problems. Modem has been working flawlessly for the past few days since I set it up. As I said, my plan only gives me up to 59Mbps, and that has not increased with this modem. It will only increase if I change my plan to a higher speed plan. But, I have a newer technology modem now that is at least ready for future speed increases should I choose to pay for that, and this DOCS 3.1 modem may have better security and more compatibility with the xFinity network. Things I like about it: 1. It has an on/off button on the back. VERY handy for resetting the modem. Much more convenient than having to pull the power plug then struggle to get it plugged back in while in a tight, dark space behind the modem. Many modems do not have an on/off button. 2. The lights are easy to see, but not too bright. On my previous Arris modem, the lights were overwhelmingly bright and flashing, so much that you could hardly read what their function was. These lights are much better. 3. The form factor is good; thin and tall, with a sturdy base. Other note: Some reviewers have said this modem gets HOT. I don't find that to be the case. It is warm, but not really any warmer than any other modem or streaming device I've had, especially one that is on 24 hours a day. Bottom line, this modem is a highly compatible modem for xFinity and all other cable systems, has an on/off button, good form factor, perfectly readable and not-too-bright lights, and is easy to set up.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I am so glad I got this!

I have a Dell laptop for work that clicks into a (Dell PR03X) docking station. I hate the docking station. It's just difficult to get the laptop connected to it and the docking station only allows for 2 extra monitors, not 3. So I had to buy an external USB video card for my 3rd monitor.

I purchased this as a replacement for my PR03X dock and it's an EXCELLENT replacement. For one thing, I can use it with all my laptops, not just my Dell. I have a Lenovo Yoga (my wife's), a Macbook Air (2011 with OS 10.9 - which required the software from http://www.displaylink.com/support/mac_downloads.php), and my work Dell laptop. All 3 work great with this little hub. And it is pretty small and lightweight.

Note: I wasn't really sure how this was going to connect to my laptop(s). It turns out it connects via a typical USB (2 or 3) port. My Macbook Air has USB 2, while my Lenovo Yoga has USB 3.0. Both work flawlessly. However, obviously the extra USB ports the device provides won't operate at USB 3 speeds if you're connected to your laptop via a USB 2 port.

Anyway, once you've connected the doc to your laptop (or desktop) via a USB 2 or 3 port, its ready for up to 3 monitors to be connected to it. Two via HDMI and a third via Dell's DisplayPort (which you can get a DisplayPort-to-HDMI adapter if needed). So with the laptop screen this gives you a total of up to 4 displays!

The One Con:
It seems like video playback might be a little choppy when watching a 1080p video clip on YouTube while connected to a USB 2 port. I'm not sure if this was the internet or a FPS limitation of the USB video throughput. However, it seems to playback video flawlessly using a USB 3 port.

So if you're considering this for video work or for gaming and you don't have a USB 3 port to plug it onto, you may find it slightly laggy and you may want to do a little more research. But again, I see no lag using USB 3.

But if you want to use typical applications like Word, Excel, PowerPoint, ect. - or in my case a text editor like Sublime Text, this little dock will work great, even when using the slower USB 2.

I decided to fetch the latest dock driver from Dell's website and push it onto the device while I had the Windows notebook plugged in. No apparent change. Switching back to Gnome afterwards was still unbearable.

So I did apt install xfce4, rebooted into XFCE, and it works really well. Tried again with clean installation of Ubuntu 16.04.1 ("normal", with Unity), and it worked surprisingly well too. I don't know what the deal was with Gnome being so awful. It's a shame, too, since I really like Gnome, and it's what I always use on my CentOS and Fedora installations.

Dock is currently connecting AmazonBasics A100 USB-powered speakers (consuming a USB 3.0 port and an audio jack), two external 1080p monitors over HDMI, and a USB keyboard and mouse over the two USB 2.0 ports. All is working as expected. I may check back in a few days after I add my third monitor.

This setup appears to have very little discernible CPU penalty.

Cool bit of kit. Kind of dense for its size, and the underside creates enough friction to keep her pretty still on a desk. Well thought out.

02.06.2017 udpate: I had trouble adding a third external display (all three external monitors are matching 1080p ViewSonic). Can't recall error message, but I couldn't populate the display on a third monitor. I just worked around the issue by running HDMI directly from laptop to one of the external monitors, and I let the D3100 feed the other two (one via HDMI, the other uses a Displayport-to-HDMI adapter for the moment). Just note you may have a problem with three displays.

Currently: Ubuntu 16.04 on Dell 5548 notebook, fully patched, tested with and without Intel-proprietary drivers, stock 4.4 kernel. I'm satisfied with the setup, and I don't intend to fiddle with it any further.

03/2017 update:
Inconsistent results coming up from sleep state or reboot. Got tired of fussing, so I sold the thing. I'll never buy a consumer-type notebook again, only business-class kit from now on. A proper dock and a computer with proper dock support is worth the spend, to me.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Well, I have been using one of these docks for almost a year now, and I have been extremely impressed. The picture quality is great, and the functionality is very reliable. I do, however, have two complaints.

Firstly, the setup is not as simple as it should be. There is firmware available on the Dell website, as well as on the DisplayLink website, but no native software application for managing the displays once installed. You are forced to use the Windows display management software, which is absolutely not user friendly, especially if you are running triple monitors or more. It takes some time to get everything set up and working properly, but once you get it done, you should not have any further issues.

Secondly, this dock has a DisplayPort output. If, however, you own or intend to purchase monitors, like my three Dell U2414H flat panels, with MST (Multi-Stream Transport) capability (aka Daisy Chaining) you will be disappointed to learn that this dock does NOT support MST. Rather than connecting multiple monitors to one display output, you have to run a separate video cable for every single monitor. What's worse, the dock only has one DisplayPort output, the other two outputs are HDMI, so if your monitors came with DisplayPort cables like mine did, you will have to buy additional HDMI cables as well...

None of these issues is a deal breaker, and now that I am set up, I am EXTREMELY happy with the end result, but just a little bit of info I wish I had known prior to making my purchases.

text:
Ich habe mir diese Dock bestellt da ich es mit meinem Tablet (Acer Iconia W700) auch als Desktop-Rechner nutzen wollte.
Dafür brauchte ich natürlich mehr USB-Anschlüsse (Maus + Tastatur, Webcam, DVD-RW-Laufwerk, USB-Stick...).
Zudem hatte ich auch keine Lust jedes mal HDMI-Kabel, 3,5-Klinkenstecker, USB-Hub und Netzstecker an und ab zu stöpseln. Daher habe ich nach einiger Recherche das Dell D3100 bestellt.

Zum Dock selbst:
- Gut verarbeitet
- Kompakt
- Anschlüsse sind gut verteilt und in ausreichender Zahl vorhanden
- von Lüftergeräuschen oder großer Hitzeentwicklung ist nichts zu merken
- etwas schade ist das es keinen An-/Aus-Schalter hat (ich lasse es über eine schaltbare Mehrfachsteckdose laufen, daher ist mir dieser Punkt relativ egal - wäre nur noch besser gewesen)

Zur Funktion:
- Aufbau, Verkabelung, usw. - alles sehr einfach
- Treiberinstallation sollte vor dem ersten Einstecken erfolgen (ich habe mir den Aktuellen von der DisplayLink-Seite geholt)
- Audio, USB-Geräte, LAN - alles läuft super

Monitor:
- Auflösung bei mir Full-HD
- per DVI und per HDMI läuft einwandfrei - ich habe den Monitor über ein HDMI-Kabel angeschlossen
- ob und wie es mit zwei Monitoren HD oder 4K aussieht kann ich nicht sagen, da ich dies noch nicht probiert habe

Von Verzögerungen beim Bild oder verschlechterter Qualität habe ich nichts gemerkt, auch nicht bei HD-Filmen. Spiele von der Xbox One auf das Tablet und somit über die Dock auf den Monitor läuft auch super. Hin und wieder hatte mein Tablet nach dem Neuverbinden mit der Dock eine Verzögerung bei der Erkennung (seit dem neuesten Treibern auch hier keine Probleme mehr).

I’ll tell you what.. typically I’m not a fan of black phone cases being a woman personally as I found it to be a little more on the masculine side BUT LET ME TELL YOU— this black otterbox looks SO elegant and professional mixed with the silver iPhone pro max! I’m a fan of bulkiness in phone cases and it enlarging my phone personally but I do know not many prefer this so if this is the case.. I’d opt for the commuter version if I were you. However, protection for this phone is superb. Installation was more difficult with this version but if you use a little tool to remove the clasps it becomes effortless.

Overall, it has BOTH protection and looks absolutely great- it’s slip resistant, durable, and looks freaking great. Cannot emphasize how much better it looks in person. PS ignore my ripped nails— I took off my fake ones 😅

Edit to add: someone else commented that it scratched their phone around the camera panel and for this specific reason, I was EXTREMELY hesitant about buying. But after having the case for a month, dropping my phone a couple times, and removing it a couple of times I had found there is NO DAMAGE or scratches around the panel. There is dirt that accumulates in those areas for sure, but they wipe off. So no issues with this case scratching or damaging the integrity of my phone! Figured this would help others in deciding whether this case is for you because that specific feedback almost swayed my decision of buying the case.

The belt clip is free on the site when you purchase the case, and it will not randomly drop your phone like other brands on the market. The set is durable and will protect your phone. I also haven’t had any problems with the case interfering with my screen protector. I haven’t had any issues since purchasing this. I highly recommend!

text: I’ve always been a fan of OtterBox since I got my first iPhone SE. it’s saved many of my phones (from falls, drops, rain puddles…you name it) over the years. I teach preschool and am very rough with my phone myself, so durability is the most important thing to me when it comes to phone covers. I recently upgraded to the newest iPhone 17 Pro and was sad to see that the brand in the defender series wasn’t offered at my local T-Mobile. They tried to talk me into the Pelican and said it was just as good. The first day back at school, the phone fell off of my belt loop, out of my chair, popped out of the Pelican belt clip AND case and cracked the screen cover (which I didn’t purchase a warranty for because my OtterBox covers always protected my glass covers too). I ordered a set of cheaper glass protectors on Amazon (which also held up better than the one from the phone shop), and gave the case another try. It happened again but this time the glass protector didn’t break. I finally stopped wearing my phone at work but it got to the point where it was constantly popping out of the belt clip while I was out and about shopping with nothing touching it. The OtterBox cases and belt clips never did that. After a few more falls, I broke down and ordered the OtterBox and never looked back. The case has the extra layer of protection where it snaps around the phone before you put the other part of the case over it, preventing it from falling out and hurting the screen when it is accidentally dropped. The belt clip is free on the site when you purchase the case, and it will not randomly drop your phone like other brands on the market. The set is durable and will protect your phone. I also haven’t had any problems with the case interfering with my screen protector. I haven’t had any issues since purchasing this. I highly recommend!

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I recently bought the new HTVRONT H17 heat press as a new hobby toy and it’s been a lot of fun. I’ve never used a press like this before, but it was easy to figure out. The instructions are clear and the buttons are simple. I just set the temp and time and it heats up fast, it has various heat levels.

The vacuum feature is pretty cool. It pulls the phone case tight with pressure so the design wraps right around the edges with no bubbles or peeling. I have an iphone but it comes with the adjustable holder to fit other types of phones and phone models. It very practical and functional, and you can use it for other things as well.
I also tried a few small things like coasters and badges and those came out great. The auto shut-off is a good safety feature.

The box included gloves, tape, some blanks, and the little design software with phone templates that helped get the sizing right without guessing.

I’m just a casual crafter, with a small side business, and this machine feels beginner-friendly but still makes the projects look really polished. I think its a good investment if you like to try new things and if you like personalizing things. Im also a teacher so I love personalizing things for my students, this add more items I can do for my students.

text: This machine is easy to use and a perfect add to my craft room! I love being able to change my phone cases and this heat press machine makes it easier now! Items you need to purchase to be successful at using this heat press machine are the sublimation film (not paper), a printer either a sublimation or a inkjet converted to a sublimation printer (consider Epson eco tank),you need the full wrap around cell phone cases, not the ones with the plates ( they don’t work with the sublimation film) . I give this product 5 stars.

Great job TORRAS!!!

Buy one you will not be disappointed.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text: A lanyards day in the life with a Park & Rec employee: Out of all the lanyards I have purchased, this one is by far my favorite. This baby worked all 16 hours with me on Saturday and pulled another solid 12 hours today. With one of our largest tournaments, I was everywhere and doing everything. My favorite part is that it’s adjustable and how easy it is to adjust it. I like my phone is a certain place 90% of the time but the other 10% I needed to pull it smaller so my phone wouldn’t go in the pot-tae, lol, that would be gross even though I can clean the toilets like a PRO! I really like that the length can go as large as using it for a cross body. Before I’d have to throw my phone on the counter and hope I didn’t forget it but I didn’t have to do that with the TORRAS Lanyard this past weekend. I love the olive green color I chose and the woven material it is made of. I sweated A LOT for 2 days and not once did the materials bother me or feel gross on my neck. It’s not itchy and even sweating in it, I didn’t notice it being wet at all. It is so well made and I pulled and tugged on it all weekend. The clasp is wicked strong, not some cheap one that bends up and warps after a couple of weeks to the point you have to buy a new clasp or a new lanyard. It’s durable, sturdy, and soft. You can buy a cheaper lanyard, but all the cheap ones you keep buying will add up to this one great one. I cannot imagine I will have to replace this one anytime soon. I had a couple of compliments on it too. THE ONLY thing I saw a problem with, and it doesn’t bother me, but I think it would someone, is the paint has scraped off the clasp already. I attached pictures, and this was only 2 days of use. Again though, it does not bother me, it’s merely cosmetic. Any paint coated metal is not going to last forever anyway. It will not keep me from getting another one in the future, or buying some for my lanyard loving employees. It really is a great lanyard!!

Taking my smartphone near the water used to be a nerve-wracking experience, but that completely changed once I grabbed this two-pack of Case-Mate waterproof pouches. Whether I'm lounging by the pool, kayaking down a river, or gearing up for a tropical cruise, protecting my device from rogue splashes and accidental drops is an absolute priority. Right out of the box, you can feel the premium construction; the material is thick yet flexible, assuring me that my expensive tech is in safe hands.

The secure locking mechanism at the top clicks shut with a reassuring snap, creating an impenetrable seal against water, fine beach sand, and dust. title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I'll start by saying i am a long-time user and fan of the Otterbox brand - having purchased their cases since my first iPhone and for every Android phone I have owned. Universally, they have been solid, reliable and free of manufacturing defects - and I have never had a phone damaged while in one.

This case arrived well-packaged in a simple cardboard case. It is a single piece of flexible polycarbonate, requires no attembly - just snap your Pixel 10a into it and it works. No gymnastics or applying ridiculous amounts of pressure to the phone or case is required, unlike some similar cases.

The buttons on the case are perfectly positioned, though a bit stiffer to use than I would have liked - at least at the outset. Same for the speaker / camera openings and the USB charging cable openings on the bottom of the case. No tight fits, and no need for USB extenders needed for some of their multi-piece cases.

The material had a nice grip to it - easy to hold and not easy to slip out of your grasp. It is also very clear, showing off the color of your Pixel - red in my case. I like that aspect of the case. It also doesn't add unneccessary size or bulk to your phone - keeping it easy to slide in and out of your pocket. It also allows for wireless charging to work through the case. The case extends far enough past the edge of the screen to provide some screen protection in drops - but i still wouldn't use one without a good screen protector.

In my opinion, the only real flaw in this case is the lack of a magnet to hold the phone in position for wireless charging - since wireless charging is an important aspect of the Pixel 10a. I was disapponted that the Pixel 10a doesn't have built in magnets of its own, so in my mind any case for it needs to include that function. You can purchase your own magnetic sticker and attach it to your phone to remedy this, but the magnetic connection won't be as strong as it would be on the outside of the case.

Overall, this is an excellent case for providing light protection in average use. Including a magnetic sticker for wireless charging position would have gotten it 5 stars.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
My previous phone wasn't cutting it. It was a Samsung A15 with only 4GB of RAM, and the Amazon Music app needed 6-8 GB of RAM to not crash, so I got the Pixel Phone 10a with 128 GB of storage. I wish I had paid the $100 more for the 256 GB of storage version. I feel like they should have not made a 128 GB version, and should instead have made a 256 GB and a 512 GB version. In any event, this phone only needs to last me until 6G becomes available in a few years. Until then, I anticipate will will serve me well. Amazon Music doesn't randomly crash on this phone like it did on my Samsung, and for that reason alone, the extra cost of this phone was worth it for me. Also, I would be remiss if I failed to mention that the cameras are way better than anything I've ever owned before.

I connected this phone to a USB-C hub with and HDMI output to a 27" computer monitor, and paired Logitech Bluetooth keyboard and mouse to it, and use it in desktop mode. When plugged into a PD wall charger into the USB-C hub's dedicated power input, it charges my phone while in desktop mode. Desktop mode is great! It comes in very handy composing long text messages. Google Docs and Sheets apps work great in desktop mode.

It kind of reminds me of the idea Canonical had for the Ubuntu phone that could be used on its own as a smart phone, but also connected to a USB-C hub with HDMI monitor, and using either Bluetooth or USB keyboard and mouse, and use it as a desktop computer like I can with my Pixel Phone. Canonical failed miserably, but I think Google has kind of pulled it off if you don't particularly mind Google spying on you to deliver targeted ads, or their Gemini integration.

One thing that annoyed me was the setting it came with that made the power button bring up Gemini instead of the power menu so I could restart or shutdown my phone. I had to go into the settings, and make changes to make the power button work for power instead of Gemini. To fix that, go to Settings > System > Gestures > Press & hold power button and change the action from "Digital assistant" to "Power menu". That's my only gripe about this phone.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Good: Just about everything, overall improvement on the Pixel 7 this replaced. Bright, sharp screen. Excellent sound quality with and without buds. Very good price for what you get.

Bad: It's a rare occasion when I pick this thing up without getting push notifications about some feature that Google thinks I need to enable. Google is quickly becoming as bad as Microsoft in this regard. And, of course, they're shoving AI down our throats, which I neither need nor want on my phone. Looking forward to seeing how much more battery life I get when I figure out how to disable it completely.

Bottom line: My old Pixel 7 was nearing end of life - a couple of unfortunate drops have the glass back cracked all the way across and starting to crumble in one corner, the face has a couple of obvious scratches, and the battery rarely lasts more than a day of light use - so it was time to upgrade. Pixel phones in general have impressed me with performance and value, and this latest Pixel 10a is no exception. It isn't top of the line, but if your phone isn't your primary computer, which mine is not, so what? Just, Google, please back off on the "engagement" messages and AI obsession, OK? Five stars.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
My previous phone wasn't cutting it. It was a Samsung A15 with only 4GB of RAM, and the Amazon Music app needed 6-8 GB of RAM to not crash, so I got the Pixel Phone 10a with 128 GB of storage. I wish I had paid the $100 more for the 256 GB of storage version. I feel like they should have not made a 128 GB version, and should instead have made a 256 GB and a 512 GB version. In any event, this phone only needs to last me until 6G becomes available in a few years. Until then, I anticipate will will serve me well. Amazon Music doesn't randomly crash on this phone like it did on my Samsung, and for that reason alone, the extra cost of this phone was worth it for me. Also, I would be remiss if I failed to mention that the cameras are way better than anything I've ever owned before.

I connected this phone to a USB-C hub with and HDMI output to a 27" computer monitor, and paired Logitech Bluetooth keyboard and mouse to it, and use it in desktop mode. When plugged into a PD wall charger into the USB-C hub's dedicated power input, it charges my phone while in desktop mode. Desktop mode is great! It comes in very handy composing long text messages. Google Docs and Sheets apps work great in desktop mode.

It kind of reminds me of the idea Canonical had for the Ubuntu phone that could be used on its own as a smart phone, but also connected to a USB-C hub with HDMI monitor, and using either Bluetooth or USB keyboard and mouse, and use it as a desktop computer like I can with my Pixel Phone. Canonical failed miserably, but I think Google has kind of pulled it off if you don't particularly mind Google spying on you to deliver targeted ads, or their Gemini integration.

One thing that annoyed me was the setting it came with that made the power button bring up Gemini instead of the power menu so I could restart or shutdown my phone. I had to go into the settings, and make changes to make the power button work for power instead of Gemini. To fix that, go to Settings > System > Gestures > Press & hold power button and change the action from "Digital assistant" to "Power menu". That's my only gripe about this phone.

timestamp_raw: Reviewed in the United States on March 17, 2026

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This is a very nice phone at a reasonable price. Usually, the "FE" designation just means the body of the phone is plastic rather than metal. This phone works just as well as the S25 and will serve most users quite well.
The 128 GB storage will hold thousands of pictures, etc. and all pictures and data can be transferred to one's computer if the memory should fill-up. If you go to the two SIM card upgrade you will pay much more for the phone for not that much more "bang for the buck".
Remember, this phone will work just fine for the MAJORITY of people who just want great calling, texting and photo abilities.
The camera does a very nice job and is quite versatile. You can do most everything you need for picture taking.
One "little" problem however, you better know what you are doing if you plan to link/connect via bluetooth to your car hands-free system. Connection takes "patience". However, stick with it for once you do get connected the connection is very solid, clear and fast. If it would be helpful, my car is a 2024 Jeep Grand Cherokee Limited with the UConnect-5 System in it. It took a little bit of "wrestling" to get the connection made but it will eventually got through.
The phone feels very good in the hand and it does have metal banding/edges all around it. Definitely get a screen protector and some form of body case for added safety. The phone works just fine with a screen protector on it because you can increase touch sensitivity through the phone settings.
Take your time setting this phone up. It has a "thousand" menus and selections that make the phone very personalized for each person. Before doing the set up I would suggest you go online and look at many of the tutorials that are offered on set up and use.
The phone is completely unlocked for ANY United States Carrier. All you may need is a new SIM card to be sure you get the company services you want. These SIM cards can be obtained at the various carrier's stores--they cost about $10.00 and the technicians will install them for you. These phones WILL allow you to use the new eSIM card set-ups also.
I would recommend purchase of this Samsung S25FE phone for certain! It is a great buy and should give you many years of service.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
With there being really no options now for a few phone or low price upgrade on any carrier this was a great deal. Not only cheaper than if I got thru my carrier locally, but it's unlocked so I can switch off I want to. IT ALSO CAME WITH A PROMO OF DBL STORAGE FOR FREE AND A 100 AMAZON GC!!!

Why I like this phone. LITERALLY took 5 minds to set up and transfer all my contacts and apps and set up on with my carrier.
It is much lighter than my old Samsung 36.

IT IS spec wise so close to the samsung s25.

It is so fast with built in AI features which are fun and helpful.

Overall if you are an android user this phone feels and acts like the phones that are 1200$ on up.

I also like the changes. It has great sound, great"cleaner" on the phone, gorilla glass screen, and the fingerprint unlock feature is no longer the power button but on the screen.

I learned long ago, even if you are super excited to start using the phone, be sure you charge it to 100% on the first charge. Then go to settings, battery , and set it to never over charge. OLD PHONE defaulted to cap at 85%, this one let's you set the top up to 95%. I used to have an electric vehicle and the batteries need to learn what 100 is but never overcharge. This will extend the life of the phone and prevent major headaches in the future. I keep mine on the charger overnight and playing my favorite sleep podcast- it stops at 95% and does not get hot.

I am always playing audible books or podcasts and using Google maps. The battery stays charged and by the end of the day it's around 70%.

I am thankful samsung put out a good "lower priced model" than the s25 ultra. I also ran into using 99% of my storage on my old phone(128gb) I have every kind of app on here and it's only using 28% of my total storage so I highly recommend getting the 512 GB of you need lots of room.

I am one of those people that keeps a phone forever and I think this one will last me a very long time.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I have owned this phone for a month now. I switched over from an iphone 15 and have been with apple for over 10 years. I can 1000% say that I am never going back to apple!

The phone is super sleek, I love how small it is when it folds up. I am easily able to fit it in my pocket or in one of my smaller purses. Even though it's thin, it has some weight to it, especially after adding a case.

It is way faster than my previous phone. There is no lag and there has been zero issues with freezing up. The camera quality is fantastic and the video recording is very crisp and steady. I love that I can also unlock it with either my fingerprint or my face.

I also love how customizable samsung is! There is so much that I can do on this one that apple is nowhere near even touching. I am constantly discovering new features that improve how I use my phone. And I love that I can actually set custom ringtones and text sounds, unlike apple lol.

I have also not had any screen issues at all. I've dropped it and slammed it shut more than I would have liked but it's still going strong! There is also a small crease where it folds of course, but it is not noticeable at all when the screen is turned on.

The only Con that I have with this phone is the battery doesn't last as long as my iphone did. I have it set to stop charging at 90% to protect the battery and I usually charge it overnight. If I don't mess with it too much during the day, the battery will definitely last. However if i play my games or watch videos for an extended period I do have to charge it 2x a day.

While there are some things I do miss about apple, mainly apple maps, I feel like my overall experience with the flip7 is way more pleasant and the OS functions way faster/better. This phone is def worth the price tag that comes with it.

text:
I hadn’t tried a Pixel phone since the Pixel 2 XL, which was one of my all time favorite devices. I decided to stick to Apple’s ecosystem since then, just for simplicity sake, since the rest of our family all use iPhones. I decided to bite the bullet and dip my toe back in the Android world with the Pixel 9 Pro Fold, and I have to say, I could not be happier with the decision.

Battery life has been phenomenal and I’ve not hit the end of a day where I was lower than 60% left. That’s with a fairly extensive use of the device, including video watching, replying to emails, using navigation, and some casual browsing. I don’t really do much game playing so I can’t speak to that.

Phone quality has felt fantastic. I’ve no complaints what so ever on how the device feels in the hand, or behaves. The OS feels buttery smooth and the hardware is just delightful to use.

All of the screens are very good, but being a foldable, it’s really all about that interior display, and I’ve been thoroughly pleased with it. There is a slight crease where the phone folds but you honestly don’t notice it when you’re using the device. Just if the light hits it just right or you’re dragging something with your finger across the length of it. But that’s true of all foldable.

Durability seems good, although it’s early days. I’d highly recommend a case that protects the hinge because I’ve been reading a few reports online of folks getting small rocks or even sand trapped in the hinge or inner display and it causing problems. No surprises there really, I’d expect that to be a risk.

The face unlock works pretty well, except in low light conditions. But the fingerprint reader works flawlessly so, unlike my iPhone, I’m not forced to immediately resort to a PIN. Also, if you pair this with a Pixel Watch 3, the watch can act like you’re biometric unlock, so you almost never need to deal with any of that anyway. Great stuff!

title: 1.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I bought this phone for my husband, thinking we were getting a good deal of $300 off list price for the Father's Day sale, but we've had a very bad experience with Google, and we hope others can avoid what we've gone through. Pasted below is a longer version of the review placed in the Google review of the Google store in Oakbrook, Illinois that we visited. We had to condense this down to fit the 4096 character limit of the Google review.

Prior to the Inner Screen self destructing, my husband was generally happy with the phone, especially the main feature of the phone of the large inner display. He did have the minor complaints others have mentioned of slower charging and less battery life than his previous midrange Motorola G100 phone.

It was clear from the beginning that this phone with the fold was more fragile than others and needed to be protected, which my husband did. We had no idea though that the inner display of the phone we received was going to fail in just over a month via normal usage.

Given our experience with Google, we won't buy Google products anymore, but if you are willing to deal with Google, we recommend you stay away from this phone or buy a protection plan from the beginning. However, even if you have the protection plan, there would still be the enormous hassle of going through support to get it fixed or replaced.

----------------
Appalling Experience with Defective Pixel 9 Pro Fold and Unacceptable Customer Service

I am utterly appalled and deeply disappointed with my recent experience at the Google Store in Oakbrook regarding a defective Google Pixel 9 Pro Fold. I purchased this phone from Amazon on June 7, 2025, and received it on June 8, 2025.

On July 16, while on a snack break at work, the inner display began to fail. It started as a thin black line precisely in the center, along the fold crease. As I opened and closed the phone a few more times, the black area expanded significantly, rendering most of the inner touchscreen unusable. Internal cracks, vertical and parallel to the crease, also developed. Unfortunately, I didn't capture a photo immediately, but I did take one later that day with my work phone, which showed less of the black area than when I brought it into the store. I showed this photo to the staff at the Google Store.

My attempts to get support before visiting the store were equally frustrating. The Google support website was a labyrinth, repeatedly asking for my IMEI and leading me in circles without providing any clear path to resolution. I eventually found out about uBreakiFix, which Google uses for repairs. I called uBreakiFix on July 17, but they informed me they only handle repairs and could not assist with determining eligibility for a replacement or refund.

Given the lack of online and phone support, I decided my only option was to visit a physical Google Store. As it was a longer drive for me, I waited until Saturday, July 19. It's worth noting that I couldn't call ahead because there's no phone number listed for the Oakbrook store on Google Maps or the official Google Store website.

We felt fortunate to even have a Google Store within driving distance, as there are only seven in the entire United States, and the Oakbrook location is the sole one in Illinois. We arrived with my wife and 10-year-old daughter, expecting premium service. At first, it seemed promising; we were greeted at the door and directed to where we could get help. I immediately showed two staff members the phone and its clearly visible inner display defect, and as they discussed the situation with us, it genuinely felt like they were going to assist rather than accuse.

After a brief examination, they asked me to remove my protective case. My wife and I struggled to get it off, and one of the staff members eventually assisted. They then examined the phone further and took it to the back, stating they wanted to show it to a repair person. After about five minutes, they returned the phone. They discussed it amongst themselves, then asked for the phone back again and huddled with another person we believe to be the manager, who later identified himself as David.

David then returned the phone to me and stated unequivocally that they couldn't do anything for us. He explained that the damage "must have been something I did," suggesting I had put too much pressure on the phone or bending the hinge too far. I reiterated, as I had several times to the initial employees, that the problem arose simply from opening and closing the phone normally. I also mentioned having seen reviews online about other users experiencing issues with the inner displays of these phones. David dismissively responded that he had not seen any such reports and, bafflingly, showed me his own Pixel 9 Pro Fold, implying that his single, undamaged phone was proof that no such issues exist for the model.

My wife and I were stunned and in disbelief. I repeatedly asked, "You're really not going to help us?" As they continued to refuse, both my wife and I started to lose our composure and raised our voices, repeating that we paid over $1500 for this phone and they were effectively "screwing us out of $1500." We are not the type of people who would raise a disturbance without exceptionally bad treatment, even without our 10-year-old daughter present; we lost our cool specifically because we were being falsely accused of causing damage we did not inflict. The only alternative they suggested was to try sending it back to Google by mail to see if Google would have a "different opinion." They shockingly threatened to call the police on us, despite the fact that we were clearly not threatening them and had our young daughter present.

I expected better support and accountability from Google, especially for a premium device with a clear manufacturing defect occurring so soon after purchase. The complete lack of accessible online and phone support channels, combined with the Oakbrook store's refusal to acknowledge a manufacturing flaw, their decision to blame the customer, and the unprofessional threat to involve law enforcement, is utterly unacceptable and a terrible reflection on Google's customer service. We will never buy a Google product again.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I got tired of Samsung removing features from their newer phones and jamming as much shoddy "AI" garbage in there as they could, so when it was time for a new phone I decided this was the one for me.
The glyph interface in particular was a huge draw for me, since I really miss my notification LEDs that have been long removed in favor of always-on displays that, in my experience, tank battery life (especially on aging phones like my old S22). Now I don't have to constantly check my phone to see if I have missed messages or calls; I can just glance over and see if anyone called or messaged me.
I really like the cameras on this phone, too. They seem to take much better photos than my old Samsung phones without the blurriness or distortion around the edges of the photos, but I'm not a professional photographer by any means either. If you're like me and use your phone for family pics and random cool stuff I think you'll be very happy with them too.
The phone also comes with a screen protector pre-installed as well as a simple but effective silicone case, although I also ordered the Spigen air cushioned case for it for the added protection. Still, it's an appreciated extra given how little you typically get with phones these days.
I don't play many games other than idle time wasters like Block Blast, but it handles that type of stuff just fine and the OS is snappy and responsive as well. If you're stateside like me you'll have to switch a couple default settings from the UK English to US English to get things like the correct currency symbol on your keyboard, but it's simple and easy, and honestly I kind of prefer the British accent on my GPS.
Initially I was having a lot of problems with dropped calls, and I even almost returned the phone due to it, but that seemed to be an issue with my VPN and after reconfiguring my settings for this phone those issues stopped as well. Sound quality both in calls and media playback is just as good or better than any other phone I've had, although you're probably going to want some wireless headphones for the best listening experience if you use your phone for music like I do.

Overall this is an extremely solid, fun, and unique phone without all the bloat of other flagship phones available in the US currently. On sale at $630 for 12GB of memory and 256GB of storage this is a really good deal in my opinion, given that other entry level Android and Apple phones charge more for less of both. The bottom line is that this is an awesome phone for those of us who don't want to be glued to our device but still use it to browse the Internet, listen to music, or take pictures.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I had been looking for a new phone on and off for a few years, and really started looking in the past few months since my existing phone was old. So old, that current apps would randomly crash. Not fancy games; no, Google messages, email, YouTube. I had an LG G8X Thinq Dual Screen(I really miss the separate/dual screens) :( It had the same specs as a Galaxy S10. Both the G8X and the S10 came out at the same time in 2019.

Why Not Samsung?!
Samsung, is outrageously over priced, and is full of bloat apps, and duplicate apps. Some, like KNOX you maybe shouldn't remove. There has been absolutely no outward innovation from Samsung in over 10 generations. All the phones look the same and all run over $1000. The phone also runs several AI agents, that I am not a fan of. The folding screens are a travesty across the board. 2 or 3 separate screens is the way to go.

Why not Apple?
Apple's history of 'playing games'(the battery limiting fiasco, fighting with app makers, internal planned obsolescence, $%&ty phone repair support without paying a kidney, for AppleCare, which the company continually tries to say 'does not cover X, Y, Z'. If you didn't have problems, great! I've worked in an Apple care approved repair company, and the number of times we had to turn down customers because AppleCare didn't cover the perfectly reasonable repair, was bonkers! Then we get to the sky high price for the phone, and the all intrusive Siri AI. "Hard No"

Why Nothing?
It's different, and leans toward use, instead of flash! Besides the Glyph features, the phone is really meant to 'get things done' In the settings, you have the options to use the normal flashy app icons, or 'grey scale' icons. You can also opt to show or hide the app names. Less clutter, so you can focus on 'that thing you are trying to do'. Yes the Nothing Phone 3 does have AI, as EVERY$$%%@#$THING does these days. Sadly, you can not fully disable or remap the 'AI' button. However, with a few minutes of tinkering in the settings, you can mostly disable the 'Nothing AI' features. Now the phone works as I really like it, plane and 'bare bones'. Great Job Nothing!

The "Glyph" features are cool, make no mistake. It's nice to have...it's kind of a 'mullet phone'(LOL Sorry). Business up front, and party in the back. LOL Spin the bottle, dice, and the sun clock are neat and great for the odd party. The dice glyph has already settled several decisions with my friends and I, with a quick 'odds or evens' decision. LOL.

The phone does have wireless charging. The coil is hidden under the decorative back façade. It's a little wonky and difficult to position on some wireless chargers(especially some portable battery banks with wireless charging), because the coil is shaped to make room for the 'glyph' button. But, it does work.

Verdict, I'm a big fan of the phone and will likely stay with Nothing if they continue on this track. The camera is much better than the G8X, but I don't really care about a camera. I take more photos of serial numbers(I work it tech) than Instagram photos. If I can read the serial number, that's all I need. I'm not a fan of AI and I'm not really a mobile gamer.
- No/minimal AI? Check!
- Camera that works? Check!
- 12/16GB of RAM for multi-tasking? Check!
- Wireless Charging? Check!
- Clean UI? Check
- The speakers are a big improvement over the G8X, still very much 'phone speakers', but a nice boost, to movies/videos chilling at home.
* I don't really have anything to say about the CPU(Snapdragon 8s Gen4) Not the Elite. I really haven't seen a problem not having the flagship proc. As the Nothing CEO said, they focused on a really good phone experience, and that's what they've done. No issue!

The only things, I would change are personal nit pick gripes.
- Option to disable/remove AI across the board
- Reduce text/UI spacing. I like a really compact interface. I want to be able to see as much information on the screen as possible.
- Make the wireless charging coil 'easier' to position.

Great job Nothing!

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Alright, so I’ve had the new Pixel 10 Pro for about a week now, and I’ve finally gathered my thoughts. Let me just say, this thing feels less like a phone and more like some gadget from a sci-fi movie.
First off, taking it out of the box, it just feels premium. It has a nice weight to it—not too heavy, but it feels solid and well-built. The matte finish on the back is a lifesaver for someone like me who hates fingerprints. The screen is the real star, though. It’s a big 6.7-inch display, and everything just looks incredible on it. Scrolling is buttery smooth, and watching videos is a treat. It’s super bright too, so I had no trouble seeing it outside, even in the afternoon sun.
But let's be real, you buy a Pixel for the camera, and this one is just insane. I took it out over the weekend, and I’m blown away. The main camera takes ridiculously sharp and colorful photos without you having to do anything. But the feature I can't stop playing with is the "Pro Res Zoom." I was at a park and saw a cool bird way up in a tree. Normally, that would just be a blurry mess on my old phone. With this, I zoomed all the way in, and the photo is actually sharp enough to see the details on its feathers. It feels like magic.
Google's AI stuff is all over this phone. They have this new feature called "Magic Cue" that tries to guess what you need. At first, it was a little weird, but now I’m getting used to it. Like, when I was heading to a meeting, it popped up a notification with the address and traffic info without me even asking. Another fun one is "Nano Banana"—silly name, I know—but it's this cool photo effect tool that lets you create some really artistic shots. Some of the results are a bit out there, but it's genuinely fun to mess around with.
Performance-wise, it's a beast. The new Tensor G5 chip makes everything feel instant. Apps open right away, and I haven't seen a single stutter, even when I'm jumping between a bunch of different apps. The battery life has been solid too. I'm a pretty heavy user—lots of photos, social media, and some videos—and I've been easily getting through a full day with some juice to spare.
So, is it worth it? It’s definitely not cheap, but if you're someone who loves taking pictures and wants a phone that feels like it’s one step ahead of you, I'd say absolutely. The Pixel 10 Pro isn't just a phone with a great camera; it’s a genuinely smart device that makes everyday tasks a little bit easier and a lot more fun. I'm still discovering new things it can do, and I'm honestly excited to see what else I find

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I have owned many high-end phones over the years, but the Pixel 10 Pro XL in the 256GB Moonstone version is the first one I genuinely do not want to put down. After two weeks of heavy daily use that includes photo editing on the go, 4K video calls, and constant work sessions with Gemini, it has already exceeded my expectations.

The 6.8 inch Actua Display is excellent. The 120Hz refresh rate makes every swipe feel smooth, and the colors are vibrant enough to make Netflix and YouTube feel almost cinematic. The Tensor G5 chip combined with 16GB of RAM handles real multitasking with ease. I can edit RAW photos in Lightroom while listening to podcasts and the phone stays fast and responsive. The 5200mAh battery easily lasts through a full day of mixed use, and the included 45W charger brings it to about 70 percent in about thirty minutes.

The cameras are another highlight. The long range zoom produces impressively clear images, and the AI support through Gemini offers helpful suggestions that consistently improve quick snapshots. Both the fingerprint sensor and the face unlock respond instantly. The IP68 protection handled an accidental splash without a single issue. WiFi 7 keeps my video calls stable, and the stereo speakers sound fuller than I expected for a phone of this size.

After using many flagship phones over the years, this one feels different. It genuinely boosts productivity and day to day convenience. If you are upgrading from anything released before 2024, this is a phone that truly feels like a meaningful step forward. I have zero regrets so far.

A slim protective case works perfectly with the XL size and keeps the grip comfortable.

text:
I’ve spent way too many afternoons glancing at the clock and wondering if my son has already left his after-school club, usually right as I’m trying to finish up a work task and he’s nowhere near a landline. This 6.6-inch budget smartphone arrived just as I was looking for a "starter" device that wouldn't break the bank—honestly, the 5000mAh battery is a total win because it stays powered through his entire school day and then some, meaning he’s not "guessing" if he has enough juice to call for a ride home. It’s roughly the size of a standard notebook and has that bright HD display that’s clear enough for him to check his homework assignments or snap a quick photo of the whiteboard. By the way, the facial recognition is a massive relief; it saves him from fumbling with a passcode while he’s juggling a heavy backpack and a lunchbox.

However, the "powerful performance" claim is definitely more suited for basic tasks than heavy gaming. While the MTK6737 processor handles messaging and web browsing just fine, I’ve noticed that once he tries to run those high-graphics games, the frame rate gets a bit "choppy"—roughly the smoothness of an old flipbook if you flip the pages too slowly. With 32GB of storage, it’s a bit of a tight fit, but the microSD expansion is about as essential as a spare tire, so I’ve already popped in a memory card for his photos. I’ve noticed the camera is okay for quick daytime snapshots, but the 16MP rear lens feels roughly as sharp as a basic webcam in low light, which is a bit of a bummer. One tiny quirk: the Type-C port is a modern touch, but the charging speed feels a bit like a "slow simmer"—it takes about as long as a long movie to get from zero back to a full charge.

It’s a decent, low-stress choice if you just need a reliable backup for a child to stay in touch or for those basic school apps. The build quality feels sturdy enough to survive being tossed around in a locker, and the triple-card slot is a solid plus if you want to keep his personal and emergency contacts separate.
