title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
In this kit there are 4 different lenses, and the first lens is a fisheye lens 198°, a 0.63x wide lens, a 15x macro lens, and a 12x Telephone lens. Apexel also provides you with a small plastic tripod with extendable legs, a phone mount as well as a little pouch to carry your small lenses in but not the big lens which seems a bit odd.

Let me talk about the macro lens as that is my favourite lens out of the bunch. If you’re not sure what a macro lens is, it’s a lens suitable for taking photographs or video unusually close to the subject. This macro lens does a really great job at that in a very small form factor. I find myself using this lens and having a lot fun with it all the time. Capturing pictures really up close photos that you can’t really get with any phone. There is also no black circle when you use the clip to attach the lens to your phone, but you will need to take your case off. All the clips are plastic but are still quite strong and will hold on your phone relatively well. There are also rubber pads on the inside of the clip to protect your phone so it won’t get scratched.

Moving to the 0.63x wide lens. The wide lens actually has to be attached to the Marco lens to work. Meaning that you will have to take the 0.63x wide lens off the macro to use the macro lens and you have to put it somewhere and try not to lose it even though it is quite small. But I do find that this lens can be used from day to day. You can use the wide lens for any picture or video you wish from family photos to scenic photos. The lens is not a super wide lens or as narrow as your phone so it fits perfectly for any photo. The is also no black circle with lens ether and I really believe this lens works great on any phone and for any picture you wish.
Next up is the Fish eye lens 198°. So the fish eye lens is rather useful lens. This lens works great for those indoor photos. For example, if you need to take a picture of your room but your camera doesn’t see it all, just use the Fish eye lens and you be able to see your whole room in just one picture. This lens does give you the fish eye effect meaning that you will have black circle in your photos.

The last lens is 12x Telephone lens. To be honest this lens is my least favourite lens as it is really big and every time I adjust the focus the clip keeps shifting out of position. So I have to readjust the lens before each shoot. This lens is only just a bit clearer then just zooming in with your phone but I believe that the hustle with the lens is really not worth it. It is just simpler and easier to zoom in with your phone.

In conclusion this lens kit is very average. I believe that this lens kit is not that greatest lens kit apexel has made, so I have linked a couple better ones in the description bellow for you guys to checkout.

text:
Let me tell you how much this kit is loved! We bought it as an early gift for my son's birthday. He loves using his phone for photos; we were headed to Yellowstone, and we were signed up for a photo safari tour with a professional photographer (highly recommend this tour to anyone considering a trip to Yellowstone, BTW). While the tour states it is great for everyone from camera phone users to professionals, we wanted him to really enjoy the photo lessons. Hence, the kit as a gift. He adored it, which was awesome, since I said he would while his father said he doubted there would be an enthusiastic response. (Haha, Mom knew best!) Our son was obsessed with it from day one of our trip, and the photos he took were pretty good! He particularly liked the macro and wide angle lenses. In fact, he like them so much, he used them everywhere we went, and he lost them at one of those locations. We retraced all our steps but had no luck finding them. He was devastated. While still in Yellowstone, where cell service sucks for everyone--but particularly anyone not using Verizon, we found a couple of bars in the middle of Hayden Valley. We quickly pulled over and ordered another kit! Then thinking it wouldn't hurt to have a back up, we ordered another one again! By the time we returned home, one of them was waiting, just in time for a trip to Zion. The son was again thrilled, until he realized the macro lens had a flaw. :( No worries though, we had another one still on the way, right? It never showed. :( We contacted Amazon, who provided a refund, so we could turn around and reorder yet another kit! It arrived last Monday. All parts are perfect, and the son is once again blowing up his Instagram.

Would I buy this kit again? Well, I've bought it 4 times already; why would I stop now? LOL Honestly though, it is a good kit for a very low price.

text: I have an older Toyota with a CD player, in fact whatever car I get from this one on will in fact have a CD player because streaming music services are mostly low quality (if you use the non-pay versions) and nothing beats the dynamic range of a CD. That said, I also have an older Samsung Galaxy that has an affixed magnet in the back of its case. Have been having problems for yrs with dash-mount, vent-based, cup-holder orientated and the list goes on of auto-phone holder devices out there. Most besides losing adhesion once temperatures inside the car go to either extreme (for some reason) end up being unsturdy made from cheap quality plastic, that just cracks or breaks apart on some unsuspecting day. Happened to me many times, and you've not mishandled the holder or did anything adversely obvious before that. The internal dash CD player/holder is a great invention taking advantage of lets face it, an audio feature for cars that will one day soon be completely eliminated for most vehicle makes and models. But in the meantime, its a good alternative the others I mentioned. This brand's model in particular fits with outstanding stability, adjustment ability using the provided torque wingnut, and holds my phone with plenty of magnetism that road bumps and other driving shifts don't influence at all. Really no downside to it that I can tell other than it took me a bit to align the threads of the wingnut into the main unit per the installation guide...not a dealbreaker by any stretch for me. Great design to have the magnet in the shape of a square, provides more magnet surface area than a circular magnetic phone reast. Bottom line: give this one a try as other ones that are larger, different shaped, and not as compact or efficient looking are also double or triple priced compared to this one. No disappointments from me thus far

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This cd mount is the very thing I’m looking for, and I don’t need to block my vent now. The magnet is very strong. Inserts into the CD player easily. It holds my wireless 9 inch carpuride screen without difficulty. But, after a few weeks, the holder fell out of my CD player. I noticed the adhesive used on the 3 little pads was not holding them in place, and they were sliding off. NO FRET…….I just put a few dabs of krazy glue on each one. Held them firmly in place for a couple of minutes and let it set out for an hour before putting it back in. I wanted to be sure the glue was dry before reinserting the mount in my cd slot. I had no plans of krazy gluing the mount to my cd slot. Now, no more falling out.
Also, I do like the wing nut used to adjust tightness. It is easily accessed. However, I found that I do occasionally give it an extra twist every few weeks just to secure tightness. But, I don’t really notice any movement…….even when going over bumps. Don’t over tighten it though, also, I inserted mines with the wing nut on the top or north end of the holder.
They also send extra pads in case you have extra movement or play when you tighten it (aka your cd slot opening is a bit wider).
As I stated earlier, I would suggest using some firm pressure to slide the pads off of the mount, , and putting some super glue or krazy glue on them. If you use the extra pads, I would suggest probably putting a few dabs of krazy glue on them too.
They also send 3 magnets with the mount. So, I can mount my car screen, or my cell phone, or my wife can mount her cell phone to it.
So, if you have an older car like me, and your CD player is bored and begging you for something to do, you are tired of your spouse complaining because your tablet or cell phone blocks the middle vent on their side, get this mount. You won’t regret it. I know I don’t.

I typically put silicone cases on my phones (I drop them a lot), so I stuck the plate inside the case instead of on the phone itself (see pic). This works very well and I have never had a phone slip from the holder even with a charging cord attached.
Highly recommend!

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This is a charming, lightweight, beaded strap that I can use for my phone and it would also work well attached to a small wallet or cosmetic pouch. It can also be used just as a key-ring. The beading seems to be well done and the beads are lovely and of high quality. I really like the beading pattern, too. It is made up of large, pea-sized round turquoise colored beads arranged in triplets, alternating with slightly smaller oval filigree beads in silver. The turquoise beads are separated by small, flat round segmented silver beads and the filigree beads are flanked by small round silver beads. The metal hardware (swivel snap and small split key-ring) looks and feels like stainless steel. The metal is highly polished and the pieces seem very sturdy.
The cording is very strong, as mentioned in the product description. The cord has some stretch, but even so, the loop is a little too small to fit over my hand, and I don't want to force it. I do have another version of this strap made of different colored beads and it does fit easily on my wrist with no problem. When I compared the two, I could see that this one is slightly smaller in circumference, maybe by half an inch or so. As this is a hand-made product, this variability in sizing isn't too surprising. Of course, I can still use the strap and carry it in my hand. But, my daughter has a smaller hand and wrist than I do, and I thought she would really like this strap so I ended up giving it to her.
I appreciate that both a tethering tab (just a thin, flat, piece of clear plastic with a small attached D-ring serving as a loop) as well as a threaded connector are included. I prefer the threaded connector -- the thread itself is thin but very tough and it feels more secure to me. I suppose the small key-ring could also be used to attach the strap to a loop on a back-pack or bag.
The phone strap arrived nicely packaged in a sturdy clear plastic bag along with the tethering tab and threaded connector in their own small bag. The price seems reasonable and the fact that this cute strap is made in the USA is a nice plus.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
If you are serious about getting the right phone tripod mount you should read this. For such a simple device I have more to say than can fit in one review so I will keep it to the essentials, the stuff you came here to know.

PREFACE

I don’t usually start reviews like a book with a preface but if you are to know if this is the right mount to get there are some things that I would like to explain. First I am a career photographer who has traveled the world, anything from fashion to photo news. My job has nothing to do with this product but decades of using tripods with cameras has taught me how valuable they are as well as how cumbersome they are to use and the value of minimalism if you want to be good at your trade. I will talk more about the minimal design later but it is very important and shopping for one of these ended up being made a bit frustrating by the companies who sell these insisting on illustrating them with all kinds of weird microphones, humungous lights and other accessories just to make the point that they have a cold shoe. Okay, point made, it has a cold shoe. So let’s get into it in more detail.

WHAT YOU GET

What you get is simple, a surprisingly solid, almost all metal, clamp that has zero frills. If it fits your phone then it will work. It is assembled and never needs to be disassembled. There are no instructions and you don’t need any.

HOW IT IS USED

There are several schools of thought about spring load vs screw-down vs ratchet. It all boils down to the fact you are buying this to hold a phone in position on a tripod while you take pictures. You’re off to a great start because any time you have the slightest inclination that you might need to brace your phone against shaking your decision is 100% correct that you should be using a tripod. What makes this a good design is that you can use any tripod in any way you would mount a DSLR or other traditional camera. There are no swivels or tilts or anything else that moves, in fact the beauty of this mount is there are no moving parts at all other than the fastener that holds your phone in place. You attach this mount using one of two threaded holes in the metal. That’s not not sound ideal but this is a very hard metsl and the weight it needs to support is minimal so I can accept that there are no brass bushings for the threads as not being a negative. If you want to shoot landscape you use one hole and if you want to shoot portrait you use the other - all adjustments from there are made on your tripod, where they should be. I say tripod but this mount is equally at home attached to almost anything you can think of that has a standard quarter inch screw, and that’s a lot of things.

WHAT I LOVE

1. It is simple, I’m confident my thousand buck phone will stay put for any normal situation whether I orient it horizontally or vertically, no other mount is as secure as one that I know I have tightened it enough to not fall out

2. I don’t have to think about any adjustments, I either attach it one way or the other for landscape or portrait pictures.

3. The part that grips the phone is relatively soft rubber so it will squish against my phone without leaving deep marks in my eighty buck leather magsafe case. This is important because I haven’t met a spring loaded mount yet that doesn’t squeeze my phone too much, and to reiterate the point, I would never trust any ratchet design - not only don’t they grip tightly enough to keep it from slipping out, especially in vertical position, all it would take is one accidental swipe against the release button and my phone would smash to the floor.

4. If you are looking for a mount that doubles as a tripod, handgrip, selfie stick, quasi-SLR camera grip or one that will hold a dozen accessories this isn’t it and from my experience that is not the way to shop for one of these. All those things add complexity, weight, security concerns and at some point will limit you - there is never the perfect accessory gadget so why try getting a mount that locks you in to only what works with it? The one thing that attracts me on some other mounts is a removable remote shutter release but after thinking it over I decided to make my own using my favorite remote button and attaching it to a lightweight plastic cold shoe plate so I could always keep it where I can find it and if I am using my phone’s self timer I can just leave it in the mount to press the button - which is how I would most likely use it anyway.

WHAT COULD BE IMPROVED

I wrote some things about the shape of the rubber clamps then I deleted what I wrote. It’s true they seem to favor phones with rounded edges like most android phones and older iphones but the are cut in such a way that they have a firm, but not too tight, on my iPhone 14 Pro with or without the leather magsafe case. I am very sensitive about messing that case up and it is a very rare mount that doesn’t do that. This one doesn’t.

YES OR NO

You wouldn’t expect me to not give five stars to the mount that I spent weeks researching until I finally chose this one, would you? I left price entirely out of the equation since the range for various mounts is from about ten to about forty bucks. I could have spent more and in the fifteen buck range there are many other fancier options. But this is the one I will carry with me, because I trust it and that makes it the final winner.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
If you are serious about getting the right phone tripod mount you should read this. For such a simple device I have more to say than can fit in one review so I will keep it to the essentials, the stuff you came here to know.

PREFACE

I don’t usually start reviews like a book with a preface but if you are to know if this is the right mount to get there are some things that I would like to explain. First I am a career photographer who has traveled the world, anything from fashion to photo news. My job has nothing to do with this product but decades of using tripods with cameras has taught me how valuable they are as well as how cumbersome they are to use and the value of minimalism if you want to be good at your trade. I will talk more about the minimal design later but it is very important and shopping for one of these ended up being made a bit frustrating by the companies who sell these insisting on illustrating them with all kinds of weird microphones, humungous lights and other accessories just to make the point that they have a cold shoe. Okay, point made, it has a cold shoe. So let’s get into it in more detail.

WHAT YOU GET

What you get is simple, a surprisingly solid, almost all metal, clamp that has zero frills. If it fits your phone then it will work. It is assembled and never needs to be disassembled. There are no instructions and you don’t need any.

HOW IT IS USED

There are several schools of thought about spring load vs screw-down vs ratchet. It all boils down to the fact you are buying this to hold a phone in position on a tripod while you take pictures. You’re off to a great start because any time you have the slightest inclination that you might need to brace your phone against shaking your decision is 100% correct that you should be using a tripod. What makes this a good design is that you can use any tripod in any way you would mount a DSLR or other traditional camera. There are no swivels or tilts or anything else that moves, in fact the beauty of this mount is there are no moving parts at all other than the fastener that holds your phone in place. You attach this mount using one of two threaded holes in the metal. That’s not not sound ideal but this is a very hard metsl and the weight it needs to support is minimal so I can accept that there are no brass bushings for the threads as not being a negative. If you want to shoot landscape you use one hole and if you want to shoot portrait you use the other - all adjustments from there are made on your tripod, where they should be. I say tripod but this mount is equally at home attached to almost anything you can think of that has a standard quarter inch screw, and that’s a lot of things.

WHAT I LOVE

1. It is simple, I’m confident my thousand buck phone will stay put for any normal situation whether I orient it horizontally or vertically, no other mount is as secure as one that I know I have tightened it enough to not fall out

2. I don’t have to think about any adjustments, I either attach it one way or the other for landscape or portrait pictures.

3. The part that grips the phone is relatively soft rubber so it will squish against my phone without leaving deep marks in my eighty buck leather magsafe case. This is important because I haven’t met a spring loaded mount yet that doesn’t squeeze my phone too much, and to reiterate the point, I would never trust any ratchet design - not only don’t they grip tightly enough to keep it from slipping out, especially in vertical position, all it would take is one accidental swipe against the release button and my phone would smash to the floor.

4. If you are looking for a mount that doubles as a tripod, handgrip, selfie stick, quasi-SLR camera grip or one that will hold a dozen accessories this isn’t it and from my experience that is not the way to shop for one of these. All those things add complexity, weight, security concerns and at some point will limit you - there is never the perfect accessory gadget so why try getting a mount that locks you in to only what works with it? The one thing that attracts me on some other mounts is a removable remote shutter release but after thinking it over I decided to make my own using my favorite remote button and attaching it to a lightweight plastic cold shoe plate so I could always keep it where I can find it and if I am using my phone’s self timer I can just leave it in the mount to press the button - which is how I would most likely use it anyway.

WHAT COULD BE IMPROVED

I wrote some things about the shape of the rubber clamps then I deleted what I wrote. It’s true they seem to favor phones with rounded edges like most android phones and older iphones but the are cut in such a way that they have a firm, but not too tight, on my iPhone 14 Pro with or without the leather magsafe case. I am very sensitive about messing that case up and it is a very rare mount that doesn’t do that. This one doesn’t.

YES OR NO

You wouldn’t expect me to not give five stars to the mount that I spent weeks researching until I finally chose this one, would you? I left price entirely out of the equation since the range for various mounts is from about ten to about forty bucks. I could have spent more and in the fifteen buck range there are many other fancier options. But this is the one I will carry with me, because I trust it and that makes it the final winner.

However, if I need to change the phone to vertical/portrait position, I need to unscrew the phone mount and change to the screw hole on the side (see picture). Found out this mount is not good for fixing the phone in vertical position on my tripod because the panning knob of my tripod is in the way of the phone. So, I think this phone mount is good for those who use the phone mostly in 1 orientation and have a tripod with a low profile panning knob.

text: Ive had on my phone a few months & my toddler has put it through the test. It’s more natural to hold than a pop socket. I love it came with 4 & it was such a good price I was skeptical & but these exceeded my expectations! Holding a iPhone15 pro max with one hand is impossible when you have small hands & so these solved that issue. I don’t put mine directly in the middle, I put it about an inch from the side since I'm right handed & I can now scroll using 1 hand & it’s comfortable & not awkward. It also great when your hands are full you can loop it on your finger like a right so your hands free to carry, for example, your tumbler & your child is on your hip. They are as pictured color wise & the gold hardware hasn’t tarnished or faded, just a few scratches that aren’t noticeable unless you’re looking for them. I do wish they were a little wider like my last one but for the price the quality is excellent. & I can still use this with my phone holders without removing the case bc it can be pushed flat when not using. It can also be used as a stand itself if you put your phone on its side. I can fit 3 fingers through it but I just use my middle & ring finger & it fits so naturally like I would normally have my fingers placed but it gives me that assistance to use one handed. title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I’ve used Samsung’s Ultra and Note series for years, so I’m very familiar with wide, boxy phones and large displays. That’s why, when I first got the Z Fold 7, the cover screen initially felt narrow compared to what I was used to. In height it’s almost the same, but the width seemed smaller. However, this feeling only lasted a few days—once I adjusted, I realized the cover display is more than enough for everyday use. In fact, it’s very similar in size to the S25 Plus, and you can comfortably run any app on it.

The magic happens when you unfold it. The internal display is huge, immersive, and makes you forget about missing the wider Ultra screen. You can run two apps side by side, or one above the other, almost like having two phones in one. For example, you can keep your email open on one side while chatting or receiving information on the other—copying, pasting, and multitasking without constantly switching apps. You can also watch a video on one half while replying to emails, chatting on WhatsApp, or doing other tasks on the other half. It’s an unmatched experience that no regular phone can offer.

Multitasking and Apps
Multitasking on the Fold is incredible. Editing photos, playing games, or browsing is simply more fun on such a large display. Most apps are optimized because Samsung’s software is excellent, and social apps like Instagram, WhatsApp, and Facebook look fantastic. If you ever prefer a narrower aspect ratio, you can quickly switch any app to “slim mode” through the multitasking options.

Addressing the Haters’ Complaints

Under-display camera: You can enable a black bar in apps to hide the camera area, so it never gets in the way.

S Pen: While there’s no built-in S Pen slot, you can use a capacitive S Pen. By enabling “increased touch sensitivity” (especially if you use a tempered glass screen protector), it works very well for everyday use.

Battery life: After weeks of use, I can confirm the battery lasts all day. With adaptive power saving and dark mode, I’ve managed up to 10 hours of screen time on the cover screen, and 7–8 hours with mixed cover and main screen use. Heavy gaming or demanding apps bring it down to 5–6 hours, which is still solid. To preserve long-term battery health, I recommend enabling battery protection (charging to 90–95%) and avoiding letting it drop below 30%.

Cameras
For 99% of users, the cameras are more than enough. The biggest advantage is using the high-quality rear cameras for selfies or streaming, which no standard phone—including the Ultra series—can match. Plus, when taking photos of others, they can preview themselves on the cover screen. Photos, selfies, and videos are sharp and vibrant. While professionals may prefer the S25 Ultra for advanced photography, the Fold’s versatility makes it an excellent choice for almost everyone.

Final Thoughts
The Z Fold 7 is an outstanding phone. Even if you’re coming from an Ultra, it only takes a few days to adjust before you realize you don’t miss the wider display. In fact, Ultras feel bulky and brick-like compared to the Fold, which is slimmer, more comfortable to hold, and far more versatile. The cover screen is fully usable for everyday apps, and when you want something larger, unfolding gives you a massive display that no traditional phone can match.

I don’t regret switching at all—this is easily one of the best devices I’ve ever used, and I highly recommend it.

I respond to emails and texts but I don't use it as a work center. I play quick games or watch tik tok or other simple apps. I watch videos in bed while my wife is watching home improvement shows on tv.. If you do more or want more this review might not help you. I dont care if a certain z fold opens an app .33 seconds quicker than another. I am always by an outlet so I don't care if a certain z fold stays charged MUCH longer than another. I love the bigger screen that the fold series offer. Now. I jumped into the z fold world at z fold 4. Here are some real problems with the z fold 4 TODAY. FIRST you are going to get a used zfold. Battery life will be an issue because it's older. BUT IF all you want is what I use it for it's a great phone. Yes it's thicker than a zfold 7 yes the screen is smaller BUT it's much less expensive and will give you the same results as a z7 at a much cheaper price. SO YOURE ASKING WHY DID I BUY A Z7 THEN. GOOD QUESTION. I had 2 z4s and what really bothered me is that the hinges will at some point fail and the phone won't open all the way. A zfold should open 180 degrees a straight line. I owned 2 z4s and after a while both hinges stopped opening all the way up. More like 175+degrees. My research showed that this was a problem with the z fold 4 5 and 6. Right now if you're new to the zfold world and you are going to use it like I DO I recommend the z4. Yes it's thicker, the battery won't last all day if you stay on YouTube or tik tok but for the price I think the z4 is great entry point. As far as battery life I Can't say better battery life on the z7 because it's newer. Not a fare comparison But I'm happy with it for now. If you have had a chance to handle a z series and like it and want to committed definitely the z7. If you're on the fence and don't or can't drop this kind of money the z4 is a great buy.

The phone is super sleek, I love how small it is when it folds up. I am easily able to fit it in my pocket or in one of my smaller purses. Even though it's thin, it has some weight to it, especially after adding a case.

It is way faster than my previous phone. There is no lag and there has been zero issues with freezing up. The camera quality is fantastic and the video recording is very crisp and steady. I love that I can also unlock it with either my fingerprint or my face.

I also love how customizable samsung is! There is so much that I can do on this one that apple is nowhere near even touching. I am constantly discovering new features that improve how I use my phone. And I love that I can actually set custom ringtones and text sounds, unlike apple lol.

I have also not had any screen issues at all. I've dropped it and slammed it shut more than I would have liked but it's still going strong! There is also a small crease where it folds of course, but it is not noticeable at all when the screen is turned on.

The only Con that I have with this phone is the battery doesn't last as long as my iphone did. I have it set to stop charging at 90% to protect the battery and I usually charge it overnight. If I don't mess with it too much during the day, the battery will definitely last. However if i play my games or watch videos for an extended period I do have to charge it 2x a day.

While there are some things I do miss about apple, mainly apple maps, I feel like my overall experience with the flip7 is way more pleasant and the OS functions way faster/better. This phone is def worth the price tag that comes with it.

text:
Updated Jan 2026 -

So 6 months later, I had to replace the screen protector. I still think it's great, but having been through lots of travel, lots gym bags, scratches do show up on this a bit more than non-anti-glare screen protectors since it's literally taking off that anti-glare layer so I ended up with a scratches that are brighter than the screen itself. It did take 6 months for it show enough to bother me, so I'd say that's a fairly good performance and durability to me. Thankfully, it did come with two pieces so I was ready. I ordered another set for when I have to do it again. Pity that Samsung.com actually has better pricing for it than Amazon the 2nd time around so I ordered from there instead.

Original review - 6/2025
Having experienced the anti-glare coating of the S25, I found this basically fills that glaring (pun intended) lack of this feature on the Z Fold 7. The application process is fairly good and aligns the protector properly along all edges. Yes, it does initially leaves a line across the middle of the screen, but it disappears within a couple of days, one day for me. The anti-glare properties of this protector is amazing without adding the frosting affects of many other generic anti-glare films. It keeps the glossy finish and doesn't reduce light transmission of the screen so you don't feel like you're sacrificing the beautiful qualify of the screen to get the anti-glare affect. Keep in mind that this protect covers the glass much further towards the edge of the glass, so many cases may not work with this. I had to modify my clear Elago case (with a Dremel) to avoid lifting at the corner edges. A reasonable compromise for me, but YMMV.

I would MUCH rather just have the same Gorilla Armor 2 that's on the S25 Ultra on my Z Fold7... that way I would get the same kind of glass ceramic cover screen but then a permanent anti-reflective coating instead of a cheap film. But no.

The AR effect on the film is actually really good though (WAY better than Zagg's XTR4 anti-reflective whatever they're using). So good that the increased contrast makes fingerprints MUCH more visible. This is kind of annoying, but they do at least clean away fairly easily. If you have swipe navigation turned on, you will likely feel the edge of the film on the sides when using the back gesture. I'd also really prefer the film cover the selfie camera - holes and cutouts in screen protectors tend to just gather dust and debris.

The install was fine - though as well as the alignment tray works, neither of the two included films were actually centered. Both ended up just a tiny bit to the right (maybe 0.1, 0.2 mm?). It's not bad, but still a "can't unsee it" thing. And since both of them did it, seems like it's an alignment issue. No issues with the split install though. Yes, there's a visible line right after the install - but it does go away within a few hours.

Overall, I'm glad there are two films in the box, but I'd still just rather the phone be anti-reflective from the factory. Or at least offer a tempered glass option.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Review for: Anti-reflective Fold 7 Screen Protector

I'm not sure what's up with the review grouping on these listings but the Fold 7's antireflective film here is GOOD. Most poor reviews seem to be for the cases here but the film is fine. I love it much more than the Fold 6's.

The pack comes with two, which is good, because if you take too long and get something under it and mess up your first (like me) you can try again. The alignment tool is very solid and very precise, I got my film aligned perfectly and there's less than half a millimeter uncovered on each side so it really is a full-coverage protector. There's so little left that you can hardly tell you have a film on at all. The film will have a middle-crease when it's applied but that'll vanish overnight. Another bonus here is that the Fold 7, despite being almost concerningly thin already, has a very slightly recessed outer screen and this film sits in that perfectly. This makes the screen protector less likely to catch on cases or your fingers at the edge. Finger-feel is a little stickier than the smooth glide of the bare screen but that's not a big con for me personally. I had my Fold7 and Fold6 side by side before trade-in and saw that the F7's film seems to block just a little more light than last year's version too. Great stuff! Wish it was like $10-12 because I want another set just in case but $18 for two is not too terribly steep for the quality you get. Just be careful that nothing gets under it.

Also, the ring bends out of shape very easily. The installation was easy, the hinge of the case feels solid and the case hugs the phone for a secure fit. The sensitivity of the screen protector seems a little low so I sometimes have to press screen buttons harder than normal to get it to respond. The phone already has a significant tile when laid down due to the camera sticking out, and the case extends the camera even more. Good protection for the lenses but decently more of a trade off instead of a solution. Also, the color of the gold is closer to rose gold. I don't care for it and don't trust the strength and integrity of the case so will be returning it. It does allow for wireless charging, but because the magnet is weak I have more than once knocked the phone off the charger accidentally, which never happened with the case I had on my Z-fold6.

The offer includes three tempered glass protectors for the screen and three camera lens protectors, along with a simple alignment frame and cleaning kits.

Installation was straightforward—thanks to the included frame, I was able to line everything up perfectly without bubbles or dust. Once applied, the protector feels smooth to the touch, and I barely notice it’s there.

In terms of performance, the screen protector maintains the phone’s clarity and brightness.

Touch sensitivity is excellent, so I don’t experience lag or reduced responsiveness.

The oleophobic coating does a good job reducing fingerprints and smudges, which keeps the screen looking clean longer.

The camera lens protectors are also clear and don’t interfere with picture quality. I’ve dropped my phone once since applying it, and the protector took the impact without any damage to the screen underneath.

The only minor issue I noticed is that aligning the protector requires a bit of patience to get it perfectly straight, even with the installation frame.

Also, while it’s marketed as case-friendly, some bulkier cases might press against the edges, though mine fit without problems.

Given that it comes with three sets, I feel reassured that if one gets cracked, I can easily replace it without buying another kit.

Pros:

✅ Includes 3 screen protectors and 3 camera lens protectors
✅ Easy installation with alignment frame and cleaning kits
✅ Maintains screen clarity and touch sensitivity
✅ Effective fingerprint and smudge resistance
✅ Good value for the price with spares included

Cons:

❌ Alignment can take some patience
❌ May fit tightly with certain bulkier phone cases

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Straight to the point. What I've experienced and a tip or two, I also do not use the belt clip as I'm exposed to heat constantly

I do baby my device, and am as careful as possible so milage may vary depending on how you are with yours and potentially your work inviroment

1. Absolutely solid - I am a restaurant cook and I have hit this phone on a plenty of edges, case always stands up.

2. DROP PROTECTION. It has held up nicely to cement. I have NOT dropped it from say general POCKET height but it has taken some tumbles

3. HINGE PROTECTION. This has not scratched my hinge at all. Albeit dust does build up from pocket lint, just blowing it out works just fine.

4. SCRATCH RESISTANCE - Again, this thing has kissed the pavement quite a few times. Has a few dings and scratches but, that is the point of the case, the phone it's self is not eating that damage :)

This way that tape can stick over the stylis, where only the butter edges of the tape are sticky so that the stylis can be both held in place, and be removable. Kind of like a little sleeve. I don’t leave many negative Amazon reviews, but when I do, it’s because a product genuinely failed.
I’ve installed inner screen protectors on previous Samsung Fold phones, so I’m familiar with the process. Unfortunately, the Fotbor [2 Pack] inner screen protector for the Samsung Fold 6 is poorly designed and extremely unforgiving.
Most inner screen protectors I’ve used in the past include some type of alignment guide to ensure proper placement. This one does not, which already makes installation more difficult than necessary.
I scanned the QR code, watched the YouTube installation video, and followed the instructions exactly. I cleaned the screen with the provided wet wipe, dried it as instructed, placed the protector, and used the squeegee while peeling back the backing paper.
After finishing, I noticed something felt off. The backing paper felt heavier than it should have. That’s when I realized that when I pulled the tabs, the screen protector came off with the backing paper. First protector ruined.
I tried again with the second protector, carefully following the instructions step by step while watching the video. Unfortunately, the second attempt failed as well.
Both screen protectors were wasted due to poor design and lack of proper installation support. For the price, this is unacceptable.
I do not recommend this product. Save your money and choose an inner screen protector with a proper alignment system.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I've tried several Fold 6 cases, and this one was my favorite. My needs were a case that was slim, didn't shift around, and had magsafe. This case covers my needs better than any other.

I have the version without the SPen holder, as on the Fold 5 Torras case, it obstructed the fingerprint reader. Maybe it's better on the Fold 6 case, but I wasn't going to risk it and add more bulk to the case.

The fit is nice and slim while seemingly providing good coverage. The hinge is unprotected, but that is desired. The case comes as two separate pieces for the front and back. I've had other cases where the front and back covers are connected with their own hinges at the top and bottom. I like that design and I feel this case would have benefitted from it. Also I would have liked the volume buttons to be covered.

The case is held on very tight. This is because it has anchor points that stick in the speaker holes. I noticed a very slight reduction in sound quality, but it's nothing that would negatively affect daily use, and I use headphones when I care about sound quality anyway. This is a wonderful trade off in my opinion, when the alternative is needing adhesive to hold the case on.

The magsafe functionality is great. It's slightly stronger than other Fold cases I've used, and it works well here because of the extra tight case fit.

My biggest complaint with the Torras Fold 5 case was that the hinge side of the front cover snapped in just a few months. There's no telling how that will hold up yet, but it does seem strong on the Fold 6 case, and it doesn't wobble around like a rubber band, as other Fold cases do on the hinge side.

The provided screen protector is not great. It's too small, as is visible in the provided picture. If it comes with a case, the screen protector should fit the case perfectly. However, it was easy to install with no bubbles.

If the front case doesn't break in a few months, and the screen protector actually fit the screen, this would absolutely be a 5 star review and worth the high cost.

UPDATE AFTER 7 MONTHS:
The front case ended up breaking on the top left corner. This was a bummer, but I contacted support and they were able to replace it. For such great customer service, I think it's worth upgrading to 5 stars.

title: 1.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I've applied my own screen protectors on many phones throughout my life. Hard, tempered glass screen protectors and soft, "self-healing" ones that require liquids and squeegees and the whole nine yards. Never have I encountered an experience as frustrating as this. Not because it's terribly hard to follow the instructions. They're pretty simple to follow. It's because I found it impossible to avoid lines and creases in the screen protector.
I went through all 3 inner screen protectors and all 3 got creases in the film. On the 3rd, I nearly got it without but in order to do that, you need to apply it in one smooth motion- no stopping to squeege the air bubbles out. The plastic over the adhesive side got caught in the gap around the edges of my screen, so I ended up with a crease and lots of air bubbles that won't go away. Including some big ones near the spine.
I'll be asking for a refund, as I am not satisfied at all. If I could've manages applying just one, I would have been fine but all 3 failed.
Also, if you use the S Pen, this screen protector feels like plastic under your pen. It feels just like a window cling vinyl.

text:
I've applied my own screen protectors on many phones throughout my life. Hard, tempered glass screen protectors and soft, "self-healing" ones that require liquids and squeegees and the whole nine yards. Never have I encountered an experience as frustrating as this. Not because it's terribly hard to follow the instructions. They're pretty simple to follow. It's because I found it impossible to avoid lines and creases in the screen protector.
I went through all 3 inner screen protectors and all 3 got creases in the film. On the 3rd, I nearly got it without but in order to do that, you need to apply it in one smooth motion- no stopping to squeege the air bubbles out. The plastic over the adhesive side got caught in the gap around the edges of my screen, so I ended up with a crease and lots of air bubbles that won't go away. Including some big ones near the spine.
I'll be asking for a refund, as I am not satisfied at all. If I could've manages applying just one, I would have been fine but all 3 failed.
Also, if you use the S Pen, this screen protector feels like plastic under your pen. It feels just like a window cling vinyl.

text:
I had a different case before this one, but I'm glad the old one cracked, forcing me to buy a new one.
This Maxdara case is great:

* It fits well.
* It has a kickstand that increases the case's thickness, which helps to lower the back camera rings.
* The pen slot works great and the pen fits well.
* The front case is especially well-designed. The edges where you swipe for the Android menu are tapered lower, regardless of the orientation.
* I don't think the front glass is real glass, but regardless, it's very clear and provides rigidity to the frame.
* The only downside, and this is a minor one, is the double-sided tape for the back cover (not the front) of the case. You have to peel it off manually, stick it on, and then peel off the other side. I wish they had done this for us so we only had to peel it once.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I have lived through the evolution of cell phones. From the early car briefcases to the clunky flips to the sleek smart phones and now the foldables. I love my ZFold5 and no longer use a phone enough to keep up with regular model updates. When the center of my TPU inner screen protector started lifting, wrinkling, and making crackling noises when folding, I started looking at new phones and realized I didn't want to pay for a new phone when mine still functioned. But I winced at past memories of trying to replace screen protectors - bubbles, misaligned - it never seemed to come out right. So I turned to Google and found that you could replace the inner screen protector and not only that, they now had kits that did everything but stick it on the phone for you!

This kit was amazing. First you put down a rubber anti-skid mat and then put down a plastic tray that conforms exactly to the shape of the phone (with cutouts for the cameras). Rip the old TPU screen protector off (push a fingernail under the center and work along the edge to loosen a corner and slowly pull it off). Note, any phone cause you have added needs to be removed. Take this opportunity to use alcohol wipes, etc to completely clean the outside of your phone (dust, old adhesive, etc). Some of the Zfold Samsung cases are held on with double sided tape. Removing the case might destroy the tape, but it will not hurt the phone or the case. Just use some alcohol wipes and the adhesive remains will come off both the phone and the case. Have some double sided adhesive ready if you need it (I think I used 3mm wide tape - I have the Samsung brand case with the stylus pen built in the back, not the spine).

The phone slots perfectly into the tray. Use the included wipes and soft microfiber cloths to completely clean the face of your phone. The new TPU screen protector snaps on to guide posts on the tray ensuring a perfect alignment. There are detailed instructions along with a QRC code for a video instruction (very helpful). You lift one side of the new screen protector at a 120 deg angle (the center is split) and use the included hard plastic spatula (one edge is cushioned) and push the screen protector across the phone. Next, lift the other side and smooth it across making sure to flatten any bubbles in the middle. Finally, you attach one of the removal stickers to a corner and then lift off the TPU screen protector cover and you are done.

There were very few bubbles and those disappeared by the next morning. The TPU film stuck firmly and due to the guide posts there is no need to struggle with alignment. My stylus just glides beautifully now! The only complaint I have had is some stactic, the screen protector attracting dust, this should subside with time.

At ~$20, the kit is more expensive than most, including only one inner and one outer TPU screen protector and no camera covers. However, you also get the anti-slip mat, alignment tray (works for inner and outer screen protector replacement), four screen cleaner wipes, two small microfiber cloths, stickers to remove dust, spatula, and tapes to remove the final cover off of the TPU screen protector. But, most importantly, it works and is of a high quality. As you can see in the picture, it is perfectly smooth with only a couple tiny bubbles remaining and some dust due to static.

text:
My perfect case, finally. I've been searching for a clear sparkle case since before I got my fold8. I ordered it the minute I found it and its even better than I would have gone for.

Pros: hinge cover which I didn't have before and feel so much safer now with it (after just spilling coffee on the hinge last week). Durable, mindful cut outs. This fits with camera protectors (tightly and you might have to redo them with the case in hand). The full body screen really is better, just so much more durable and no flimsy front edge frames (those flimsy front edge fames on other cases break). It is a beautiful clear sparkle case, I bought the special fold8 color cause I love it and this is exactly how I want to show it off.

Mag Safe note: be warned. This has the full camera surround. It is not compatible will all magsafe products. The camera 'bump' forces misalignment to the magnet for a LOT of accessories. My rectangle wireless chargers are not compatible with this case (but circle ones are). My car mount works on my wallets outter magsafe, but not with the case; back to wired charging there.

Cons: the sparkle is also in the screen protection part of the body. Assuming it makes for a more solid body, seamless product. It was a bit odd at first but after only a day of use I stopped noticing it entirely. I'll take the extra protection and durability and just fold open the phone when im watching something as I already do.

Mag Safe note: be warned. This has the full camera surround. It is not compatible will all magsafe products. The camera 'bump' forces misalignment to the magnet for a LOT of accessories. Good news is, just search for the right accessories. I have an offset magsafe wallet that is PERFECT for this case. Works exactly as needed. My rectangle wireless chargers are not compatible with this case (but circle ones are). My car mount works on my wallets outter magsafe, but not with the case; back to wired charging there.

Cons: the sparkle is also in the screen protection part of the body. Assuming it makes for a more solid body, seamless product. It was a bit odd at first but after only a day of use I stopped noticing it entirely. I'll take the extra protection and durability and just fold open the phone when im watching something as I already do.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
My perfect case, finally. I've been searching for a clear sparkle case since before I got my fold8. I ordered it the minute I found it and its even better than I would have gone for.

Pros: hinge cover which I didn't have before and feel so much safer now with it (after just spilling coffee on the hinge last week). Durable, mindful cut outs. This fits with camera protectors (tightly and you might have to redo them with the case in hand). The full body screen really is better, just so much more durable and no flimsy front edge frames (those flimsy front edge fames on other cases break). The magsafe magnet is strong and doesn't fail with my double magsafe set up for my car set up. It is a beautiful clear sparkle case, I bought the special fold8 color cause I love it and this is exactly how I want to show it off.

Mag Safe note: be warned. This has the full camera surround. It is not compatible will all magsafe products. The camera 'bump' forces misalignment to the magnet for a LOT of accessories. Good news is, just search for the right accessories. I have an offset magsafe wallet that is PERFECT for this case. Works exactly as needed. My rectangle wireless chargers are not compatible with this case (but circle ones are). My car mount works on my wallets outter magsafe, but not with the case; back to wired charging there.

Cons: the sparkle is also in the screen protection part of the body. Assuming it makes for a more solid body, seamless product. It was a bit odd at first but after only a day of use I stopped noticing it entirely. I'll take the extra protection and durability and just fold open the phone when im watching something as I already do.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
When I get a new phone, I usually go for a liquid screen protector instead of glass ones. The glass versions never seem to register my touch properly, while the liquid ones have saved me more than once. I’ve taken a few falls, and even cracked the glass on my camera once, but the phone screen itself never got a scratch from those drops. Pretty impressive. Over time, I did end up with some hairline scratches on the screen, so they’re not perfect, but overall the liquid protectors did a really solid job, just not what I wanted this time around. The biggest drawback is that they need hours to set, which means leaving your phone untouched overnight or longer. That’s not easy when your whole life is on your phone like mine. So, with my new Pixel 10, I decided to try a protector that applied more like a sticker.

This case caught my eye because it included that type of protector, and the instructions (plus the installation videos) were clear and helpful. I’ve been applying screen protectors for over 15 years, but it’s still nice to have a quick refresher, especially when using a new brand.

I did have one hiccup. When I pulled the tab off the screen protector, only the tab came off, not the adhesive covering the sticky side. For a minute, I thought it was the type that just rests on the glass and is held in place by the case, which was frustrating. I even started trying to clean off the tab residue and almost reached for the Goo Gone. Luckily, I noticed a faint line that suggested there really was adhesive to peel. It took some careful finessing (and double-checking the video) before I got it off properly. Once I did, the application went smoothly. Watching the protector adhere when you run your finger down the middle is oddly satisfying. I used my driver’s license to press out bubbles and make sure it was even, but any card works, and if you don’t have one handy, fingers will do the trick.

Getting my phone into the case itself took a little force, which I actually like. It feels secure, and I know it won’t slip out even if (realistically, when) I drop it.

I’m really glad I bought this. Great product for my new Pixel 10!

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
When I get a new phone, I usually go for a liquid screen protector instead of glass ones. The glass versions never seem to register my touch properly, while the liquid ones have saved me more than once. I’ve taken a few falls, and even cracked the glass on my camera once, but the phone screen itself never got a scratch from those drops. Pretty impressive. Over time, I did end up with some hairline scratches on the screen, so they’re not perfect, but overall the liquid protectors did a really solid job, just not what I wanted this time around. The biggest drawback is that they need hours to set, which means leaving your phone untouched overnight or longer. That’s not easy when your whole life is on your phone like mine. So, with my new Pixel 10, I decided to try a protector that applied more like a sticker.

This case caught my eye because it included that type of protector, and the instructions (plus the installation videos) were clear and helpful. I’ve been applying screen protectors for over 15 years, but it’s still nice to have a quick refresher, especially when using a new brand.

I did have one hiccup. When I pulled the tab off the screen protector, only the tab came off, not the adhesive covering the sticky side. For a minute, I thought it was the type that just rests on the glass and is held in place by the case, which was frustrating. I even started trying to clean off the tab residue and almost reached for the Goo Gone. Luckily, I noticed a faint line that suggested there really was adhesive to peel. It took some careful finessing (and double-checking the video) before I got it off properly. Once I did, the application went smoothly. Watching the protector adhere when you run your finger down the middle is oddly satisfying. I used my driver’s license to press out bubbles and make sure it was even, but any card works, and if you don’t have one handy, fingers will do the trick.

Getting my phone into the case itself took a little force, which I actually like. It feels secure, and I know it won’t slip out even if (realistically, when) I drop it.

I’m really glad I bought this. Great product for my new Pixel 10!

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
When I get a new phone, I usually go for a liquid screen protector instead of glass ones. The glass versions never seem to register my touch properly, while the liquid ones have saved me more than once. I’ve taken a few falls, and even cracked the glass on my camera once, but the phone screen itself never got a scratch from those drops. Pretty impressive. Over time, I did end up with some hairline scratches on the screen, so they’re not perfect, but overall the liquid protectors did a really solid job, just not what I wanted this time around. The biggest drawback is that they need hours to set, which means leaving your phone untouched overnight or longer. That’s not easy when your whole life is on your phone like mine. So, with my new Pixel 10, I decided to try a protector that applied more like a sticker.

This case caught my eye because it included that type of protector, and the instructions (plus the installation videos) were clear and helpful. I’ve been applying screen protectors for over 15 years, but it’s still nice to have a quick refresher, especially when using a new brand.

I did have one hiccup. When I pulled the tab off the screen protector, only the tab came off, not the adhesive covering the sticky side. For a minute, I thought it was the type that just rests on the glass and is held in place by the case, which was frustrating. I even started trying to clean off the tab residue and almost reached for the Goo Gone. Luckily, I noticed a faint line that suggested there really was adhesive to peel. It took some careful finessing (and double-checking the video) before I got it off properly. Once I did, the application went smoothly. Watching the protector adhere when you run your finger down the middle is oddly satisfying. I used my driver’s license to press out bubbles and make sure it was even, but any card works, and if you don’t have one handy, fingers will do the trick.

Getting my phone into the case itself took a little force, which I actually like. It feels secure, and I know it won’t slip out even if (realistically, when) I drop it.

I’m really glad I bought this. Great product for my new Pixel 10!

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
When I get a new phone, I usually go for a liquid screen protector instead of glass ones. The glass versions never seem to register my touch properly, while the liquid ones have saved me more than once. I’ve taken a few falls, and even cracked the glass on my camera once, but the phone screen itself never got a scratch from those drops. Pretty impressive. Over time, I did end up with some hairline scratches on the screen, so they’re not perfect, but overall the liquid protectors did a really solid job, just not what I wanted this time around. The biggest drawback is that they need hours to set, which means leaving your phone untouched overnight or longer. That’s not easy when your whole life is on your phone like mine. So, with my new Pixel 10, I decided to try a protector that applied more like a sticker.

This case caught my eye because it included that type of protector, and the instructions (plus the installation videos) were clear and helpful. I’ve been applying screen protectors for over 15 years, but it’s still nice to have a quick refresher, especially when using a new brand.

I did have one hiccup. When I pulled the tab off the screen protector, only the tab came off, not the adhesive covering the sticky side. For a minute, I thought it was the type that just rests on the glass and is held in place by the case, which was frustrating. I even started trying to clean off the tab residue and almost reached for the Goo Gone. Luckily, I noticed a faint line that suggested there really was adhesive to peel. It took some careful finessing (and double-checking the video) before I got it off properly. Once I did, the application went smoothly. Watching the protector adhere when you run your finger down the middle is oddly satisfying. I used my driver’s license to press out bubbles and make sure it was even, but any card works, and if you don’t have one handy, fingers will do the trick.

Getting my phone into the case itself took a little force, which I actually like. It feels secure, and I know it won’t slip out even if (realistically, when) I drop it.

I’m really glad I bought this. Great product for my new Pixel 10!

For a minute, I thought it was the type that just rests on the glass and is held in place by the case, which was frustrating. I even started trying to clean off the tab residue and almost reached for the Goo Gone. Luckily, I noticed a faint line that suggested there really was adhesive to peel. It took some careful finessing (and double-checking the video) before I got it off properly. Once I did, the application went smoothly. Watching the protector adhere when you run your finger down the middle is oddly satisfying. I used my driver’s license to press out bubbles and make sure it was even, but any card works, and if you don’t have one handy, fingers will do the trick.

Getting my phone into the case itself took a little force, which I actually like. It feels secure, and I know it won’t slip out even if (realistically, when) I drop it.

I’m really glad I bought this. Great product for my new Pixel 10!

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text: Cases are subjective and it depends on what you are after for your zfold4 so I will try to give my fair assessment of this product. If you are looking for a minimal case to prevent scratches and marks during daily use, and if your are careful with your phones - this is a perfect case. The case back "is" leather but not your typical what you'd think or expect (Samsung actually states this is the real deal and not vegan or faux leather) - the front piece is plastic. Fitment is excellent and yes, you'll have to use the tape for the front cover to ensure everything stays tight (back cover does not use or need tape). I have no need for the s pen, if you do then this case is probably not for you. I have purchased half a dozen high dollar cases for this phone and have been disappointed in all of them becuase of one or more failures in functionality or design (too thick, can't wireless charge, sloppy fitment, built in screen protector, erratic hinge protection movement, cheap feeling, and the list goes on) - this is the first case that meets most of my criteria. That is the true problem with this phone, you have to prioritize your needs from an accessory standpoint. I happen to like minimal cases to keep an already bulky phone in check. My only gripe so far is the price is a bit absurd but the zfold4 is the fancy new flagship phone so accessories are always going to be a premium. If you are going to swap cases a lot, I can see a couple of potential issues with this case - 1. You'll need to be careful removing the front cover after initial install as the tape is quite strong and you could break the front portion. 2. I don't know how well the tape holds up after multiple swaps. 3. How the leather holds up - only time will tell.

title: 3.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Updated:
After using this screen protector for a day, I noticed my eyes were getting really fatigued whenever I look at my screen. Then I noticed there are faint diagonal lines all over my front screen when viewed through the screen protector, making my front screen look striped wherever the screen is white. The lines are not visible when the screen is any other color than white. I figured that was what was making my eyes tired, fighting to read my screen through the fuzzy "floating" diagonal lines. I looked this phenomenon up on Google and discovered that the lines are cause by bad die-cutting alignment on the screen protector. Removing the protector eliminated the issue. I tried the second protector in the package in case the first one was defective, and the same issue ensued. It may not bother some people, but the lines really tire my eyes out and drive me crazy, so, unfortunately, I cannot use these screen protectors. I have since switched to another brand of anti-spy screen protector and do not have this issue with the other brand, while retaining comparable or slightly better anti-spy capabilities.

Original:
I've installed many screen protectors over the years. This one is the easiest installation with the best fit for the intended device that I've come across. The screen protector seems to be made of high quality materials, and the installation was perfect and bubble free on the first try. Privacy function works as it should though the angle is closer to 60% before the screen is completely dark and no letters can be made out. The fit is excellent - allowing me to place a cover over my phone without the corners of the protector detaching from the screen while no part of the screen is exposed. The camera cutout is perfect, with about 1mm buffer all around the front screen camera aperture. I haven't dropped my phone yet, but so far I'm impressed. If my opinions change in the future concerning the durability or quality of this screen protector, I will come back and update this review.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text: Like many others, I bought the Samsung cover for the Fold 4, only to have the thin rail on the front cover break. Don't waste a moment of your time trying to fix it and DO NOT waste your money on another one from Samsung. This comes with a rear and front cover that is a perfect match for the Samsung cover. Differences are... the rear cover does not have a place to hold the pen/kickstand. The front cover is a much stronger and clearly better design. The rail is thicker and the entire front cover is held together with a good screen protector. There were no real instructions, so... Give your screen a good cleaning. I use the Screen Mom product for all my screens. It works great. Make sure to clean the metal frame with a little alcohol on a soft rag where the cover's rail will be attached with the thin sticky tape that is pre-installed on it. Once it's all cleaned and dry, peel the protective layer off that thin tape on the side rail. Then peel off both large protective layers from the screen protector. Then carefully snap it into place and smooth out any bubbles (I had none, it went on beautifully). One big plus for me is that my phone screen was incredibly sensitive even with the touch sensitivity set to minimum. This added just the right amount to touch "resistance" to make it perfect. Each press and swipe is perfectly controlled and responsive. If you don't have the pen or kickstand or don't have a cover then install the back cover too. In my case, probably like a lot of other people, I was only searching for a replacement for the broken front cover. I looked at so many of these that my head was spinning. Thank goodness some other people gave good reviews for this as a replacement. I'm adding my review to theirs. It's a great solution. The only addition it could use is if the manufacturer added the pen holder/kickstand, but I am very happy with this solution. I hope this helps others to make a good, informed decision.

text:
So far I'm very impressed with this case. I wanted something that would offer good protection for my Fold7 - as I don't have a great record when it comes to not dropping my phones - and this case delivers. It offers very good protection for the hinge area and the back of the phone and is one of the best options I've seen for the front screen and its bezels as well.

The case is made from thick composite material that feels sleek and yet not slippery. The phone's camera is surrounded by a raised ridge which should safeguard the lenses if the phone is dropped. All the cutouts are precise and perfectly match the Galaxy Z Fold7's shape.

The magnet in the case is strong and despite the thickness of the plastic I have no issues using wireless chargers with it (that is, as long as they don't interfere with the phone's camera bump, which is definitely an issue, but not the case's fault).

The phone's hinge is well protected and fully covered by a thick flap. I'm impressed that the manufacturer actually used high quality spring-loaded hinges to attach that section - I've seen other cases just relying on a thin plastic piece as a hinge. This feels very nice, works great and should be quite durable.

Built into the hinge there is a folding kickstand. It works well when the phone is opened up, both in portrait and landscape orientations, but unfortunately it is not usable when the phone is closed. The kickstand has a pretty strong retaining clip and whenever I open it up, it feels like I'm about to break something. I'm hoping that it will smooth out with use.

The front of the case is a separate piece that attaches to the external screen of the phone. This case comes with an integrated screen protector - I was a bit apprehensive about this option, but it actually works perfectly - no issues with touch sensitivity or anything else - it's just like an edge to edge screen protector. The added bonus of this design is that the frame that on most cases attaches with only a strip of adhesive tape, here gets the additional strength from the adhesion of the protector. My only concern about this design is that if you break the screen protector, the whole front of the case would have to be replaced.

Overall, if you are looking for a protective case for the Galaxy Z Fold7, this is a very nice option. The materials feel great, functionality is very good and the case feels secure. The negatives are that the case adds a lot of bulk to the phone, the kick stand could be improved and that at least at the time of my order, this case is very expensive, putting it in direct competition with offers from well known and respected brands.

text:
When initially trying to remove blue films, one film would not come off and required a bit of force and scratching at to actually get it off, which i did not like.

The durability of the stand is not great if you like to use your phone in landscape mode (on it's side). The jackstand hinge on mine has already broken because of frequent use in that way. This is why it's a 3 star rating.

For context as for what is broken, the side where the hinge enters the spine of the case is cracked which makes the stand lose it's rigidity when it's in landscape mode, further the metal pad that it seems connected to is wobly and loose in it's seating, adding to the instability. Keep in mind when i have my phone like this I'm usually not touching it directly so this is the result of the phone's own weight and time, which has only been a few weeks of what I'd call standard use.

If you like to use your phone in portrait mode, the stand should be fine. I don't use it like that because it denies access to the charging port and imo less good for viewing, especially if you like to game on the phone.

The overall protection so far has been living up to normal life, though I don't exactly try to be reckless with my phone even with a case. The fact the stand connects with a clip is also nice to keep it snug to the spine. No dangling or weird snagging because of it.

Side note, if you were for some reason hoping the case would get rid of.the flat wobble, let me dash those hopes by informing you the spine of the case is far too large for that and it becomes a seesaw.

title: 3.0 out of 5 stars
text:
It works well as a case while protecting the hinge. I also appreciate the full body length kickstand. A very innovative solution that results in a sturdy stance without room to wobble.

There are two faults that are, unfortunately, deal breakers if I were to buy it again:
- The hinge protector prevents wireless charging while unfolded in the case where your charger would expect the phone to be flat. However, that's something I should've recognized before purchasing, as it's not a design flaw.
- I wish it didn't have the built in screen protector. I removed the one I already had, that was a far better quality one, because the case can't go over it. However the screen protector is attached to the front frame piece. This piece is secured to the front screen fold with some adhesive pads. However, these pads only do a subpar job of keeping the frame secured. And an unfortunate side effect of that is that the front frame will raise the screen protector, and allow dust to collect under the screen. That's not a problem you can solve with an alcohol wipe, because it's the inside of the screen protector, which needs to be pristine.

I have to do routine farm chores, so perhaps this won't issue won't apply to everyone, but it sure is annoying. I believe I will try and remove the screen protector from the frame some how, and reapply my old one, to allow them to move independently, and prevent the protector from raising to allow future dust.

text:
To start off the case fits the phone just right. Not so tight that you have to force it, not loose that it rattles, overall a good protective case. The privacy feature is nice but doesnt darken the screen nearly as much as I anticipated. It does however blur any text but any shapes or photos are somewhat visible.

If you have a "Claw" style mount that clamps your phone in, this case will be useless just a heads up.

I have some issues with the design however.
To start off with, the screen side of the case is independent from the rear and spine. It does have an adhesive strip that will stick to the edge of the screen but it's not strong enough. I am constantly having to adjust the screen side of the case as a result. Nothing falls off but that feeling of it not being straight drives me insane sometimes.
As for the metal attachment on the back. It states that it will work with magnetic mounts, and it technically does, however the metal is not large enough for the three different mounts I have tested it with. It doesnt fall off but for instance if you're taking an on or off ramp from a freeway the phone will rotate on the magnet. I believe this is due to the size and quality of the material. Frustrating to say the least.

Overall it will protect you phone but it's not worth the $30 price I paid.

**UPDATE**

After a month of use the rotating stand/magnet has become loose and unusable. This causes the phone to fall off the magnetic base constantly. The finish is peeling/chipping off also. Not worth the money at all

title: 2.0 out of 5 stars
text: I've used makavo phone cases for a wide variety of devices over the years and they're nice and simplistic and get the job done without breaking the bank and they've never failed with providing drop protection. I'm sure this phone case would have done exactly the same however the hinge connections on this phone case are well problematic. It's a flexible TPU style hinge that connects the front and back of the phone case together and in practice in theory it should work just fine. However the material used here for the hinge is well a bit too stiff and it pulls on the phone case away from the hinge leaving the edge of the screen and the hinge itself more exposed than it should be. This creates a lip and the phone case flops around a little bit on that edge of the screen making it hard to do any kind of edge gestures or swiping and at the same time has a tendency to push on any screen protectors due to it not being as secure or stiff of a material. If you can get past that then the phone case is relatively fine however there are certain design elements on it that are just obnoxious. The camera and Flash protection lip being the biggest offender in my honest opinion. It's a perfect example of trying to be different but going too far and a more simplistic approach probably would have been better. Also if the camera Ridge was a little more simple and they offered an actual clear back for the phone case then this could have easily been my go-to case to show off the blue of the fold seven. Unfortunately that won't be the case here. Hopefully they do a better phone case in the future that meets those needs and tries to be a little less flashy with some of its edges

The Z fold 7 is my first folding phone, and I was really unhappy with the case options. I was initially skeptical of a case that didn't protect the front half of the phone, thought it would look dumb, feel dumb, and assumed the protection it would offer would be near zero.

The Aramid fiber is quality and feels premium in the hand without adding any bulk to the phone at all. It's a little on the expensive side, but it's a premium price on a premium phone case.

All that said, I know someday I'm gonna drop the phone, it's gonna land on the front half, and I'm gonna be sad.. but that's what insurance is for. I just can't bring myself to put a bulky case on such a sleek phone.
