title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
The Pitaka Z Fold 6 Moonrise Edition case is truly a premium product that showcases exceptional craftsmanship. The overall fit and finish are immaculate, and the quality of the aramid fiber used here is clearly a step above other brands. Having previously owned the original Black version of the Pitaka case, I have to say I prefer the texture of the Moonrise Edition. The 1500D Aramid Fiber used in this version gives the back a beautifully textured, woven feel that not only enhances grip but also adds a unique aesthetic. It strikes a perfect balance—grippy without being too coarse, and just right in my opinion. Compared to the Black version, which has less texture, the 1500D fiber is definitely superior in my eyes.

The camera guard is another highlight. It fits perfectly and offers ample protection for the camera array. However, my only minor gripe here is that I wish the camera guard had a matte finish rather than the shiny look it currently has. The glossy finish creates a stark contrast with the rest of the case, and a matte option would have blended in much more seamlessly. That said, the cutouts for the microphones, power button, volume buttons, and charging port are spot-on, with no sharp edges—something you often see in cheaper cases. It’s clear from these details that this is a premium product built with premium quality.

However, the one significant drawback for me is the lack of a front part to the case. Pitaka’s case is already minimalistic, designed more for scratch protection than heavy-duty impact resistance due to how thin and light it is. But not offering front screen protection at all seems like an oversight. For users like myself who prefer feeling as though there’s no case on the phone, this case does a great job—however, not having the option to protect the front screen makes the phone feel uneven. One side with a case and the other without feels and looks a bit off, and that’s my biggest frustration with the design.

All in all, if you can overlook the lack of front screen protection, Pitaka’s aramid fiber case (in any color) is leagues ahead of the competition when it comes to fit, finish, and overall quality. For those who dislike bulky, chunky cases on their Z Fold 6, this is undoubtedly one of the best options out there. If minimalism and premium quality are your priorities, the Pitaka case deserves your attention. Overall 4.5/5 stars.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
If you're looking for an affordable case, this is a decent choice as long as you don't have high expectations.

Pros:
-Good quality considering the price
-Very thin and lightweight
-Fitment of the rear case was perfect, clips on snugly
-PC material is slightly grippy
-All corners and camera bump have moderate protection
-Included glass screen protector for the front case

Cons:
-While it is clear, the rear case has this rainbow oil slick look when it reflects light
-The edge of the rear case next to the hinge was not smooth, there were 2 spots with sharp burrs
-The case isn't recessed enough near the power button so my fingers would be slightly blocked by the case when using the fingerprint sensor
-The front case/integrated screen protector has these pixel dots in a grid pattern which are used to increase touch sensitivity but looks ugly (to me)

Ultimately, my experience was putting on the rear case and then seeing the dot matrix on the front case, which turned me off. I didn't bother trying the front case at all and removed the rear case with less than a minute of use.

If my little nitpicks don't bother you, I do think this case is good if your goal was to get a budget case that is clear and can show off the colors of your Fold 7. I will be returning this and sticking with an aramid fiber case.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I bought the Fold 7 at release and have had this case since the start. Here are my thoughts:

Pros:
The plastic is like a soft touch hard plastic that feels nice in the hand. It provides some grip but if my hands are dry, it can feel too smooth and slippy in my hand.

It does feel sleek and clean when it's put on. The Fold 7 is one of the slimmest foldable, so I think this case does a decent job keeping it's form factor and avoiding bulkiness (the Fold 7 with this case is thinner than my friend's Pixel 10 Pro with another slim case, it's amazingly slim).
The case doesn't affect functionality as its still easy to reach the buttons + also slightly easier to open the phone due to the case providing a space to put my fingers to pry the phone open versus the when the phone is naked.

Unfortunately, I have dropped my phone 2-3 times in the past several month onto concrete from waist level. The case has gotten scuffed on the corners near the hinge, and a bit near the charging port. Importantly. The phone itself has not been scuffed or dented at all to my surprise. So the case saved my phone several times now.

Cons
I found the same as other reviews, putting the case on leads to the phone not fully closing. There is a small gap where the corners of the 2 halves of the phone don't meet fully. I have not removed the case to see if it is permanent or temporary...

The front protective glass feels like a cheaper plastic. Due to finger oils or something there is occasionally a rainbow sheen on the front screen as a result. It also feels much lower quality than the actual front screen making me wish they let me put my own glass screen protector rather than this one.

Overall, I'm a bit disappointed by the front screen protector quality, and the phone not fully closing. But it being the among the cheapest case you can buy for the Fold 7 and that it legitimately stopped my phone from being damaged 2-3 times, it has achieved my goal for a case.

I bought it as a stop-gap case to see if other magsafe compatible cases come down in price, but I've been generally happy with it enough to leave it on this entire time. For its price, it's one of the best options on Amazon.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I bought the Fold 7 at release and have had this case since the start. Here are my thoughts:

Pros:
The plastic is like a soft touch hard plastic that feels nice in the hand. It provides some grip but if my hands are dry, it can feel too smooth and slippy in my hand.

It does feel sleek and clean when it's put on. The Fold 7 is one of the slimmest foldable, so I think this case does a decent job keeping it's form factor and avoiding bulkiness (the Fold 7 with this case is thinner than my friend's Pixel 10 Pro with another slim case, it's amazingly slim).
The case doesn't affect functionality as its still easy to reach the buttons + also slightly easier to open the phone due to the case providing a space to put my fingers to pry the phone open versus the when the phone is naked.

Unfortunately, I have dropped my phone 2-3 times in the past several month onto concrete from waist level. The case has gotten scuffed on the corners near the hinge, and a bit near the charging port. Importantly. The phone itself has not been scuffed or dented at all to my surprise. So the case saved my phone several times now.

Cons
I found the same as other reviews, putting the case on leads to the phone not fully closing. There is a small gap where the corners of the 2 halves of the phone don't meet fully. I have not removed the case to see if it is permanent or temporary...

The front protective glass feels like a cheaper plastic. Due to finger oils or something there is occasionally a rainbow sheen on the front screen as a result. It also feels much lower quality than the actual front screen making me wish they let me put my own glass screen protector rather than this one.

Overall, I'm a bit disappointed by the front screen protector quality, and the phone not fully closing. But it being the among the cheapest case you can buy for the Fold 7 and that it legitimately stopped my phone from being damaged 2-3 times, it has achieved my goal for a case.

I bought it as a stop-gap case to see if other magsafe compatible cases come down in price, but I've been generally happy with it enough to leave it on this entire time. For its price, it's one of the best options on Amazon.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
The Galaxy Z Fold 7 is a significant investment, and I can confidently say this is one of the best cases available to protect it. This case offers the heavy-duty security required for such a high-end device, maintaining full functionality with a seamless hinge cover and reliable MagSafe compatibility.

I have dropped my phone numerous times, but the ultimate test occurred when I inadvertently left it on my car's trunk. It tumbled onto the asphalt as I turned out of my subdivision, and while I feared the worst, both the case and the phone were completely undamaged. Only the belt clip holster broke during the impact, which is a testament to the rugged, shockproof build of the case itself.

Beyond the product's durability, TONGATE’S customer service is outstanding. I reached out to them six months after my initial purchase regarding the broken holster, provided photos of the damage, and while I only requested a new holster, they promptly sent me a full replacement case and holster. It is rare to find a company that stands behind such a high-quality, feature-rich product so long after the sale. This is a great product backed by professional service, and I highly recommend it to any Z Fold owner.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I bought this TONGATE screen protector for myself and I'm very happy with it.
The product packaging is top-notch. The box is rigid and the protector comes very well protected. The installation kit comes with everything you need: a wet wipe, a dry cloth, and dust-removing stickers, which is very useful.
Installation was very easy. I followed the instructions, and the protector adhered to the screen almost effortlessly, leaving no bubbles. The tempered glass feels very solid and is incredibly transparent. I haven't noticed any loss of touchscreen sensitivity, and so far, it has resisted fingerprints very well.
I definitely recommend it. It's a quality product.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I have previously been using the TORRAS Magnetic Armor Stand for a while. I liked the kick stand design of that case better than the TONGATE as it could be used in both portrait and landscape orientations where the TONGATE is pretty much only for landscape. The kickstand of the TORRAS is also easier to open (especially one-handed) compared to this TONGATE case.

But everything else - the TONGATE is significantly better. TORRAS' design is not nearly as good as this TONGATE case. The TORRAS has a spring system for the hinge cover that is backed by thin plastic clips. When one of the two of those breaks, the hinge cover will no longer automatically close, and the spring can move to where it actively keeps the hing cover closed. I took a chance that the TONGATE would be better-built and it seems to be. I have only used it for a week now but I do feel it is a better design. I can definitively say that the magsafe magnet included with this TONGATE case is MUCH stronger than the TORRAS case. TORRAS did honor their warranty when my case failed the first time. I did not bother asking TORRAS for another replacement the second time.

To sum up - the only downside in comparison to the TORRAS Magnetic Armor Stand case is the kickstand design. On balance I highly recommend this TONGATE case over the TORRAS.

The functionality of the case itself is great. S-pen holder, wide stand, hinge protection... All very nice to have. It feels solid and is fairly bulky, although I don't think the hinge protector would survive much of an impact since only 2 little springs/staples hold it on.

Two issues that make me give this 3 stars (other than the weak hinge):

-1) I didn't quite expect that the privacy screen protector makes your screen that much darker. Even when facing it head on. You can see the huge difference form the camera cutout on the front screen. I wish they had a non-privacy option.

-2) the magnets that make the stand stick to the back of the case cause 2 dead zones for the s-pen. This means that there are 2 large circles on the large screen where the s-pen simply doesn't register. This is especially bad considering I was excited to use this case and its stable stand to draw on the phone.

I initially bought 2 of this case, since I thought everything was great but wanted to keep a spare for when the hinge protection inevitably breaks, but now I'll be returning one of them and look for something without these issues for the next one

text:
The functionality of the case itself is great. S-pen holder, wide stand, hinge protection... All very nice to have. It feels solid and is fairly bulky, although I don't think the hinge protector would survive much of an impact since only 2 little springs/staples hold it on.

Two issues that make me give this 3 stars (other than the weak hinge):

-1) I didn't quite expect that the privacy screen protector makes your screen that much darker. Even when facing it head on. You can see the huge difference form the camera cutout on the front screen. I wish they had a non-privacy option.

-2) the magnets that make the stand stick to the back of the case cause 2 dead zones for the s-pen. This means that there are 2 large circles on the large screen where the s-pen simply doesn't register. This is especially bad considering I was excited to use this case and its stable stand to draw on the phone.

I initially bought 2 of this case, since I thought everything was great but wanted to keep a spare for when the hinge protection inevitably breaks, but now I'll be returning one of them and look for something without these issues for the next one

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Well what can you say. The fold is two phones on top of each other when folded. Add a case that will protect it and you have a very fancy brick. I measure about .75" thick with this case closed. It feels like I have armor on my phone now. Like I have a construction grade tuxedo on my very expensive gadget.

That being said the case is nice quality and fits well with adhesive points to make sure it stays put. I have had no issues with the case staying on. It has fairly raised bezels on the front face of the phone and around the camera (the camera really feels like it needs this). I purchased the black faux leather.

The biggest surprise is the hinge cover. The way it works is novel, and in my opinion, quite functional. It behaves kind of like a book end when the fold is opened partially or fully. This gives a grip point for holding in one hand (which is no simple task if you are lying in bed with it fully opened otherwise). The texture of the hinge cover also feels nice when it is in closed mode to grip. It is important I think to note that the hinge cover is the bulkiest aspect of the case and is not a removable piece at first glance. If you think you would drop your phone then you have that peace of mind. If you don't you should consider if the added bulk is needed for you. I am accepting that I now carry a 5lb personal defense device in my pocket from the future.

The phone will not lay flat in this case open or closed (not that you are likely using your phone flush flat on a table on a regular basis). Either the book end hinge cover will leave it angled up when fully open or the stand area on the back will prop the phone a bit when closed on a flat surface. It is not a big deal but perhaps worth a note. The hinge cover does give it a nice small angle boost if you are going to prop it in half open on a surface for whatever reason like a laptop.

The stand is very solid feeling and the correct length for the phone being so tall to stay stable. It can only be used when the phone is turned horizontal (opened or closed) which is the way you would likely use it to watch content anyways if you were to set it somewhere. This type of stand may not work best on anything other than a solid surface.

Lastly a note on the built in screen protector: The protector seems nice, is clear, and touch works without issue. It does not seem to be oleophobic. Neither does anything about this phone without the case. Furthermore it is not recommended an inner screen protector be used, so glossy is just another part of the experience. If you don't like to ever see any smudges or shine this screen protector is not going to be checking that box. I plan on just cleaning the phone a little more often.

Overall it feels smooth in the hand, functional, and decently grippy. It makes an already large phone feel ever so larger, but that comes with the territory. Buy if you have not been turned away by this point!

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This is my 2nd ZFold and this is by far the best case out of 5 (including the one Verizon sells specifically for the ZFolds). First, I liked that I didn't have to purchase a screen protector for the outside since the shell includes protection. Second, I like that the case adds minimal size to the phone but still feels sturdy. The case's texture makes it easy to grip the phone when closed and the hinge protector adds "gripability" to the phone while it is open.

The hinge protector can open while the phone is closed but not easily (which is good). It also does not make the phone seesaw if you lay it flat while open. What seals it for me though is that the kickstand (which can be used with the phone open or closed) is really sturdy. It doesn't fold like a lawn chair if you touch the screen nor does the phone easily tip over during its use.

The only CON is that the kickstand does get rather heated during the phone's extended use. Overall though, it is the best case I've purchased for the money. UPDATE: Everytime I drop my phone, the case cracks somewhere rendering it unusable. I'm on my 3rd case in less than a year.

I installed this cover right when it was at my door steps.

Overall, it seems nice. Unfortunatly, the details aren't there at all.

The hinge cover is attached by rubber strips that makes it very flimsy and makes me wonder when it will break. On the up side, the magnets on the hinge cover is very strong.

The front cover with built in screen protector isn't well made. The dimensions are off because you are loosing a little portion of the screen left side. It's hidden behind the cover so don't attempt to have the side bar on the left.

Built in screen protector is one of the best one yet but still doesn't compare to a real tempered glass screen protector. No bubbles when installed and looks good but you will loose a little bit of sensitivity. Some might not notice but it's real.

Can't comment on the stand as I just got it and it hasn't been even 30min that's installed. Although, i've tried it and works very well with some resistance to keep it closed.

The whole case is adding considerable weight. Saying that everyone is having their pinky under the phone to hold it, your pinky will get tired really quick.

Overall, it's a nice case for the price but I will be returning to more expensive cases that all the details are met

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Well what can you say. The fold is two phones on top of each other when folded. Add a case that will protect it and you have a very fancy brick. I measure about .75" thick with this case closed. It feels like I have armor on my phone now. Like I have a construction grade tuxedo on my very expensive gadget.

That being said the case is nice quality and fits well with adhesive points to make sure it stays put. I have had no issues with the case staying on. It has fairly raised bezels on the front face of the phone and around the camera (the camera really feels like it needs this). I purchased the black faux leather.

The biggest surprise is the hinge cover. The way it works is novel, and in my opinion, quite functional. It behaves kind of like a book end when the fold is opened partially or fully. This gives a grip point for holding in one hand (which is no simple task if you are lying in bed with it fully opened otherwise). The texture of the hinge cover also feels nice when it is in closed mode to grip. It is important I think to note that the hinge cover is the bulkiest aspect of the case and is not a removable piece at first glance. If you think you would drop your phone then you have that peace of mind. If you don't you should consider if the added bulk is needed for you. I am accepting that I now carry a 5lb personal defense device in my pocket from the future.

The phone will not lay flat in this case open or closed (not that you are likely using your phone flush flat on a table on a regular basis). Either the book end hinge cover will leave it angled up when fully open or the stand area on the back will prop the phone a bit when closed on a flat surface. It is not a big deal but perhaps worth a note. The hinge cover does give it a nice small angle boost if you are going to prop it in half open on a surface for whatever reason like a laptop.

The stand is very solid feeling and the correct length for the phone being so tall to stay stable. It can only be used when the phone is turned horizontal (opened or closed) which is the way you would likely use it to watch content anyways if you were to set it somewhere. This type of stand may not work best on anything other than a solid surface.

Lastly a note on the built in screen protector: The protector seems nice, is clear, and touch works without issue. It does not seem to be oleophobic. Neither does anything about this phone without the case. Furthermore it is not recommended an inner screen protector be used, so glossy is just another part of the experience. If you don't like to ever see any smudges or shine this screen protector is not going to be checking that box. I plan on just cleaning the phone a little more often.

Overall it feels smooth in the hand, functional, and decently grippy. It makes an already large phone feel ever so larger, but that comes with the territory. Buy if you have not been turned away by this point!

The original review is still applicable. The base is great with the exception that my case made swiping (particularly in the top left corner) very difficult. The seller was very helpful. Overall, this seems like it will be a solid case from a protection and features perspective. Easy to install. Adds enough grip to keep me from being terrified of the phone slipping out of a pocket. Kickstand works well - hopefully, that continues to be the situation a few months from now. No issues with wireless charging.

The big challenge - presses on the edges of the screen are hit-and-miss. Using gestures is an incredibly frustrating experience. Swiping from the bottom-up, top-down, and left to right is inconsistent. Sometimes they work OK - other times it will not work at all. I'll have to open my phone and then swipe. I have turned on the recommended setting for greater sensitivity on the screen.

I've had 2 other cases with this device and have used the device without any cases. None of them had this problem. My guess is that during the manufacturing process, the edges of the case creep a little too far into the screen real estate. That's preventing swipes from the edge not registering. The case is installed properly. There are no gaps.

Going to give it another couple of weeks before I decide whether to send it back.

text:
I picked up the ZAGG Glass+ for my Galaxy Z Flip 7 because I wanted something that would give me real drop protection without sacrificing clarity and overall it delivers.

Installation:
The included EZ Apply tray makes the whole process surprisingly smooth and simple especially for a phone with a foldable design. It lined up well and went on without bubbles in the center, which i worry about a lot. I did notice that getting the corners to stay perfectly flush took a bit of pressing but once it settles the protector looks clean and nearly invisible. Compared to other protectors I tried this is one of the easiest installs I've had.

Protection & Daily Use:
The glass feels smooth and premium, very close to the feel of an actual screen. It has smudge resistant coating that helps with fingerprints, which is a lifesaver on a device that gets folded and touched constantly. ZAGG claims its up to 3 times stronger than a unprotected screen and while I haven't dropped my phone (yet), it definitely feels tough and reassuring.

Compatability:
One thing to note is that depending on your case, you may notice slight lift along the edges. With my slimmer case it feels fine, but my old very slim case kept on raising the corners constantly and no matter how much pressing down I did It wouldn't wouldn't away. This isn't a deal breaker but its worth keeping in mind if you use a thinner case.

Bottom Line: The ZAGG Glass+ id a dependable clear and strong protector for the flip 7. It keeps the phone looking sharp, resists smudges and makes me feel confidant about tossing my phone in a pocket or bag without worrying about scratches. While it isn't 100% perfect in terms of edge fit with every case, its still one of the best screen protectors you can get for a foldable right now.

This isn't a deal breaker but its worth keeping in mind if you use a thinner case.

Bottom Line: The ZAGG Glass+ id a dependable clear and strong protector for the flip 7. It keeps the phone looking sharp, resists smudges and makes me feel confidant about tossing my phone in a pocket or bag without worrying about scratches. While it isn't 100% perfect in terms of edge fit with every case, its still one of the best screen protectors you can get for a foldable right now.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I will start with the most important part of the review: this case has saved me likely hundreds of dollars in screen repairs and / or frustration over a damaged screen. I think it's designed to work like the crumple-zone in a car, cracking to absorb and distribute the shock from falls in order to protect the screen beneath, rather than trying to create an impervious shield. Honestly it's worked for me three times now, so whatever it is they're doing, I no longer doubt the efficacy.

Personally, I only use the front screen protector part of this item--the wallet case I got did not include one and I have little kids, so I looked for an inexpensive one that I could steal just that portion from. It's super easy to install, came in the color I wanted to match (black), doesn't scratch easily, fits over the screen very nicely (not SUPER tight, but tight enough that it rarely comes off) and only minimally interferes with the screen sensitivity and fingerprint functionality. But the 'not perfect quality' is expected for $10, and the protection it has offered has made up that cost many, many times over now. I've paid a grand total of $30-35 on these cases (half the cost or less of most of the 'impervious shield' type cases that always seem to affect touch sensitivity and audio) and my phone's survived all the major snafus my kids have thrown it into or off of.

text:
Hard to believe the quality of this case at this price.
While waiting for my BENKS case, which is still weeks away from production, I needed something to protect my phone. I’ve purchased over five cases for my Fold 5 in the past, averaging around $40 each, and none lasted more than three months because the front cover kept failing—so I know the usual weaknesses of cases like this.

This one surprised me. It has been working flawlessly so far, and I think that’s because the front cover comes with a built-in screen protector, which makes it fit more securely.

The price is also unbelievable. I don’t know how a company that puts this much thought into design can sell it for under $10.

If they could upgrade the front screen protector to glass instead of the current plastic (which actually feels similar to glass but could be more fingerprint-resistant) and slightly enlarge the cutout on the front cover for easier fingerprint scanning, it would be a perfect case even at $29. Add a slim hinge protector that levels with the camera bump so the phone sits flat when unfolded, and I’d happily pay $49. That would make it the best and slimmest Z Fold 7 case out there. And if they release a MagSafe version, it’s an instant buy for me.

The grip is just right—not too sticky, not too slippery. Overall, I’m genuinely impressed with the value and thoughtful design.

text:
This case was good overall. It fit well, hinge protection was good, and slip. Overall, the case did not add much girth to the phone which is nice since the phone is already big as it is.

The ONE drawback is: wireless charging. Although for the most part it does work with wireless charging, but it can be finicky. The Bump for the stand on the back makes the back uneven, and I noticed because of this you have to sometimes "play" with the positioning of the phone when charging, on standup wireless charges it was even more picky, and you had to get it just right to make sure it stayed on for a charge. I also have wireless car charger, and in this it worked at tad better, because I have the type of charger that auto adjusts the positioning for the phone when charging, HOWEVER it seems the gap created by the hump caused 2 things to happen, First the charge was fairly weak, so if you were using android auto fairly heavily it will not keep up with the usage and only slow down the battery usage, not charge it up. The second thing I noticed that when this happens the "hump" on the back of the case got real hot, more so than the rest of the charging area, So this may be were most of the charging conduction was taking place and the gap was causing it to overheat.

In the end I had to return the case and go for another one that had not stand, because in the end wireless charging for me is necessary and more important than the kickstand.

I bought this case and an Otterbox (for double the price) at the same time. This case provides HANDS DOWN way better protection for the phone! The cases sticks with a double sided "tape/glue" like material, on the edges and really holds it in place. I was kind of concerned with this however it seems fine after 2 weeks. The front screen protector allows the same touch capabilities as when there was nothing covering it. The kick stand on the back of the case seems a little small but it works fine on a flat surface.

I would 100% recommend this case for the fold 4.
timestamp_raw: Reviewed in the United States on December 3, 2023

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This case was good overall. It fit well, hinge protection was good, and slip. Overall, the case did not add much girth to the phone which is nice since the phone is already big as it is.

The ONE drawback is: wireless charging. Although for the most part it does work with wireless charging, but it can be finicky. The Bump for the stand on the back makes the back uneven, and I noticed because of this you have to sometimes "play" with the positioning of the phone when charging, on standup wireless charges it was even more picky, and you had to get it just right to make sure it stayed on for a charge. I also have wireless car charger, and in this it worked at tad better, because I have the type of charger that auto adjusts the positioning for the phone when charging, HOWEVER it seems the gap created by the hump caused 2 things to happen, First the charge was fairly weak, so if you were using android auto fairly heavily it will not keep up with the usage and only slow down the battery usage, not charge it up. The second thing I noticed that when this happens the "hump" on the back of the case got real hot, more so than the rest of the charging area, So this may be were most of the charging conduction was taking place and the gap was causing it to overheat.

In the end I had to return the case and go for another one that had not stand, because in the end wireless charging for me is necessary and more important than the kickstand.

title: 3.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I used this case brand for my Fold 3 and was really happy with the protection and performance. It's bulky yes, but that provides some good protection all around. The eventual thin bezel breakage on the outer part of the screen was no longer an issue. I bought same case for my Fold 4, expecting similar results. This was not to be. The protection as expected is great. The main problem is the screen cover on the outer small screen. It's not responsive and to the point, it's practically useless.

You have to swipe, swipe, swipe on many instances just to get it to respond. If you need to use a PIN, that leads to many errors. I message the company thru Amazon seller's contact but no response provided. Overall, I'd say get it. Just keep in mind what I said about the outer screen protector.

text:
This was my choice after extensive online shopping comparisons.

First of all I'll emphasize that, while it has an S-pen holder built into the hinge protector, IT DOES NOT INCLUDE AN S-PEN! (Some customers said they had misunderstood this.)

PROs:
• It fits great.
• All edges, including the hinge, are protected.
• The lens cover keeps the lenses clean and well-protected, and it clicks into place to stay open or closed).
• The flip-out back panel works very well as a stand, and it can also be used as a sturdy handle when holding the phone unfolded.
• The built-in front screen protector doesn't adhere to the screen, so you don't have to deal with trapped dust particles and air bubbles during application. And it's working perfectly without having to increase the screen's sensitivity in device settings.

CONs:
• After just a few days, my S-pen started falling out of the holder slot. But I've overcome that by applying a short piece of electrical tape just above the pen button. (If it starts to peel, I'll probably switch to a short piece of shrink tubing.)
• While there seems to be something inside the back of the case that a magnetic phone holder is attracted to, it's not nearly enough to support the weight of the phone. But applying a stick-on metal plate (I had one on hand) easily solved that problem.

Previously rsviewed: Finally, a case for the Samsung Fold-6 phone that does it all. Often, when the screen protector with previous cases had to be removed for some reason, it was a problem because the adhesive strip would not re-seal when the protector was put back on the phone. Now I have two extra adhesives for resealing the protector to keep dust out. But, as I said, this case does it all - sturdy stands for both landscape or portrait, S-pen holder, and camera lens cover. text:
I had a Kaiiecal case for my fold 5 and this one for the fold 7 is a huge improvement and is almost perfect. I tried a couple of other cases, but I keep going to this one. Compared to the old fold 4 case, it is sturdier, the screen protector fits better, and in general, the whole case feels really premium.

Compared to other fold 7 cases I tried, this case wins on the fact that the hinge protector has a soft pad to prevent scratches, the dual portrait/landscape stand capability is unique and quite useful, the screen protector, while not glass, is relatively sturdy, and the case does not require any kind of adhesive. I have taken it off and on to clean the phone, and it goes back on perfectly.

The only downsides are that the screen has no coating, so it collects oil and fingerprints quite easily, and that there is one spot on the top left corner of the case that has a little bump (which the manufacturer told me by design to allow easy removal of the case) so it causes the top frame not to be entirely flush with the phone. It doesn't functionally affect the case, but once I saw it, I can't unsee it. Additionally, the portrait mode stand on the hinge protector feels a bit flimsy, and I was worried it would break, but it has held strong so far. I also wish it had magsafe.

text: This case is exactly as advertised. It holds my S Pen for the Fold 6/5 in the hinge, and all the cutouts for ports, buttons, and camera are precise. text: So, I have tried multiple cases but this one seems to be my favorite--I keep going back to it. I like the option of carrying cards with me--although it will only hold 2. The stand is a little less durable than some others, but it has not broken yet and it is mostly stable enough (on varied surfaces it is a bit shaky sometimes). The stand does NOT work if you don't open the phone to tablet mode; however, if you open the card storage, that cover WILL work as a stand--you just have to keep track of the cards while you are using the cover as a stand (the cards don't 'clip' in). The case itself is durable enough to protect the phone (duh--that is the point, right?). It does allow wireless charging with the Samsung multi-device charging station. The open face portion of the phone case cover does provide protection for the face of the phone, but it collects skin oil worse than some other cases I have used. (so, if keeping smudges off your phone face is a 'thing' for you, you might not like this case). The phone buttons are easy to access/use with the case in place. All in all, a pretty good case. If you guys can figure out a way to keep the cards in--or have a split cover to use as a stand--and find a clear protective material that doesn't hold skin oil so stubbornly, you'd have the best case on the market!

title: 1.0 out of 5 stars
text:
The thin bar on the front shell broke in less than 6 months without rough, unusual, or unreasonable use. I got this because it was the only product I could find at the time that had the combination of things I was looking for - something thin, simple, and that would lay relatively flat when open. It more or less fit those criteria and worked reasonably well, although I would mention that the design of the front shell makes it very difficult to use the navigation or keyboard buttons that sit at the low end of the outside screen when the phone is closed. It also came with sticky spots on the inside of the case, which I assume were intended to help the case stay in place; however, one of those spots was right over the SIM tray, and it would tug at that, occasionally unseating my card, which was annoying.

Prior to this breaking, I probably would have rated it 2-3 stars, but now, not only did it break in less than 6 months, I found a better replacement for about $10. When I bought this, it cost over $50 after tax, which was a rip off, but at the time it was really the only thing I could find that seemed to be what I wanted. Once upon the time I looked to Otterbox to be at the forefront of quality design. Lately, I find their products to be exceptionally basic and way overpriced. I certainly would avoid this product.

I purchased this Samsung phone case specifically for my device, expecting at least a basic level of quality and, most importantly, a proper fit. I was severely disappointed on both counts.

First, the fit is non-existent. The case is clearly molded incorrectly. It either warps the phone, preventing the buttons from being pressed, or simply fails to snap onto the device fully, leaving entire edges exposed and vulnerable. This makes the case completely useless and defeats the entire purpose of having phone protection.

Second, the quality is abysmal. The material feels cheap, flimsy, and brittle, not durable at all. The cutouts for the charging port and speakers are rough, misaligned, and poorly finished. I have serious doubts this case would survive even a minor drop, given how poorly it's constructed.

I am very disappointed with this purchase. I feel like I've wasted my money on a product that was clearly never tested. Save yourself the trouble and avoid this case entirely. It is a massive fail in both design and manufacturing.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Pros
Feels drop safe.
Snaps well to the phone.
Opens and closes well.
Other features are neat too. (Hoping I can put a pop socket on it though. Probably not.)

Cons
1. Anti-slip strips aren't built into the phone case. You have to install it yourself and there's not much instruction to go by. I placed one on the edge of the phone since there's a bit of slack/looseness there. Not a huge problem but I'm cautious of adhesive residue remaining on the phone if I ever replace it.

2. I installed Mr. Shield Tempered Glass onto this phone and there were some air bubbles formed due to the front casing. Had to sand the corner down with a nail file. But after sanding the corner down it stopped the air bubbles from forming. So, that's something to note if you happen to have any air bubbles form after installing a screen protector.

3. Will admit kinda bulky and can't read NFC (chipped bank cards) and probably won't wirelessly charge.

I cannot recommend this case for the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 7. While it appears sturdy at first glance, the actual performance is disappointing. The included screen guard does not stay in place and frequently falls off, leaving the display unprotected. One major flaw is the absence of an actual screen protector—the design relies only on the raised plastic edges to safeguard the screen, which is far from sufficient for real protection. The kickstand is also flimsy and not practical for regular use.

For a phone valued at nearly $2000, protection should be the top priority, and unfortunately, this case does not provide the level of durability or reliability required for long-term use. The hinge protection and overall build quality feel inadequate, and I do not trust this case to safeguard the device against drops or daily wear.

In my opinion, this product does not live up to its description and should be reconsidered by anyone looking for genuine heavy-duty protection.

My 2020 flagship Moto Razr 5G was a great phone on its own right, but after the daily grind of a teachers life, it finally expired. I loved the foldable design and so went for this new Razr 2023 as it's replacement.
Wow, what an astonishing improvement in only 3 years. This new Razr has all the benefits of it's folding predecessor, while sporting an amazing assignment is improvements that make it superior in every way.

- My old Razr had a small but usable 6.1 inch POLED screen. This new Razr is gigantic by comparison, at 6.9 inches - it's a huge noticeable difference, and higher resolution.
- Despite it's substantially bigger battery and screen, this new Razr is noticeably thinner and lighter than the 2020.
- the vegan leather cover is 'Da Bomb! No slips, no fingerprints, no back glass shattered.
The 2020 was fast, but this thing, with the Snapdragon 7 Gen 1, is screaming fast, over 660kb on Antutu!
- both have a super high quality feel, crazy good looks, and the benefits of the foldable design cannot be overstated. It just ROCKS.
- Better colors. Mine is the super lavender/purple, looks terrific.
Highest recommendation.

** Update ** after two months, just about everything above still holds, only one negative/ caveat to add: in two months of heavy daily use, I have pinched my index finger twice upon opening. Ouch! In two years of ownership, that never happened once with the old Razr. The hinge can bite when snapped open to is full flat condition...
* A slick plus is the wireless charging - slow but high tech, works great overnight on your bedside table. It doesn't come with one, but they are dirt cheap (and I already had one
Still highest recommendation.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Overall the Moto G Pure is a good phone for the money.

I do not play games or take a lot of photos. I do not have a lot of apps installed either. I use the phone for calls, texts, navigation, browsing the interwebs, and using a few apps (amazon, ebay, offer up, banking, health care). For these purposes, the phone is more than adequate. I am VERY happy with the purchase. I was going to use this phone as a temp phone until the new iPhone SE reviews came out. I like the G Pure so much that I might just keep it long term. So, if you have a similar use case, then do not be scared of the reviews showing horrible geekbench scores for the MediaTek Helios processor. Also, the near stock Android experience with no bloatware is refreshing. I like the little moto tweaks, like chopping twice for the flashlight.

However, there are some caveats:

There is no 5G and no NFC. So no google pay (do you trust google?). The lack of 5G is not a deal breaker for me as my carrier charges extra for 5G anyways.

The face unlock is unreliable (boo). I do not take selfies, so it could very well be that I am holding the phone incorrectly when trying to unlock the phone. However, I feel like an idiot moving the phone around trying to get the phone to unlock with facial recognition until the phone gives up and begs me to use fingerprint or PIN unlock. I was really hoping this feature was going to make me feel like I have a cheap iPhone. I was mistaken. This is not a deal breaker, but it is a let down.

The storage is a pitiful 32 GB. The OS alone with the preinstalled google aps uses about half of that. So if you have/need lots of apps look elsewhere. My previous 2017 phone also had the same amount of storage but more carrier bloatware. Still, the 32 GB feels cramped for me and will definitely feel cramped for most people.

The OS is android 11. This is already one version behind the current android 12 (at the date of purchase Feb. 2020), but the G Pure is supposed to get updated to android 12 and then that's probably it. This is the reason that I chose the G Pure over the G Play. The G Play has a bigger battery and a more commonly targeted Qualcomm processor. But the G Play has android 10 and will only get updated to android 11. Why does Motorola makes such good phones and have such a horrible update policy? If any Motorola bots are reading this, please note that I would buy a more expensive Motorola phone AND recommend Motorola to others if this were not the case. As it stands, I expect every Motorola phone purchase to result in being abandoned before you even get your new phone in the mail.

I know that there are more "cons" listed than "pluses", but I think some of the "cons" would be deal breakers for a lot of people. BUT, overall I am VERY happy with the purchase for my use case and expect to sue the phone for quite some time at the moment. So if you have similar needs, then you should expect to be happy as well.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I was looking for a phone or tablet to use with my DJI Mini 2 drone. The remote control with the Mini 2 requires the use of an Android or Apple smart phone or tablet since the remote control doesn't have it's own display and the phone or tablet serve as the display. There are lots of phones you can use for this purpose, but you need something with a very bright display. I have an iPhone 11 Pro as my primary phone and when flying in bright sunlight, the display dims to prevent the phone from overheating. It gets so dim that it is almost unusable for this purpose. I was looking for a new or used phone or tablet with a very bright display. So far, this phone seems to work very well and the display is bright enough to view in direct sunlight. I believe it is capable of 1300 nits under certain circumstances, but that may be while playing HDR content. The Google Pixel phones are great, as are the Samsungs, but the Pixel's screens don't get this bright and Samsung models that do have bright screens are much more expensive.

I've used my sim card from my iPhone to make calls (AT&T) and I think the Motorola Edge 2022 actually sounds better than the 11 Pro. I have tested Wi-Fi speeds and the Edge 2022 is consistantly 10% to 15% faster than the 11 Pro. I've seen complaints about the camera quality but the photos, especially macro photos, look as good or better than the 11 Pro. If my entire family didn''t use iPhones, I think I would actually start using the Edge 2022 as my primary phone as it is much easier to see with the larger screen. Considering all of the features you get with this phone, I think the price is probably impossible to beat. I have only had the phone for a week, but I am extremely happy with my purchase which was less than $250.00. Would I prefer a better IP dust and water resistant rating and more premium materials? Of course, but you can't have everything at this price point. Is it a good deal at $500.00? Probably not a great deal, but at $250.00 it is an absolute bargain and a fine phone. I realize that there are a few negative reviews and I'm sure it's possible to get a dud every once in a while, but some of the reviews seem to be issues not with the phone itself, but due to receiving the wrong phone or a problem with the ordering process. I don't doubt that those problems exist, but I would prefer that reviews of a product, focus on the quality of the actual product and not so much with the process. This is just my opinion. I hope this helps someone else who is on the fence about buying this phone. If you can get it for $250.00, it's an absolute steal! Knowing everything I know now, I would purchase another one if needed and would recommend it to family or friends if they needed a good phone with at great display at a great price.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I've bought Motorolas for a long time now. I've ventured out to Samsung and LG on occasion, but I've always come back. Motorola makes great solid, reliable midrange phones with about as authentic of an Android experience you can get. I was reluctant after the company was acquired by Lenovo, but I can attest they're still good phones.
I bought this to replace my Moto X4 not because the Moto X4 was broken or didn't work, but because I wanted to take advantage of wireless android auto in my Jeep and the newest OS for the X4 was incompatible. I had gotten my money's worth out of that phone already anyways.

One of my favorite changes is that the fingerprint reader is built into the power button.. this is MILES better than any in-screen fingerprint reader I've used. It's almost instantaneous. Press the power button like normal and it likely already processed your fingerprint and unlocked the phone.
Battery life, as with all of my Motorolas, seems to be a step above the other brands.
Other than a Pixel, Motorola offers as close to an authentic Android experience as you'll find. They're not trying to force you into some stupid ecosystem you don't want. Bloatware is minimal. Again, this is why I keep coming back to Motorola.
Screen quality is very good. I used to think anything greater than 1080p on a little phone is overkill, but I admit the text does look noticeably more crisp.

I have two disappointments, which are fairly minor:
1) The phone has stereo speakers built-in, but as others have noted, the second speaker is just the earpiece, and therefore it's much quieter than the main speaker, giving it a lopsided soundstage. I guess it's better than nothing, but not by much. Speaker quality is still decent, but nowhere near iPhone quality. I've yet to hear an Android that competes, though.
2) Camera software seems laggy/low FPS. I'm guessing it has to do with the multiple cameras and the phone processing them together to create one image, but it feels like the camera "viewfinder" runs at <30fps. The images that come out are still good. Again, not iPhone quality, but perfectly good for a midrange-priced Android phone. I was just disappointed compared to my Moto X4 because that thing was always smooth as butter and image quality was 90% of what this fancy three-camera setup achieves. I still think these multi-camera setups are a bit of a gimmick. Or maybe Android/Motorola just aren't utilizing them optimally.

All of my other complaints are with Android itself, so they'd be present on any brand. Having owned both iPhones and Androids, I like Android for their flexibility, but with each new version of Android I feel drawn back to the 'everything just works like it should' quality that iOS has. Apple feels like it was designed by a small group of people who understood the mission well; Android sometimes feels like it was designed by a thousand of different people who never talked to each other. As these mobile OSs get more complex and feature packed, I'm starting to think I'd rather have stability than flexibility/customisation. For my next phone, I may go back to iPhone... Again, though, this is not specific to this phone--just Android itself. So I guess this rant wasn't really necessary..

Good phone if you're looking for an Android! Not the best-of-the-best, but a great balance of capability and price. Probably the sweet-spot of the market.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I dropped my pretty new Samsung s23 ultra on a jobsite and cracked the screen bad. replacement screen for my color phone is not available. so I needed a new phone. I had this one overnight'ed to me. I got a case that looked like it would be the most protective. and i set it up to use as a temp phone. I have been very impressed! so far it's been awesome.

Pro's: - Incredible battery life
- smooth operation (it is fast and responsive),
- flat screen (no useless curved edges)
- crisp screen with good colors,
- good cameras (not the single best out there, but still very good),
- handy, light weight, easy to set up and use.
- 'Ready For'!!! holy cow, they did it right! better than Dex, better than old continuum, single best phone to PC user interface i have seen. fast, smooth, and so extremely useful!!! when I'm in the office it is great for sharing pics and contacts and websites between devices, it is brilliant! probably the most understated feature of the phone. the 'Windows 365' for large corporations and such is lost on most of the world, but most basic users can really benefit from the 'Mobile Desktop' mode. it's awesome!

Con's: it is only missing 2 things.
1: stylus. Motorola already has a stylus phone, they have the technology, should have put it with this phone, or maybe used the surface protocol so when you have a surface pen you can use it on the phone too. really a huge benefit that not enough manufacturers offer. marking up pictures precisely, finite controls with something smaller than the tip of my finger. stylus is huge and should be an option on the next iteration.
2: micro-SD card. I know all the phone companies think we live next to a cell tower and have 5 bars all the time, but that is not true. in the mountains the signal strength is always changing. it is so much better to have room to store important file on the phone that you can rely on being there, and plenty of them without have to wonder if you will run out of room. that would make all newer phone better. cloud storage is awesome, but it's not always as accessible as the commercials indicate. local storage is a must. and being able to have more would give this device an advantage over all the rest of the phones that don't offer it anymore.
3: More case options. The case that comes with it is a joke. It needs a good rubbery Otterbox defender style case. I have not seen one yet.

In short, I really like this phone, the Ready For is so useful that there is a good chance that I will not go back to my Samsung after it is fixed.
If this phone had a stylus, it would be no competition, ThinkPhone for the win!
If it had a stylus and micro sd card slot, it would be just that much better.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I haven't owned a Motorola device since the 2nd generation Moto X back in 2014. The Galaxy S22, while a nice phone, was too small and I found that I missed the stock android experience, so when I found the Edge+ on sale for way less than most flagships go for these days, I went for it.

The basics: setup is easy, especially if you're upgrading from another android phone. You could do things wirelessly, or you could get a fast USB 3.0 cable and immediately copy all of your photos, call history, texts, apps, and everything else over in minutes. You don't need to power this phone off to install your sim card either. Just pop it in, and your carrier will be recognized in moments. The fingerprint reader can be a bit finicky if you're using a screen protector, so keep this in mind: if you set your prints before you installed it, delete them, and re-apply them. You shouldn't have much issues after this.

Performance: The Snapdragon 8 Gen 2 is a incredibly processor. It's more than capable of handling whatever you throw at it. Even after installing several system updates it's speed remains top notch.

Features: You'll have access to all kinds to personalization and gesture features that you can tune to your liking. Chop to turn on your flashlight and twisting the phone to enable the camera are both great features that were on the OG Moto X, so it's cool to know that they were kept on newer devices.

Condition: Always check your sellers on this platform. The model I bought was shipped and sold from Amazon.com, which made the purchase a no brainer as returns/refunds/shipping would be a simple process. Still, when I received the Edge+, I noticed that the seal on the actual manufacturer's box was already cut. While nothing was missing from the box and the phone was clearly in new condition and hadn't been touched, it was still a bit odd.

Either way, less is more. $399 for a phone with these specs is a bargain in a time where the current culture is pushing you to spend $1K on a phone. Are the cameras the best? No, but it takes solid photos and videos. And while Motorola only provides 3 years of software upgrades and four years of security updates, you honestly don't need to have the newest version of android as soon as they release. Trust me. These devices are already feature rich, and as far as security is concerned, use common sense: don't download sketchy apps or suspicious files onto your phone, or give your phone number to any sketchy characters.

That said, this is a solid device.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I purchased the Moto E (2020) during the holidays when Tracfone had a $100 rebate for activating an unlocked phone with them. The phone ended up costing about $30 after the rebate which is an outstanding value. It was purchased for my kids to use as an emergency phone, since I already use a Galaxy Note 10+ as my daily. I can verify that the Moto E is unlocked and works with US networks, as I’ve alternated between a T-Mobile and Tracfone (Verizon) SIM with no issues. In the settings, the phone lists "XT2052-1" as the model#. Here’s a list of Pros and Cons after having used it for about a month.
Pros:
- Runs smoothly. Having only 2GB of RAM, I’ve found it still runs smoothly doing routine things with multiple apps opened (e.g. make calls, texting, surf internet, watch Youtube, view social media).
- No bloatware. Aside from 2 or 3 Motorola apps, this is essentially a stock Android phone (running Android 10 as of this review). It uses Google Photos, Gmail, Google Messages, Google Calendar and other Google apps as defaults. There are no duplicate or redundant apps like you find in a Samsung phone.
- I’ve found it to have good battery life with the 3550mAh battery, but YMMV base on use.
- MicroSD expansion. SD card can be formatted as Internal or External Storage. I’m using a 128GB SD card and defaulted the camera app to store all photos/videos to the card.
- Fast Fingerprint reader on rear.
- Fully unlocked. Tested with T-Mobile and Tracfone SIM (Verizon version).
- Medium sized phone with good sized screen. Larger than an iPhone SE (2020), but smaller than a Galaxy Note 10+. Most people can’t tell it’s only a 720p screen.
- Excellent Photo/Video quality in good lighting.
Cons:
- 32bit Operating System (OS). Some apps and games require a 64bit OS and will not work on this phone (e.g. Animal Crossing: Pocket Camp). Not all apps can be moved to SD if you’ve formatted it as External storage.
- 32GB internal storage. 13GB of the 32GB is taken up by System files, so there’s really only 19GB of internal storage.
- Camera can be frustratingly slow in low-light conditions. Sometimes, a couple seconds will pass after pressing the shutter button before the camera captures the image. Again, this mainly occurs in low-light.
- Micro USB charging port. Really wish this was USB C instead.
- Phone always displays “Charging Rapidly” when charging, but it’s not a true “Fast Charge” like Samsung or OnePlus phones. This displays regardless of the port or wattage being used.
- No wireless charging, but not expected at this price point.
Overall, this is an excellent phone for the price, even better if you’re able to get it for less than $50.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text: Personally I wasn't ready to buy a new smart phone. My 2016 Samsung J series phone as far as I was concerned continued to meet my needs as my basic everyday cell phone. However, my cell phone provider informed me that my older 3G version CDMA phone was no longer to be supported by T-Mobile/Sprint and I was left with no choice but to find a replacement. I use Tello which is an MVNO cell phone service . I pay around 12.00 a month for unlimited call/text service and 1 GB's of fast data. The rest of the data I get free via WIFI or Hotspots. Consequently, paying much more than $100.00 for an unlocked phone seemed out of the question for me. I'm so grateful that I selected this Moto E (2020) phone and I think you will too. This budget phone came the closest to meeting all of the objectives I laid out and still kept me within my overall $100 price range. Maybe off by just a little bit... LOL. As you will soon see I'm a researcher by profession. It literally took months for me to evaluate budget cell phones as I didn't want to switch my cell phone provider. However, If I did switch providers the Moto E (2020) gave me the most choices in choosing a new phone service versus any other budget phone sold out there in the market.. Basically I needed a phone that was VoLTE friendly and this phone is DUAL VoLTE friendly. I needed a phone that supported bands 66 and 71. Only this budget phone met that category in (GSM) and yet offered full (CDMA) compatibility as well. Budget phones for Samsung, One Plus, TCL , LG, Nokia, BLU, Oukitel etc... all of them failed miserably at the $100 price range let alone not offering the same number of frequency bands as the Moto E. Why then only 4 stars ? Sadly, this Moto E phone has an antiquated slow charging Micro USB adapter. ( SEE PIC ) This phone uses an LCD screen and the resolution display is adequate but not exceptional. Any senior whose used to pressing front and back arrows instead of swiping to change pages will find that difference annoying . Overall, it just takes some time getting used to it. However, on the positive side the phone is BIG. The screen is Easy to Read. It has a modern slim bezel more like an expensive upper scale smart phone. (SEE PIC) Although the phone is big , it's still easy to hold in your hand. I'd strongly recommend though getting a phone case because of all the plastic components comprised in it. (SEE PIC ) Most importantly, and I can't stress this enough is that the Moto E meets ALL the band requirements for GSM and CDMA compatibility when choosing most phone carriers. This includes all the Major Carriers - EXCEPT IN RARE INSTANCES MAYBE VERIZON AND THE MVNO's LINKED TO THEM. For instance, the Verizon website by entering the IMEI/MEID # cites compatibility by saying " it looks like your device the MOTO E Unlocked XT2052-1 is compatible." However, it also states in smaller print "some devices may not support all features and services." The Motorola corporate website confirms the Moto E (2020) is compatibility using Verizon including their MVNO's. My research has uncovered that the Moto E phone also does work with most low cost MVNO's including many cheaper upstarts out there like Red Pocket using only (GSM). Many of you out there I see like Cricket Wireless through AT&T. I put my IMEI # in with their checker tool and it came back with a Yes. Unfortunately Cricket thinks this device is a GIN Lite phone. Whatever that means? The Motorola corporate website states US Cellular which uses a CDMA network won't work but yet the US Cellular compatibility tool asking only for my IMEI # says YES. A similar scenario applies to BOOST Mobile. The Motorola site says NO but when I enter the requested IMEI # in the Boost checker tool it says YES. I agree very confusing. I did figure out that the " Pre Paid" plans are the only ones that seem to be the most restrictive when using the Moto E unlocked. This is likely the case for Boost which offers many Pre paid plan services. Such plans do differ from a "Pay as you Go" plan or an "MVNO." They also seem to be the plans with no phone compatibility checker to confirm BYOP. Most negative reviews you'll see here online center around services with these Prepaid plans. Lastly, make sure that any phone service you're considering supports a Nano SIM card for your phone to operate. Just know that If you're using an older cell phone with a Micro SIM card it will not fit. However, this alone shouldn't be a problem. Most carriers provide a free SIM card or a new one at a very nominal cost. My phone didn't come with a SIM tool so I easily used a paper clip to open the SIM door on the phone to enter mine. I know I threw a lot of information out there to digest in only a single review. However, I believe knowledge is the key in selecting the right phone and carrier service. I hate it when I make a wrong decision due to lack of information. I encourage all Seniors out there to ditch your flip phones and get yourself the Moto E (2020). It's overall user friendly especially with Google Assistant. It's 100 % compatible with MOST EVERY cell phone service carrier out there in the US. Soooo..... I guess if I go on any further I'm just beating a dead horse here... huh? LOL How can a Senior on a fixed budget go wrong with this purchase. It's top rated by PC Magazine and Digital Trends. Check out their great reviews online. Heck, even a tightwad and proud of it, like consumer warrior Clark Howard loves Motorola phones. What's that I hear ? Yes of course, AARP members can also take this phone to Consumer Cellular with no problem. That's about it friends. I hope everyone enjoys their new phone. No matter which one you choose to buy :)

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I am a mobile apps developer. I purchased this phone with no intention whatsoever to use it as my daily phone, put to debug Android applications. For that purpose, it works great. But as I got used to the phone, I found myself liking it more and more, to the point where I ultimately removed my SIM card from my iPhone 7 (AT&T) and am now using the Moto G Fast as my primary device.

Compared to my aging iPhone 7, the battery life is great. I had almost forgotten that a smartphone could actually last the entire day without a recharge. The screen is also phenomenal at the price point. Granted, it does not get quite as bright as my iPhone 7 does (that phone actually hurts my eyes if I turn the brightness all the way up), but beyond that it's a great screen and the phone bezels basically do not exist.

Performance is great. I have noticed no slowdowns whatsoever, and I would rate it as being at least on-par with the iPhone 7. Now, the iPhone 7 is an older phone so that might not be saying a lot, but to me that phone is snappy as well. I am not doing any gaming or heavy tasks with these devices, so neither phone has slowdowns in my everyday usage.

I said I do not do much phone gaming, but I did test it out on a couple of games. I installed Minecraft, which runs great on the phone. The only issue I had is that i find the larger screen size uncomfortable to hold while playing a game in landscape mode such as Minecraft. Maybe uncomfortable is not the correct word, but there are instances where I have to let go of the phone with my right hand to tap on something towards the left side of the screen. Maybe it's just the way I hold it though, again I am not really a gamer. I also tested streaming my son's Xbox One to the phone using the Xbox app and a bluetooth controller, and it worked without issue.

Camera quality is hit or miss, possibly the only major con of the phone. If camera is your #1 concern then look elsewhere, of course if that is the case you probably are not shopping in this price range anyway. In well-lit conditions, the camera quality is about on par with my iPhone 7. In poor lighting though, pictures are not that great. It can theoretically record 4k video, but I honestly did not think that the 4k videos looked any better than the 1080p videos, so I kept the setting on 1080p.

Built in storage is a weak 32mb, but unlike many "high end" models out there, you can add a Micro SD card, making the low storage basically a non-issue. I put in an old 64gb card I had lying around, and you can have the phone format your card to use it as additional internal storage.

The phone charges via USB Type C, and charging seems fast enough, although I've really only had to charge it a few times in the week and a half I've had it, and I've done at it night time so the charge time was largely unnoticed and irrelevant. The phone also includes the illusive headphone jack, which is always welcome these days.

There is almost no bloatware included with this device, just a couple of Motorola apps. It is mostly stock Android with minor Motorola customizations. I installed an AT&T SIM card and I am getting good reception and good data speeds. WiFi connectivity is also good. I have not tested out hotspot tethering yet.

All in all, I am blown away by how much phone you can get now days at this price point. I was planning on upgrading to an iPhone 12, but I think I am going to stick with this cheap Motorola for the time being. For the price of a new iPhone, I could just get a brand new Motorola every single year for the next six years, at which point the iPhone would be long past due for a replacement anyway. If you are looking for a good budget phone, or even just a good phone period, I would save your money and not hesitate to get this thing. I don't see any reason whatsoever to shell out upwards to a thousand dollars (and even more now days) on a "flagship" phone, when a sub-200 phone works perfectly fine.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I come to Motorola’s G Stylus after a Samsung Droid Charge (a very aptly named power hog), a Note 3, and a Note 4. I use smart phones till they fail. In the case of the Notes, after they’ve failed several times: the Note 4 was the last Note model that was easily user serviceable.
After my middle-school son had good experiences with a couple of Motorola budget phones, I had decided I’d try that brand and give up the stylus. Then my Note 4 failed with a main board problem just after the 2020 G Stylus was introduced, so I didn’t have to.
Forgetting about the stylus for the moment, this is an incredible bargain for a smart phone. As far as technology’s ability to delight, it’s a great time we live in. I’m easily impressed because I’m comparing it to 4-year-old technology, but this thing is available for under $300, and for a brief while was available to new Verizon customers for $150. That is remarkable.
For that, you get great basic cell phone functionality, more than sufficient speed and storage, and okay (with hopes of better in time) stylus operation.
This is the first cell phone I’ve owned that I could charge up in the morning and have last the whole day without constantly plugging it in whenever and wherever I could find an outlet. In fact, to improve battery longevity, I only charge it to 80% capacity, and it’s still enough to do that. There’s been criticism of the G Stylus’ 4000 mAh battery compared to the G Power’s 5000, but that hasn’t been a factor for me.
Reception at the coast has been better than with Iphone 8 Plus and 11 Pro Max phones belonging to other family members. My phone is always the first to have a usable signal.
The fingerprint security is spot on. This is not the first phone I’ve had with that feature, but it’s the first where it could be relied on.
It is also absolutely wonderful to have a phone loud enough to play music or conference using speaker phone without an accessory speaker.
The three cameras give a lot of options. The Iphone owners in the family are probably right that their phone cameras are better. But this is plenty good enough for me, and an improvement over anything I’ve had. I’ve even found the macro camera useful. Haven’t used the panorama camera yet.
I’ve seen a couple of Youtube videos that persuade me the G Stylus will be user serviceable if/when the time comes, unlike some of the lower-end Motorolas. I’d rather not deal with adhesives at all, but I don’t think that’s a choice left to smart phone owners. If the battery or the USB port needs replacing or there’s water ingress, I could deal with that. Will parts be available as they’ve been with the Note phones? I’m not sure. Fewer G Styluses will be sold; the model life will be 12 months or so; and it’s so cheap many people will replace rather than fix a damaged phone. I have an Otterbox and sapphire glass on it, which has already survived a couple of drops on a concrete floor.
After two months, the few things less than ideal are:
- The display has neither the color subtlety or the ultimate brightness that Samsung OLED displays have long had. Use in bright sunlight is difficult. Elsewhere it’s just fine.
- Motorola’s minimalist version of Android is mostly a plus, especially since all the Samsung bloatware isn’t present. But I do really miss organizing apps into folders. I’ll look further for a work-around.
- Motorola’s stylus use doesn’t screen out palm touches as you write at the opposite side of the screen. Samsung’s implementations have done this so well and for so long that I’d never realized it was even necessary. This is really frustrating with the G Stylus. But I think it’s something Motorola could correct in software, and I hope they’ll do that.
- The stylus apps Motorola supplies are limited. I installed and am happy with Microsoft OneNote instead.
- I’ve mislaid the stylus a couple of times, as I did with my Samsung phones. Motorola and accessory vendors haven’t yet offered replacements.
A lot of what makes me happy with the G Stylus is due to maturing technology and packaging that now allows a well-executed feature-laden budget phone. But I still give Motorola a lot of credit for doing this.

One is left wondering why motorola has chosen to not publish the complete open source code to review so that a level of confidence and trust can be established. I might be paranoid, but I am old enough and have the experience and background to realize that when ANY tech company refuses to share important details about "security", there is likely some monkey business happening they don't want anyone to know about. Final: I like the phone. the build quality is good and seems just as durable as the old 2020 g power model. I don't regret buying this new model, but I was somewhat surprised that motorola and amazon do not advertise or even mention the think shield security. That does raise some red flags. So far, that is the only workaround. So much for "almost stock android"!

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I bought this phone to replace my Moto Z4 because the Z4 split in half along the left side of the phone and I could see the battery through the split.

I purchased this phone based upon price and a few reviews I read that complimented the phone. I have to say, the battery is outrageously good. I'm not sure why, but it compares like this. I always leave my phone in the kitchen when I go to bed. If I set my Z4 on the countertop with 100% battery at 8pm, and picked it up at 4am the next day, the battery would usually be at 80%, plus or minus. If I put the Moto G Power on the countertop at 8pm, and pick it up at 4am the next day, the battery is usually 95%, plus or minus.

During the normal work day, I plug in my phone on the way to work and take it back to 100 %. If I left the Moto Z4 unplugged at the office with regular use (texts, email checks, no social media) the battery would be at 60% by 1pm and I would plug it in at work for about an hour or so to get it back to 85/100% before leaving for home. The Moto G Power, with the same usage at work, will be at 92% at 1pm, and I don't have to plug it in at all until I leave for home and plug it in in the truck.

I have left the Moto G Power unplugged all day on a weekend and it barely goes under 90%. Maybe 85%, plus or minus. Could possibly be app related, but I don't know for sure. The only app I don't use on the new phone is the "News" app. Decided not to install it this time, but that's about it.

Even took this phone to Cheap Trick/Blue Oyster Cult concert here in SoCal and left with battery around 79% after Snaps and Instagram posts during the concert. Usually concerts would kill my phone battery or at the very least take the battery to 20% plus or minus.

Camera is okay. Not as sharp as the Moto Z4, and coloring could be better too, but it works. Selfies are great with the G Power as the lens is wider than the Z4.

Everything else works great for a $200 plus or minus phone. I highly recommend it for a value purchase

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Up until 4 years ago, I used Android, but AT&T offered me a "Customer Loyalty" deal for $50.00 a month and an iphone for .99 every two years.

I'm glad I tried it, but the iPhone was too finicky, and lord help you should you lock yourself out.

I now have a plan with another company which has unlimited everything; talk, data, wireless etc, all free for life.

As the iPhone was paid off, I did an early termination with AT&T and switched back Android and Motorola.

Motorola had always been a favorite of mine, and was thrilled when I could buy an unlocked Moto stylus 2021.

I've always wanted one but either unlocked or as part of a plan were out my reach.

I bought this on Amazon for an excellent price. All I had to do was put in the new SIM card and I was off and running.

This phone is packed with features you can actually use right away instead of having to seek out and unbury them like the iPhone.

While this is a big phone with an almost 7" screen it's comfortable to hold even with a heavy duty case.

Overall more than pleased, but there are a few caveats you should be aware of.

Face recognition is very spotty and have tried several times to redo it, but always with the same lackluster results.

Gave up on it and use the fingerprint unlock instead, though because of it's placement by the power key tends to throw it off sometimes.

2 Day Battery life. Are we talking about 24 hour days x 2 or 2 twelve hour days with actual phone use?

There is simply NO way you'll be getting anywhere near 48 hours (even factoring in sleep, downtime etc.)

Battery life is very good; I can get a 8:00 A.M. to 10:00 P.M (14 hours +-) with fairly heavy use, but you better be sure you charge it overnight.

Out of habit I carry a 20,000 power pack in my laptop case, or a slim "It will get you through" in my suit jacket pocket.

As I told a friend of mine "Any phone can claim a 2 or even 3 day battery life... Provided you don't turn it on much or actually use it for what you bought it for."

It's a very good phone, feature packed with a big enough, but not too cumbersome screen and more than adequate battery life. Just not 2 days worth.

Order arrived early, in original packaging and well packed for transportation.

I do employ some of the power saving features such as power save @ 50% and black screen when practical.

I love the phone, and use the stylus constantly, which
