As a customer who purchased the Motorola Moto G Stylus 2021, I can say that overall, this smartphone is a great value for the price. The 2-day battery life is a big pro, as it's convenient for those who are on-the-go and don't want to constantly charge their phone. The 4/128GB memory capacity also allows for plenty of storage for all your apps, photos, and files.

The 48MP camera is another huge pro, as it takes clear and vibrant photos. The stylus feature is also a nice touch, and can be useful for taking notes or drawing on the screen. I appreciated that the phone is unlocked and made for use in the US, which adds to its versatility and flexibility.

However, there are a few cons to note. One is that the phone's overall performance can be sluggish at times, especially with multiple apps open. The phone's design is also somewhat bulky and outdated, which may not appeal to some users who prefer a sleeker, more modern design. Additionally, while the camera is great for photos, it struggles with low-light shots.

Overall, the Motorola Moto G Stylus 2021 is a solid smartphone with some attractive features, but it's not without its drawbacks. If you're looking for a mid-range phone with a good camera and long battery life, this could be a great option for you.

I just needed to upgrade my phone. I used to have a moto g7 plus and it was starting to freeze, glitch, and was lacking storage space. I deleted hundreds of media files, pictures, apps, and backed up downloads, but no matter my efforts, my phone was still low on storage. It also said that my phone was susceptible to viruses (like every piece of technology is) so I downloaded an anti-virus software, a VPN, and a number of other apps that had reviews promising to fix the problem, but it didn't do anything for me. An upgrade was my last option.
This newer moto is so much better! It includes a stylus, a better camera, more storage space, and it accepts the sim card from my previous moto so it was a steal. I'm still waiting on the case, but I got the camera and screen protector and they work like a charm. Everything was included and I was able to transfer all of my apps, backgrounds, and backed up photos and contacts from my last phone without any trouble. I still have to sign into everything and remember passwords, but luckily I found a notepad app that backed up all my passwords to the cloud so that isn't a problem either.
I'm still waiting to see if the 2 day battery holds up. So far from what I've seen, the battery drains pretty fast. It goes down about 2% every 5 minutes. I haven't charged the phone since I unpackaged it, but the rate that the battery is draining isn't very promising.
Despite that one minor setback, the phone is great and has worked perfectly for everything else. It's so much more refreshing to have a phone that will take pictures without glitching and deleting them or can open websites without completely exiting google and sending me to my home screen.
Overall, I'm happy with the purchase. I hope this phone has a couple of years in it so I don't have to upgrade again any time soon.

Edit: the phone goes through a software update every single night and I have to restart it every single morning. I thought I would wait to see if it only updated because of all the new sign ins and media I had to add, but it hasn't stopped. I'm not too unhappy because updates aren't bad, it's just getting frustrating having to constantly restart the phone and wait for the update to finish before I can use my phone for the day. Which also means some of my alarms get delayed and it's mildly inconvenient.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This has turned out to be a great buy, and it DOES work on Verizon. (More about that in a bit) Purchased it on Prime Day to replace an old Samsung Note 2 that my wife was using.. Did not realize it did not come with a SIM card, so did not order one.

While the phone will not work on Verizon without the SIM card, it will do everything else except calls and text messages connected to wi-fi. So I used that to get it set up. I logged into her Google account and everything from her existing phone loaded on the new phone, easy breezy. The Device Help app that comes loaded on the phone is super helpful. I am using a Moto Z Play, and in setting up the new Moto X I learned some new things for my own phone.

Now for Verizon. We have gone to prepaid plans and are saving a lot of money, but the service is not the same. I went on the website to read how to activate a bring your own phone but kept getting to dead ends. I could find no way to get my questions answered, and tried calling twice, only to have the call dropped both times. So I read the Amazon on-line reviews and found a variety of experience in activating it with Verizon... some easy and some that never worked, with some saying that this phone will not work with Verizon. After reading all the reviews I decided to try the local Verizon store for the SIM card, rather than ordering it online, or going to Best Buy which would be 40 miles away. The Note 2 uses a micro Sim card, and the MotoX4 uses a nano SIM card, so I could not use the old one.

The local store did sell me a nano SIM card for $10.00 BUT said they would take no responsibility for it working. They claimed that only about 50% of phone bought on Amazon would work on Verizon, and that as of June 30th, 2018, Verizon was no longer allowing activation of some phones because of the coming move to 5G. The did not offer to try to activate it for a fee and I did not ask them to.

Came home, followed the instructions in the Device Help app to inset the Nano Sim Card and a 64GB memory card purchased from Amazon, no problem. Logged onto My Verizon, and indicated that I wanted to switch the device on that line. It said to input the ID number for the new VERIZON device... but by then I had learned that they would want the IME number that is printed on the MOTOX box. I gave that, and no problem.
The they wanted the SIM card ID number. Fortunately another review said to save the packaging for this number, which I had done... but there were 4 numbers on the packaging and Verizon was no help in showing how to find it. So I googled and found that the SIM ID number would be 20 digits long, and only one of the numbers fit that. I put it in and it worked. The website asked me to confirm that I wanted to switch devices, and I did. It said it might take as much as 15 minutes for their records to update. DONE! Works perfectly!

If you think you have to be tech savvy to do this, I'm an 80-year old not so tech savvy guy...but willing to keep looking until I find an answer. You can do this.

Bottom line, for under $250 I have a wonderful phone that does everything we want and more, on an affordable plan ($40.00 a month prepaid with 6GB data) on a good network, with 96GB of memory. NOT Bad! I won't repeat details of the phone that have been covered in other reviews and yes, you will want at least a minimal case... it is VERY slippery, and probably a screen protector, but it is a super phone that will hold its own against ones that cost 4 times as much.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I had a Motorola Moto X Pure phone for 3.5 years, when I dropped it and cracked the screen. Until then, I really liked it. I replaced it with this Motorola Moto G7, thinking it would be about the same, only a little faster and better. For the money, the Moto G7 is a really good phone. It has a beautiful display, is nicely responsive and does everything at least at a good level. I'm not on my phone a lot, but I do use some features such as Fitbit, the camera, music playing, e-mail, YouTube videos, the phone and texting. I also occasionally use my phone for audio recording.

My bottom line is that I liked my Moto X Pure better, mostly because I thought it took better photos. Photos with the Moto G7 are okay, but seem to lack the snap that older phone's photos had.

Otherwise, the Moto G7 has worked well for me. The phone sounds excellent, watching YouTube videos on the big 6.2-inch screen is good (and there is plenty of volume in a quiet room), and it is great for texting, music playing and all the typical stuff.

One thing that really surprised me about the Moto G7 was that it does not have a standard micro-USB port for charging and data exchange -- it has a USB-C port. This really caught me by surprise, and I still am somewhat disappointed that it does not have a micro-USB port, since I have micro-USB cables and chargers everywhere. Since the Moto G7 uses USB-C, I had to go out and buy adapters and cables so that I could charge the G7 in a variety of convenient places. I like that USB-C connectors are easy to insert (you don't have to guess on which way to insert it) but the phone came with only one USB-C cable. It would have been nice to come with a cable and a couple of adapters to eliminate charging anxiety.

I typically charge my phone every morning, charging it to 100 percent every day. When I plug the Moto G7 into the charger in the morning, it is usually down to 82 to 85 percent, which seems a little low to me for my relatively light use.

Otherwise, the Moto G7 is a nice phone for the $250 or so I paid for it. I've never had a pricey Samsung or Apple phone, but they cost $400 to $700 more than the Moto G7. The Moto G7 looks and feels good, and it works well -- I can't imagine paying 2 or 3 times the price to get just a little more functionality. It's just not worth it to me.

The Motorola Moto G7 is not perfect, but it's pretty good... I recommend it.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Alright, so I’ve had the new Pixel 10 Pro for about a week now, and I’ve finally gathered my thoughts. Let me just say, this thing feels less like a phone and more like some gadget from a sci-fi movie.
First off, taking it out of the box, it just feels premium. It has a nice weight to it—not too heavy, but it feels solid and well-built. The matte finish on the back is a lifesaver for someone like me who hates fingerprints. The screen is the real star, though. It’s a big 6.7-inch display, and everything just looks incredible on it. Scrolling is buttery smooth, and watching videos is a treat. It’s super bright too, so I had no trouble seeing it outside, even in the afternoon sun.
But let's be real, you buy a Pixel for the camera, and this one is just insane. I took it out over the weekend, and I’m blown away. The main camera takes ridiculously sharp and colorful photos without you having to do anything. But the feature I can't stop playing with is the "Pro Res Zoom." I was at a park and saw a cool bird way up in a tree. Normally, that would just be a blurry mess on my old phone. With this, I zoomed all the way in, and the photo is actually sharp enough to see the details on its feathers. It feels like magic.
Google's AI stuff is all over this phone. They have this new feature called "Magic Cue" that tries to guess what you need. At first, it was a little weird, but now I’m getting used to it. Like, when I was heading to a meeting, it popped up a notification with the address and traffic info without me even asking. Another fun one is "Nano Banana"—silly name, I know—but it's this cool photo effect tool that lets you create some really artistic shots. Some of the results are a bit out there, but it's genuinely fun to mess around with.
Performance-wise, it's a beast. The new Tensor G5 chip makes everything feel instant. Apps open right away, and I haven't seen a single stutter, even when I'm jumping between a bunch of different apps. The battery life has been solid too. I'm a pretty heavy user—lots of photos, social media, and some videos—and I've been easily getting through a full day with some juice to spare.
So, is it worth it? It’s definitely not cheap, but if you're someone who loves taking pictures and wants a phone that feels like it’s one step ahead of you, I'd say absolutely. The Pixel 10 Pro isn't just a phone with a great camera; it’s a genuinely smart device that makes everyday tasks a little bit easier and a lot more fun. I'm still discovering new things it can do, and I'm honestly excited to see what else I find

text:
I have owned many high-end phones over the years, but the Pixel 10 Pro XL in the 256GB Moonstone version is the first one I genuinely do not want to put down. After two weeks of heavy daily use that includes photo editing on the go, 4K video calls, and constant work sessions with Gemini, it has already exceeded my expectations.

The 6.8 inch Actua Display is excellent. The 120Hz refresh rate makes every swipe feel smooth, and the colors are vibrant enough to make Netflix and YouTube feel almost cinematic. The Tensor G5 chip combined with 16GB of RAM handles real multitasking with ease. I can edit RAW photos in Lightroom while listening to podcasts and the phone stays fast and responsive. The 5200mAh battery easily lasts through a full day of mixed use, and the included 45W charger brings it to about 70 percent in about thirty minutes.

The cameras are another highlight. The long range zoom produces impressively clear images, and the AI support through Gemini offers helpful suggestions that consistently improve quick snapshots. Both the fingerprint sensor and the face unlock respond instantly. The IP68 protection handled an accidental splash without a single issue. WiFi 7 keeps my video calls stable, and the stereo speakers sound fuller than I expected for a phone of this size.

After using many flagship phones over the years, this one feels different. It genuinely boosts productivity and day to day convenience. If you are upgrading from anything released before 2024, this is a phone that truly feels like a meaningful step forward. I have zero regrets so far.

A slim protective case works perfectly with the XL size and keeps the grip comfortable.

text:
I honestly LOVE this phone! For anyone looking for a "dumb" phone that focuses solely on calling and texting, this is the one! It does everything I need it to do and doesn't have any useless preloaded apps. The build quality is truly excellent, and I can tell that a lot of care and precision has gone into the design. The buttons feel so great to press and are very precise. The software is intuitive and well thought out. Most importantly, it has great reception for texting and calling on the Ting network (which uses Tmobile). On occasion there are a few areas where the menus are a bit convoluted, but I don't mind.

Some specific things I really like about this phone: you can choose between predictive text or regular old school texting, which I prefer; you can customize the screen lock so it only activates when pressing the "end call" button; you can longpress the zero key to turn on the flashlight; you can plug it into your PC and add custom ringtones; you can customize the function of the left and right buttons; you can also set specific times for it to automatically power on and off, which extends battery life. On a full charge so far I have had it on for five days and it still has three of five bars left on the battery icon.

Some people have complained about the camera, but I found it to be entirely adequate. Sure, it won't take the best pictures in the world, but it gets the job done when it needs to, which for me is what matters most. In terms of size it's perhaps slightly larger than I would prefer, but that also makes the buttons easier to press, so I don't mind. The last feature phone I had was the ZTE Cymbal U, and this AGM M9 puts that to shame. THIS IS A TRULY EXCELLENT PHONE!!

TL;DR: A solid no-frills rugged feature phone, but T-Mobile network only.

I've used this AGM M9 a few times now and it does exactly what it says. It appears to be made of high quality materials and the value is solid for what you're getting.

The buttons are large, fonts are easy to read, and the call volume is loud and clear. It supposedly holds up to IP68/IP69K water and dust protection and can survive drops up to about 6 feet (1.8m), which is reassuring for anyone working outdoors or in rough conditions 💪

No Wi-Fi, no apps, no distractions. Just calls, texts, FM radio, and a music player. Honestly refreshing in a world where your phone judges you for screen time 📻

Now the big thing: this phone is fine if you already have a T-Mobile based carrier voice plan in place or in mind. The compatibility with other carriers is the main drawback. Don't skip that part of the listing.

One useful tip: activate your new SIM card in a different phone first before inserting it into the M9 to avoid setup headaches 🔋

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
In a nutshell, this is a great phone to just make and receive calls and that can last several days on a single charge. It comes with some extra features that are rare even on high end phones like the ability to automatically record conversations and an FM radio.

The phone is large enough to fit very comfortable in my hand. It's light for its size and feels like the plastic would be able to flex a bit before breaking if dropped. It comes with 2 removeable batteries that are oddly small (1000 mAh) compared to the size of the phone. Each gives several days of light use on a single charge.
Opening the phone to insert a SIM and micro-SD card requires a bit of force. I used a T-Mobile SIM that I had previously used in a smartphone. The phone connected immediately and displayed a text message from the network stating that the device had limited support, but it has been working well so far, including calling, sending SMS/MMS, and even some very limited internet use. Sounds quality is good but could be better when in speaker mode.
The user interface is very simple and basic. Keys are large and comfortable to use. It works well with Bluetooth headphones and charges with a standard USB-C charger.
There are a few pleasant surprises when exploring the configuration menu. A setting allows you to record conversations (when enabled, you get a prompt at the start of each call to confirm if you want to record). There is also an FM radio that also allows you to record a program and listen to it later. There is even a hidden Opera mini web browser (that will appear if you open a text message that contains a web address).
I haven't figured out an effective way to input text on the phone, something you'll need to store contacts, as the phone tries to predict what words you'll type but overriding wrong predictions requires a lot of scrolling left/right.
The screen and camera are both very low resolution, and while the phone can technically take and display pictures, I'm not sure I'd ever want to do that. You can send these low-quality pictures via MMS.
It has been a very long time since I used a simple "candy bar" phone.
The phone is technically unlocked but only supports one operator according to the listing. At $50 at time of order, the price is in line with similar phones, but cheaper that getting a phone directly from the carrier.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I have always been a die-hard fan of the Motorola Razr V3 and V3i.
Back in the day, and even still nowadays, this phone has always been more successful for its thin, groundbreaking and futuristic design than for its technical features.

(Note : This highly upgraded Razr V3 has been manufactured by Vortex Cellulars in 2024, and sold on Amazon until the end of the year 2025. Now it's designed with no brand whatsoever (Generic).
I made this review for the Vortex V3, so I thought it would be convenient and interesting to share it again for potential buyers).

When I saw the V3, I instantly loved it !

I LOVED :
- The V3 is unlocked and works on all carriers (I live in France, and I'm using it on SFR, one of the 4 major phone carriers).
- The design is completely true to the original Motorola Razr V3. It has been upgraded with this beautiful Galaxy Gray color (even if it is all plastic, which makes it lighter than the original Razr).
- The micro-USB port has been replaced by a USB-C port at the exact same spot.
- The screen size has also been upgraded.
- The connectivity still offers the Bluetooth, and they added the WIFI.
- The storage capacity of 16Gb (expandable with a memory card up to 64 Gb).
- The multimedia player (music and video)
- The real internet browser (upgrade of the poor little WAP browser of 2004).
- The camera with its 3 definition levels (VGA, 2 Megapixels, 5 Megapixels) is very decent too.
- The menu is very intuitive and the apps are easily accessible.
- There is an economic mode which allows to extend the battery life of 1000mAh, and I managed to extend it to more than 3 days without charging, because I use this phone exactly like I used the Motorola Razr V3/V3i : no browsing, no music, no video. Simply because the screen is not designed for this.

I HATED :
- There are 3 pre-installed apps (Facebook, WhatsApp, Google App Store) which I personally didn't want, and they can only be deactivated, not uninstalled from the phone (unless you install ADB and remove the apps which you don't want, but I strongly advise to not tamper with the original Launcher, otherwise you might lose the ability to make phone calls,...
- It took me some time to find how to switch between the writing modes R9, ABC, Abc, abc, 123 (FYI : exactly with the same button as in the original Razr). I even installed the TT9 but removed it as soon as I found how to switch modes.
- The backlight of the keypad only illuminates the symbols and numbers, but doesn't include the famous iconic blue luminescence of the Razr.

I am sad that the company Vortex Cellular discontinued the Vortex V3, but I am really glad that the legacy is being taken care of by Generic, and sold on Amazon at the price of $44,99, because this legendary phone hasn't lost its sexiness, beauty and class 💎💎💎

Since the processor is not the strongest, the battery tends to last a long time. Providing a good screen on time. I did not use face unlock, but the finger print scanner is extremely fast and provides a good and accurate readings.
The screen is very smooth to scroll and I was surprised to find 120 hz display option. It looked really our of place in this budget phone.
VOLTE with TELUS will not work, because of TELUS whitelist policy and I do not blame UMIDIGI for that. Overall, this is a very decent phone that ca be used by seniors or international travelers as it offers multiple convenient options without breaking the bank.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I’m going to be brutally honest — this phone is impressive for what it is. The UMIDIGI Note 100 is a performance-packed budget device that makes you seriously question why anyone’s still paying $1,000 for a mainstream flagship. But while the hardware speaks for itself, the seller’s misleading information and silence on crucial limitations make this purchase a minefield for the average buyer.

Let’s talk about what works first — and then we’ll get into the problems they’re conveniently glossing over.

✅ The Positives — Why I Still Recommend This Phone
8GB of RAM (plus virtual memory support)
This phone absolutely chews through multitasking. App switching is fluid, background processes don’t constantly reload, and basic gaming is handled with ease. This alone puts it lightyears ahead of most other phones in the same price range.

128GB storage with microSD support
Storage is generous and expandable — a feature most major brands have killed off in the name of profit. I appreciate having control over my own storage again.

All-day battery life
Even with moderate to heavy use, this device lasts. The power efficiency is clearly dialed in.

Clean, bloat-free Android experience
No weird overlays. No carrier bloat. No unwanted apps draining performance. It's Android the way it should be — clean, smooth, and responsive.

Unlocked GSM bands
I activated my SIM card from a $70 prepaid AT&T Samsung phone, then popped it into this UMIDIGI. Result? Flawless calling, texting, data, and even VoLTE — despite the device not being “certified.” This trick won’t be obvious to everyone, but it’s a power move once you understand how to sidestep carrier gatekeeping.

Dual SIM support
Useful for anyone juggling personal and work lines, international travel, or data-only SIMs.

⚠️ The Technical Drawbacks (That You’ll Never See Mentioned in the Listing)
Wi-Fi Signal is Weak
Here’s a big one: Wi-Fi performance is underwhelming. Even sitting just one room away from the router, signal strength drops noticeably. Streaming and basic tasks remain usable, but speeds degrade, and latency-sensitive tasks like video calls can suffer. This points to a weak internal antenna design — a common flaw in budget phones, but nowhere in this listing does the seller even hint at it.

Camera is functional, not impressive
It gets the job done in daylight, but low-light shots and video clarity leave a lot to be desired. It’s acceptable, not exceptional.

Speaker quality is flat and tinny
Loud enough to hear, but not enjoyable. Headphones or external speakers are a must for any media.

Not Verizon-compatible
This is GSM only. No CDMA support, which means no Verizon, no Visible, no luck. You wouldn’t know that unless you already understand the U.S. mobile landscape. And again — the seller says nothing.

🔥 Now Let’s Talk About the Seller — and Why This Listing is Misleading
Here’s the part that genuinely annoys me: the seller is either completely out of touch with the U.S. mobile market or willfully omitting critical information — and neither is acceptable.

This phone is not carrier-certified in the U.S., and they don’t make that clear. They list all the supported LTE bands, but fail to explain that band support ≠ full compatibility. In the U.S., phones need to be whitelisted for VoLTE and network access — especially on AT&T and Verizon. If you just drop your SIM in and expect it to work, you’re in for a rude surprise.

They don’t warn you that you might need to activate your SIM in another phone first, or that your new SIM could get rejected entirely. They don’t disclose that AT&T can block unsupported IMEIs at any time. They don’t even address the Verizon/Visible incompatibility, which is a flat-out dealbreaker for many buyers.

And let’s not forget the Wi-Fi signal issues, which are very real and not acknowledged anywhere in the product description. That’s not an oversight — that’s intentional omission to make the phone sound flawless.

🎯 The Bottom Line
Here’s the truth: if you know what you’re doing — if you understand how to work around AT&T’s activation requirements, and you don’t mind dealing with a few signal quirks — this phone is a phenomenal value. The performance is real. The RAM, storage, and software experience are excellent for the price.

But if you’re a regular consumer just looking for a plug-and-play solution? You’re not getting the full picture from this listing — and the seller clearly has no intention of helping you get there.

Buy this phone if you’re tech-savvy and want power on a budget. Avoid it if you expect full U.S. carrier support out of the box. And sellers — do better. People deserve the truth, not marketing spin.

It's a little hard to judge a phone on initial impressions since so much of what makes a phone good takes time to figure out; battery life, reception, etc. I'm not planning on using this connected to a cell network, just as kind of a little tablet, so unfortunately I can't say anything about network compatability. What I can say is that I did give it a run down on wifi and here's what I found:
Good - Youtube videos and basic web browsing run just fine. It doesn't get hot trying to do these basic tasks, and an hour used about 15% of the battery. -It has a fingerprint scanner, which isn't something I'm used to seeing on super-budget phones.
-Updates. The OS was patched recently and there was a new hardware revision ready to upgrade to. Neutral - The build quality. It doesn't feel amazing; I have a Umidigi tablet and it shares the same rough edges, but the case is sturdy and doesn't flex. If you use the included protector, you don't notice the roughness and itfeels sturdy.
- The size and screen. The phone is actually a little larger than my 2024 Moto Stylus, but the screen is about the same size. It has a bit of a 'chin' on it. -The screen. It claims 90hz but it doesn't feel like 90hz; it could be that the processor isn't up to driving a fast screen, but it feels much choppier, closer to 50. That said the colors are vibrant and the screen is bright; the blacks are dark and the viewing angle is very wide.
-The OS. It uses Android 14 Go, not full Android. Some software may not work.
Bad
- While using the ui is snappy enough, it does get notacably laggy at points. Most obviously swiping down the top screen menu.
- Very slow charging. The charging is so slow that when I was using it while plugged in, the battery percentage was actually going down.
- Terrible camera. Just bad. Blurry, noisy, essentially unsuable. - Only 2.4ghz wifi - there doesn't appear to be any 5ghz wifi functionality at all.

少し古いですが、グーグルのAndroidなので、アプリの種類や数に関しては全く問題ありません。

値段を考えたら、かなり優秀なスマホです。

子どものスマホとしてや、特定の用途で使用したいAndroidスマホを探している方にはかなりおすすめできます。

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
There are dozens of these Android Auto/Apple Carplay screens out on the market. Most are short and long but I wanted one with more screen area so I went with the IK9 and it does not disappoint! If you have an older car that does not have an infotainment screen and/or a back up camera - this is a must get! (Note: This is not a free product review - I purchased this product from Amazon just a few days ago)

1. Price: For just around $100, you're not just getting wireless Android Auto/Apple Carplay, but you're getting a 64 GB SD card (you can always upgrade for more space) so your dash cam can record right out of the box, a front facing dash cam (with wireless connectivity to pull down clips), and a back up camera (which also records). That is insane! For comparison, my other two cars have two-way dash cameras in them (neither came with SD cards), and neither was close to this price.

2. Quality: From the package, down to the tools used to install - nothing feels cheap about this system. Touch screen is extremely responsive and picture is great. What surprised me the most was the picture quality on the back-up camera. It is heads and tails above the built in camera on my brand new Honda Civic.

3. Installation: If you've ever installed a dash camera in your car, this is exactly the same. So long as you're comfortable popping off interior panels, pulling off the car door gaskets, and snaking wires behind airbags (all extremely simple), this is a job that takes no time at all. From start to finish - I think it took me about 2 hours. The only step that might cause some DIYers pause is tying in the back-up camera to your rear reverse lights (so that the screen switches to the back up camera automatically when you reverse). This is really simple though. Just head to YouTube, find out how to remove your tail light, and find the positive wire to the reverse light and then all you need is a razor blade (to expose the wire) and some electrical tape and you're good to go. I would strongly recommend not skipping this step so that you do not have to manual switch to the camera every time you head in reverse.

4. Connectivity: Simple and easy. Just followed the on screen instructions and my phone was connected and Android Auto was up and running in seconds. I had some trouble connecting the unit's sound to my car via BT (I think my car's BT might actually be the problem), but I just switched to the FM transmitter and it's perfect - crystal clear!

Overall: This has only been in our car (2008 Ford Focus) for a day, but it has already transformed it into a modern day vehicle. Most importantly, since my sons will likely be driving this car one day, the addition of a back-up camera is great and gives me peace of mind. If you're tired of relying on your phone for navigation or you do not have a back-up camera - this is an easy and affordable way to bring your car into the 21st century. Highly recommend!

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I wanted to upgrade my car with the latest screen tech but I found replacing it with a aftermarket stereo was very expensive with all the adapters and backup camera required to keep things looking and working stock. The IK9 covers just about all the boxes in a compact solution and low cost. I gave it a 4 star due to some issues I had with the device. Some I was able to overcome and others I was not but still find this to be a huge upgrade for my and extremely happy with the results.

In the box:
Inside the box you get the screen, a window mount, dash mount , backup camera (tied to wire), a 32G micro SD card (inserted in screen), double sticky for the backup camera, the manual, and a little plastic tool to shove wiring into the wide panels while routing it. All the things you need to install and setup the screen. It's all packed nice, neat, and it's sealed. So you know it's new and not someone else's return. Pay attention to the plastic on the screen, it has instructions to extend your warranty, I didn't pay attention and peeled it off.

Wiring up:
All the connections are on the left side of the screen, so it's best to run the wiring from the drivers side. you will have to remove panels in one form or another in the trunk to run the camera (you can purchase a panel removal tool). There is no direct power wiring for the device, so you have to use the 12VDC adapter to power it. The adapter has a USB -A port to power your phone and it states you can also do Android Auto via wire that way too. I found the red cable for the backup camera you tie to the Positive on the backup light was a bit too short by about a foot. That cable was run more direct and didn't follow the path of my stock wiring harnesses. It won't snag but I would prefer to run it with other wiring to keep them together. I was able to route the backup camera easily from the trunk to the front dash, tucking it under the floor panels. The backup camera provides double sticky tape, but not a license plate bracket. I bought the license plate bracket to mount the backup camera to. I'm not a fan of using double sticky tape, it doesn't always hold. The third party bracket is also stainless steel, so it's more resistant to rust. The camera mounted to the bracket easily and has a clean look to it.

The screen plugs into the DC plug without issue and powered up. I did use a 3.5mm cable and ran it to the AUX port on my car, allowing the car speakers to be used. Though you do have options to connect you car's Bluetooth or FM radio modulator from the screen. The music sounded great but calls were a bit gritty, I luckily had a ground loop adapter to reduce noise, I added that to the AUX cable, and the calls come in perfect now.

Operation:

Android Auto (Only Tested this version):
I synced my Android phone to the screen. It took seconds for it to connect both Bluetooth and WIFI (its required). It does take a minute or so for it to connect to your phone after starting the card but I consider that engine warm up time. Android Auto has some settings you can select on the screen itself and others on your phone. Make sure to check them all to see how you want the operation to work. Android Auto interface is limited to only certain apps on your phone, for safety. Though the VLC app I use to play music is allowed so it's all good there.

I am able to take and make calls without issue and they sound perfectly clear. This is a good thing as the Bluetooth on my car radio died and left me holding my phone while on calls, not safe. This is completely hands free now. I decided not to view text messages on the screen to keep it safer and less distracting, I also muted text notifications, keeps from constant pinging. Those can wait for when i'm not actively driving

The screen provides front camera, back camera, or view of both while you drive. Both views are recorded onto the MicroSD card while the screen is on. I find that to be a nice feature to ensure everything is recorded while you drive. You can also record voice inside the vehicle but you can mute that, I did. If you want GPS tracking or enter a location on the screen, it will mute music while it provides direction. There is a nifty button that floats on the screen when you are in Android Auto that lets return you to the Main screen for any reason. The screen is really bright so I'm running it at 70% during the day and 2% at night. You can enter the times you want it to switch between day/night, it's not automatic.

The backup camera is crystal clear. You also have the ability to adjust the backup lines width and depth. You can only adjust the whole line, not the colors separately. My red line marker starts about 3 feel from the car but know when to stop. When I first installed the backup camera the view was the opposite. There is an option in settings to mirror the backup view to make it normal but sometimes it would return. I used the company's self help guide and ended up updating the firmware (pay close attention to the steps). The backup camera works flawlessly now. Music will mute while you are backing up as well, it's a nice touch to be less distracting.

This comes with a front camera that is mounted on the screen. Which is a plus as some don't come with it. You can pull the camera a bit higher for a better view but still fell short from where I mounted the screen, so my front upper dash is visible. That's on me, not the screen, for the cost I'm not complaining. The front camera comes in real clean and the screen records both front and back camera while you are driving. So this is a huge plus while taking trips or ever needed in court.

I was about ready to return this, because it would never automatically reconnect, in Android Auto, or Android Cast modes. But I discovered that it needs to lose power and regain power to automatically reconnect. My car's socket stays on when the car is off. (2008 Pontiac GXP) Guess I need to figure out how to work around that. Rufus gave me a few suggestions:
"Great troubleshooting! You've identified the root cause—the screen needs a power cycle to reconnect. Here are some practical workarounds for your 2008 Pontiac GXP's always-on socket:

Use a smart power switch: Install an inline automotive relay or timer switch that cuts power after the car is turned off. These are relatively affordable and straightforward to install.
Switch to ACC power: If possible, wire the screen to your car's ACC (accessory) power circuit instead, which powers down when the ignition is off. A professional installer can help if you're not comfortable doing this yourself.
Manual disconnect: Use a quick-disconnect adapter or inline switch you can physically flip when exiting the car.
USB power bank workaround: If the screen supports USB power, you could use a portable battery that you disconnect when parking (less convenient but requires no installation).
Since you maintain your own vehicles, you may be comfortable tackling a relay installation yourself. The parts are inexpensive ($15-30), and there are plenty of YouTube guides for automotive relay wiring.

This fix should save you from returning the screen—glad you found the solution!"

title: 3.0 out of 5 stars
text: Seems pretty good, but my card doesn't have a cigarette lighter, and the only switched USB port is a USB-C. Unfortunately it doesn't work connected to a USB-C source because the unit was made very cheaply and tied both of the CC pins of the USB-C circuitry together, which is not valid for the USB-C specification, so the car and other power devices wouldn't turn on. I ended up opening up the device, lifting one of the CC pins, and tying a 5.1k ohm resistor between that pin and ground, and now the unit powers up fine when connected to a USB-C port. They could have literally spend 1/10th of a cent more to add another 5.1k ohm resistor and it would have worked fine.

text:
What a clever, practical and awesome device!

I love the small size and portability of this flexible (legs) tripod. And my iPhone 15 Plus fits beautifully, even with the case on!

But what I may love as much, or even more, is the tiny remote (clicker) I paired with my phone.

So cool to just “click” the button, and it takes your photo! Just click away!!

You don’t need to run to your phone ever to set the self-timer. And works just as great when taking a selfie, again, no need to use the self-timer (if you have your remote handy or close by.)

And it’s super easy to pair ( Bluetooth) with your phone. Took maybe 30-60 seconds to connect, and now it’s permanently paired with my iPhone! Of course this is wireless, so WiFi must be around somewhere in your home or outdoors, to use the remote clicker.

But I bought the small tripod itself specifically to take a Passport photo (from an approved app), so I will need to stand back around 5 feet in front of the camera. That way, I can first take picture after picture, if I want, until I find the one I like best and upload that picture to the Passport app (which approves your picture (or not) initially - and if the app approves your pic, it changes your uploaded photo to an all white background (and brightens or lightens the photo to Passport standards), AND crops your photo to proper Passport sizing; how terrific is that?

And the tripod’s small, flexible legs are so practical - I will be attaching mine to my blinds, that are on a window that provides great, natural light for picture taking. It will be great to bend (contort, ha) the legs at the correct height, for me to then stand 5 feet away at the correct distance and angle for picture taking.

Can’t wait to looking beautiful again with my new (renewed) Passport - thanks to a wonderful, easy app I discovered AND with this flexible tripod with remote control.

NOTE TO MANUFACTURER: If there is any criticism, the instructions you receive in the box are terrible, lol. They send in multiple languages and the English part is just poorly instructed in general. And nothing that explains the wireless remote and pairing process - or not in an understandable manner..

Fortunately, I’m tech savvy enough to figure out or do a quick Google search, but the manufacturer needs to re-write the paper instructions you receive. And the video online is great to showcase how the tripod works in general (super easy to set up), but they need to show someone pairing with their phone and then taking pics with the remote - please add to your “how to” video - you’ll get even more sales that way ;-)

But the product itself is an A+. Thank you!

Snappy Shots Made Easy: A Quick Love Letter to My New Bluetooth Shutter

I’ve been hunting for a hassle‑free way to capture steady selfies and group shots without constantly tapping the screen, and this little Bluetooth remote hit the sweet spot. The moment I paired the sleek red and white units with my iPhone, the connection was instantaneous—thanks to Bluetooth 5.2, there’s virtually no lag, even when I’m a few feet away. The app‑free setup is a breath of fresh air; just press the power button, hit “pair” on your phone, and you’re ready to snap.

What makes these two‑pack remotes a real win is the thoughtful extras. Each button comes with its own wrist strap, so I can keep it on my wrist while I’m jogging through a park or dancing at a party without worrying about misplacing it. The button itself feels solid yet lightweight, with a satisfying click that lets me know a photo or video has been triggered. I’ve used it for everything from time‑lapse videos of sunrise hikes to quick group selfies at birthday gatherings, and the results are consistently crisp—no more blurry fingers or shaky frames.

Battery life is another pleasant surprise. The tiny coin cell powers each remote for weeks on a single press, and the battery compartment slides open and shut without any fiddly tools. I appreciate that the designers chose a battery‑powered solution over a rechargeable one—no more hunting for a charger when you’re out shooting. The red and white color scheme adds a fun pop of personality, and I’ve even found myself using the red button for “photo mode” and the white for “video mode,” a little trick that keeps my workflow organized.

All in all, the Wireless Camera Remote Shutter feels like a small but mighty accessory that upgrades my smartphone photography without breaking the bank. It’s reliable, easy to use, and comes with all the little conveniences (like the wrist strap) that make it feel premium. If you love taking photos on the go and want to ditch the awkward arm‑reach, these two remotes are definitely worth the buy.

I appreciate that the designers chose a battery‑powered solution over a rechargeable one—no more hunting for a charger when you’re out shooting. The red and white color scheme adds a fun pop of personality, and I’ve even found myself using the red button for “photo mode” and the white for “video mode,” a little trick that keeps my workflow organized.

All in all, the Wireless Camera Remote Shutter feels like a small but mighty accessory that upgrades my smartphone photography without breaking the bank. It’s reliable, easy to use, and comes with all the little conveniences (like the wrist strap) that make it feel premium. If you love taking photos on the go and want to ditch the awkward arm‑reach, these two remotes are definitely worth the buy.

El único problema que tiene es que la punta se desenrosca con el uso y de repente falla hasta que la vuelves a enroscar un poco. Eso le resta un punto porque ocurre con cierta frecuencia.

Por lo demás, muy contentos con él y lo estamos usando diariamente para aplicaciones de diseño gráfico como Sketchbook, Ibis Paint X y MediBang Paint. ¡Perfecto!

title: 3.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This gimbal is a good and affordable choice if your primary use is shooting videos where the camera remains stationary and only needs to track a moving subject. It struggles significantly when both the camera and subject are in motion.

👍 Strengths
1. Smooth Stationary Tracking: The device performs its core function well. The tracking is smooth and highly effective for scenarios like dancing in front of the camera or cooking demonstrations.

2. Affordability: It represents a strong value for its specific use case.

👎 Limitations and Technical Issues
1. Movement Performance: When the camera is moving (e.g., while walking) and the subject is also moving, the gimbal does not perform well. My videos were often jittery, making steady recording while walking a genuine challenge.

2. App Dependency & Resolution: Recording and tracking work exclusively through the Aochuan app. I was disappointed to find that the app did not offer a 4K video option for my Pixel 8 Pro.

3. Confusing "3-Axis" Claim: The technical specifications are a bit misleading. This gimbal features only two main rotating axis motors for stabilization. The third motor simply rotates the phone between landscape and portrait orientations. Other premium gimbals typically feature three actual stabilizing rotating motors, separate from the rotation motor.

Who Should Buy This?
1. Content creators who shoot seated interviews or static cooking/craft videos.
2. Users looking for an affordable subject tracker for stationary setups.

Who Should Avoid This?
1. Vloggers or travelers who require smooth footage while walking or running.
2. Users whose phones require access to native 4K recording features.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Pros:
- Passive + Active Noise Cancellation = Good Noise Isolation
- Sidetone is loud, clear, and volume-adjustable ; just wish they did the same for ambient mode
- Surround Sound is Seriously Excellent ; ignore the reviews saying the audio sound warped in 7.2 THX mode, the positional audio makes it up for competitive games
- Color Scheme is Great ; Playstation's Blue stitching on Razer's white looks cool. Though I would have appreciated more blue than just the headband stitching.
- Cross-platform support though I do not need it
- Clear and rich microphone ; I find broadcast + voice normalization presets gives the best quality-sounding mic
- Swivel hinges ensure better durability than BS V2 Pros.
- Repairable Battery ; ensures that Li-ion battery degradation will not be a hindrance in the future
- Responsive overall ; I can't measure the audio signal latency but in general, changing any feature on the headset feels very seamless and quick.
- Expansive connectivity ; a long usb-c to audio connector, usb-c to usb-a connector
- simultaneous audio ; hear bluetooth and PC audio at the same time
- smooth plug-and-play
- very long battery life and can charge while using headset
- removable microphone when I don't need a mic
- hardware level mic mute switch is very convenient

Cons:
- no case/bag
- ANC is OK ; Not the best, but certainly not a dud
- Ambient Mode is OK; volume is somewhat low comparing to Sony's.
- Hinge is still mostly plastic ; hopefully it won't break on me earlier than the battery
- Headset by default turns off too early ; it doesn't have an a sensor to see if you are wearing the headset or not compared to Sony's, it just seems to turn off based on audio use.
- Audio not tuned for music so some things sound off, but are intended to maximizing competitive game audio
- headband fabric might not last as long as the headset itself
- only female voice notifications; no male
- ugly mic pop filter
- no magnet on dongle

Summary: At first, coming from an audiophile background, I couldn't immediately appreciate the use case for this headset. However, after using it for awhile, the ease and competitive edge I get from this headset is worth it in games that require it. The ANC is not too bad, it's enough to muffle most of the annoying background noises, but you will still hear some noise that a Sony would block out better.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I like the Nulaxy brand, just because they've been around for years with the solid A4 and A5 models that I'm familiar with, and I appreciate the A4 being offered in so many colors. This basic "trifold" design, which is hard to beat, is offered by many vendors, and I own quite a few in different sizes. They look and function similarly.

Details that distinguish excellent models from average models (like this Nulaxy, sadly) include:
- How high off the desk does it hold the base of my phone? (I don't like to put pressure on the cable or connector, when charging in portrait mode.)
- How good is the silicone padding?
- Are the edges of the aluminum beveled?

This Green Nulaxy appears to be much the same as a black Hi-Tech tri-fold stand I've had for years. unfortunately, the Nulaxy is inferior to the Hi-Tech (no longer available) in three ways (see photos).
- MINIMAL SILICONE PADDING on Nulaxy backplate and base: small dots and squares applied slightly askew in places. On the Hi-Tech, the padding seems designed for the piece, and precision cut and applied, in larger custom pieces.
- NO BEVELED EDGES: I was surprised the Nulaxy did not have beveled edges, unlike most of my other aluminum trifold phone stands. Every single edge on the little black Hi-Tech phone stand is beveled. Nobody but I will notice, but the Hi-Tech does feel better in the hand than the Nulaxy with plain square edges. It's fine, for keeping costs down, but for $9.99, from the Nulaxy brand, I expected beveled edges.
- HOLDS PHONE LOW: The Nulaxy backplate is longer than the Hi-Tech backplate, hence, even though both stands are essentially the same height, the hooks of the Nulaxy hold my phone much lower, closer to the desktop, than the Hi-Tech. This really bums me out and makes me not want to purchase more of this model.

I bought this particular stand at this time because I wanted green for my application, and there was not a suitable alternative in green. I would have preferred a taller model that held the base of my charging phone further up off the desk.
Nonetheless, it's a good looking. excellent bomb proof. cell phone stand at a very reasonable price.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I like the Nulaxy brand, just because they've been around for years with the solid A4 and A5 models that I'm familiar with, and I appreciate the A4 being offered in so many colors. This basic "trifold" design, which is hard to beat, is offered by many vendors, and I own quite a few in different sizes. They look and function similarly.

Details that distinguish excellent models from average models (like this Nulaxy, sadly) include:
- How high off the desk does it hold the base of my phone? (I don't like to put pressure on the cable or connector, when charging in portrait mode.)
- How good is the silicone padding?
- Are the edges of the aluminum beveled?

This Green Nulaxy appears to be much the same as a black Hi-Tech tri-fold stand I've had for years. unfortunately, the Nulaxy is inferior to the Hi-Tech (no longer available) in three ways (see photos).
- MINIMAL SILICONE PADDING on Nulaxy backplate and base: small dots and squares applied slightly askew in places. On the Hi-Tech, the padding seems designed for the piece, and precision cut and applied, in larger custom pieces.
- NO BEVELED EDGES: I was surprised the Nulaxy did not have beveled edges, unlike most of my other aluminum trifold phone stands. Every single edge on the little black Hi-Tech phone stand is beveled. Nobody but I will notice, but the Hi-Tech does feel better in the hand than the Nulaxy with plain square edges. It's fine, for keeping costs down, but for $9.99, from the Nulaxy brand, I expected beveled edges.
- HOLDS PHONE LOW: The Nulaxy backplate is longer than the Hi-Tech backplate, hence, even though both stands are essentially the same height, the hooks of the Nulaxy hold my phone much lower, closer to the desktop, than the Hi-Tech. This really bums me out and makes me not want to purchase more of this model.

I bought this particular stand at this time because I wanted green for my application, and there was not a suitable alternative in green. I would have preferred a taller model that held the base of my charging phone further up off the desk.
Nonetheless, it's a good looking. excellent bomb proof. cell phone stand at a very reasonable price.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I found this product reviewed on WIRED as one of the Ten Best Cell Phone Mounts. I vote it #1. I stuck this to a non-smooth dashboard surface, and it’s never come loose in several months or use. I did not use the included mounting disc; I simply adhered the suction surface on the mount to the dashboard surface.

The lock and release mechanism is beyond compare, very easy to operate. You place the phone on the mount’s feet, which hold it in place, and press lightly on the phone to activate the clamp. To release the phone, you squeeze the two tabs below the clamps together, and the phone is free but still supported by the feet so that it doesn’t fall. Some design engineer really thought this out well.

The location of the mount it obviously a personal choice. I mounted mine on the dash-top to the left of the driver. I can see the phone clearly without distraction from driving. The mount is stable and does not shake or wobble.

You might want to consider being able to attach a charging cord from the mount location. I have a USB port close enough to connect the cord to the phone while driving. I found no need for the included magnetic cord attachment with my IPhone 14. The cord fits snugly enough without it.

I initially set up the mount with the arm extended to its maximum length to bring the screen closer to me. However, this resulted in minor shake and wobble of the phone. I found that I had excellent view of the phone’s screen with the arm contracted to its minimum setting where the phone was very stable. Do make sure that you securely tighten the round locking nut that allows rotation of the mount. I discovered shortly after installing the mount that the looseness of this nut was the cause of phone wobble. This was a “user” mistake.

I am super impressed with the design and quality of this product.

I've had phone holders that are suction cups or magnets. Suction cups surprisingly suck (meaning they do a poor job of holding your phone). The only suction cup holder that I've had success with are the Ram X-Grip mounts and even then, in certain weather, the suction cup will lose grip and fall.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This is a nice size for a high power, multi outlet charger. I have an older multi-outlet charger which works great for overnight charging. This one however can charge much faster than my older one which can be handy at times.

I don't have a great setup for testing the various protocols a charger can do (something I working on fixing soon). For now, I just hooked up a phone on the USB A side and I could see that the voltage stayed right around 5.1 v and the phone drew up to about 1.5 amps. One thing I checked for was any unusual heat build up and, as expected for such a light load compared to total capacity, I couldn't feel it warming at all.

It's nice the ac plug folds up nicely to a nice compact package. The older model I mentioned requires me to carry a separate cord along with the unit. I won't say if I've ever traveled and got somewhere with the charger but not the cord (cough cough).

Overall, this one is now my primary travel charger for US travel.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This is a useful Bluetooth remote camera control (clicker) for smartphones. It works with your phone's stock Camera app as well as TikTok and some other apps. In addition to the shutter button, it has zoom-in, zoom-out and switch camera buttons that work in the stock Camera app, as well as a four-way controller for short video apps like TikTok.

It pairs easily, although the short name VN11 is non-descript so after a while you may not recognize it. It uses USB-C for charging -- a short charging cable is included.

I give this 5 stars because it's easy to use and has good functions like zoom in and zoom out. But its build quality is not too great; it feels entirely plasticky, unlike what the product photo may suggest. The buttons are also a little hard to press, especially the side switch-camera button. But these are minor gripes. The functionality and price are both great, and the convenience in situations where you need a remote clicker cannot be beat.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I purchased this remote specifically for use with an iPhone, based on the advertised features (photo shutter and zoom control).

Pairing with the iPhone was straightforward and stable. The device reliably triggers the shutter, which is useful.

However, the zoom function does not work at all on iPhone (tested on iPhone 14 Pro Max). The “+” and “–” buttons have no effect in the Camera app. In addition, several buttons do not behave as described in the instructions (multiple buttons trigger the shutter instead).

Based on my testing, this device behaves as a basic Bluetooth shutter remote only. The advertised zoom capability for iPhone is not supported in practice.

This is not a hardware quality issue—the device appears well built—but a mismatch between advertised features and actual iPhone capabilities.

I am returning the product, not because it is defective, but because the description is misleading for iPhone users.

Users should be aware that iOS does not expose full camera control over Bluetooth, so third-party remotes are generally limited to shutter functionality.

title: 3.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Look, I bought this little gizmo so I could take majestic, windswept selfies from a safe distance—without fumbling for the timer or yelling “CHEESE” at a brick wall. And to be fair, it does do the job. Click the button, picture gets taken. Voilà.

BUT... the thing feels like it was built from the leftover plastic in a Happy Meal toy. The power switch has already developed a personality of its own—flick it once and it kind of shrugs, like “Ehh, maybe I’m on, maybe I’m not.”

It also claims to work with phones and tablets and maybe even your microwave for all I know. It’s trying way too hard to be the life of the party, when I just wanted it to show up, press a button, and leave. Sometimes less is more, and this one is doing the tech equivalent of jazz hands.

I’ll keep using it until it dies or runs off to join Cirque du Bluetooth, but next time I’m getting a remote that sticks to one job and does it well. Like a dog. Or a light switch.

Would I recommend it? Sure, if your standards are somewhere between “meh” and “ehh, close enough.”

This purchase was an experiment. Would it be a better user experience to occasionally use my Apple Watch Ultra like a dumbphone? The answer is mixed. As others have pointed out, the design involves a good deal of screwing. The watch is secure, and the click wheel is mostly responsive. Unfortunately, i do still like to use my Apple Watch for runs and other workouts, but it’s no longer a daily driver. I wish that either this design worked like the RePod, where a single quarter turn is enough to free up the watch. Sadly, that brand doesn’t currently fit the Ultra. (They have one in crowdfunding at the moment, but it’s nearly $100, which is probably more than this is experiment is worth.

In short, I’m returning this. But if you’re someone who is fine not ever wearing the watch again, this might be worth a shot.

text:
Unlike others in these reviews, I did not even attempt to use the vent mount. Honestly, vent mounts just seem ridiculous, prone to falling, and of course, they block the vent.

What I needed was a way to mount my phone in front of the one flat open space on my dashboard, as if it were a permanent mount built into the car. This mount was one of very few that offered a good mount with a flush mount option like this, so I tried it out.

I had planned on screwing the mount to the dashboard, since I never expected the tape to hold, but when it arrived, I thought I'd try it out. Well, I just used the tape, and it stuck remarkably well. It's great. I never needed screws, and the mount is holding perfectly and looks fantastic in my car. The iOTTI phone holder is also great, so a win win.

I was really psyched about the little magnet that holds the charging wire too, but somehow, the magnetic tape they provided opened up, fell off the wire, and was never seen again. Not sure what happened, but they should have included three to five of these on-cent pieces. Oh well.

Buy it.

title: 3.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I like this mount overall, but found a couple small issues.
First, the best feature is its one-handed operation. I can attach my phone to the mount with one hand because of the button-release for the clamp arms. I was also able to remove my phone with one hand by pressing the opening lever with my pinkie finger to release the pressure of the clamp arms. Very ergonomic!

My largest problem is that the "feet" on the bottom of the unit that are there to stop the phone from slipping downward aren't adjustable enough. I have a longer phone with volume and on/off buttons at the middle of the side of the phone. When I clamp my phone into the mount, the clamp arms press the power button on the phone and turn the screen off! The ostensible solution is to adjust the height via the feet at the bottom of the holder, but they don't move down low enough -- instead of pressing the power button, the clamp arms press the Volume Down button, which makes it so I can't hear music or GPS directions.
If the feet extended downward another inch or two, this would be an almost perfect product, but as it is, it's basically unusable.

My solution was to use scraps of foam, stack them up and cut them to size, and then tape the foam block on top of the feet to boost the phone up high. This way the clamp arms are positioned underneath the buttons. This makes the mount less stable and very top-heavy, but it does allow me to use it.

My only other criticism is that the rubber vent mount portion can slip over time, especially if the weight of the phone forces the vent fins to angle downward.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text: I've tried out multiple cell phone car mounts over the years, and iOttie has consistently been the best-in-class among them all. I already own iOttie dashboard mounts, which have terrific adhesion to the dashboard and excellent clamps to hold your phone in place that are sturdy and well-designed. This vent mounted option from iOttie has the same clamping system to hold your phone firmly in place, as well as a great ball-and-joint swivel to set a comfortable viewing angle. The vent mount itself is pretty sturdy, but you'll have to carefully work the vent attachments into your air vent as deep as possible and tilt the air vent blades to their lowest possible angle to allow the mount to brace against gravity, otherwise your mount and phone will pop off the vent at your first bump in the road. Once I figured out how to keep this mount firmly in place, I was just as pleased as I have been with iOttie's dashboard mounts. To top it all off, with years of experience, I can say with confidence that iOttie offers some of the best customer service around. They really stand behind their product and work hard to resolve any problems that may arise. I haven't had any problems arise with this air vent mount, and don't anticipate that I will. But it is reassuring to know that if anything does come up, they will make it right. I highly recommend this product due to it's excellent design, ease of use, sturdiness, and the option to use this mount in multiple vehicles.

Several years ago I bought a Bluetooth keyboard for use with one of my electronic devices and the stupid thing stuttered. Every time I typed a key it would show it twice. I searched and searched online for a fix for this and was unable to find one. In the past, I've purchased computer mice and keyboards from other big name companies and almost every time there has been some sort of hassle: you don't have the right driver, it's not compatible with your device, you need to install this invasive software, etc. So it was with some trepidation that I decided to purchase this keyboard.

The KEY (pun intended) deciding factor was the brand name LOGITECH!

Although I've only purchased 3 or 4 different devices from LOGITECH, without fail, they have been plug in, turn on, work! I have NEVER had a problem with a LOGITECH device, PERIOD! It has been several years since I've purchased from them and it seems that their insistence on QUALITY and RELIABILITY has not wavered.

Okay, so the Logitech Bluetooth Multi-Device Keyboard K480. Just buy one!

It is a substantial keyboard, meaning that it has some heft to it and it's solidly built. It's size is 11 1/2" wide X 7 1/2" long X just over 1/2" thick. If it's not regulation keyboard size it's pretty damn close. I was able to touch type on it immediately without having to adjust how I type.

As usual, LOGITECH, realizing that people today have more than one device has made this keyboard switchable to three different devices. I recently purchased a new tablet and wanted to use the old one with this keyboard as a "typewriter" that I could easily take to work. I HATE onscreen keyboards because I'm a touch typist and I can type much faster on a keyboard than any teenage girl can thumb-type on her cell phone! So the first job was to pair the keyboard with my old tablet...took less than five minutes and that includes the time I took to go to the LOGITECH site and read through their documentation. WORKED PERFECTLY! Absolutely no delay in keyboard to tablet. It was as though I was typing on a typewriter!

This morning I thought I might have a need to use the keyboard with my new tablet, so I turned the selector to "2" and paired my new tablet as well. WORKED PERFECTLY!

Then I thought, "oh yeah, one of the reasons I'd started looking for a Bluetooth keyboard, that I'd since forgotten (duh!) was that I'd recently purchased a Fire stick and HATED their onscreen keyboard (no surprise there!). So I took the keyboard into the living room and sat on the couch and turned the selector to "3" and paired it with my Fire TV. WORKED PERFECTLY!

I shouldn't really be surprised as LOGITECH has a perfect track record with me. I guess they take the extra time to make sure that their devices work as they are designed to do and work out any bugs before they release them to the marketplace, unlike many other companies.

Since I'm using this keyboard on Android type devices I really don't have a lot of use for a lot of the computer type keys, but I'm sure that some others out there will make use of them and critique them for you. The fact that this keyboard can be used with three different devices with the turn of a dial and that it can be used with Windows/Apple/Android devices makes it one of the most flexible on the market and the LOGITECH brand name ensures that it is a QUALITY product, which my experience has proven has not faltered.

I don't usually spend this much time on reviews. Amazon nags me about reviews of items that I've purchased and I will usually type one or two lines just to get them to SHUT UP! But this keyboard reminded me how reliable and serious LOGITECH is about providing electronic devices that do what they are supposed to do and prompted me to make sure that I wrote a review that I hope will encourage you to buy one!

Because of another review I also purchased a carry case for it at the same time and I am rather pleased with it.
It's great because the mesh area that they show with a cable in it is big enough for me to put my old tablet in and so I have one case with the keyboard and tablet. So it's my own version of an old fashioned typewriter case!

UPDATE: After realizing I had a defective unit and was outside of the amazon return period - I submitted a support request with Logitech and I was helped very quickly and courteously by customer support. I was dreading the interaction with Logitech (for no reason, just that I have typically found dealing with manufacturers to be more difficult than say, Amazon). My dread was completely unfounded and I'm happy to say Logitech sent me a replacement keyboard that has resolved most of my complaints in my original review. Keyboard switching WORKS! I can switch between a windows computer and an iOS device seamlessly without any extra key-presses. The power switch works as well. I cannot comment on battery life yet as I only just received my replacement unit. I'm updating 1 star to 4 stars but leaving my original review below.

ORIGINAL:

I have a defective unit and missed the return window by a day. I'll try to get a warranty replacement through logitech but be warned that this review is biased.

Persistent problems:
- Key presses will stick and I'll have to turn the device on and off and re-connect and hope that the 'a' key is no longer on repeat.
- Switching doesn't automatically connect to a device (this could be the devices problem or my defective unit, I don't know). If I switch from position 1 to 3, I would expect it to automatically connect to my computer (or phone), instead I have to press the bluetooth connect button once. Sometimes it connects and sometimes it does nothing and I have to just kind of wait as there is no obvious feedback of connection or not. I think blinking blue light is attempting to connect and solid blue light is connected? but that's not always accurate on my device. Never auto connects to my iOS devices - I have to go to the settings and pair, every time. This could be an iOS problem though, I never have consistent luck with bluetooth devices and iOS.
- Biggest faulty issue is my power switch doesn't work. I thought it was working fine until I realized one day when I faced a stuck key problem that when I looked at the powerkey, it was off, yet I was connected to a device. Also, toggling the power button triggers a reconnect - so the power button does SOMETHING, but I have no idea what.
- Batteries are dead after about 4 weeks of very intermittent use. I'm only in my home office for 1 day a week, so this keyboard got a maximum of 8 days worth of typing over the course of a month (being very generous with the amount of usage, it's probably closer to 5 days of use). title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
When I have to travel, I have a work laptop that has one of those full-sized keyboards that are incredibly difficult to type on. I had to leave on an extended trip, and wanted to get a comfortable wireless keyboard instead of taking the full-sized wired keyboard I normally use when I'm at my home office. This Logitech K585 is just amazing:

1. The rubber feet on the bottom grip like glue. That's not to suggest that you can't lift the keyboard from the desk; instead, it will not slide while you type. There is no movement at all.

2. There is enough of an angle, so you're typing in an ergonomic position.

3. The keys are quiet, and the scissor mechanism gives you an authentic feel that you'd get from a laptop. So, it is comfortable to use and comfortable for everyone else around.

4. It is plug-and-play. There is optional software you can install, but you don't have to. The USB-A dongle can be stored in the battery compartment. It takes two AAA batteries, which make it very easy to have spares.

5. It has a solid feel to it and has some heft. This will add weight to your backpack if you travel with it, yet it is small enough to fit in a backpack.

6. My Google Pixel 7 with a case fits in the slot. I will likely never use this slot for that purpose, but I was curious since I had read so many reviews that said a case and phone would not work.

7. It has a power switch to save power.

So, what are the cons?

1. Engaging the NUM LOCK button. It works, but you have to know the magic secret. There are no written instructions. Press the FUNCTION and the CLEAR buttons simultaneously.

2. no LED indicators tell you if CAPS LOCK and NUM LOCK are engaged. You find out when you type.

The cons are pretty minor in the scope of what is otherwise a fantastic wireless keyboard. Cheers!

text:
This is a great product. I've used almost 100 different magnetic mounts and this one is one of the best due to it's magnetic strength and versatility.
The magnetic strength is one of the strongest I've dealt with, definitely no worries about using a full sized tablet with this (tried with a Samsung Galaxy Tab S3 with no slippage even on bumpy roads). But this probably contributes to the minor flaw that I'll describe a little later.
The build quality is great. Everything is mostly solid.
The suction cup had 2 methods of adhesion that works together. First, there's an actual adhesive, which alone would be enough to keep on my dashboard without moving. Then there's the standard lever suction, which adds more security, especially if mounted to windows.
The elbow adjustment locks with a turn knob which keeps it mostly solid. The main issue I have is the arm that extends. They market the fact the main arm can be adjusted with one hand due to the fact it uses a spring and bearing detend so you can just extend and retract the arm by a simple push or pull. While this is true, it leads to a problem I've come across. Like I mentioned earlier, the magnets are strong. If you adjust the arm to a length that is NOT at full extension, you'll more than likely end up pulling it to full extension when removing the phone from the mount. The magnets are so strong that they overpower the strength of the arm detents. My perfect adjustment is with the arm fully retracted (shortest length) and when trying to pull my phone straight off, it pulls the arm to full extention. I've found 2 ways to remedy this without permanently altering the product.
First, place the metal plate between your phone case and phone. This increased distance decreses the amount of magnetic force being applied, allowed the device to be removed with less energy. On my phone, the metal plate is on the outside of the case, so this option does not work for me.
Second, pay attention to how you pull the device off the mount. Depending on which metal plate you use (it comes with 3 different size/shapes) lifting it off the mount from one side decreses the energy required to remove the device. Using both the rectangle plates on the outside of my case, I was able to remove my device without accidently extending the mount arm by lifting the device off the mount from one side. When in portrait orientation, if I life my phone off from either the left or right side only, it comes off without extending the arm.
Overall, one of the best mounts I've used.

text:
I previously used a phone mount with a long, bendable arm, but it looked a bit tacky. It lasted a few years before the suction cup finally failed, so I decided to upgrade to this one for a cleaner, more minimal look.

I chose to mount it on my dashboard. The package includes a flat, black mounting plate that you stick to the dash first, creating a smooth surface for the suction cup to grip. There's also a UV protective film included if you prefer to mount it on the windshield.

The suction cup holds very securely to the provided plate. For the magnetic attachment, I stuck the metal plate to the back of my phone case. In my experience, these metal plates often fail and come off over time, so I always take extra steps to ensure a strong bond. I lightly sand the surface of my phone case, then use super glue with a plastic primer. This method has never failed me. Once applied, the metal plate stays put, preventing my phone from detaching and falling which happened frequently before I figured out to use plastic super glue primer then super glue.

Personally, I avoid mounting anything on my windshield because it can lead to cracks over time. The dash mount option is much safer and works perfectly for me.

Overall, this mount is a great choice if you’re looking for something sturdy, simple, and clean-looking.

** ONE complaint I do have is the extension arm is not really too good hence why I am giving 4 stars. I may run a tiny screw in it to keep it extended because it easily clicks back to not extended when i set my phone on it but I want the arm to stay fully extended every time. I found myself consistently pulling the arm back out to my phone is easier to reach on the dash.
