title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This is a great product. I've used almost 100 different magnetic mounts and this one is one of the best due to it's magnetic strength and versatility.
The magnetic strength is one of the strongest I've dealt with, definitely no worries about using a full sized tablet with this (tried with a Samsung Galaxy Tab S3 with no slippage even on bumpy roads). But this probably contributes to the minor flaw that I'll describe a little later.
The build quality is great. Everything is mostly solid.
The suction cup had 2 methods of adhesion that works together. First, there's an actual adhesive, which alone would be enough to keep on my dashboard without moving. Then there's the standard lever suction, which adds more security, especially if mounted to windows.
The elbow adjustment locks with a turn knob which keeps it mostly solid. The main issue I have is the arm that extends. They market the fact the main arm can be adjusted with one hand due to the fact it uses a spring and bearing detend so you can just extend and retract the arm by a simple push or pull. While this is true, it leads to a problem I've come across. Like I mentioned earlier, the magnets are strong. If you adjust the arm to a length that is NOT at full extension, you'll more than likely end up pulling it to full extension when removing the phone from the mount. The magnets are so strong that they overpower the strength of the arm detents. My perfect adjustment is with the arm fully retracted (shortest length) and when trying to pull my phone straight off, it pulls the arm to full extention. I've found 2 ways to remedy this without permanently altering the product.
First, place the metal plate between your phone case and phone. This increased distance decreses the amount of magnetic force being applied, allowed the device to be removed with less energy. On my phone, the metal plate is on the outside of the case, so this option does not work for me.
Second, pay attention to how you pull the device off the mount. Depending on which metal plate you use (it comes with 3 different size/shapes) lifting it off the mount from one side decreses the energy required to remove the device. Using both the rectangle plates on the outside of my case, I was able to remove my device without accidently extending the mount arm by lifting the device off the mount from one side. When in portrait orientation, if I life my phone off from either the left or right side only, it comes off without extending the arm.
Overall, one of the best mounts I've used.

text:
I’ve been looking for a car mount to safely hold my phone while using maps for directions that would be low-profile, could sit horizontally on the dash, and was easy on/off for my phone.

Pros:
• Adhesion seems good so far. I have a wide, flat horizontal space on my dash in front of one of the screens where it sits perfectly - can’t comment on how it sticks to a textured or curved dash. I applied it in winter but waited until the afternoon so it wasn’t freezing cold - we’ll see how it does in summer, but so far so good.
• Perfect amount of “stick” to the magnet. My iPhone X is held securely with no wobbling but can also be pulled off easily if needed. I put the magnet sticker on the back of my phone case, below my phone holder, and it works great. I like not fumbling with clamping it in, like other mounts.
• If you place the sticker in the center of the phone, you could pop the phone on either vertically or horizontally
• Locking ring means I can twist it tight and it will stay in position without coming loose, rattling around, or starting to droop while driving.

Cons:
• Would have been nice if it folded away or popped off the mount for storage when not using it; I guess I could have gotten the suction version but they’re notorious for not sticking well.
• Of course, only phones with the magnetic sticker on them can use it; not great for road trips with multiple drivers using their own phones to navigate or listen to music. Would have been nice if they included extra magnet stickers so multiple people in the household could add it to their phones, or to use if you get a new phone/case.

Overall a low-profile, secure mount that’s easy on-and-off so I can read directions safely.

I did another review but It's not here. Maybe they deleted it because I got the refund?

They include something called a magic plate that goes between the sticky metal plate and your phone to make it easier to remove the plate if you want to. Wife has a Samsung S22 and that magic plate wouldn't stick to it. 3M Blue masking tape wouldn't stick to it either. It must have some kind of coating. The wife didn't want it stuck directly to the phone so it's held in place by the protective case. It seems to work okay. I have a different unit in my car with a metal plate and it stays in place with just the case holding it there.

The car mount was easier. I cleaned up 2 areas on the dash of our 1999 Sienna. I cleaned them with a cleaning tissue for glasses, put one on the driver's left above the A/C vent and the other just below the rear window defrost button. It seems pretty strong so we'll see. I'll update here if there's a change.

My phone is a Samsung S8. I added a second metal plate to mine but they slide around, so I peeled off the paper from this holder's plate and put it on the back of the phone and it stuck. I put the other one from the different mount below that one and used the 3M Blue masking tape to see if it stays in place. I put the Otterbox case back on.

This seems like a good system. It is certainly designed like what I had in mind. The one in my car mounts in the A/C vent. It's good but once mounted you cannot control the vent. I had to set the vent the way that's most convenient then put the vent mount on and there it stays. With this mount it is on the plastic near the vent so it can keep the phone cool on long trips when I'm using it for navigation. It's adjustable in several directions and the vent can also be adjusted.

I'm giving these mounts 5 stars for now. Hopefully everything will go well. I like the convenience of the magnetic mount. If all goes well with the adhesives then I'll keep it 5 stars.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I’ve been looking for a car mount to safely hold my phone while using maps for directions that would be low-profile, could sit horizontally on the dash, and was easy on/off for my phone.

Pros:
• Adhesion seems good so far. I have a wide, flat horizontal space on my dash in front of one of the screens where it sits perfectly - can’t comment on how it sticks to a textured or curved dash. I applied it in winter but waited until the afternoon so it wasn’t freezing cold - we’ll see how it does in summer, but so far so good.
• Perfect amount of “stick” to the magnet. My iPhone X is held securely with no wobbling but can also be pulled off easily if needed. I put the magnet sticker on the back of my phone case, below my phone holder, and it works great. I like not fumbling with clamping it in, like other mounts.
• If you place the sticker in the center of the phone, you could pop the phone on either vertically or horizontally
• Locking ring means I can twist it tight and it will stay in position without coming loose, rattling around, or starting to droop while driving.

Cons:
• Would have been nice if it folded away or popped off the mount for storage when not using it; I guess I could have gotten the suction version but they’re notorious for not sticking well.
• Of course, only phones with the magnetic sticker on them can use it; not great for road trips with multiple drivers using their own phones to navigate or listen to music. Would have been nice if they included extra magnet stickers so multiple people in the household could add it to their phones, or to use if you get a new phone/case.

Overall a low-profile, secure mount that’s easy on-and-off so I can read directions safely.

text:
My intended use is for stable video captures of dog training.
I am not sure whether this will work in the long run successfully.

IF your intended use is a stationary desk setup / semi permanent placement - to allow you to use, your phone, see incoming messages, calls or watch movies, etc, while working. This device should be Great (5 stars).

1️⃣. I have a iPhone 14 pro max with a hard case attached. The power button on the phone is larger and on the right edge of the phone, two vol buttons on the left edge.
⚠️ First time I clamped to the Mount phone holder - my phone turned off (the power button is in the way for center holding. The second time my phone went to place an emergency SOS call, because the buttons being held down together for more than a few seconds... Need to turn off that phone feature.
Need to place my phone in holder further towards the bottom of the phone.

2️⃣. The gooseneck is visible in the camera view. Very Difficult for me to adjust to get it out of view. I was finally able to get it out of view. I will have to juggle this everytime I try to use.

3️⃣. The rigid sturdiness (a plus) of the gooseneck. I doubt this portion will break or wear. You will not be moving it much, because it is not a pliable, easy to adjust feature. Sturdy - absolutely. It will not cause the mounted phone to slip out of position due to this part!

4️⃣. Clamp to hold phone itself. Appears to be lightweight, low cost, cheap plastic - that could easily break if you are not careful. It did easily hold my iphone 14 pro max. It can NOT be rotated. This clamp really needs a ball-head.

5️⃣. Clamp for the Base. Easy to turn handle to open and close the clamp. The sleeve that you turn, may break off - if you intend to move the mount to different tables/desks often. If using only at your desk - and will be stationary - this will work Great.

➡️ Recommend Re-Design:
(1) Could definitely use a ball-head feature for the phone holder. That will provide increased and easier flexibility for users, and it will allow the gooseneck to easily be rotated out of view.
(2) Swivel at the gooseneck base. Can have a locking lever to lock in place. Unlock - to just swivel the sturdy gooseneck out of the way, when you get up & down.

Overall - I will be searching if there is a better option for my 'heavy & large' iPhone for quick, impromptu, sturdy video captures, that can be used almost anywhere.

Side NOTE: I do not see this device holding a Pad. I think my phone is the largest device it would comfortably hold.

The APP2 MagSafe Cup Holder Mount works great. I bought this on Amazon after trying some other MagSafe holders which either had weak magnets or required you to adhere a metal plate to your phone in order for them to work. The APP2 worked great right out of the box with my iPhone16 Pro Max - it holds it very well.

The adjustable base fits snug into my cup holder, leaving one free for, you know, cups. There is also a short telescopic height adjustment (which I might not use but it's nice to have the option). It also comes with an optional metal ring with a 3M adhesive to attach to just about any case or phone, making it almost a universal mount. While the included instructions are pretty basic, there's really nothing you shouldn't be able to figure out on your own. The mount pops right onto the plastic ball mount and that's about it.

Please note that this is **NOT** a charging mount - it is just designed to hold a MagSafe compatible phone. But since I wasn't looking for a charging mount, this was just what I needed. It is constructed of heavy-gauge plastic so I'm hoping it survives our hot summers. But at a little under $28, it wouldn't be a big deal if I had to replace it in a couple of years.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Seldom do I review much of anything I buy from this site, but given there's not a lot of information about my specific use case for this, I'd figure I'd leave one for anyone that happens to be curious and is in a similar position.

Context: I'm an overnight Walmart Team Associate, five nights a week, and I stock shelves all night long. A majority of my nights are spend in the Frozen food isles stocking there and creating inventory tags for the product. (Vizpick Label if you're familiar with the terminology.) We recently had been shipped Samsung Galaxy XCover Pro phones to replace the old TC70 and ect, handheld devices we use to find items, print labels, price changes, and so on. This was company wide, btw. The old devices had a barcode scanner built into it, but these new devices don't. While it's possible to use the camera, it's often a pain depending on the lighting, the focus, the item itself, just slower overall.

Most of the workers are obviously annoyed at this, and there's no plans to send any scanners with the phones as far as I know. There's an argument to be made about workers having to purchase this kind of stuff, that the company should be paying for this, but this review isn't about that. I had cashback stacked on my Prime rewards card so I hardly paid for this. If you're looking for something for a very similar use case, or work at Walmart in a similar position, and don't care dropping the $35 for a scanner, read on.

The scanner itself is obviously not top-tier engineering, cheap plastic, could use some grip for the handle. Kind of bulky, but I have a tool holster and it fit in the widest hook pretty well. The button has maybe 2MM of travel before it clicks, but it's not bad. Got some weight to it, not as much as the hand-scanners at the registers. On the bottom is where the USB dongle is stored, but there's no cover for it. I just left it in the box. The USB cable plugs into the bottom as well, uses a big 'printer cable' USB port. I'm unsure if you can use the cable for a printer, and probably would have tested it if I had one. Also, the USB port is exposed. While the port itself is about half an inch deep, I wouldn't be surprised if it died because some liquid got into there. Be mindful of that.

The light on top has at least 3(?) colors. When you initially plug it in to charge, it'll probably be orange, but turns to green when it's completely full. Pressing the button once wakes it up. Assuming you're using the bluetooth, it'll sync to your phone the same as pulling out any wireless earbuds. But sometimes it takes a moment, it's been as short as 5 seconds, but sometimes takes 15-20. Not sure why, as there's no other devices paired to the phone.

Once it's on and connected, the light turns blue, and that's it. It handles the barcodes by acting like a bluetooth keyboard. When you scan a barcode, it types it out, then presses enter. I haven't read through the manual to see if it can be tweaked, but for the most part is consistent. Sometimes it can scan only half of the barcode, so be sure the red line light is picking up the whole barcode.

Also, time to bring up the manual. Somewhat not as bad broken English, if you're tech savvy and have comprehended my review up to this point, it's not hard to set up. To change any of it's settings, (Sleep time, bluetooth mode, ect,) it has a series of barcodes that you scan to set those settings. It's strange, but given it only has one button, I don't know how else it could have been done without a computer. (Maybe a dedicated BT button?) All you really do is scan a barcode that puts it into bluetooth pairing mode, and have your phone pair it like any other bluetooth device, didn't take long and was ready to go in only a minute.

So, for the Walmart workers that know about the new phones and how handling inventory works, well, it's more consistent than the camera. Assuming you're in the Me@Walmart app and in the shelf availability menu, you just hit the search icon, then scan. It types it in and hits enter. Given I had the phone a week before getting the scanner, I can say for me it's been a lot more faster and consistent. If I'm printing vizpick labels for overstock, after I hit print, I hit the search again so I'm ready to scan another item immediately after. It's held up well in other departments from pets to automotive, from garden to housewares.

For OGP, I'm not too familiar with, and they haven't taken away all of our old devices for OGP (yet,) but every OGP associate that uses a phone has told me it'd be better given the sleep time for the scanner could be set to up to 30 minutes. I should also mention the manual has a barcode to turn it off manually, might have to print it out with some online barcode creator, or a good picture on your phone.

As far as battery life goes, sleep mode being 1 minute and using it at least 2 hours a day roughly, it's lasted 10 days over 2 weeks of work. I did notice it drained the phone's batter a bit more, but I charge it when I wake up before work anyway, so it's never been a big issue.

Durability, still unsure of. I did drop it once from about 3 1/2 feet, onto concrete, and didn't have or see any issues. Dunno about the next fall, but will update it when it does fall and break.

---

Overall, it's been pretty good. My main issues are the cheap plastic possibly falling apart on a really bad fall, the exposed USB charging port at the bottom, and the scanner only picking up part of the barcode. But otherwise, it's been consistent, faster, and the night I walked into work with it, I felt like the cool kid at school that got a Gameboy for his birthday, and everyone was asking to try it out and in envy that I have a scanner with a decent handle.

I'll update this review if anything comes up, but overall, if you're a Walmart worker looking for a cheap scanner for freight, labels, and tagging stuff, this is a good option if you can get over it being slightly bulky.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I've been looking for a relatively inexpensive bar/QR code scanner to recommend to my customers for the inventory control system on my website and decided to give this one a go. I'm glad I did, as for a value product, it actually works quite well.

It isn't without its quirks, that's for sure. And some of those aren't really its fault. It behaves a bit weirdly when connected with Bluetooth. Don't get me wrong, it does work. But there are occasions when it does some odd things. The biggest annoyance is that iOS won't pop up the built-in keyboard when this scanner is connected (either Bluetooth or USB), which isn't the scanner's fault, and it does include some barcodes in the manual that you can scan to cause the keyboard to appear when needed. Again, that's an iOS quirk, but something you'll have to deal with if using the scanner with an iPhone or iPad.

The USB receiver that came with my unit fell apart the first time I pulled it out of its storage slot, and I had to glue it back together, but it did work. So it may be that quality control could be better.

But in terms of its advertised functionality, it absolutely does do with it claims to do. Programming it wasn't too difficult for the most part, though switching between USB and Bluetooth modes is a little confusing at first. And once setup, it scans quite quickly. Not as fast as the Symbol units I use myself, but performance is quite acceptable.

All-in-all, I wouldn't have an issue recommending this to someone looking for a budget-friendly bar/QR code scanner. It's built well enough to hold up for most people, and it works as advertised.

While it's possible to use the camera, it's often a pain depending on the lighting, the focus, the item itself, just slower overall.

Most of the workers are obviously annoyed at this, and there's no plans to send any scanners with the phones as far as I know. There's an argument to be made about workers having to purchase this kind of stuff, that the company should be paying for this, but this review isn't about that. I had cashback stacked on my Prime rewards card so I hardly paid for this. If you're looking for something for a very similar use case, or work at Walmart in a similar position, and don't care dropping the $35 for a scanner, read on.

The scanner itself is obviously not top-tier engineering, cheap plastic, could use some grip for the handle. Kind of bulky, but I have a tool holster and it fit in the widest hook pretty well. The button has maybe 2MM of travel before it clicks, but it's not bad. Got some weight to it, not as much as the hand-scanners at the registers. On the bottom is where the USB dongle is stored, but there's no cover for it. I just left it in the box. The USB cable plugs into the bottom as well, uses a big 'printer cable' USB port. I'm unsure if you can use the cable for a printer, and probably would have tested it if I had one. Also, the USB port is exposed. While the port itself is about half an inch deep, I wouldn't be surprised if it died because some liquid got into there. Be mindful of that.

The light on top has at least 3(?) colors. When you initially plug it in to charge, it'll probably be orange, but turns to green when it's completely full. Pressing the button once wakes it up. Assuming you're using the bluetooth, it'll sync to your phone the same as pulling out any wireless earbuds. But sometimes it takes a moment, it's been as short as 5 seconds, but sometimes takes 15-20. Not sure why, as there's no other devices paired to the phone.

Once it's on and connected, the light turns blue, and that's it. It handles the barcodes by acting like a bluetooth keyboard. When you scan a barcode, it types it out, then presses enter. I haven't read through the manual to see if it can be tweaked, but for the most part is consistent. Sometimes it can scan only half of the barcode, so be sure the red line light is picking up the whole barcode.

Also, time to bring up the manual. Somewhat not as bad broken English, if you're tech savvy and have comprehended my review up to this point, it's not hard to set up. To change any of it's settings, (Sleep time, bluetooth mode, ect,) it has a series of barcodes that you scan to set those settings. It's strange, but given it only has one button, I don't know how else it could have been done without a computer. (Maybe a dedicated BT button?) All you really do is scan a barcode that puts it into bluetooth pairing mode, and have your phone pair it like any other bluetooth device, didn't take long and was ready to go in only a minute.

So, for the Walmart workers that know about the new phones and how handling inventory works, well, it's more consistent than the camera. Assuming you're in the Me@Walmart app and in the shelf availability menu, you just hit the search icon, then scan. It types it in and hits enter. Given I had the phone a week before getting the scanner, I can say for me it's been a lot more faster and consistent. If I'm printing vizpick labels for overstock, after I hit print, I hit the search again so I'm ready to scan another item immediately after. It's held up well in other departments from pets to automotive, from garden to housewares.

For OGP, I'm not too familiar with, and they haven't taken away all of our old devices for OGP (yet,) but every OGP associate that uses a phone has told me it'd be better given the sleep time for the scanner could be set to up to 30 minutes. I should also mention the manual has a barcode to turn it off manually, might have to print it out with some online barcode creator, or a good picture on your phone.

As far as battery life goes, sleep mode being 1 minute and using it at least 2 hours a day roughly, it's lasted 10 days over 2 weeks of work. I did notice it drained the phone's batter a bit more, but I charge it when I wake up before work anyway, so it's never been a big issue.

Durability, still unsure of. I did drop it once from about 3 1/2 feet, onto concrete, and didn't have or see any issues. Dunno about the next fall, but will update it when it does fall and break.

---

Overall, it's been pretty good. My main issues are the cheap plastic possibly falling apart on a really bad fall, the exposed USB charging port at the bottom, and the scanner only picking up part of the barcode. But otherwise, it's been consistent, faster, and the night I walked into work with it, I felt like the cool kid at school that got a Gameboy for his birthday, and everyone was asking to try it out and in envy that I have a scanner with a decent handle.

I'll update this review if anything comes up, but overall, if you're a Walmart worker looking for a cheap scanner for freight, labels, and tagging stuff, this is a good option if you can get over it being slightly bulky.

The USB receiver that came with my unit fell apart the first time I pulled it out of its storage slot, and I had to glue it back together, but it did work. So it may be that quality control could be better.

But in terms of its advertised functionality, it absolutely does do with it claims to do. Programming it wasn't too difficult for the most part, though switching between USB and Bluetooth modes is a little confusing at first. And once setup, it scans quite quickly. Not as fast as the Symbol units I use myself, but performance is quite acceptable.

All-in-all, I wouldn't have an issue recommending this to someone looking for a budget-friendly bar/QR code scanner. It's built well enough to hold up for most people, and it works as advertised.

text:
We set up a multi-block charging area in our lunchroom about a year ago. Since then, we’ve spent a fair amount of money replacing two things: the charging blocks and the cords. So I liked the idea of being able to purchase a complete solution with a bit more upfront cost but having better organization and more security around the cords and blocks.

This unit mounts like a TV (bracket to the wall, sign to the bracket) and comes with 2 Micro-USB, 3 USB-C, and 3 iPhone cables. In our office, no one uses Micro-USB anymore, so we removed the back panel and swapped out the cords—we opted for 4 USB-C and 4 iPhone cables. Each side has two small screens, and the plate that holds the cords slides out of the way, making it easy to swap them. I appreciated that it came with a total of 6 USB-C, 4 Micro-USB (which, let’s be honest, are pretty much obsolete in 2025), and 6 iPhone cords.

You can also remove the board using four bolts, which makes it easy to apply your own vinyl to the front. It’s simple to trim with the board removed—a nice touch for customization.

What I like best is that the cords and blocks are secured, so we won’t need replacements unless a cord actually breaks. With the ability to swap out cords as needed, this feels like a solid long-term solution for us. Customizing the backer is worth it, though the green looks good as-is too.

✅ Pros
- Secure Setup: Cords and blocks are locked in, reducing theft and wear.
- Customizable Design: Easy to apply vinyl for branding or aesthetics.
- Cord Swapping: Flexible configuration—swap out cables to match your needs.
- Good Cable Variety: Comes with a generous supply of USB-C and iPhone cords.
- Compact & Organized: Mounts cleanly like a TV, with built-in screens and cord management.

⚠️ Cons
- Obsolete Cables: Includes Micro-USB cords, which are mostly irrelevant in 2025.
- Initial Setup Required: Swapping cords and customizing takes a bit of effort.
- Fixed Mounting: Not ideal if you need a portable or movable charging station.

🏁 Verdict
This charging station is a smart investment for shared spaces like offices or lunchrooms. It offers a clean, secure, and customizable setup that reduces cord replacements and clutter. While the Micro-USB inclusion feels outdated, the overall flexibility and build quality make it a worthwhile long-term solution—especially for environments with frequent use and multiple device types.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I think this is probably the most useful phone kickstand/grip I have ever used! I love it.
It will prop the phone upright, or sideways with good stability. You can set the phone on a table and the stand will hold it well enough for you to tap screen and use phone without having to hold onto it.
The stand can also be used to hang the phone from your finger or on a hook when fully extended. And when it's bent into the proper position, will even allow the phone to be hung from the edge of a computer screen or surface edge.
When folded down against the phone, it is very much out of the way and does not interfere with pulling the phone in or out of pocket/purse.
Amazing design!

After using for quite some time, however, it can lose some of the strength in the hinges and become a little floppy and weak at holding some positions. But I guess anything will wear out eventually with a lot of use.

So, I still recommend this highly useful and multi-purpose phone stand.

text:
I was excited to try this, my only experience with gimbals has been the one on my drone so I was curious to see how this translates into a phone version.
It is quite different, a drone camera is very light and responsive to smooth out the effects of drift and shake in flight. This is a heavy piece of kit more designed to provide slow speed smooth tracking for a more cinematographic result.

I was terrified opening out the arm, it felt like breaking something expensive, but its just got a stiff latch to hold it open/closed.
Fitting my phone in, on power up it centres the motors and moves silently and smoothly, it feels quality!
I tested initially with the AI module, I found once powered up and fitted with the strong magnet, pressing the other button provokes it to look for a subject, it even took a liking to a newsreader on the TV screen, then movement of the unit resulted in the gimbal moving to keep the subject on screen, within reason. Fascinating!
Loading the app and selecting XE model opens many more aspects. It doesn't like you to Bluetooth pair the gimbal before the app, it prefers you to do it via the app.
Once paired it was interesting to play around with, to be honest its pretty intuitive, a menu lets you tell it to track an object for example and simply highlight it with a draw box on screen. From then on the gimbal tries to keep it centre screen, although I was caught out trying to do a 360 walk around an object as the gimbal can't turn 360, it has to return to start so it lost track.

This unit could be brilliant for youtubers making demo videos who don't have a camera operator and wants the footage to follow the action or a subject.
My interest is in outdoor cinematography with a more polished motion look.

My only disappointment is its only designed for phones. I would have loved if you could change the phone mount for a camera mount and use the system with a compact digital camera instead. Obviously the app couldn't be used, but the AI module would work.

The AI module has no 'charging' or 'charge level' indicators so its just plug it in and leave it a while?
The gimbal does have indicators.

It does seem a lot of money, currently 92 quid. But its not a toy, its a weighty proper bit of photography equipment so the price is inevitable. Looking around, it actually looks competitive.
Technology.. got to love it!

text:
こちらの商品は、3バリエーションあり、

Smart XE：ジンバルのみのシンプルなタイプ
Smart XE Kit：AIセンサーによるトラッキング
Smart XE AI：AIセンサーによるトラッキング＋モーションキャプチャー

の3バリエーションがあり、今回はAIのバリエーションをレビューさせていただきます。

近年は、YoutubeやTiktokなどのスマートフォンによる動画撮影の機会が非常に増え、それに伴いスマートフォン向けのジンバルや三脚が増えています。
こちらの製品は、製品側にAIセンサーを搭載しており、面倒なアプリ等を入れずに手持ちのスマートフォンで、まるで高価なVlogCamのようなトラッキングを行うことができます。

そもそもスマートフォンが非常に高価な製品でありますが、スマートフォンは多くの人が持っているものだと思います。その上さらに高価なVlogCamを購入するのは若干気が引けますが、この製品は、それらと比べると非常に安価に入手をすることが魅力だと思います。

実際に、使用した感想としては技術の進歩に驚かされるばかりでした。
DJI pocket等も所有していますが、それらと遜色のないような動きをしてくれました。

モーションキャプチャーの速度としても、類似製品同等で、あまりに早すぎる動きには当然どのような製品も追従はできないものです。
また、手振れ機能に関しても手持ちで撮影するのとは雲泥の差で、手元のスイッチでズームやシャッターの操作もお手の物でした。

Vlogの撮影はもちろんですが、スマートフォンを用いた動画撮影全般に強くお勧めできる商品です。

但し1点注意点としては、ジンバル＋スマートフォンの重さがありますのでそれなりの重量になるということです。それ専用に開発されているVlogCamは非常に軽いですが、スマートフォンの重さ次第では片手で保持し続ける製品特性上つらい場面も出てくる可能性があります。

その点については製品重量とお手持ちのスマートフォン重量を確認すること、また近くの家電量販店等で取り扱いがある場合は、実際に確認してみることを強くお勧めします。

総じて、非常に良い製品かと思いましたので、☆５とさせていただきました。
ご参考になれば幸いです。

text:
Sencillo, útil, se queda en la posición que elijas y no se mueve ni se abre si no quieres, acabado perfecto, funcionalidad perfecta, no tengo ninguna pega que ponerle.

Se puede poner muy cerrado, de manera que el teléfono o tablet queda totalmente vertical, o muy abierto, lo que resulta muy cómodo para tablets. Cualquier dispositivo encaja perfectamente tanto horizontal como verticalmente, y como está hecho de plástico suave, no hay riesgo de que raye nada aunque el teléfono o tablet no tenga una funda. Para su transporte se cierra del todo, pasando a ocupar poco más que una cajetilla de tabaco.

Veo que en otras opiniones se quejan de que no permite cargar el móvil en posición vertical, lo cual es evidente, ya que se apoya por la parte de abajo, y ahí es donde tienen la conexión de carga la mayoría de dispositivos móviles. No creo que haga falta ser ingerniero para darse cuenta de que ningún soporte de este tipo permite carga en vertical, ya que eso solo es posible en los dispositivos de carga inalámbrica.

Me gustó tanto este soporte que acabé comprando otro igual y, tras un año de uso, ambos siguen impolutamente blancos, la pequeña resistencia que permite que se ajuste la apetura al ángulo deseado sigue funcionando como el primer día y hasta la goma antideslizante que llevan por la parte de abajo está impecable. Parece que los acabara de sacar de la caja.

Si estás buscando un soporte bonito y versátil para tu teléfono o tablet y no necesitas carga inalámbrica, dudo que vayas a encontrar un producto mejor ni por calidad ni por precio.

Si mi opinión te ha resultado de utilidad, agradecería que te tomaras un segundo para valorarla pinchando en "Sí" más abajo, donde pregunta "¿Esta opinión te ha parecido útil?". Muchas gracias.

text:
I've liked this holder during it's lifespan, and like anything there's always pros and cons. I got this coming from a popsocket, so adjusting to holding the new shape took some getting used to, but the extra functionality from the movement made that pretty smooth. I even got compliments from folks when I'd prop my phone to reference something while working on a project, and the grippy rubber on the kickstand keeps it in place while tapping on the screen.
The hinge is the main reason I'm coming to write a review, unfortunately not for a positive reason. I got this product at the end of August, and now throughout December I noticed it clicking more and sort of dangling when it used to stay flat to the back of the phone. Eventually I noticed the problem was the hinge coming loose, and just last week it finally gave out entirely. Right now the only thing keeping the kickstand on is a safety pin, since I didn't have anything else that really fit as a replacement.
A couple additional things to note, the "360° swivel" is certainly a stretch, because while you can technically swivel it, you either have to pull hard on the hinge whichever way you're moving it, or pull it off and pop it back on. Not really a big issue in the moment, but with the hinge already being the weak point, tugging on it all the time just to try and angle the phone properly isn't great. The magnetic side of the kickstand is not especially strong either, and if you're planning to try to prop your phone up with only the magnetic force as support, the phone will drop shortly after unless you have additional support under it.
Overall really enjoyed it while it lasted, but the hinge is the killer for repurchase, since I don't really want to have to replace it every 3-4 months. If you're someone who likes to swap out phone accessories regularly and want something unique for a few months, this is still a good buy.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I've liked this holder during it's lifespan, and like anything there's always pros and cons. I got this coming from a popsocket, so adjusting to holding the new shape took some getting used to, but the extra functionality from the movement made that pretty smooth. I even got compliments from folks when I'd prop my phone to reference something while working on a project, and the grippy rubber on the kickstand keeps it in place while tapping on the screen.
The hinge is the main reason I'm coming to write a review, unfortunately not for a positive reason. I got this product at the end of August, and now throughout December I noticed it clicking more and sort of dangling when it used to stay flat to the back of the phone. Eventually I noticed the problem was the hinge coming loose, and just last week it finally gave out entirely. Right now the only thing keeping the kickstand on is a safety pin, since I didn't have anything else that really fit as a replacement.
A couple additional things to note, the "360° swivel" is certainly a stretch, because while you can technically swivel it, you either have to pull hard on the hinge whichever way you're moving it, or pull it off and pop it back on. Not really a big issue in the moment, but with the hinge already being the weak point, tugging on it all the time just to try and angle the phone properly isn't great. The magnetic side of the kickstand is not especially strong either, and if you're planning to try to prop your phone up with only the magnetic force as support, the phone will drop shortly after unless you have additional support under it.
Overall really enjoyed it while it lasted, but the hinge is the killer for repurchase, since I don't really want to have to replace it every 3-4 months. If you're someone who likes to swap out phone accessories regularly and want something unique for a few months, this is still a good buy.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text: This is one of the better quality phone mounts that I have seen or used. It is definitely a bit expensive compared to most other car phone mounts, and this is the first time I decided to go with a mount with built in wireless charging and I was not disappointed. I'm using the dashboard/windshield mounting version of the product. Other mounts of this style that I have used in the past usually end up having some free play in the suction cup base or in the pivoting joints that let the phone and the whole arm flop and bounce around a bit especially when trying to use your phone while driving on rougher roads which can be irritating to say the least. This iOttie mount on the other hand is very solid, using the plastic dashboard mounting pad this thing is firmly attached to my dash and with all the picots tightened down snuggly my phone down not move around at all even on the roughest of PA roads making it very easy and safe to using while driving. It's only been a week so far but the adhesive on the dash mounting pad and the suction cup base is very strong and stays firmly in place even on hot summer days when the inside of the car is like a sauna. The arm on the mount is extendable however it does not extend quite as far as others of this type I have used previously, although it is still long enough to be used comfortably. The charging cord that it came with was long enough to reach from the mount on the dash and into the power outlet in my center console while routing the wire our of the way with cable management clips. This QI charger is able to fast wireless charge my Samsung S22 Ultra through an Otterbox defender series case with no issues at all. The bottom "foot" of the mount that the phone sits on is adjustable up and down for wireless charging, with it adjusted up for smaller phones my S22 Ultra still fit in the mount perfectly fine but it did not start charging like it should so make sure to have that set up correctly for whatever size phone/case you have. The back of my phone does get a little hot from this charger compared to my usual Samsung wireless charging pad, I am hoping that does jot become an issue in the future. I am still a little skeptical about the auto open/close, it opens and closes flawlessly like it should and gets a really firm grip on my phone when closing on it. I actually think it is very cool but am not sure how the open/close mechanism will hold up say a year or 2 from now but only time will tell. Overall this is the best phone mount I've used so far and I think for convinience and comfort alone it is worth the price.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
TLDR: Bought 2 of the 3 device models back in 2020. I have put them through the wringer and they still work great. Worth buying.

Long story:
Getting ready to move for the second time since buying 2 of these chargers and my roommate was talking about how much they loved having one of them out in the living room. Figured I'd check if it was on sale for cyber monday so I could leave the one in the living room for him and they were sale! (yay for me!). Then when I saw the Amazon notification that I bought my original 2 way back in 2020, it was clear they have definitely earned a glowing review for surviving all they have with me.

The Purpose: 10/10
As someone who loves to host and who also has ADHD (i.e. tends to set my phones and other things down in places and then forget where they are), I initially bought two of these 3 device chargers to have one by my bed and the other on the bar between my kitchen and living room. The intent of the later, was for guest to have a quick & easy place to charge their phones, and for myself, to have a naturally purposeful and logical place to hopefully set my phone down when out in the common area so as to lose track of it less often. For both of the goals, through 2 apartments and too many different phone and headphone and qi compatible devices to count over the last 2 years 10/10.

Performance/Functionality: 9/10
As I stated at the beginning, I bought both in 2020 and they are still both working great at the end of 2023. They are used on a daily and nightly basis by varying generations of androids, iphones, airpods, and sony earbuds.
The one con I could say, is they charge pretty slowly for todays standards but it appears the new generations have helped addressed that issue (I'll know for sure with my latest order).
Otherwise, I have put these things through the wringer. I definitely would not recommend any of this of course, but these both have had food, water, wine and an assortment of other alcohols spilled on them. The have been accidental coasters for drinks, had every kind of cleaning product used on them and have had a ton of items set on them that have no business being set on them. All that with no negative effect to the charging. I've also brought one with me to travel and it definitely made life easier enough that I am buying another today just for travel.

Customer Service: 10/10
I did go back through my emails as I vaguely remembered having an issue with one of them right after I purchased it and I did; one of them was not charging on just the right hand coil. However, I reached out the the company, explained the issue, and they sent me a replacement within 5 days (assuming based on our correspondence, because I don't remember that far back) and they followed up to make sure it was working correctly. 10/10

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I was excited about the idea of a sleek, multi-device wireless charging pad like this ZealSound unit. The promise of charging three devices simultaneously with a stylish PU leather design was appealing. However, as a Google Pixel 6 Pro owner, my experience has been nothing short of frustrating, leading to a disappointing 2-star rating.

My main issue stems from the fact that this pad simply does not reliably charge my Pixel 6 Pro. It constantly flashes between "charging" and "not charging," which means I can never trust it to charge overnight. It's incredibly difficult to find the "sweet spot" for alignment, and even when I do, the connection is so finicky that the slightest bump or vibration can break it. This makes the charger unreliable for essential daily use, let alone fast charging.

While the product boasts "3x10W Output" and a "24W Power Supply," my Pixel 6 Pro certainly doesn't fast charge on this pad, and the constant on-again, off-again connection probably hinders any potential for efficient charging. The "Unmatched Safety" features like heat dissipation are good in theory, but when the phone is struggling to maintain a connection, the overall charging experience is anything but safe or efficient.

The premium PU leather is a nice touch aesthetically, but it doesn't compensate for the core functionality failing so spectacularly with my phone. This charger might work for other devices, but if you have a Pixel 6 Pro and are looking for a reliable wireless charging solution, I strongly advise looking elsewhere. This one has added more hassle to my routine than convenience.

** EDIT **

The company reached out to me and offered me a full refund because I was unhappy with this charger. I am upgrading my review to 5 stars simply because the company stands by their product, but I am leaving the original review and hope that people read it and know what the'y're getting.

I have a few of these in different vehicles, and they don't necessarily fit perfectly in every single one.
Sometimes you have to play around or make some modifications to get them to fit nice and snug, but where they do fit properly, they are excellent.

The phone sticks well and if the vents are such that they don't move when this thing is snugged in, it makes a fantastic mount.

It has a rubber base and clamps as well so it will not damage the plastics in the car. It's strong and it really tightens down well. You can tighten it to the point where you can actually snap the vent slats in half, so just be careful on tightening. Depending on the vehicle that you're going to install it in, it may or may not fit. It would be suggested that you measure the depth of the vent slats to make sure it'll fit. The adjustable clamp is quite long... But some vent slats are longer than that.

I got it into a 2019 Bentley GTC, a 2022 GMC Sierra 2500, and a 2023 Porsche Macan. In the Bentley, I had to put a dab of hot glue on the vents to prevent the vents from moving with this thing clamped onto it and that solved the problem. It bolted in perfectly into the other two vehicles with no modification necessary.

It's not my first choice for a magnetic mount in a car, but sometimes there just is no other place and this will work in almost any vehicle.

I absolutely love this keyboard! I purchased it back in February 2022. It’s now May 2025 and the keyboard is still working well and holds a charge just fine even after 3+ years of use. Pairing the keyboard to a device is easy and I love how you can connect to 3 different devices with the keyboard. I generally use it with my desktop computer but over the years I have used it was my laptop and mobile devices as well. The keyboard is compact but it’s easy to type on. My only complaint about the keys is the UP and DOWN arrow keys—they’re the smallest on the board. Honestly, it’s a great little keyboard. It’s got a bit of weight to it which is nice when you’re using it with a tablet. It seems to be solidly constructed.

My only complaint is that I can never tell how much of a charge the battery has left. I wish there was a battery gage on the keyboard or that the battery level showed up on my computer or tablet, but it doesn’t. If it only had that, it would be perfect. It’s not a major issue, since the keyboard can be used when it’s being charged.

All in all though, I love it. The price is fair as well. I’ve purchased Apple keyboards before and those are far more expensive. This one was far cheaper and it seems to have great longevity. I’ve had other bluetooth keyboards but this one has been the best and has lasted the longest. I actually just purchased a second one to use with my tablet. One other thing is that this keyboard is FCC and EC certified. It’s listed on the label on the underside of the keyboard.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Overall this keyboard is exactly as described and works as intended. I debated on whether to give it a 4 or 5 star review because I was aware of the one issue I would have with it, but felt that it was still the best option for what I needed. I decided to go with a 4 star for the reason I give below, but don’t get me wrong, this is a solid solution.

The good:
- Way easier to type on than I anticipated when looking at the photos. This really is a full feeling keyboard with correct key size and spacing. Even the round keys didn’t bother me as I expected.
- I’m specifically using this for an iPad without a case. I’m a musician and my iPad doubles as my music stand and needs to fit into a stand holder which prevents me from having a case on it, otherwise I would just have a keyboard case for this iPad. However, since I don’t want to keep putting it in and taking it out of a case every time I use it for other reasons, this keyboard was the perfect solution. Unfortunately not having a case on it also has a slightly negative effect on the fit.

The (somewhat) Bad - The only issue I have, which I was fully aware of from the product listing photos, is that the iPad lays back at a fairly extreme angle (most pronounced in portrait orientation). I put a slim case on my iPad and it fit great (still had plenty of angle without risk of falling out, yet provided a better overall view). The reason I gave this 4 stars is that a minor design change would fix this. If there was a sliding lever on the back of the keyboard that pushed a shim along the inside of the holder gap, then I could adjust the angle of the iPad to my preference with or without a case on it.

Overall the best and most sturdy option for the money. Don’t hesitate to buy this. You just may want to find a way to shim it if you don’t have a case on your device.

title: 3.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Pros:
- Magnets inside so you can stick it to the side of a tablet if applicable
- no button on the side so you won’t accidentally press it unless you slide the pen down a lot when your write/draw
- it comes will a lot of replacement nibs
- charges fairly quickly (DO NOT LEAVE IT ON CHARGE TOO LONG ONCE ITS GREEN UNPLUG IT OR IT WILL GLITCH OUT)
- I found with most pens on here the actual area where you press is a little to the left or right, iykyk but this pen doesn’t have this problem so it’s easy to draw with
- it’s lightweight
- there’s a flat side so it won’t roll away
- the pen functions fine enough (see cons for more details)
- the size is good and the diameter around the pen isn’t too slim so it should work for most sized hands
- very easy to use
- the pen is nice quality
- the latency (lag when being used) isn’t an issue
CONS:
- The pen will randomly turn off sometimes
- sometimes it just won’t tap
- if you leave it on charge to long it will turn off randomly when you’re using it
- obviously no palm rejection so you’ll need to buy an external glove
- it’s lightweight so if you prefer heavier pens it might take some getting used to
- sometimes the nib comes untwisted and the pen won’t work even if it only open a little
- sometimes the nibs stop working even if they have no visible wear

text:
UPDATE #1: After this review was posted, the seller contacted me and offered what I felt was more than fair compensation. I turned it down since I was able to cobble together a crude replacement which, while not ideal, does the job of the original knob.

UPDATE #2: I exchanged emails with the seller discussing the challenges of stocking replacement parts for a seller in China and I certainly can understand that. The seller also insisted on sending a replacement unit at no charge, and I accepted the offer. I will say that it is clear that the seller wants to do everything possible to have only happy customers.

One of the things I liked about this gimbal is the replaceable battery. This allows me to carry charged spares, and of course replace a defective battery -- something you generally can't do with most devices with internal rechargeable batteries. It was this feature that tipped the balance in my picking it. I also found this gimbal to be reasonably easy to use, but...

Both the side zoom knob and small joy stick button eventually came off the gimbal and were lost. The zoom knob was not a problem for me since I don't use it, but the missing joy stick button is needed for all other manual controls. This might not make a difference to you if you use the app exclusively, but I really need that control. So for me the device is now pretty much useless -- all for the lack of a 10 cent part. Since NO parts are available, that also means you're out of luck if you lose the battery door as well, which is held in place magnetically.

I can understand not stocking small replacement parts for inexpensive items, but the investment in a device like this is not trivial, and it should not be rendered disposable for lack of a simple part that the manufacturer could easily keep on hand and supply to their customers.

text:
This gimbal is simply amazing. I have recently started taking videos for my business, plus for my travels. I’ve used a few gimbals previously and have to say this one is definitely an upgrade.

The gimbal is easy to set up. I charged it using the included USB-C cable, and installed the recommended software. Note that with the AI Vision sensor that you don’t need to use the software, as it will interface with your native phone app (I was using an iPhone 15 in a phone case). With the AI sensor it allows you to do many of the things the AOCHUAN app will do, including tracking and gesture control. But if you’re using the app (which I recommend), you probably won’t find any improvement using the AI tracker.

Now back to the gimbal setup. I used the app and paired the device with my phone and it worked immediately. The gimbal has a great digital display that shows the battery power, plus the setting it’s on. The settings will allow it to do horizontal tracking, panning, point of view, and full follow. It doesn't call them by those names, but that’s basically what it does. It also has a decent ring light that lets you add a little extra lighting to your scene if you’re close, and a mini-tripod that can be attached to the base.

The gimbal has the ability to go zoom / wide using a button on the side, plus a well-textured scroll wheel on the side to manually focus. There’s a record button, plus a small thumb joystick button to move the head through its motions. As for weight, it’s actually not too bad and I’d be more than happy to make space for it in my travel luggage.

The app has quite a few features that are extra helpful for your use. These include things such as “Hitchcock mode”, “Inception mode”, and more. The ones that I was drawn to included an added anti-shake mode, gimbal joystick adjustments (I reversed the movements), speed of moving, time delay photos, and more.

While not app-specific while using the AI sensor, the gimbal can do things such as track faces, bodies, or specific objects when selected. And that’s simply amazing to me.

title: 3.0 out of 5 stars
text:
A phone mount below the mirror seemed like a great idea, but I ended up finding it too distracting during routine driver scanning. Closer to, or just below, top of the dashboard is just as easy to check and not in the way or distracting — for me anyway.

This was for an iPhone 13 in a '91 'Yota Hilux. I don't consider that mirror large at all, but it was a force fit for this clamp. Didn't break anything, but I could have. The clamps were deep enough for the mirror, but the way they adjust is to stick out into the passenger space instead of behind the mirror — so I had to cut off 1/2" of excess from each of the four corners to make a presentable installation.

It is also a force fit for iPhone 13 in an Otterbox. Even with a tight fit, the phone is too heavy to remain in vertical position by holding only the sides. I wanted a horizontal orientation, and the clamp was secure for that.

Ok, so it's in. Vibrates too much while the vehicle is in motion. Maybe barely tolerable on good pavement or at slow speeds. On mediocre pavement at speed, or gravel pretty much any time, it's a jackhammer. Worse than the effect on the phone, shaking transfers to the mirror, impairing its utility. That did it for me.

DISCLAIMER: The breakaway mount of my rearview does allow a tiny bit of motion which I cannot tighten out of the fitting — that makes no discernible motion in ordinary use, but it becomes s a pretty big deal when magnified by the weight of the phone. I'm not sure whether flexing of the mount itself would allow problematic vibration. If your mirror is rock solid, maybe it would remain that way with the phone on it.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
The initial reviews for this product seem to be overwhelmingly negative. After a few days (and a couple hundred miles due to some longer trips recently) I can share my experience using this mount/charger for hours at a time and minutes at a time.

To start, I tried out the Belkin MagSafe mount (basically the same price) first. It “worked” but for the price I felt it was a let-down. This brings us to this product. When I purchased it there were no reviews and I figured “let’s give it a shot”.

The air vents in my car have vertically oriented slats (doesn’t really matter but you get the picture). The material for this mount is like a soft plastic/silicone feel. It feels solid and durable. I mean, what do you plan on doing with this thing? It should just be staying inside your car…doesn’t really need to be built like a tank if you ask me.

In terms of comparability, it works great with my iPhone 13 pro (even with a MagSafe case on the phone). The phone snaps on and off with ease and feels like it is attached well to the mount. This is confirmed by my hundreds of miles of driving with my phone on this mount. The phone stayed on and didn’t rotate or do anything crazy all throughout my journey. Adjustment is very convenient if you want to tilt/angle your phone a certain way.

Now, for the CHARGING aspect of this device. I love the idea of wireless charging implemented into a car mount. I think it just makes sense (coming from someone who has had their phone charge by wire in the car for years). With this device, I find that charging works very well. At the max Qi output of 7.5W, charging speeds were adequate. I am guessing that the phone receiving cool air directly from the air vent behind the mount helps keep components cool and increase charging efficiency (if you’ve ever used a wireless charger you know a byproduct of the process is a decent amount of heat). To give you an idea of charging speed, my iPhone 13 pro went from ~20%-80% in 1.5hrs WITH maps running the entire time, music playing in the background, and brightness ~70%. Not too shabby if you ask me.

My ONLY gripe with this device so far is that the wire running from the car charging power adapter to the charging unit connects directly to the unit. Meaning that the CABLE can’t be replaced, which I find a bit silly given that the end of the cable is a standard USB-C connector going into the car charging adapter provided. In a future version of this product, I hope they consider using a standard USB-C to USB-C cable to power the charger from the car. Just my $0.02.

Hopefully you found this somewhat helpful. I use this product every time I get in the car so I’ll be sure to update if anything notable changes regarding my opinion/experience with it :)

It was hard for me to choose between the Dash version and the Vent version, but I eventually decided to go with the dashboard version as I didn't want to block my car's air vent. That's although all the dashboard mounts I ever bought have dried-out in time due to the hot weather in my country and didn't hold anymore. But I decided to give this one a try anyway.

I was very glad to see that the box contains what in first glance looks like a coaster, but it's not(!) It actually serves for a scenario that you have a textured dashboard (like in my case) where the suction of the base of the mount doesn't hold very well since it's not on a flat/smooth surface. The "coaster" comes specifically to aid you in this case - it has a sticky part at the bottom which you need to peel-off the protecting film from, and to stick it in the preferred location on your dashboard – choose the location you put it carefully as once it’s sticked, it would be difficult to take it off to relocate to a different spot. THEN - you need to raise the suction lever of the mount base, to put it on the other flat/smooth surface of the "coaster" and to lower the lever of the mount base firmly. It will hold the mount arm in place like a solid rock! And the telescopic arm is a very convenient feature! Oh, I almost forgot - the MagSafe works great at both holding my iPhone 12 mini in place and in charging it.

The only down-side I can point out about (which made me give this review only 4/5 stars and not 5/5) is that the piece that goes into the car's lighter socket doesn't have a led indicator, so you can't really tell if you have a bad fuse if/when it suddenly stops charging.

All that said, even with its shortcomings, the price and build quality still makes it above average in my opinion.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Let me first say that I have bought car mounts of different types in the past, but this is the only one that really worked for me. Quite honestly, I love this thing. My car is old enough that I still have a CD player and as a bonus, I have an additional "navigation" CD slot that's separate from my CD player that is for my outdated navigation CDs to use with the car's outdated navigation system. Since the navigation CD slot is not in use and it's perfectly located high up on the dash, this was a good decision just from a "where to locate the smartphone car mount" perspective.

I chose to put the metal plate on the outside of my ballistic jacket case. They aren't manufactured anymore, but they were way better than the otterbox (only comparing this to give people an idea of the metal plate placement for this car mount) and perhaps that's why putting the plate on the inside of the phone's case or on the outside of the phone's case (not the ballistic jacket case itself) just didn't create a strong connection to the magnet.

Putting the magnetic plate on the outside of the ballistic case has caused absolutely no problems with my handling of my phone during normal use when the phone is off of the car mount. It is a thin metal plate that does not add to the form factor thickness of the case. People who are having trouble getting a strong magnetic connection may consider doing this. One thing of note, I put this on during the hot summer months. About 3 weeks later, the glue failed and the phone dropped off the mount with the metal plate being attached to the magnet on the car mount, instead of remaining glued to the case. Since I was satisfied with the overall function of the magnetic connection to the mount, I simply put superglue on the the metal plate and it has been perfect ever since.

I did have the experience to position the magnetic mount such that the phone was perfectly vertical. When you hit those bad potholes (I do try to avoid them for the sake of my car's suspension, but sometimes you simply can't avoid them or they sneak up on you), the phone would dislodge from the mount due to the jolt. The solution is simple and that's to angle the magnetic mount such that the phone is on a little bit of the slant so that the vertical force of the vehicle's jolt on the mount has some horizontal opposing force upwards against the vertical downward jolt. Works perfectly.

My phone has incurred absolutely no negative effects as a result of it's proximity to the magnet mount point. For those who are saying the magnet isn't strong enough, I would suggest purchasing a stronger magnet and placing it on the already magnetized mount. Problem solved. I didn't have to do this, but instead of throwing your money away on a perfectly good car mount, simply drop a few cents to remedy your magnetic connection if moving the metal plate to the outside of the case still doesn't work for you (after all, some phones or some phones + their case can be pretty heavy and you may need a little more of a boost, although my Samsung S5 phone with it's ballistc case and a bit of a tilt of the mount is all I needed to establish a sufficiently strong magnetic connection).

I'm glad I took the chance on buying one more car mount. This time, it was definitely worth it!

title: 1.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I purchased this initially keyboard/mouse setup to use with Samsung Dex and it worked well with my cell phone connected to a monitor.

The keyboard took a few tries to connect to my windows 11 laptop but seems to connect easily now. On my chromebook I had to use the USB transmitter to connect the mouse but was able to connect the keyboard with bluetooth.

The lights on the keyboard and mouse are nice; on the keyboard they are adjustable, however on the mouse they are not adjustable and vary.

The USB C Charging cable it comes with is very short and not usable while using the device, however both devices seem to be holding charge and I don't have numbers yet on how long.

The bottom of it is metal, which doesn't look very good with the rest of the device

the keyboard does slid around fairly easy on a smooth desk without anything added to it. On top of a mouse pad this is a little better, and it should be easy to stick things onto the back of the keyboard if this is what you use regularly.

The keyboard and mouse have been able to work across a living room when using a device connected to a TV so the range seems functional, I haven't tested how far it goes before it stops working.

I tested gaming on a TV with the keyboard, and the keyboard was responsive for a high level PC game, the only main disadvantage is the FN key is opposite of the control key compared to my other larger keyboard.

It is nice to have a smaller keyboard for gaming away from home as the keyboard fits easily in a normal sized laptop case, whereas my full sized keyboard could barely close inside the case and may have damaged the case trying to fit it in.

For a low priced keyboard/mouse combo this setup is good as a backup or travel keyboard/mouse; I would not use the keyboard as a full time keyboard at least without additional securement in the back, but for a travel keyboard it does the job.

At under 16 dollars I'll rate this product 5 stars with respect to the price; at a higher price I would rate it lower as there are higher quality keyboard/mouse setups out there at not much higher of a price.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I got this to accommodate a new iPhone with magsafe case. I already had a Scosche magnetic holder on my dash with the 3M adhesive and it worked well. Because the magsafe magnet sits higher than the plate I had put in my old phone case it hid a good portion of my new phone behind the steering wheel. I saw this product and thought it would work but it was out of stock forever. In the meantime I went to a magsafe vent mount but my center vents don't have an on/off just directional and I didn't like the hot air blowing on the phone. The good is that the ball on this fit fine with the old mount I had on my dash. It gives you a few extra inches to get it out of the way of a vent or higher or lower viewing angle. I was worried about wobble and vibration because it moves the weight of the phone out to the end of an arm but I've found that with the arm at the 12 oclock and 6 oclock position it is pretty solid. At 3 oclock and 9 oclock it tends to wobble and vibrate and bounce around a little more. The magnet itself feels very secure.
The bad? At $40 the price is ridiculous for what you get but it fit a specific need so I ponied up. The end that attaches to the dash has a ball end that snaps into a mount and then a large nut that tightens down so if it gets loose you can just tighten it up. The magnet end that the phone mounts to is sufficiently stiff but moveable but has no visible way to tighten it when it starts to loosen. It seems that it just works on friction and after a few years of vibration and adjustment and removing the phone I have my doubts that it won't start sagging every time you put the phone on it. But I just got this product so we will have to wait and see. Good product, great product if it fits a specific need for you, but extremely overpriced and questionable durability.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I got this to accommodate a new iPhone with magsafe case. I already had a Scosche magnetic holder on my dash with the 3M adhesive and it worked well. Because the magsafe magnet sits higher than the plate I had put in my old phone case it hid a good portion of my new phone behind the steering wheel. I saw this product and thought it would work but it was out of stock forever. In the meantime I went to a magsafe vent mount but my center vents don't have an on/off just directional and I didn't like the hot air blowing on the phone. The good is that the ball on this fit fine with the old mount I had on my dash. It gives you a few extra inches to get it out of the way of a vent or higher or lower viewing angle. I was worried about wobble and vibration because it moves the weight of the phone out to the end of an arm but I've found that with the arm at the 12 oclock and 6 oclock position it is pretty solid. At 3 oclock and 9 oclock it tends to wobble and vibrate and bounce around a little more. The magnet itself feels very secure.
The bad? At $40 the price is ridiculous for what you get but it fit a specific need so I ponied up. The end that attaches to the dash has a ball end that snaps into a mount and then a large nut that tightens down so if it gets loose you can just tighten it up. The magnet end that the phone mounts to is sufficiently stiff but moveable but has no visible way to tighten it when it starts to loosen. It seems that it just works on friction and after a few years of vibration and adjustment and removing the phone I have my doubts that it won't start sagging every time you put the phone on it. But I just got this product so we will have to wait and see. Good product, great product if it fits a specific need for you, but extremely overpriced and questionable durability.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I got this to accommodate a new iPhone with magsafe case. I already had a Scosche magnetic holder on my dash with the 3M adhesive and it worked well. Because the magsafe magnet sits higher than the plate I had put in my old phone case it hid a good portion of my new phone behind the steering wheel. I saw this product and thought it would work but it was out of stock forever. In the meantime I went to a magsafe vent mount but my center vents don't have an on/off just directional and I didn't like the hot air blowing on the phone. The good is that the ball on this fit fine with the old mount I had on my dash. It gives you a few extra inches to get it out of the way of a vent or higher or lower viewing angle. I was worried about wobble and vibration because it moves the weight of the phone out to the end of an arm but I've found that with the arm at the 12 oclock and 6 oclock position it is pretty solid. At 3 oclock and 9 oclock it tends to wobble and vibrate and bounce around a little more. The magnet itself feels very secure.
The bad? At $40 the price is ridiculous for what you get but it fit a specific need so I ponied up. The end that attaches to the dash has a ball end that snaps into a mount and then a large nut that tightens down so if it gets loose you can just tighten it up. The magnet end that the phone mounts to is sufficiently stiff but moveable but has no visible way to tighten it when it starts to loosen. It seems that it just works on friction and after a few years of vibration and adjustment and removing the phone I have my doubts that it won't start sagging every time you put the phone on it. But I just got this product so we will have to wait and see. Good product, great product if it fits a specific need for you, but extremely overpriced and questionable durability.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This thang. Fabulous, fabulous, fabulous. Did I mention it's fabulous? This is probably the purchase i will enjoy using the most, second only to my Samsung Note 10 Plus. This tripod is to use with said phone. Hence my excitement. If we ever get paroled from Covid Quarantine, I will be able to take pictures of EVERYONE using this bundle of joy. There will be no more people missing from group and family portraits because one fool always had to be taking a picture.

I've never been one prone to the silliness of using a selfie stick. I do, however, LOVE taking pics. Amateur photography is my thing, and this little toy has already brought me so much joy. It's super easy to flip up to whichever height you want it at to quickly set up for the perfect shot.

I should mention that my phone is very well protected in a nifty little case which I also got on Amazon. It's therefore even bigger than the phone would be by itself. In it's case, my phone measures 6.75" by almost 3.4". The retractable phone holder opens adequately wide to accommodate and then securely hold my phone in whatever way I set it.

I've got an alarming number of friends who drank iKoolaid and are in love with their iPhones. My Samsung though, with it's screen size and resolution, takes far superior pictures. They can snap inferior pictures with their iWatches, BUT I HAVE... THIS! The added beauty that an iWatch can't cover is being able to use the far better rear camera, instead of being confined to selfie mode, as seen on an iWatch. So this wins, every time, hands down.

The knobs to adjust the height of the tripod are straightforward. You get increments of height added on for every know you unlock, as shown on the product description pictures. You can also stop it at any interim point you like. So if you need your camera at a very specific height, that is easy to accomplish. It is also super easy to switch your phone back and forth between portrait mode and landscape mode: it's a snap to do.

I must confess that I have not bothered to link the remote control that came with this tripod with my phone to use it to take pictures. I can do that with a simple voice command or with my nifty phone stylus. So I may NEVER get around to sampling that aspect of this product. Either way, this has been the best gift to myself ever.

Assembly, from pulling it out of its handy carrying case to full set-up with your phone clipped and ready to say cheese could be done in about 10 seconds easily. I can also use this for birdwatching, nature shots, and anything else I want to do. Really easy to carry around and flip out whenever you see a shot you want to line up. I love going out on nature trails to snap pics, so this will be used heavily by me. If I had any suggestion for improvement, it wouldn't actually have anything to do with the tripod: it would be that they probably could have put a light shoulder strap on the carrying case, a bit longer than the cord that is currently on it. So i may run a different cord through the loops, but I'm absolutely thrilled with this baby. Happy happy happy customer!

I've never been one prone to the silliness of using a selfie stick. I do, however, LOVE taking pics. Amateur photography is my thing, and this little toy has already brought me so much joy. It's super easy to flip up to whichever height you want it at to quickly set up for the perfect shot.

I should mention that my phone is very well protected in a nifty little case which I also got on Amazon. It's therefore even bigger than the phone would be by itself. In it's case, my phone measures 6.75" by almost 3.4". The retractable phone holder opens adequately wide to accommodate and then securely hold my phone in whatever way I set it.

I've got an alarming number of friends who drank iKoolaid and are in love with their iPhones. My Samsung though, with it's screen size and resolution, takes far superior pictures. They can snap inferior pictures with their iWatches, BUT I HAVE... THIS! The added beauty that an iWatch can't cover is being able to use the far better rear camera, instead of being confined to selfie mode, as seen on an iWatch. So this wins, every time, hands down.

The knobs to adjust the height of the tripod are straightforward. You get increments of height added on for every know you unlock, as shown on the product description pictures. You can also stop it at any interim point you like. So if you need your camera at a very specific height, that is easy to accomplish. It is also super easy to switch your phone back and forth between portrait mode and landscape mode: it's a snap to do.

I must confess that I have not bothered to link the remote control that came with this tripod with my phone to use it to take pictures. I can do that with a simple voice command or with my nifty phone stylus. So I may NEVER get around to sampling that aspect of this product. Either way, this has been the best gift to myself ever.

Assembly, from pulling it out of its handy carrying case to full set-up with your phone clipped and ready to say cheese could be done in about 10 seconds easily. I can also use this for birdwatching, nature shots, and anything else I want to do. Really easy to carry around and flip out whenever you see a shot you want to line up. I love going out on nature trails to snap pics, so this will be used heavily by me. If I had any suggestion for improvement, it wouldn't actually have anything to do with the tripod: it would be that they probably could have put a light shoulder strap on the carrying case, a bit longer than the cord that is currently on it. title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
My situation was how do I get audio from my computer to my iphone for recording and general use on social media. Before I had been able to do it with one interface attached to the iphone and another to my computer and then some cables between them in stereo. With this little device (really just a short usbc - female 1/8 inch TRS) I can plug into the headphone jack of my computer interface, listening to the monitors still, and anything that comes out of my monitor/headphone mix will go to my phone.

The only mild downside is there's obviously no volume control on the iphone side (at least not with the stock iphone video app) but my interface (a motu M2) has a volume control. For the record I keep it at about 9 or 10 o'clock, but you'll need to experiment there.

This greatly simplified my setup and setup time (since it's my phone and I just do videos for the fun of it), all I need to do is plug in a couple wires and I'm good to go. As a bonus you could hook up anything with a standard aux output from a minidisc player to a walkman to a synthesizer direct to your phone. I wasn't sure it would work, but I'm so happy that it did.
