title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I've always despised car phone mounts. I live in CA, where you're not allowed to attach mounts to your windshield, so I suffered through tons of different mounts that connected to my dash with a suction cup that inevitably came loose, or attached to my A/C vents with tiny hooks that would easily break. Cup-holder mounts placed the phone too low, requiring me to take my eyes off the road. I considered them a necessary evil.

I heard about the Kenu after I got a Prius. The mount I had on my old car wouldn't fit the A/C vents on the new one (surprise surprise). I wanted something that was easy to use, durable, and versatile, able to hold many different types of phones. The Kenu caught my eye because it was so simple. It had one moving part, the extendable arm, and they claimed to be able to fit onto any A/C vent. I had to go to an Apple Store to get one, and as soon as I got into my car, I attached it to a vent, slotted in my 5S, and I was off to the races. I loved the original Kenu and saw no reason to upgrade, until Apple announced the iPhone 6 Plus. Of course I got that beautiful monster of a phone, for which the original Kenu was too small.

This time there was no research needed. I saw that there was a plus sized airframe, so I ordered it. I swapped out my old airframe, put in the new one, and that was it. No crazy installation, no cleaning off the dash for a suction cup or adhesive. Took me one minute. It holds my 6 Plus firmly with or without a case, and I can rotate it into landscape mode to take advantage of those features on the 6 Plus. And if I really needed a stand for my phone in a pinch, I could grab the Kenu off the vent, slap it on the back of the phone, throw a credit card onto the back end, and voila! Instant stand. Personally I think this is a bit cumbersome, so I rarely take advantage of it, but it's a nice hidden feature. And when you're done it's a snap to put it back onto your car vent.

If I ever move out of CA, I'll likely get a windshield mount so I can free up my AC vent. But until that day, the Kenu Airframe+ is the only phone mount I need for my car.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I got this for my Galaxy S7 Edge phone which is in a sturdy case used in a belt holster. So the width of the package is exaggerated a bit but this has room to spare. The other negative is that it sits flush against the vent and because my phone and case are so large it effectively blocks the entire vent so I get no air from it. On the very positive side, that sitting flush against the vent gives me a very secure screen to enter things like getting to Google Maps or typing in a phone number whereas my prior mount clipped over the horizontal vane and stuck out a ways so that it bounced a bit especially when trying to type something in. There were a few times with that prior mount where I hit a big bump and the phone jumped out of the mount...that has not happened with this one.

I do text while driving but use the voice to text feature of the phone...you still have to do a couple of clicks to get there...or even to navigate you have to click a couple of times to get to Google maps and turn on the voice to text feature to give it an address. The absolute steadiness of this mount makes that easy and quick for maximum safety while driving...although I try to do these things while stopped at a stop sign or light!

text:
What can I say? A great surprise in a small package.
I have purchased five of these so far, one for myself and the rest for family members. It is very difficult to find a good car holder and near impossible to find a decent air vent car holder. So behold the Kenu Airframe+. I had to go for the plus model as I mostly use large 5.5 inch screen phones and the smaller Kenu Airframe is for standard phone sizes. The item is not cheap by any means, this has a recommended retail price of £29.99. I first came across this company on Amazon and judging by the reviews I decided to go ahead and take the plunge. For something so small it seems so expensive.
When I opened the packaging the first thing that struck me was the quality, this little thing is very well made. The back of the item which has a revolving mechanism so you can use your phone sideways if you wish has a solid rotating click to it (quite satisfying actually). Please note this style of air vent holder will not fit every car as some manufacturers have very odd shaped air vents so please check this before you buy it. But saying that this will fit most cars.
Once I chose my desired spot on my dash the Kenu Airframe+ slotted into my air vent perfectly. The left side of the holder widens out in an elastic motion so you can place your handset into the holder. When you release the arm it closes and holds the phone very strongly in place (this mechanism is quite nicely hidden in the holder). After taking quite a few journeys, the holder has never dropped out of my air vent once. I have quite a firm suspension on my car, I feel most bumps in the road but the holder has performed admirably. As I mentioned before you can rotate this holder 360 degrees and it will hold any phone securely at any angle.
This is one of the items which is essential for drivers and for us to drive safely and responsibly. If you have a compatible air vent in your car I don't think you will find a better holder on the market.
By the way, I have read some reviews of sellers selling fake versions of this item. If you want to be guarantee a perfect original item then buy direct from Amazon.

text:
Twinkle Gold:

I should have taken a better look when I was purchasing, (this part was on me!) but I didn’t realize that it did not pop in and out- it literally only sticks out. In the same breath, I’ve been messing around with this all day and it comes on and off so easy! It’s also very helpful with the iPad, because I have the keyboard case it is bulky when I try to use it flat with the keyboard folded on the back, but this fixes that issue and gives me more stability when holding the heavy iPad in the case in that position.

I have to say, not what I thought I was getting (as a lack of my own research), but very happy with what I got. I’ll be buying another one!

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
The headset buddy (hereafter HB) totally works as advertised, but it didn't at first and I want to share with you the trick.

So I was hooking up a PO-20 (don't worry what that is; it makes sounds) to my iPhone. First, I plugged the male end of the HB into the PO-20, hooked a male2male cable from the line out of the HB to the iPhone and plugged my headphones into the headphone jack of the HB. This enabled me to hear the PO-20 in my headphones but the iPhone heard nothing. Then I realized I had the HB backwards.

So I plugged the male end of the HB into the iPhone and ran the male2male from the HB to the PO-20. That got the iPhone to hear the PO-20 but I heard nothing from the headphones. I loosened the headphone plug and jiggled it and heard sound. The problem? The headphones had a microphone (mic) built in.

I inserted an adapter I had between the headphones and the PO-20 and everything worked as it should.

If you look at the jack on headphones with a mic you'll see 3 black lines. These separate the jack into 4 sections: left, right, mic, and ground. If you look at headphones without a mic you'll see 2 black lines: left, right, and ground. If you look at a pair of mono headphones, or a single earbud, the jack will have one line: signal and ground.

So the headphone jack on the Headset Buddy needs a plug with 2 black lines. That means using either headphones without a mic or getting a cheap converter plug. I hope this is helpful. :)

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
What I bought this for: I have an iPhone XS with IOS 14.5 installed. I have several old family videos on VHS tape and I want to digitize them without paying a company to do it for me. Putting my iPhone on a tripod with iPhone adapter (both from Amazon), the iPhone remains still enough to record from the TV - and it does it really well - even for long video tapes. When I tried this before, the audio got messed up by the occasional loud car driving down my street, or dogs barking across the street. I tried several times very late at night, but something always interrupted the audio.

The only solution to that was for the audio to come directly from the TV headphone jack into the iPhone instead of using the TV speakers and iPhone mic.

I used a Male to Male "TRS" headphone cable (from Amazon) - nothing special - it's basically a 3.5mm stereo headphone extension cable with a male connector on each end. Each male connector should have 3 connection points (which is often described as "TRS" - or otherwise referred to as 3 rings. One end of this male to male extension cable goes in the TV headphone jack or your other audio source. The opposite end goes into the female connector of this "TRS to TRRS" device, which you would plug into your iPhone 3.5mm headphone jack. Doing this, you should be able to record audio into your iPhone - but read on if your iPhone is newer that an iPhone 6 series.

Note: If your iPhone doesn't have a 3.5mm headphone jack, you need a "Lightening to 3.5mm" jack from Apple. If using the Apple "lightening to 3.5mm" adapter, there is a connection sequence you have to follow or this won't work. First make sure your iPhone is turned on, then plug the Apple "lightening to 3.5mm" into your iPhone. That has to be plugged in to the iPhone FIRST without anything plugged into it for this to work. Connect one end of your 3.5mm stereo headphone male to male cable into your TV headphone jack if you haven't already done so, then connect the opposite end of the 3.5mm stereo headphone male to male cable into the female end of this "TRS to TRRS" adapter. Then, plug the male end of this "TRS to TRRS" device into the Apple "Lightening to 3.5mm" adapter. Doing these steps, in that order - should let you play audio from your TV (or other audio source) and record it directly into your iPhone using the iPhone camera video app. The audio is recorded in "mono" - not stereo.

My VHS tapes are recorded in mono audio. If you are recording from a stereo source, you will need another 2 adapters so that you record both the left and right audio channels into a single mono channel. Those adapters are sold by Amazon. They are: #1: 3.5mm Stereo to Mono Adapter, 2 Pack Gold Plated 3.5mm 1/8" TRS Stereo Male Plug to 3.5mm 1/8" Mono Female Jack.
and #2: 3.5mm Mono to Stereo Adapter, 2 Pack 3.5mm 1/8" Mono Male Plug to 3.5mm 1/8" TRS Stereo Female Jack RF Adapter for Radio, Headphone .
The first adapter "#1) has a female "mono" socket (and a male stereo plug - and the second adapter #2 has a male "mono" plug and a stereo female socket. You need to plug the male "mono" connector into the female "mono" socket. This leaves you with a stereo female socket at one end and a stereo connector at the other end when these are plugged in together correctly. Now, unplug the male headphone "TRS" stereo cable from your TV (or other audio source) and plug the male stereo plug end of this 2 adapter combination into the TV headphone jack, then plug the male headphone "TRS' stereo cable into the female jack of the 2 adapter combination. That converts stereo into mono so that you get both stereo channels into a signal mono channel. If this seems confusing - I apologize. I'm good at figuring things out - but not always good at explaining how I did it.

If you do this, you will need to turn your TV volume down pretty low. Mine is set a 10% and that is perfect for the iPhone. Any louder and the sound will distort or cut out on the iPhone.

I tried using a different "TRS to TRRS" adapter and it didn't work. I suspect it was wired wrong or was defective. When I tried again using this MOVO MC3 "TRS to TRRS" adapter, it worked perfectly and I was able to record audio directly into the iPhone using both the Voice Memo app, and the Camera Video app while recording my home videos playing on my TV.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I purchased a Shure VP83 Lenshopper shotgun style mic for use with my DSLR a few years ago and wanted to use that mic with my iPhone. This cable works perfectly with the Shure Lenshopper and my iPhone 11 Pro using the official Apple lightening dongle. I recorded a few test videos and the audio on all of them came out great using this combo. I initially purchased a similar cable from another brand that was supposed to do the same thing as this cable but, that one did not work. There was (likely) nothing wrong with the cable itself however, there was a technical issue with it that prevented it from working. I only learned that after I contacted Shure to see if they knew of a reason it may not be working. It comes down to how the TRS to TRRS cable is wired. This one is wired in the correct way to work with my mic/iPhone combo using the lightening dongle. The cable the Shure rep links to below is this one.

The following is Shures’ reply for anyone who may need to know this information.

SHURE:

The most likely issue is the way the TRS-to-TRRS adapter is wired.

The 3.5mm TRS connector on the end of the VP83 cable is wired in this way:

Tip = (mono) audio
Ring = (mono) audio
Sleeve = ground/shield

The earphone jack on iPhones (and most Android phones) is a 3.5mm TRRS jack. This jack is wired according to the CTIA standard which is:

Tip = Left earphone out
Ring 1 = Right earphone out
Ring 2 = earphone common and microphone ground
Sleeve = microphone input

This wiring also is used in the Apple Lightning-to-earphone adapter. This wiring is also used in many computers that have a single 3.5mm jack that is used for both earphones and a microphone.

Some 3.5mm TRS-to-TRRS adapters are made to adapt TRS earphones to TRRS mobile 3.5mm jacks strictly for listening, with no provision for a microphone input. These are wired in this fashion:

TRS TRRS
Tip > Tip
Ring > Ring 1
Sleeve > Ring 2
Sleeve (no connection)

A proper 3.5mm TRS-to-TRRS adapter for connecting the VP83 to a mobile device would be wired in this fashion:

VP83 iPhone
Tip > Sleeve
Ring > Sleeve
Sleeve > Ring 2
Ring 1 (no connection)
Tip (no connection)

An adapter that seems to satisfy this wiring scheme is this:

https://www.amazon.com/Movo-MC3-Microphone-Adapter-Smartphones/dp/B01N9CJDVE/ref=sr_1_1?crid=2920ZD3JAK5SP&dchild=1&keywords=3.5mm+trs+to+trrs+adapter+-+microphone+adapter+for+iphone+and+android&qid=1598370405&sprefix=3.5mm+TRS+to+TRRS+adapter%2Caps%2C168&sr=8-1

Since the VP83 has its own power via the internal battery, it should work with this adapter into the typical CTIA-wired TRRS connector found on most mobile devices.

2. If you're using this keyboard with a Mac you're going to have to switch the Cmd and the Option keys around. Its fairly simple to just potpie keys off with the tool that's included with the keyboard. 3. This uses batteries. If this was rechargeable it would be absolutely perfect!

Other than that this is a wonderful keyboard and I highly recommend it. Crossing my fingers that they come out with a Mac specific version that is also rechargeable!

text:
Venía de un móvil de gama media anterior y el salto ha sido brutal. El Redmi Note 15 Pro 5G lo tiene absolutamente todo para este precio.
Cámara que sorprende de verdad:
La cámara principal de 200MP con sensor grande de 1/1.4" captura detalles con una nitidez que no esperaba encontrar en esta gama. Las fotos nocturnas y los retratos quedan espectaculares.
Batería que aguanta de sobra:
La batería de 6580 mAh con carga turbo de 45W me aguanta fácilmente un día y medio de uso intenso. Y cuando necesito cargarlo, en poco tiempo está listo.
Resistencia real:
Ha superado la prueba de resistencia al agua de 2 metros durante 24 horas certificada por TÜV SÜD , con hasta 17 componentes sellados. No es marketing — es resistencia real y duradera.
Pantalla y rendimiento:
La pantalla AMOLED de 6,83 pulgadas con 120Hz y resolución FHD+ ofrece colores vibrantes y una fluidez que engancha (WatchNation) tanto para ver series como para jugar.
Lo que más valoro a largo plazo:
Xiaomi garantiza 6 años de actualizaciones de seguridad , hasta 2032. Para mí ese detalle marca la diferencia frente a la competencia.
¿Algún pero?
El cuerpo es plástico, aunque con el acabado mate apenas se nota. Y no incluye cargador en la caja — hay que comprarlo aparte.
En resumen: pantalla brillante, batería de larga duración, buenos altavoces y resistencia real (Helveti) a un precio difícil de batir. Muy recomendado. 📱✅

text:
Très bon téléphone d'entrée/milieu de gamme, fluide et réactif, idéal pour une personne qui a besoin d'un téléphone avec une bonne capacité de stockage, pour checker les mails, surfer, regarder des vidéos et disponible à chaque instant. Prend des photos correctes mais n'égale évidemment pas un appareil photo ou un téléphone à 1500€ 😀

Les + :
- Batterie qui tient facilement 2 jours malgré une utilisation importante.
- Très bonne connectivité (excellente portée du bluetooth)
- Très fluide, réactif et intuitif.
- Performances plus qu'honorables pour une utilisation classique (les gamers ne seront pas de mon avis 😀)

Les - :
- Écran un peu grand pour une utilisation d'une main (impossible de trouver un tél plus petit de nos jours 😠)
- De trop nombreuses applications préinstallées qu'il faut supprimer ou désactiver lors de la configuration initiale.
- Haut parleur perfectible (correct mais sans plus)

En résumé, un excellent téléphone qui a répondu à toutes mes attentes, et même au-delà, depuis 2 semaines d'utilisation, le tout pour moins de 150€. Imbattable.

Très bon téléphone d'entrée/milieu de gamme, fluide et réactif, idéal pour une personne qui a besoin d'un téléphone avec une bonne capacité de stockage, pour checker les mails, surfer, regarder des vidéos et disponible à chaque instant. En résumé, un excellent téléphone qui a répondu à toutes mes attentes, et même au-delà, depuis 2 semaines d'utilisation, le tout pour moins de 150€. Imbattable.

text:
Un téléphone normalement "bas de gamme" pour Xiaomi qui est pourtant très performant !

Fonctionnalité générale :

En appel, que ce soit whatsapp ou appel classique, l'interlocuteur n'entend que notre voix et non pas les bruits environnant (excepté les autres voix). J'ai testé de taper sur une table en fer avec des couverts, de claquer les portes, de faire aboyer le chien, ect.. il n'entend rien !

La qualité audio est super, le son est fluide et les hauts parleurs sont puissants.

Les photos sont de très bonne qualité, même sur grand écran ! L'IA peut d'ailleurs les améliorer sans la modifier.

L'écran est magnifique, les couleurs sont parfaites et on peut choisir entre plusieurs modes (réalité, spécial jeux, amélioré, ect..).

Le tactile est fluide et non pas saccadé comme sur certains téléphones même avec une protection d'écran.

Les jeux fonctionnent parfaitement. Si l'option est activé, le mode "gaming" du téléphone se met en route pour offrir une super fluidité.

L'IA est intégré mais peut être désactivé. Elle offre de super options comme : animer nos propres photos pour les mettre en fond d'écran, lui poser des questions même en mode hors ligne, traduire directement quand un interlocuteur étrangers nous parle, ect...

La batterie est performante, après 2h30 d'appel vidéo whatsapp, elle n'est descendue que de 11%. La charge rapide est aussi un super point.
Attention, le fil pour la charge rapide est fourni mais pas l'adaptateur.

Les options de personnalisation (police, taille de la police, widget, ect..) sont nombreuses, parfait pour ceux qui aiment avoir un téléphone unique

Niveau sécurité:

La reconnaissance faciale est top, rien à redire

Le lecteur d'empreinte est si puissant qu'il supporte un verre trempé sans problème. Pas de bug et aucune difficulté à ouvrir le téléphone.

Petit plus qui pour moi est important : en fouillant dans les paramètres, on peut activer une option où en cliquant 2 fois sur un endroit vide de l'appareil, il s'éteint. Pas besoin d'utiliser les boutons, pratique pour ne pas les user ou pour empêcher les regards au dessus de l'épaule.

Seul point négatif, il n'y a pas d'emplacement carte SD. Mais avec autant de stockage, normalement on est tranquille un moment !

En bref, je recommande, un super rapport qualité/prix

text:
Il Redmi Note 15 5G si presenta come uno smartphone di fascia media molto equilibrato, ideale per chi cerca buone prestazioni e un’ottima esperienza multimediale senza spendere troppo.
Esteticamente da un'ottima impressione, ben realizzato, molto simmetrico e soprattutto sottile. Entrambi i lati hanno i bordi stondati, una soluzione utilizzata sempre meno e dall'apprezzamento molto soggettivo, ma che fa il suo effetto.
Monta un processore Snapdragon serie 6 di 3ª generazione che garantisce fluidità nelle operazioni quotidiane e una discreta potenza anche nel gaming, almeno nella versione che ho acquistato da 8 GB di RAM e 256 GB di memoria, espandibile fino a 1TB tramite micro SD (una combinazione rara in questa fascia di prezzo). Essendo dual SIM, il carrellino offre appunto lo spazio per due sim o una sim più la micro sd.
Bellissimo il display AMOLED da 6,67", molto ampio, con una frequenza di aggiornamento da 120 Hz, offre fluidità, colori vividi e leggibilità eccellente anche sotto la luce diretta.
La fotocamera principale da 108 MP produce scatti dettagliati e bilanciati in condizioni di luce ottimali, ma perde abbastanza in condizioni di scarsa luminosità, mentre l’ultra-grandangolare da 8 MP è sufficiente per foto panoramiche occasionali. La fotocamera frontale da 20 MP regala buoni selfie e video abbastanza nitidi anche in Full HD.
Ottima anche la batteria in silicio-carbonio da 5520 mAh con ricarica rapida a 45 W, che assicura autonomia di oltre una giornata.
Il lettore d’impronte sotto il display è rapido, gli altoparlanti stereo offrono un volume alto, ma mancano di bassi, il jack per le cuffie è assente.
Alcune caratteristiche degne di nota sono la resistenza ad acqua e polvere IP65 e la porta infrarossi da usare come telecomando con l'app integrata nel sistema operativo di Xiaomi, HyperOS 2, aggiornato ad android 15.
Si spera che venga aggiornato a breve alla versione 3 che è molto più performante, comunque sono garantiti 4 aggiornamenti alle versioni android principali.
Nella confezione, come ormai di prassi, manca il caricatore. In compenso sono presenti una cover di buona qualità ed un pratico anello per sorreggere lo smartphone o appoggiarlo su un piano.
A mio parere, Il Redmi Note 15 5G è uno smartphone completo, da preferire nella configurazione con 8 GB di RAM (quasi indispensabile se si pensa a lungo termine), sconsiglierei le versionsi con meno RAM e senza il 4g, a meno di esigenze di budget.
In definitiva, questo smartphone è perfetto per chi cerca un dispositivo affidabile con un ottimo rapporto qualità-prezzo, senza rinunciare praticamente a nulla rispetto ad altri prodotti di fascia più alta.

text:
Il Redmi Note 15 5G si presenta come uno smartphone di fascia media molto equilibrato, ideale per chi cerca buone prestazioni e un’ottima esperienza multimediale senza spendere troppo.
Esteticamente da un'ottima impressione, ben realizzato, molto simmetrico e soprattutto sottile. Entrambi i lati hanno i bordi stondati, una soluzione utilizzata sempre meno e dall'apprezzamento molto soggettivo, ma che fa il suo effetto.
Monta un processore Snapdragon serie 6 di 3ª generazione che garantisce fluidità nelle operazioni quotidiane e una discreta potenza anche nel gaming, almeno nella versione che ho acquistato da 8 GB di RAM e 256 GB di memoria, espandibile fino a 1TB tramite micro SD (una combinazione rara in questa fascia di prezzo). Essendo dual SIM, il carrellino offre appunto lo spazio per due sim o una sim più la micro sd.
Bellissimo il display AMOLED da 6,67", molto ampio, con una frequenza di aggiornamento da 120 Hz, offre fluidità, colori vividi e leggibilità eccellente anche sotto la luce diretta.
La fotocamera principale da 108 MP produce scatti dettagliati e bilanciati in condizioni di luce ottimali, ma perde abbastanza in condizioni di scarsa luminosità, mentre l’ultra-grandangolare da 8 MP è sufficiente per foto panoramiche occasionali. La fotocamera frontale da 20 MP regala buoni selfie e video abbastanza nitidi anche in Full HD.
Ottima anche la batteria in silicio-carbonio da 5520 mAh con ricarica rapida a 45 W, che assicura autonomia di oltre una giornata.
Il lettore d’impronte sotto il display è rapido, gli altoparlanti stereo offrono un volume alto, ma mancano di bassi, il jack per le cuffie è assente.
Alcune caratteristiche degne di nota sono la resistenza ad acqua e polvere IP65 e la porta infrarossi da usare come telecomando con l'app integrata nel sistema operativo di Xiaomi, HyperOS 2, aggiornato ad android 15.
Si spera che venga aggiornato a breve alla versione 3 che è molto più performante, comunque sono garantiti 4 aggiornamenti alle versioni android principali.
Nella confezione, come ormai di prassi, manca il caricatore. In compenso sono presenti una cover di buona qualità ed un pratico anello per sorreggere lo smartphone o appoggiarlo su un piano.
A mio parere, Il Redmi Note 15 5G è uno smartphone completo, da preferire nella configurazione con 8 GB di RAM (quasi indispensabile se si pensa a lungo termine), sconsiglierei le versionsi con meno RAM e senza il 4g, a meno di esigenze di budget.
In definitiva, questo smartphone è perfetto per chi cerca un dispositivo affidabile con un ottimo rapporto qualità-prezzo, senza rinunciare praticamente a nulla rispetto ad altri prodotti di fascia più alta.

text:
Estou muito satisfeito com o Poco X7 Pro 12GB/512GB. É um ótimo aparelho, excelente para diversas tarefas do dia a dia, como redes sociais, vídeos, navegação na internet, aplicativos de banco e até jogos mais pesados. O desempenho é muito fluido graças aos 12GB de RAM, e o armazenamento de 512GB é mais do que suficiente para guardar fotos, vídeos e aplicativos sem preocupação com espaço.
O custo-benefício é um dos grandes destaques. Pelo que entrega em desempenho, memória e recursos, é um aparelho que compete facilmente com modelos mais caros. Vim de um Samsung Galaxy Note 20 Ultra, então senti algumas diferenças na parte de configuração e organização do sistema no começo. A interface tem suas particularidades, e é preciso um pequeno período de adaptação. Mas depois que você se acostuma, percebe que o sistema é rápido, personalizável e muito funcional. A bateria é excelente: com uso normal, está durando praticamente um dia e meio, o que para mim é um grande diferencial. Não fico mais preocupado em carregar o aparelho no meio do dia. Outro ponto muito interessante é a função de Segundo Espaço, que permite criar como se fosse um outro celular dentro do mesmo aparelho, acessado por outra digital, por exemplo. Funciona de forma semelhante à Pasta Segura da Samsung, sendo ótimo para quem quer mais privacidade ou separar vida pessoal e profissional. A tela tem ótima qualidade, o aparelho é rápido na abertura de aplicativos e até agora não apresentou travamentos. Para minhas necessidades, atendeu muito bem e até superou expectativas. Enfim, só tenho elogios até o momento. Excelente escolha para quem quer desempenho, boa bateria e bastante armazenamento sem pagar o valor de um top de linha premium.

text:
Im Vergleich zu meinem alten N9T ist das Note 15 um Klassen besser. Leider hat die Kamera keinen Makromodus mehr, dafür aber eine Ultra HD Einstellung. So lässt sich in das Foto hineinzoomen und erhält ähnlich detailreiche Nahaufnahmen.
Der Akku ist größer geworden und hält deutlich länger durch. Das Display ist seitlich abgerundet (curved), da sollte man bedenken, dass eine zusätzlich aufgebrachte Schutzfolie sich nicht mit jeder Schutzhülle verträgt. Besser, man ordert extra CASE FRIENDLY Schutzfolien. Diese bedecken nur den flachen Teil des Displays, so dass die Ecken der Schutzhülle die Folie nicht mehr berühren und nach oben drücken können.
Das Einlesen des NFC-Chips auf der Krankenkassenkarte war auch etwas fizzelig, da die Karte ganz flach hinten angelegt werden muss, die Rückseite direkt berühren muss. Dazu muss die Schutzhülle abgenommen werden. Durch den großen Kamerabereich, der sich von der Rückseite abhebt, ist die Einlesestellung für den Chip schlecht zu finden, ging dann aber doch noch.
Ansonsten ist das Gerät in dieser günstigen Preisklasse ordentlich ausgestattet.
Ich kann das Redmi Note 15 empfehlen.

Cameras are never on my top 5 must haves but this one I am enjoying more than I expected to.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
A really solid device, honestly. I was previously using an S22 Ultra until the cellular antenna went bad, switched to a moto g stylus 2024 which was cool, but I wanted something more premium with similar features, and after a bit of research I landed on the Note 13 Pro 5G.

-Connectivity: I'm US based on a T-Mobile plan. Device works with no issues. Was stated that comparability might be a thing, but it works as any other device I've used on the network. Doesn't support e-sim, got a physical card and it's been smooth sailing.

-Security: Only negative I'd say is the face unlock. Will work accurately in well lit situations but cannot be used for biometric unlocking (Banking and finance appsfor instance) so it's a little half cocked, but still functional to an extent. Keep that in mind. If you don't mind not having a privacy screen protector, then fingerprint will work with a regular glass no problem for biometrics.

-General features: Camera is good, definitely better than Motorola, almost as good as Samsung. I prefer having an aux connector, and the ir blaster is fun to use and is useful in general. Storage is good despite not having sd expansion. Processing speed is good (better with a few tweaks in developer options and changing ram settings). Hyper OS reminds me of custom roms and the customization is really good. Battery life is solid, haven't noticed the device getting too hot or anything like that. I am a little sketchy about the lithium polymer battery and long term use but I'll cross that bridge when I cross it. So far so good though after a few weeks of use. Build quality is really good just be sure to get camera protectors or a good case for the lens bump on the rear.

Really good phone.
timestamp_raw: Reviewed in the United States on January 31, 2025

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
ONE WEEK REVIEW:
After using this phone for over a week now, I'm very happy with it and it exceeded my expectations with its build quality, speed, design and function of this phone. Overall a great purchase for the money.

THINGS THAT IMPRESSED ME:
- The phone is fast and the screen vivid and responsive.
- Phone is duel SIM compatible.
- Comes with a screen protector already installed AND a basic phone case which I actually like and use.
- OS is very similar to an Apple experience and works well.

THINGS I DIDN'T CARE FOR:
- Bloatware: unnecessary programs you'll want to remove.
- Camera: is not quite as good as hoped for. Main camera almost always makes something blurry. The 200mp is better, but not perfect. Honestly it may have something to do with the default camera software not being very good. You may want to find a better camera app for taking pictures.

But for the price, I would definitley recommend this phone!

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
A really solid device, honestly. I was previously using an S22 Ultra until the cellular antenna went bad, switched to a moto g stylus 2024 which was cool, but I wanted something more premium with similar features, and after a bit of research I landed on the Note 13 Pro 5G.

-Connectivity: I'm US based on a T-Mobile plan. Device works with no issues. Was stated that comparability might be a thing, but it works as any other device I've used on the network. Doesn't support e-sim, got a physical card and it's been smooth sailing.

-Security: Only negative I'd say is the face unlock. Will work accurately in well lit situations but cannot be used for biometric unlocking (Banking and finance appsfor instance) so it's a little half cocked, but still functional to an extent. Keep that in mind. If you don't mind not having a privacy screen protector, then fingerprint will work with a regular glass no problem for biometrics.

-General features: Camera is good, definitely better than Motorola, almost as good as Samsung. I prefer having an aux connector, and the ir blaster is fun to use and is useful in general. Storage is good despite not having sd expansion. Processing speed is good (better with a few tweaks in developer options and changing ram settings). Hyper OS reminds me of custom roms and the customization is really good. Battery life is solid, haven't noticed the device getting too hot or anything like that. I am a little sketchy about the lithium polymer battery and long term use but I'll cross that bridge when I cross it. So far so good though after a few weeks of use. Build quality is really good just be sure to get camera protectors or a good case for the lens bump on the rear.

Really good phone.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
[edit]
I forgot to mention that I use this with Mint mobile. I've also swapped with a T-Mobile card too and found the phone calls work just fine. Internet needs a little config to get going. In short, I need to add the proper APN settings for different carriers. This is a limitation of the carrier and not the phone. Luckily, these settings are easily found with a quick google search and you can get the settings from Mint and T-Mobile quite easily. Once you've found the page, you have to go into your phones settings, go to the mobile provider settings and add a new access point network (APN) profile. Then I just enter the info found in the table.
Now it's easy to screw up these settings, but that's no big deal. Just delete the profile and try again, a wrong setting won't brick your phone.
I've had this for about 4 months so far and it runs circles around my son's iPhone 16. I still get superb battery life and have enabled a feature where it reboots automatically every night.
After these months of usage, I'm happy with the camera, but that's because I'm not a big camera kind of person. Also, I found that the dolby sound setting kind of sucks, so I leave that turned off. I still feel like it's the best money I've ever spent on a smartphone in decades. I recently visited GeekBench just to see how this phone stacks up and again I'm proud to say that other phones within the same score are all north of $900. If I may nerd out just a bit, this phone is like the Millenium Falcon... “She may not look like much, but she's got it where it counts, kid.” - Han Solo
[/edit]
Simply put, you will not find another snapdragon 8 Gen 3 with 12 GB of RAM for under $1000 anywhere else.
Read the reviews of the snapdragon versus the Tensor chip (Pixel 9) for yourself.
As for the OS, it's the XiaoMi OS which is at its heart, Android 14. and it is truly Android 14, play store and all.
The Xiaomi OS customizations aren't too bad and there's very little bloatware (reminds me of how much I dislike Samsung).
There is a neat battery saving feature where you can choose between some limited charging profiles to just straight up limiting the maximum charge to 80% (note that this limit setting does not work when the phone is powered off).
The thing just sips power. I've installed a couple of emulators just to game around a bit and even though I limit the charge to 80%, I've never really seen my phone dip below 50% of battery life. I only charge it during the day and the 90W power supply provides me a full charge in about 2-5 minutes. (note that this is only going from 50% to 80% and I have overheating protection enabled).
The clock app is a little funky. make sure you're using the built in clock app and not the one from google. You'll get some strange error notification that I can't seem to remember at this time.
I got this phone because my old phone (galaxy 9s) just didn't have the processing power and had a very hard time with Android Auto wirelessly.
I kind of wish this thing had an SD card slot.
It does have a tray that supports two nano sim cards (Back to back) and the box does come with a silicone case for the phone as well as a qc car adapter.
It does not support wireless charging and does not have a headphone jack.

text:
Xiaomi Poco F6 5G + 4G LTE: Rendimiento y Estilo a un Precio Competitivo

El Xiaomi Poco F6 5G + 4G LTE es un smartphone que combina potencia, diseño y funcionalidad, posicionándose como una opción destacada en la gama media-alta. Aquí te contamos por qué este dispositivo merece tu atención.

Diseño y Pantalla:
Con una pantalla AMOLED de 6.67 pulgadas y resolución CrystalRes 1.5K, el Poco F6 ofrece una experiencia visual impresionante. Su tasa de refresco de 120 Hz garantiza una navegación fluida, mientras que el brillo máximo de 2400 nits asegura una excelente visibilidad incluso bajo luz solar directa. Además, está protegido por Gorilla Glass Victus, lo que lo hace resistente a rayones y caídas.

El diseño minimalista y elegante, disponible en colores como negro, titanio y verde, combina funcionalidad y estilo. Aunque su carcasa es de plástico, el acabado mate y los bordes redondeados le dan un toque premium.

Rendimiento:
Equipado con el procesador Snapdragon 8s Gen 3 y hasta 12 GB de RAM LPDDR5X, este dispositivo ofrece un rendimiento excepcional. Ya sea para multitarea o juegos exigentes, el Poco F6 responde sin problemas. Su almacenamiento UFS 4.0 de hasta 512 GB asegura velocidades rápidas y espacio suficiente para tus archivos.

El sistema operativo HyperOS, basado en Android 14, optimiza la experiencia del usuario con una interfaz intuitiva y fluida.

Cámara:
El sistema de cámaras incluye un sensor principal de 50 MP con estabilización óptica (OIS), que captura imágenes nítidas y detalladas incluso en condiciones de poca luz. La cámara ultra gran angular de 8 MP y la frontal de 20 MP completan el conjunto, ofreciendo versatilidad para fotografía y videollamadas. Además, permite grabar videos en 4K a 60 fps.

Batería y Carga:
Con una batería de 5000 mAh, el Poco F6 promete una autonomía de un día completo con uso intensivo. Su carga rápida de 90 W permite recargar el dispositivo al 100% en tan solo 35 minutos, ideal para quienes siempre están en movimiento.

Conectividad y Extras:
El soporte para 5G y 4G LTE asegura una conectividad rápida y estable. También incluye características como altavoces estéreo con Dolby Atmos, NFC, sensor de huellas en pantalla y resistencia al agua IP64.

Conclusión:
El Xiaomi Poco F6 5G + 4G LTE es una excelente opción para quienes buscan un smartphone potente y bien equilibrado sin gastar una fortuna. Su pantalla vibrante, rendimiento de primer nivel y carga ultrarrápida lo convierten en una opción difícil de superar en su rango de precio.

Pros:
- Pantalla AMOLED de alta calidad.
- Rendimiento excepcional con Snapdragon 8s Gen 3.
- Carga rápida de 90 W.
- Sistema de cámaras versátil.

Contras:
- Carcasa de plástico.
- Sin certificación de resistencia al agua completa.

text:
Adquirí el Xiaomi Redmi 15 5G pensando que sería una evolución natural de mi confiable Redmi Note 11S, que sigo usando diariamente en mi rutina (trabajo, redes y multimedia). ¡Gran error! El Note 11S no solo mantiene su vigencia, sino que aventaja al nuevo modelo en calidad real de uso. El 15 5G parece más un downgrade en lo que más importa. Te detallo la comparación punto por punto, basada en semanas de prueba lado a lado:

Cámaras: Aquí está la mayor decepción. Mi Note 11S tiene 4 cámaras funcionales que brillan en todo tipo de escenarios: la macro para detalles cercanos (flores, comida), la ultra-angular para paisajes amplios, la impresionante principal de 108MP para fotos ultra detalladas y nítidas (incluso impresas), y la frontal para selfies decentes. En contraste, el Redmi 15 5G solo tiene una cámara realmente funcional (la principal), mientras que los otros dos lentes son pura simulación o decoración inútil – no capturan nada útil, ni macro ni angular real. Las fotos del 15 5G salen con menos detalle, colores lavados y ruido en poca luz. Si te gusta la fotografía casual, el 11S gana por goleada.

Velocidad de respuesta: El Note 11S responde como un rayo: apps se abren en segundos, multitarea fluida sin lags, incluso con docenas de pestañas en Chrome. El 15 5G, pese a su hardware "moderno", tartamudea al scrollear TikTok, cambiar entre WhatsApp y email, o jugar juegos ligeros. Sientes demoras frustrantes que rompen el flujo diario.

Altavoces y audio: Los altavoces estéreo del Note 11S entregan sonido envolvente, con graves decentes y volumen alto para videos o música sin auriculares. Perfecto para ver series en el bus. El 15 5G suena plano, con volumen bajo y sin esa inmersión – como si escuchara de un teléfono viejo.

Puerto 3.5mm para audífonos: El Note 11S lo incluye, lo que me permite conectar mis audífonos cableados favoritos al instante, sin latencia ni baterías extras. El 15 5G lo eliminó por completo, forzándome a Bluetooth (que a veces falla) o adaptadores USB-C. Un paso atrás innecesario en 2026.

Tiempo de carga y manejabilidad: El Note 11S carga del 0 al 100% en menos de una hora con su cargador rápido incluido en la caja, más earbuds inalámbricos de la marca (como Redmi Buds) y audífonos cableados como bonus – ¡todo listo para usar de inmediato! Su tamaño compacto (6.43") cabe perfecto en el bolsillo y se maneja con una mano sin esfuerzo. El 15 5G no trae cargador en la caja (¡ni earbuds ni audífonos cableados!), y para alcanzar los tiempos de carga prometidos en la web de Xiaomi (rápida supuestamente), necesitas comprar uno específico de la marca – genéricos no cumplen. Resultado: carga más lenta en la práctica, y su diseño más grande/pesado lo hace incómodo para uso prolongado.

Relación precio: Pagué por el Redmi 15 5G ~$150-240 USD (precio actual/launch similar), casi lo mismo que el Note 11S en su lanzamiento (~$180-280 USD), que hoy se encuentra por ~$110-120 USD en stock nuevo/usado. Por ese dinero, el 11S te da más funciones reales, accesorios incluidos y duraderas; el 15 5G se siente sobrevalorado, como si pagaras premium por promesas vacías.lacuracaonline+3

Dicho esto, el Redmi 15 5G tiene méritos en conectividad moderna: 5G para descargas ultrarrápidas (ideal para streaming en 4K), una batería de mayor capacidad que aguanta 1-2 días con uso moderado, Android más reciente con actualizaciones prometidas, y NFC para pagos sin contacto en tiendas (algo que mi Note 11S no ofrece).

En conclusión, si priorizas cámaras versátiles, rendimiento snappy, audio inmersivo, comodidad, accesorios y valor por dinero, quédate con el Note 11S – ¡sigue siendo el rey! El 15 5G no justifica el cambio para mí; lo estoy devolviendo. 2 estrellas solo por la batería y 5G.

title: 2.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Adquirí el Xiaomi Redmi 15 5G pensando que sería una evolución natural de mi confiable Redmi Note 11S, que sigo usando diariamente en mi rutina (trabajo, redes y multimedia). ¡Gran error! El Note 11S no solo mantiene su vigencia, sino que aventaja al nuevo modelo en calidad real de uso. El 15 5G parece más un downgrade en lo que más importa. Te detallo la comparación punto por punto, basada en semanas de prueba lado a lado:

Cámaras: Aquí está la mayor decepción. Mi Note 11S tiene 4 cámaras funcionales que brillan en todo tipo de escenarios: la macro para detalles cercanos (flores, comida), la ultra-angular para paisajes amplios, la impresionante principal de 108MP para fotos ultra detalladas y nítidas (incluso impresas), y la frontal para selfies decentes. En contraste, el Redmi 15 5G solo tiene una cámara realmente funcional (la principal), mientras que los otros dos lentes son pura simulación o decoración inútil – no capturan nada útil, ni macro ni angular real. Las fotos del 15 5G salen con menos detalle, colores lavados y ruido en poca luz. Si te gusta la fotografía casual, el 11S gana por goleada.

Velocidad de respuesta: El Note 11S responde como un rayo: apps se abren en segundos, multitarea fluida sin lags, incluso con docenas de pestañas en Chrome. El 15 5G, pese a su hardware "moderno", tartamudea al scrollear TikTok, cambiar entre WhatsApp y email, o jugar juegos ligeros. Sientes demoras frustrantes que rompen el flujo diario.

Altavoces y audio: Los altavoces estéreo del Note 11S entregan sonido envolvente, con graves decentes y volumen alto para videos o música sin auriculares. Perfecto para ver series en el bus. El 15 5G suena plano, con volumen bajo y sin esa inmersión – como si escuchara de un teléfono viejo.

Puerto 3.5mm para audífonos: El Note 11S lo incluye, lo que me permite conectar mis audífonos cableados favoritos al instante, sin latencia ni baterías extras. El 15 5G lo eliminó por completo, forzándome a Bluetooth (que a veces falla) o adaptadores USB-C. Un paso atrás innecesario en 2026.

Tiempo de carga y manejabilidad: El Note 11S carga del 0 al 100% en menos de una hora con su cargador rápido incluido en la caja, más earbuds inalámbricos de la marca (como Redmi Buds) y audífonos cableados como bonus – ¡todo listo para usar de inmediato! Su tamaño compacto (6.43") cabe perfecto en el bolsillo y se maneja con una mano sin esfuerzo. El 15 5G no trae cargador en la caja (¡ni earbuds ni audífonos cableados!), y para alcanzar los tiempos de carga prometidos en la web de Xiaomi (rápida supuestamente), necesitas comprar uno específico de la marca – genéricos no cumplen. Resultado: carga más lenta en la práctica, y su diseño más grande/pesado lo hace incómodo para uso prolongado.

Relación precio: Pagué por el Redmi 15 5G ~$150-240 USD (precio actual/launch similar), casi lo mismo que el Note 11S en su lanzamiento (~$180-280 USD), que hoy se encuentra por ~$110-120 USD en stock nuevo/usado. Por ese dinero, el 11S te da más funciones reales, accesorios incluidos y duraderas; el 15 5G se siente sobrevalorado, como si pagaras premium por promesas vacías.lacuracaonline+3

Dicho esto, el Redmi 15 5G tiene méritos en conectividad moderna: 5G para descargas ultrarrápidas (ideal para streaming en 4K), una batería de mayor capacidad que aguanta 1-2 días con uso moderado, Android más reciente con actualizaciones prometidas, y NFC para pagos sin contacto en tiendas (algo que mi Note 11S no ofrece).

En conclusión, si priorizas cámaras versátiles, rendimiento snappy, audio inmersivo, comodidad, accesorios y valor por dinero, quédate con el Note 11S – ¡sigue siendo el rey! El 15 5G no justifica el cambio para mí; lo estoy devolviendo. 2 estrellas solo por la batería y 5G.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I came into this not expecting much, but I got blown away instead.
PROS
I'm not sure where to start.
So, how about I START with this? For those complaining about the phone having 8GB of RAM, the phone is actually 12 GB. I think we've reached the point where people should know about the restrictions placed on RAM for all devices. The phone clocks out around 8GB and gradually goes up to 9 or even 11 GB, and continuously fluctuates from there with usage.

There's literally no lag in the phone's U.I. The MediaTek 8400-Ultra is a beast, making both the phone's animations and gaming performance absolutely flawless. Pictures are absolutely stunning, with the only takeaway being abnormally high contrasts in how the Xiaomi Poco X7 Pro takes its pictures. The battery life, including Xiaomi's new hyper-charge 90 WATT Technology, combined, makes for a phone that holds for a very long time but also recharges within mere MINUTES. The phone also comes with a ton of features (including AI features) that set it apart from its competitors. In most lower graphic games, I got an FPS reading of around 118-120 FPS, in higher graphic games, I got a reading of 110-117 FPS, and in extreme graphical games, I got a reading of 90-95 FPS. The resolution, unlike most phones I've used, is so sharp and breathtaking here, and it can be improved further by activating SUPER RESOLUTION. Imaging apps like Instagram, Threads, and other media-based apps all look amazing. In terms of performance, Gaming, features, and design, the Xiaomi Poco X7 PRO comes insanely close to the level of a FLAGSHIP title, all for a reasonable price point in the Android competitive space. HOWEVER, I did say ONLY CLOSE.

CONS
The Xiaomi Poco X7 PRO ONLY lasts as long as 1/2 day with heavy usage; you'll find yourself having to charge it after that.
The Xiaomi Poco X7 PRO comes with a lot of ADS & bloatware, unfortunately ( but this can all be deactivated and removed, rest assured)

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I bought this to replace a single-sim Xiaomi Redmi Note 8 Pro that was in excellent shape but didn't support 2 sims (unless you lose the microSD), so I had to look for a replacement and chose this one.

Overall the phone is good, you can find plenty of reviews on the internet, so you can go there, what I've found is that those reviews are mostly a quick overview, but not an in-depth review, so here it comes.

I don't love, I even dislike the rounded screen, I don't see the use for it or any advantage, if anything, it just makes the phone harder to hold with one hand without accidentally pressing the screen with your palm, but it is what it is, right?

The camera is ok, it takes good pictures provided you have enough lighting, but I've found that in less than optimal light, the saturation is weak, you'll need to edit your photos to add more color when shooting interiors.

Now, the phone is fast, no concerns there, it's fast and responsive, I've never had to wait for anything to load and the mobile carrier internet works much faster on this one than on my previous Note 8 Pro. Sometimes I've had to install an app using my mobile data, and it downloaded blazing fast.

In terms of screen, I've found that I would like to have a dimmer option, sometimes I use my phone at night and even the lowest brightness is too much, even with the night time settings enabled, it's just too bright for bed but, again, this is what it is.

I have another issue with the volume, while the speaker is very loud, I've also found that the volume settings on the lowest one and the next one up are very off. If you press the volume down all the way to mute and then press the button once to turn it up, you can't hear anything, not even holding your phone 5 inches from your face, you need to put it in your ear to hear anything. If, on the other hand, you press the volume up once more, it jumps just one step (as expected) but the next volume setting is too loud to listen to in bed.

Now, I thought it was perhaps an issue of miscalibrated volume steps. At the end of the day, you can always use your finger to move the volume bar exactly where you want it, but this is not the case, even if you move the volume bar between these 2 steps, the phone doesn't register that, it only goes from almost muted to that loud setting. Again, if you plan to doomscroll in bed, this is not the option.

That's mostly it, in terms of battery, it lasts about 14 hours of regular use, sometimes I've used it intermittently at the office and by 6:00 PM I have only 20% left, the last 10% lasts about a couple of deep breaths. Not sure about this one, I was expecting better battery life.

Hope this helps, it's a nice phone, it's not expensive, but it has some issues, perhaps that's the downside of buying this brand.

I almost forgot, it doesn't come with a charger adapter, but it does come with a USB-C cable and a flexible (yet nice built) case, so you can start using it right away while you order a proper case.

text:
Der Snapdragon 7Gen2 ist nicht nur laut diversen Test's ein echtes Highlight. Seine Leistungsmerkmale sind auf Flagship-Niveau und Spiele, sowie Apps laufen absolut ohne Verzögerung. Das Amoled / OLED Display mit 120Hz ist ebenfalls qualitativ hochwertig mit einer hohen Helligkeit. Das 67 Watt Ladegerät lädt das Handy von 0 auf 100% in rund 30 Minuten. Die Kamera ist durch den verbauten Chipsatz solide und macht gute Fotos.
Das Überspielen vom alten Xiaomi Smartphone war problemlos. Allerdings muss man sich zum Einrichten trotzdem ca. 3-4 Stunden Zeit nehmen. Nach dem Löschen der Bloatware, dem Ausschalten der Werbung und dem optimieren der Oberfläche ist es derzeit das beste Smartphone der Mittelklasse. Im direkten Vergleich zum Redmi Note 12 Pro oder dem Samsung Galaxy A54 ist das Poco F5 um mindestens 1 Klasse besser. Wer auf induktives Laden besteht und Fingerabdrucksensor im Display sollte die Poco F5 Pro Variante nehmen. Hier ist der Snapdragon 8Gen1 verbaut, hat aber nur minimal bessere Eigenschaften als der Chipsatz des normalen F5.

text:
Questo telefono è una bomba, con un rapporto qualità prezzo incredibile.
Adoro la MIUI perchè la trovo veramente funzionale e arriva già con la v14 e android 13.
Il processore è super veloce, così come ram e disco, mai un piantamento finora.
Il display è buono, ma non eccelso, così come la fotocamera, ma a questo prezzo, non ci si poteva aspettare un flagship, comunque promossi entrambi.
L'audio è in chiamata è buono, sia in capsula che in vivavoce ed è buono anche dagli altoparlanti per le applicazioni multimediali.
Si ricarica in un niente e la batteria dura veramente parecchio, anche sotto stress, in più viene fornito l'alimentatore da 67W.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I've had a horrible run with tech lately; I bought a new 3D printer during Prime Days, and Amazon sent me a used one that has clearly seen better days, I had to get a new phone because my old one couldn't be updated anymore due to poor memory, one of my graphics tablets is suddenly on it's last legs... and now I find that soon, my venerable old Samsung Galaxy Tab A7 Lite will soon cease getting updates due to it's Android version approaching sunset.

Most if not all of you are asking "What does this have to do with this Xiaomi tablet?" Bear with me. At the time of writing, Samsung tablets are EXPENSIVE. And I wanted to upgrade a little, since I'm using a tablet more and more these days. Don't even think about suggesting an iPad to me; I will never buy an Apple product, but I'm already on a soapbox, so I won't go there.

So I did some research, and came across Xiaomi, among other brands that are much more affordably priced than Samsung or Apple. Well, due to the 3D printer incident, I really didn't want to buy such a device on Amazon. But to my surprise, eBay and other vendors were asking more for this tablet than Amazon was!

Next point of concern: Overseas brand tablets like this one can be scams. Usually, they're obvious to spot if you're tech-savvy. You'll see tablets here on Amazon that claim "1TB memory" with "18GB RAM!". Bogus specs; don't ever buy such a tablet (at least at this time of writing, tech is always improving!). So, not only was I loathe to buy tech like this from Amazon, but a lot of tablets like this are scams.

Well, I scrutinized this listing and had two different AI do same, and this tablet seemed like a genuine deal. And although I'm still wary about getting a used, beat up product, Amazon still has an amazing return policy. So I ordered this tablet.

Those who are still reading, thanks for enduring my long prelude. I was SHOCKED at how many falsely spec'd tablets are sold here on Amazon, so I wanted to get the word out. Now onto the tablet.

I received a NEW, not used tablet. It was in a tightly sealed box with all accessories, and testing it via my PC confirmed it was indeed new (making the PC pull specs like battery cycles, processor lag, etc.).

Now, here's where I focus on the first part of my review title: I only give this tablet five stars if it's "de-bloated". Since my prelude is stretching this review out, I'm not going to explain that process in depth. Basically, you download Android software licensed by Google, and in doing so, accept that you either know what you're doing and will only hold yourself liable, or don't know but will still only hold yourself liable.

De-bloating this Xiaomi tablet is a must in my opinion; EVERY SINGLE XIAOMI APP in this tablet wants to track as much information about you as possible and send it overseas. I know not everyone cares about that, but I do. So I removed as many software packages from this tablet as I could, and disabled a few that I could not remove using the de-bloater software. Without a de-bloat, I would give this tablet 1.5 stars. It's that bad.

With all that tracking software removed, I loaded my desired apps on, and I am really impressed by this tablet's performance! As per the second part of my review title, this tablet is punching way above it's weight for the price! At the time of writing, a comparable Samsung tablet would have cost $700, and I got this one for $330!

Running one of my heavyweight apps, Nomad Sculpt, can make my old Galaxy Tab A7 Lite beg for mercy when my sculpted 3D models start to get really detailed. This Xiaomi has carelessly laughed off all my latest detailed works. I never thought I'd say this, but I'm going to bump up some of the limits of Nomad Sculpt for more functionality since this tablet can clearly handle it! Using VLC, all my video and CD backup files play smoothly, and both my headphones and new Bluetooth-capable graphics tablet sync right up to this tablet. As an added plus to de-bloating it, the graphics tablet is super smooth running on this tablet!

Anyway, I'll close this review in a summary: If you are not tech-savvy but don't want a bunch of data gathered about you and sent overseas, then I'm afraid you'll have to look at the big brands. If you're comfortable with running de-bloat software or can learn and execute it properly (just have an AI help you!), then again, you're going to get serious bang for the buck with this tablet!! Or, if you just don't care about this nuance but want a tablet that performs well at a good price, again, this tablet is right up your alley in my experience!

Next point of concern: Overseas brand tablets like this one can be scams. Usually, they're obvious to spot if you're tech-savvy. You'll see tablets here on Amazon that claim "1TB memory" with "18GB RAM!". Bogus specs; don't ever buy such a tablet (at least at this time of writing, tech is always improving!). So, not only was I loathe to buy tech like this from Amazon, but a lot of tablets like this are scams.

Well, I scrutinized this listing and had two different AI do same, and this tablet seemed like a genuine deal. And although I'm still wary about getting a used, beat up product, Amazon still has an amazing return policy. So I ordered this tablet.

Those who are still reading, thanks for enduring my long prelude. I was SHOCKED at how many falsely spec'd tablets are sold here on Amazon, so I wanted to get the word out. Now onto the tablet.

I received a NEW, not used tablet. It was in a tightly sealed box with all accessories, and testing it via my PC confirmed it was indeed new (making the PC pull specs like battery cycles, processor lag, etc.).

Now, here's where I focus on the first part of my review title: I only give this tablet five stars if it's "de-bloated". Since my prelude is stretching this review out, I'm not going to explain that process in depth. Basically, you download Android software licensed by Google, and in doing so, accept that you either know what you're doing and will only hold yourself liable, or don't know but will still only hold yourself liable.

De-bloating this Xiaomi tablet is a must in my opinion; EVERY SINGLE XIAOMI APP in this tablet wants to track as much information about you as possible and send it overseas. I know not everyone cares about that, but I do. So I removed as many software packages from this tablet as I could, and disabled a few that I could not remove using the de-bloater software. Without a de-bloat, I would give this tablet 1.5 stars. It's that bad.

With all that tracking software removed, I loaded my desired apps on, and I am really impressed by this tablet's performance! As per the second part of my review title, this tablet is punching way above it's weight for the price! At the time of writing, a comparable Samsung tablet would have cost $700, and I got this one for $330!

Running one of my heavyweight apps, Nomad Sculpt, can make my old Galaxy Tab A7 Lite beg for mercy when my sculpted 3D models start to get really detailed. This Xiaomi has carelessly laughed off all my latest detailed works. I never thought I'd say this, but I'm going to bump up some of the limits of Nomad Sculpt for more functionality since this tablet can clearly handle it! Using VLC, all my video and CD backup files play smoothly, and both my headphones and new Bluetooth-capable graphics tablet sync right up to this tablet. As an added plus to de-bloating it, the graphics tablet is super smooth running on this tablet!

Anyway, I'll close this review in a summary: If you are not tech-savvy but don't want a bunch of data gathered about you and sent overseas, then I'm afraid you'll have to look at the big brands. If you're comfortable with running de-bloat software or can learn and execute it properly (just have an AI help you!), then again, you're going to get serious bang for the buck with this tablet!! Or, if you just don't care about this nuance but want a tablet that performs well at a good price, again, this tablet is right up your alley in my experience!

text:
Xiaomi Redmi Pad SE: A Budget Champion

When it comes to affordable Android tablets, we often expect a familiar story: mediocre build quality, outdated internals, sluggish performance, and a short lifespan. But the Xiaomi Redmi Pad SE defies those expectations. It’s the first Xiaomi device I’ve used, and I must say, I’m impressed—even though this is a budget tablet1.

Here’s why the Redmi Pad SE stands out:

Impressive 90Hz Refresh Rate: What sets this tablet apart in its price range is its 90Hz refresh rate. Most budget-friendly tablets stick to the standard 60Hz, but the Redmi Pad SE steps up the game. With smoother animations, fluid transitions, and remarkably responsive scrolling, it feels surprisingly premium2.
Solid Build Quality: The metal body of the Redmi Pad SE feels good in hand. Xiaomi didn’t compromise on materials, and it shows. You won’t mistake it for a flimsy paperweight anytime soon.
Decent Performance: Powered by the Qualcomm Snapdragon 680 4G, the tablet handles everyday tasks well. Whether you’re browsing, streaming, or multitasking, it won’t leave you frustrated.
Multimedia Features:
Quad Speakers: The Redmi Pad SE boasts quad speakers, making media consumption enjoyable.
Expandable Storage: With 128GB of storage (expandable via microSD card), you won’t run out of space for your apps and files.
High-Refresh Display: The 11-inch IPS LCD display with a 90Hz refresh rate ensures a pleasant viewing experience.
Affordable Price: The Redmi Pad SE won’t break the bank. At around $240 for the 128GB/8GB model, it’s easy on your wallet. Plus, you get three color options: Mint Green, Graphite Gray, and Lavender Purple.
Of course, there are some trade-offs:

Graphics performance isn’t mind-blowing.
No official support for an active stylus.
No fingerprint scanner.

text:
Tracks everything I wanted. Comfortable to wear day and night. Have charged it once since purchase in less than an hour. It easily made it 2 weeks and still had 19% battery left which is impressive when for the first week I had everything on continuous tracking, 3 vibration alarms daily and app/phone notifications on while I was constantly playing with my new "toy"!
Note that step count will be low if you use a walker or are pushing a shopping cart. Your arm movements being static in these situations will not show your walking activities. You could change the location of the band to your shoe or ankle, but will lose the other health monitoring if you do so. Using a separate pedometer or your cell phone in your pocket would be best in that situation.
Solid 5 stars for: look (lots of free watch faces), lightweight, feature/app options, battery life, and value. Kudos for it's silent vibration alarm that doesn't disturb others but will keep you on time for waking, meds or other activities.
Solid choice and budget friendly.

text:
Ho acquistato l'UMIDIGI G5A con molta curiosità, attratto dalle specifiche tecniche e dal prezzo relativamente competitivo. Dopo averlo utilizzato per circa un mese, posso dire che, purtroppo, non sono del tutto soddisfatto del prodotto. Ecco un'analisi dettagliata delle mie impressioni.

Design e Display:
Partiamo dal punto positivo: il design è abbastanza moderno e accattivante. Il display da 6,52 pollici è ampio e ha una risoluzione decente per il prezzo. I colori sono abbastanza vividi e la visibilità alla luce del sole non è male. Tuttavia, la qualità del touch non è sempre precisa e talvolta l'interazione con lo schermo può risultare imprecisa, soprattutto quando si scorrono pagine o si usano app che richiedono un tocco rapido.

Prestazioni:
Il processore e la RAM da 8GB (4GB+4GB virtuali) e i 64GB di memoria interna sono certamente promettenti sulla carta, ma nella pratica non sono riuscito a ottenere la fluidità sperata. Le app si aprono con un po' di lentezza e talvolta c'è un evidente lag durante l'uso multitasking. Anche nelle operazioni più semplici, come navigare tra le app o scorrere i social media, si notano dei rallentamenti. Ho anche avuto qualche crash delle app più pesanti, come quelle di editing foto o video.

Nonostante la memoria espandibile fino a 1TB, non credo che il dispositivo sfrutti pienamente le potenzialità della RAM aggiuntiva. Il supporto per una memoria SD è utile, ma purtroppo non compensa l'esperienza complessiva di prestazioni non ottimali.

Fotocamera:
Le fotocamere (principale da 16MP e frontale da 8MP) sono nella media per un dispositivo di questa fascia di prezzo, ma non mi hanno particolarmente impressionato. Le foto in condizioni di buona luce sono accettabili, ma appena le condizioni di illuminazione peggiorano, la qualità diminuisce notevolmente, con immagini sgranate e poco definite. Anche il focus non è sempre preciso, e la modalità notturna lascia molto a desiderare.

Batteria:
La batteria da 5150 mAh è un altro punto positivo. Con un utilizzo medio, riesco a coprire tranquillamente tutta la giornata senza problemi. Tuttavia, la ricarica non è così rapida come mi aspettavo, e ci vuole un po' più di tempo rispetto ad altri modelli simili per raggiungere una carica completa.

Software:
L'Android 13 è sicuramente un punto a favore, con un'interfaccia abbastanza pulita e un'esperienza utente piuttosto simile a quella di altri dispositivi Android. Tuttavia, ho riscontrato qualche bug e lag qua e là, specialmente con le notifiche che talvolta non arrivano in tempo. Inoltre, alcune app preinstallate (che non si possono rimuovere) sono fastidiose e occupano spazio inutile nella memoria.

Connettività e Audio:
La connettività (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, 4G) è buona, ma non mi ha impressionato particolarmente. In alcune zone con segnale più debole, ho riscontrato qualche difficoltà nella navigazione internet. Per quanto riguarda l'audio, la qualità dello speaker non è delle migliori, con un suono abbastanza piatto e poco potente. Non è un dispositivo che consiglio per l'ascolto di musica o per guardare video senza cuffie.

Conclusioni:
In sintesi, l'UMIDIGI G5A ha alcune caratteristiche interessanti, come il design e la durata della batteria, ma nella pratica non riesce a soddisfare completamente le mie aspettative. Le prestazioni non sono al livello che mi aspettavo da uno smartphone con queste specifiche e la fotocamera, pur non essendo pessima, non offre risultati eccellenti. Se cercate un dispositivo per uso quotidiano senza troppe pretese, può andar bene, ma se siete utenti più esigenti o abituati a dispositivi di fascia medio-alta, credo che dovreste cercare altrove.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
If you're like me, and like saving a few bucks if you need to upgrade or replace your old Android phone, consider this one.

I bought this one to replace a BLU G20 Android phone that the battery was not charging very well any longer, so I decided to upgrade. Overall, the phone feels solid, like a premium phone.

The camera is OK, but like others said, it struggles in low light situations. The phone has 3 lenses, one in the front acting as a 5MP selfie, and 2 in the back, one 8MP for wide angle photos, and one 16MP for main use. Unlike other budget phones in this price range that has 2 lenses in the back, like my old phone has, only one is actually in use. In this camera, all three are used for what you want to do. In other budget phones with 2 back lenses, the second lens is kind of like the 4th funnel on the Titanic. It doesn't do anything but is there for anesthetics. This phone utilizes both rear lenses.

If Internet is your thing, this phone does not use 5G data. It uses the classic 4G-LTE. However, it does have a dual band Wi-Fi controller so you can connect to either the 2.4ghz or 5ghz band so you can use your homes 5G Home Internet to get faster speeds.

Battery life is good, it got me through a day and a half already before it needed charging when my battery reached 35%. As for charging itself, it does not allow for quick charging, so keep that in mind when you see the battery getting low.

Since this phone is unlocked, it was quite easy to swap my SIM card from the old phone to the new one. This phone will work with practically any carrier that uses T-Mobiles towers.

Another thing I liked was how well this phone works with 3-D wallpapers. The quality of the display is very sharp and offers both 60Hz and 90Hz refresh rates. While using 90Hz does drain the battery more than using 60Hz, I keep mine at 90Hz. It does make a difference.

Another feature I like is the Extended Ram function. This phone features 6GB of physical RAM plus 6GB of extended RAM (virtual RAM), effectively giving it up to 12GB of RAM for smoother multitasking, especially for a budget phone. This virtual RAM borrows from the 128GB of internal storage, allowing more apps to stay open in the background for better performance. I have mine set to maximum size, and it makes a very big difference in the apps speed when I compare it to my old phone running the same apps.

This phone is powered by a 1.6GHz Octa-Core processor and runs Android 15, making it capable for light tasks, streaming, and general use, though not high-end gaming. So, if gaming is your thing, you may want to look elsewhere.

Overall, a very solid basic Android phone that looks, feels, and runs like a premium one.

Summarizing, the N20 is a decent, low-cost secondary phone and is reasonably priced for its features and capabilities. It could be used as a main phone as long as your needs are moderate, but it is not a replacement for a new iPhone or Galaxy.

text:
If you're like me, and like saving a few bucks if you need to upgrade or replace your old Android phone, consider this one.

I bought this one to replace a BLU G20 Android phone that the battery was not charging very well any longer, so I decided to upgrade. Overall, the phone feels solid, like a premium phone.

The camera is OK, but like others said, it struggles in low light situations. The phone has 3 lenses, one in the front acting as a 5MP selfie, and 2 in the back, one 8MP for wide angle photos, and one 16MP for main use. Unlike other budget phones in this price range that has 2 lenses in the back, like my old phone has, only one is actually in use. In this camera, all three are used for what you want to do. In other budget phones with 2 back lenses, the second lens is kind of like the 4th funnel on the Titanic. It doesn't do anything but is there for anesthetics. This phone utilizes both rear lenses.

If Internet is your thing, this phone does not use 5G data. It uses the classic 4G-LTE. However, it does have a dual band Wi-Fi controller so you can connect to either the 2.4ghz or 5ghz band so you can use your homes 5G Home Internet to get faster speeds.

Battery life is good, it got me through a day and a half already before it needed charging when my battery reached 35%. As for charging itself, it does not allow for quick charging, so keep that in mind when you see the battery getting low.

Since this phone is unlocked, it was quite easy to swap my SIM card from the old phone to the new one. This phone will work with practically any carrier that uses T-Mobiles towers.

Another thing I liked was how well this phone works with 3-D wallpapers. The quality of the display is very sharp and offers both 60Hz and 90Hz refresh rates. While using 90Hz does drain the battery more than using 60Hz, I keep mine at 90Hz. It does make a difference.

Another feature I like is the Extended Ram function. This phone features 6GB of physical RAM plus 6GB of extended RAM (virtual RAM), effectively giving it up to 12GB of RAM for smoother multitasking, especially for a budget phone. This virtual RAM borrows from the 128GB of internal storage, allowing more apps to stay open in the background for better performance. I have mine set to maximum size, and it makes a very big difference in the apps speed when I compare it to my old phone running the same apps.

This phone is powered by a 1.6GHz Octa-Core processor and runs Android 15, making it capable for light tasks, streaming, and general use, though not high-end gaming. So, if gaming is your thing, you may want to look elsewhere.

Overall, a very solid basic Android phone that looks, feels, and runs like a premium one.

text:
It's a slick phone at a great price. Complete with Android 13 and even a headphone jack. Based on price and other reviews, this is one of the best rated phones from independent carriers, at a price that can't be beat.

I purchased it because my 4 year old phone Motorola G7 Power was having battery and charge port issues (and running out of memory with only 32 gigs). On the first few charges of the new Ulefone, it charged to 100% and displayed 'Fully Charged'. However, it quickly started failing to charge fully, getting only to 94% and never stating 'fully charged'.

I contacted Ulefone support through their website and they routed me to their Amazon support team. I also contacted Amazon support 8 days after the return window closed. The agent authorized a return and I immediately ordered a new phone (one step up, the model with up to 16 gigs of RAM - which includes 8 virtual). The two models are otherwise identical, so I think my battery issue may have been related to older stock (product fulfillment was via Amazon).

I received my new phone, set it up and it's been about 5 days and it's charged fully to 100% AND is definitely holding the charge longer. It also doesn't seem to have any issues when it goes into battery saver mode (the original phone seemed to have issues crashing games like Wordscapes in battery saver mode). The original also seemed to drain quickly.

Other pros and cons - the camera is decent for the price. This is about 90% less in price than an iPhone, so the camera is as expected. There's no indication of remaining battery life estimate in settings, which I got spoiled with on my Motorola. That phone also had the shake to turn on flashlight which I will miss too. This one has a flashlight but you turn it on through the drop down menu (like most phones).

I had issues with Amazon customer service on the return/refund and wish I had contacted only Ulefone first as I think it may have been resolved with an exchange, I am not sure, but in the end, it was resolved after speaking to a supervisor.

I hope to get many years of enjoyment out of this really nice looking phone at a phenomenal price. It even includes a clear plastic case so I don't have to buy one additionally.

text:
Auf der suche nach einem günstigen aber technisch für diese Preisklasse gut ausgestatteten Smartphone für ein Familienmitglied, bin ich auf das UMIDIGI C1 Max gestoßen. Der Hersteller UMIDIGI wird wohl hier zu Lande nicht sehr bekannt sein, ich habe mich jedoch dazu entschieden dieses Smartphone zu nehmen und es ist wirklich begeisternd.

* Das Smartphone wurde über Amazon Prime wie immer schnell geliefert.
* Es war sicher und gut verpackt. Das Design ist schlicht aber solide
* Überzeugt hat mich aufjedenfall der Lieferumfang, hierbei ist ein Ladegerät vorhanden, sowie eine angebrachte Display-Schutzfolie und eine Durchsichtige Schutzhülle. All das ist für diese Preisklasse mehr als Fair vom Hersteller. Bei den großen Playern im Markt ist dies ja leider nicht mehr üblich.
* Optisch sieht das Smartphone edel und hochwertig aus.

Mit Android 12 und dem Unisoc Octacore Prozessor ist das Smartphone sehr flott unterwegs, hierbei muss man aber auch fairerweise sagen das es keine Ultra-Gamingmaschine ist :) Ich denke aber alle altäglichen Aufgaben sollte dieses Smartphone jedoch meistern können.

Auf der Speicherseite sind 128GB interner Speicher und 6GB Arbeitsspeicher sind für diesen Preis sehr gut. Der Speicher ist hierbei sehr Peformant, was mich positiv überrascht hat. Eine Erweiterung des Speichers ist mit einer Micro-SD Karte möglich, ich persönlich bin kein großer Fan von SD-Karten im Smartphone, da es in der Vergangenheit immer wieder zu problem kam mit den SD-Karten, unabhängig vom verwendeten Smartphone. Wer also auf viel internen Speicher setzen will oder sogar muss, der sollte sich nach einem anderen Model umschauen.

Das Display hat eine gute helligkeit ist aber sicherlich mit keinem FULL-HD Display vergleichbar, auch hier sollte das HD+ Display für viele Anwender jedoch ausreichend sein. Hätte dieses Smartphone ein FULL-HD Display, wäre es der totale Preis/Leistungskracher :)

Die Anbindung im WLAN ist einfach und läuft sehr flott auch die 4G Nutzung ist gut und man kommt unterwegs ohne Probleme durch den Altag.

Die akkuleistung ist solide und man kommt entspannt einen guten Tag ohne Steckdose mit dem Smartphome aus, hier ist der Verwendungszweck eines jeden Anwenders unterschiedlich und so kann die Akkudauer sicherlich bei jedem einzelnen anders ausfallen.

Ob ein Update auf Android 13 folgen wird, hängt jetzt sicherlich am Hersteller UMDIGI.

Mein Fazit:

Das Smartphone erhält von mir 5 Sterne, weil es mich einfach im Gesamtpaket überzeugt hat und ich würde in dieser Preisklasse immer wieder zu dem UMIDIGI C1 Max greifen. Wer also ein günstiges und solides Smartphone für ein kleines Budget sucht, erhält hiermit und gutes Gerät.

Würde der Hersteller UMIDIGI ein FULL-HD Display einbauen in dieser Preisklasse, dann wäre dieses Smartphone einfach ein TOP einsteiger bis sogar untere Mittelklasse Smartphone :)
