text:
October 24, 2024 So, what is the big deal about 5G vs. 4G wireless service? An internet search of “is 5G better than 4G” produced a number of similar answers including: “The main advantages of 5G over 4G are that it offers faster potential speeds, much lower latency, and support for more simultaneous devices.” and “5G offers significantly faster downloads, quicker uploads, and more people to be connected at the same time. That means fewer delays when using your phone and accessing web content.”

Next, I checked what my Canadian carrier is offering: “As Canada's largest 5G network, we cover over 32 million people in over 2,400 communities across the country.” I should be good to go with my current carrier, especially if 5G access is included in their plans at no extra cost. If you are curious, then “5G” stands for fifth generation while “5G+” (or the 3500 MHZ spectrum) is the latest network technology that will reportedly improve my carrier’s existing 5G network. While I checked to confirm that my home location is in the 5G coverage area, it seems that a cell phone is most often used when not at home. I’m satisfied that my carrier offers coverage which will be useful.

Now, in order to take advantage of the benefits of a 5G network I need an enabled cell phone such as the Umidigi G9 5G while noting that my purchase of this phone is recent, and so these are my first impressions.

A quick review of the specifications show that it possesses a number of worthwhile components such as a processor introduced earlier this year (2024). One review site says: “The Unisoc T765 is a mid-range chipset offering balanced performance, suitable for general smartphone tasks and moderately demanding games...” This is a Dual-SIM and Dual-Mode 5G processor. There is 6+6GB Extended RAM along with 128GB ROM. My preference is to use only on-board RAM, rather than extending it, for a seemingly faster experience (although who can really tell); however, your needs may require more RAM. It is always nice to have options. Users can add a SD card with the potential of up to 1TB of storage for photos and music.

If you are into photography, then the G9 has three lenses: 50 MP, f/1.8 (wide), AF 2 MP f/2.4, (macro) and a 2 MP, f/2.4, (depth) plus a LED flash. While I have a macro lens for my DSLR camera, I haven’t seen one on a phone. I’m looking forward to using this feature. Recently the Northern Lights were very visible in my home town. Using a phone camera provided a great way to see and photograph this wonderful display in the night sky. The selfie camera is 8 MP f/2.2 (wide) with both front and rear cameras offering video.

Other features which caught my eye include: the 5000mAh battery with fast 18W charging, the quality of the 6.75" 90Hz display, and a FM radio with built-in antenna thus providing the possibility of local information during power outages (e.g., weather events).

The G9 5G package contains the phone, a pre-applied protective screen film, phone case, power adapter, C-type cable, etc. One quibble is the phone case which while seemingly flexible/durable is also quite opaque so the space black colour of the phone is not really evident. I’ll probably look around for another (perhaps black matte) case.

As mentioned, I haven’t had this Umidigi G9 5G smartphone for long and so I’m looking forward to learning more about the included Android 14 operating system, security via a side fingerprint sensor or AI face unlock, and navigation using GPS, Glonass, Beidou, or Galileo. I’m very pleased with my purchase, especially with the potential of a fast 5G connection.

Update: April 24, 2025 I've been using this phone for many weeks now and everything has been working as expected. Photos are fine, texting works great, and I have no complaints about the audio quality during telephone calls. I'm still happy with my purchase. Alas, I don't understand reviewers who haven't had a good experience.

text:
Auriculares inalámbricos cómodos y con buen sonido para uso diario

He estado usando los Xiaomi Redmi Buds 8 Lite varias semanas y, por el precio que tienen, me han parecido unos auriculares inalámbricos Bluetooth muy equilibrados para el día a día. Son ligeros, se ajustan bien al oído y no cansan aunque los lleves puestos durante bastante tiempo.

El sonido es claro y con buenos graves para su gama, y la cancelación activa de ruido (ANC) —aunque no es de nivel premium— ayuda bastante a reducir ruidos ambientales como conversaciones o ruido de fondo en transporte o en casa. La conexión Bluetooth es estable, y los controles táctiles funcionan bien para pausar música, cambiar pista o responder llamadas.

La batería dura varias horas con una carga completa, y el estuche permite recargas adicionales, lo que es ideal para llevarlos contigo todo el día sin preocupaciones. También me gustó que la latencia es baja al ver vídeos en el móvil, lo cual mejora la experiencia multimedia.

No son los auriculares más avanzados del mercado, pero para uso casual, música, llamadas y contenido multimedia, ofrecen una experiencia sólida por el precio.

👍 Lo que más me gustó

✔ Comodidad y ajuste adecuado al oído
✔ Sonido equilibrado para música y vídeos
✔ Cancelación activa de ruido decente en su gama
✔ Batería duradera y estuche con carga adicional
✔ Controles táctiles intuitivos

👎 Cosas a tener en cuenta

➖ La ANC no es tan potente como en modelos de gama alta
➖ El estuche no tiene carga inalámbrica
➖ No tienen funciones avanzadas (EQ personalizada o audio de alta gama)

Conclusión

Los Redmi Buds 8 Lite son unos auriculares muy competitivos en relación calidad‑precio, ideales si buscas confort, buen sonido y cancelación de ruido básica en el uso diario. Perfectos para desplazamientos, llamadas, música y vídeos sin complicaciones.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
When I get a new phone, I usually go for a liquid screen protector instead of glass ones. The glass versions never seem to register my touch properly, while the liquid ones have saved me more than once. I’ve taken a few falls, and even cracked the glass on my camera once, but the phone screen itself never got a scratch from those drops. Pretty impressive. Over time, I did end up with some hairline scratches on the screen, so they’re not perfect, but overall the liquid protectors did a really solid job, just not what I wanted this time around. The biggest drawback is that they need hours to set, which means leaving your phone untouched overnight or longer. That’s not easy when your whole life is on your phone like mine. So, with my new Pixel 10, I decided to try a protector that applied more like a sticker.

This case caught my eye because it included that type of protector, and the instructions (plus the installation videos) were clear and helpful. I’ve been applying screen protectors for over 15 years, but it’s still nice to have a quick refresher, especially when using a new brand.

I did have one hiccup. When I pulled the tab off the screen protector, only the tab came off, not the adhesive covering the sticky side. For a minute, I thought it was the type that just rests on the glass and is held in place by the case, which was frustrating. I even started trying to clean off the tab residue and almost reached for the Goo Gone. Luckily, I noticed a faint line that suggested there really was adhesive to peel. It took some careful finessing (and double-checking the video) before I got it off properly. Once I did, the application went smoothly. Watching the protector adhere when you run your finger down the middle is oddly satisfying. I used my driver’s license to press out bubbles and make sure it was even, but any card works, and if you don’t have one handy, fingers will do the trick.

Getting my phone into the case itself took a little force, which I actually like. It feels secure, and I know it won’t slip out even if (realistically, when) I drop it.

I’m really glad I bought this. Great product for my new Pixel 10!

text:
Sto usando questa cover da qualche giorno sul mio Oppo Find X9 Pro e finora sono molto soddisfatto.

Il telefono entra perfettamente nella cover, tutto è ben allineato e si percepisce subito una sensazione di sicurezza. Una volta montata, il dispositivo risulta ben protetto senza diventare troppo ingombrante. Aggiunge un po’ di spessore, ma in senso positivo, perché dà più tranquillità nell’uso quotidiano.

La prima cosa che ho notato è la presa. I lati e il retro hanno una texture piacevole che rende il telefono più facile da tenere in mano, cosa che apprezzo molto visto che è uno smartphone piuttosto grande. Non risulta scivoloso. Anche i materiali danno una buona sensazione, solidi e non economici, con un buon equilibrio tra rigidità e flessibilità.

I pulsanti funzionano bene, sono abbastanza reattivi e facili da premere, anche se non sono i più morbidi che abbia provato. I ritagli sono precisi e tutto resta comodo da usare.

Apprezzo anche i bordi rialzati intorno a schermo e fotocamera, che aggiungono un livello extra di protezione quando si appoggia il telefono.

Se devo trovare un piccolo limite, non è la cover più sottile in assoluto, ma è chiaramente una scelta legata alla protezione.

Nel complesso è una cover affidabile e ben costruita, pensata più per proteggere e offrire una buona presa che per l’estetica, ed è esattamente quello che cercavo.
